example_sentences.english: I feel like eating chicken wings for dinner tonight.

notes: "You have big writing letters. What do you think these are? THAT WOULD HAVE TO BE UPPERCASE LETTERS, RIGHT? Whoops, sorry, caps lock was on for a moment, there." "The readings for the kanji in this word are a bit strange. The 大 portion is actually read using the kun'yomi, the same reading as you learned with 大きい (おおきい). Everything else is just on'yomi. So, you'll need to remember the one exception with 大. If you do, you should be okay."

example_sentences.japanese: さいしょの字は、大文字でかいてください。
example_sentences.english: Please capitalize the first letter.

example_sentences.japanese: タイトルを大文字でかき直してください。
example_sentences.english: Please rewrite the title in uppercase letters.

example_sentences.japanese: 何故だかわからないけど、小文字より大文字の方が好きです。
example_sentences.english: For some reason I like uppercase more than lowercase.

notes:
"The gold star is Venus. It's the only planet in our solar system that's the same color as gold." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"Things are equal in how they're arranged. They have perfect symmetry and balance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこに見えているのは、金星です。
example_sentences.english: What you see over there is Venus.

example_sentences.japanese: 金星の学こうには、うんどう会はありますか？
example_sentences.english: Do they have Sports Day in the school on Venus?

example_sentences.japanese: 人類はいつか金星に移住することになるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Someday humans will migrate to Venus.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はとても均整のとれた体形をしている.
example_sentences.english: She has a very well proportioned body.

english: After This, From Now On, After, Since
notes:
"From after, just means after this or from now on." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"The game of go is one where you surround the enemy with your go pieces. So, adding this to the name of go makes sense, and just makes this the go board game." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「以後、このようなことがないように、気をつけるんだぞ。」「はい、先生。以後、もっと気をつけます。」
example_sentences.english: """After this you need to be more careful so this doesn't happen again."" ""Yes, teacher. I'll be more careful from now on."""

example_sentences.japanese: 10月29日のトーフグの日以後、ビエトは行方をくらましているんだ。
example_sentences.english: Viet hasn't been heard of since October 29—Tofugu Day.

example_sentences.japanese: それ以後、その作家は酒を一滴も飲まなくなった。
example_sentences.english: After that, the writer stopped drinking alcohol, not even a single drop.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は囲碁トーナメントの決勝に進みました。
example_sentences.english: He advanced to the finals of the Go tournament.

notes: "This is a strange one, but only at first glance. You make a house. You'd think this would mean something like ""building a house"" or ""construction"" or something. Instead, it means author. Think of it this way: An author makes (writes and creates works) in their home. Authors don't make their word magic in a corporate office!" "The readings are on'yomi readings, though さく from 作 gets shortened to さっ. Just be sure to remember that and you should be able to read this word just fine."

example_sentences.japanese: あこがれの作家さんから、サインをもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got an autograph from an aspiring author.

example_sentences.japanese: この作家、ずいぶん思い切ったね。
example_sentences.english: This novelist pushed things pretty far, eh?

example_sentences.japanese: あのベストセラー作家の趣味はサッカーだ。
example_sentences.english: That best-selling author’s hobby is playing soccer.

notes: "A wind boat. This is a strange one for sure. You may assume this is like one of those giant balloons you can go ride around in, and you'd be partly right. Really, this word covers the general word balloon, though it especially has to do with the toy-style balloons (or smaller balloons). It's a little round wind ship!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あのピエロが、風船で犬を作ってくれたんだ。
example_sentences.english: That clown made a dog out of a balloon for me.

example_sentences.japanese: ひ行きによったば合は、この風船をエチケットぶくろの代わりにごしようください。
example_sentences.english: Please use this balloon as a motion sickness bag when you feel air sick.

example_sentences.japanese: 風船を使って実際に空飛ぶ家を作った人たちがいます。
example_sentences.english: Some people actually made a house float using balloons.

hiragana: ちかぢか, きんきん, ちかじか
notes: "When something is close close (the 々 character repeats the kanji that was before it) it will happen before long." "The reading is the kun'yomi reading twice; that's the one you learn with the vocab word 近い from the previous level. The second 近 gets converted to ぢか, though, so take note of that."

example_sentences.japanese: それについては、近々はっぴょうがあると思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: I think there will be an announcement about it soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 近々雪がふるはずなので、たくさんつもったらかまくらを作ります。
example_sentences.english: We're supposed to get snow soon, so if we get a lot, I will make a snow igloo.

example_sentences.japanese: もしタバコを吸い続けるなら、あなたは近々癌を発症するでしょう。
example_sentences.english: You’ll get cancer before long if you keep smoking.

notes: "This is simply a blue sky (aka a blue sky!)." "You'd think that this word would use on'yomi readings to read it, but it doesn't (shake that angry fist at the kanji gods!). Instead, it's double kun'yomi, probably because this word is really like two separate words put together, ""blue"" and ""sky."" In the previous level you unlocked these two separate words, learning their readings. That means you should be able to read this as well. One quick note is the rendaku-fication of 空 as well. It becomes ぞら."

example_sentences.japanese: 青空のせいで海は青いの？
example_sentences.english: Is the ocean blue because of the blue sky?

example_sentences.japanese: 未来の子どもたちに、今と同じくらいうつくしい青空をのこしてあげましょうよ。
example_sentences.english: Let our future generations have the same beautiful sky as we do.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は一日中晴れて、青空が広がっていました。
example_sentences.english: Today, it was sunny all day and the blue sky was above us.

notes: "The teaching room is just a classroom." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 学生は、教室ではじめに何をしますか。
example_sentences.english: What will the students do in the classroom first?

example_sentences.japanese: かれは教室でタバコをくわえたところを、先生に目げきされました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher witnessed him putting a cigarette in his mouth in the classroom.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生がいなくなったのはたったの五分間だけだったが、大学生たちは完璧に教室を滅茶苦茶にしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The teacher had only been gone for five minutes, but the university students had completely trashed the classroom.

notes: "You know that 活用 means ""conjugation"" and that 〜形 means ""form, so that means this is the conjugated form!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このどうしの活用形を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach me the conjugated form of this verb.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日から、じょどうしの活用形をべんきょうし直してます。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I started re-learning the conjugated form of auxiliary verbs.

example_sentences.japanese: この辞書アプリでは、活用形から動詞の逆引き検索も可能です。
example_sentences.english: In this dictionary app it’s possible to look up verbs using their conjugated forms.

notes: "When you write down your day (and do it every day) that's your diary." "This jukugo word uses the on'yomi readings, except the 日 (にち) is shortened with a small っ, making the reading にっき."

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの日記も、この本と一しょにここにおいておきます。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to leave your diary with this book here.

example_sentences.japanese: 北米には、こうかん日記みたいな文化はないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: We don't have a culture of diary exchange in North America.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の夜、フグの日記を読んだんだけどさ、実はとても悲しい日記だったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I read Fugu’s journal last night and, to be honest, it was really sad.

notes: "Something that is person shaped that isn't a person? That has to be some kind of doll or puppet." "The reading for 人 is pretty normal, though the reading for 形 is different from the one you learned. To remember this, think of a doll... made totally of gyoza (ぎょう) dumplings. This doll is crazy (like most dolls) and it's eating itself and trying to get you to eat some of it too. Hey... why you no eat me? Mmmm. Gyoza doll."

example_sentences.japanese: たん生日プレゼントに、人形をもって行きます。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to bring a doll for her birthday present.

example_sentences.japanese: その人形、ちゃんと元のところにもどしておいてね。
example_sentences.english: Put the doll back the way you found it.

example_sentences.japanese: 17歳まで、私の親友は靴下で作った腕人形だった。
example_sentences.english: Until the age of 17, my best friend was a sock puppet.

english: Elementary School Student, Primary School Student, Elementary Schooler, Primary Schooler, Grade Schooler, Grade School Student
notes: "You know 学生 is student, so what is a small student? Think young. That would be an Elementary School Student." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生だからって、あまく見てるとけがするぜ！
example_sentences.english: I may just be an elementary school student, but if you underestimate me, you'll regret it!

example_sentences.japanese: きょうしつのドアをあけると、一人の小学生が石ころみたいにぐっすりねむっていました。
example_sentences.english: When I opened the classroom door, there was a grade schooler sleeping like a rock.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生の頃、いつもコインを投げて自分の行動を決めていました。
example_sentences.english: When I was an elementary school student, I always made my decisions by flipping a coin.

english: End Of The Month, Month End
notes: "You know how 月 can also mean month? If you add 末 on there you have the ""month end"" aka the end of the month." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 月末までに五キロやせます。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to lose five kilos by the end of this month.

example_sentences.japanese: ここ、ブラックきぎょうすぎるから、月末ににげ出すわ。
example_sentences.english: This company exploits its employees too much, so I'm bailing out at the end of the month!

example_sentences.japanese: 私の上司は、コアラで給料を払います。毎月末、わたしには二匹のコアラが支払われます。
example_sentences.english: My boss pays me in koala bears. I get two at the end of every month.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: Imagine a fish. Now imagine the fish playing soccer, while wearing a nun's outfit. This is a soccer nun (さかな)."

example_sentences.japanese: 魚はすきですが、生魚はにが手です。
example_sentences.english: I like fish, but I don’t like it raw.

example_sentences.japanese: バランスのいいちょう食をとるために、いつもグラノーラと魚を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I always eat granola and fish for a well-balanced breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: もう絶対にメキシコの軽トラの積み荷から魚を買うもんか。
example_sentences.english: I’ll never buy fish from the back of a pickup truck in Mexico again.

english: Full Name, First And Last Name
notes: "Both of these kanji have to do with names. You have both family name and name. Both of those names together makes for a First And Last Name... a full name if you will." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の氏名ぐらいは、日本ごでかけるようになりたいよね。
example_sentences.english: You at least want to be able to write your full name in Japanese, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ごさん考までに、わたしの氏名は、高 一子です。
example_sentences.english: For your information, my name is Ichiko Ko.

example_sentences.japanese: そちらの誓約書に氏名をご記入頂ければ、大砲で貴方の頭の上の林檎を撃ちぬいて差し上げます。
example_sentences.english: If you would please write your first and last name on the waiver, we will proceed with shooting an apple off of your head with a cannon.

notes: "The reason the earth is the way it is is because of the geography of it. Though it may seem kind of strange that geography is bringing reason to the earth, if you think of geography as a study, then you can think about how you try to get reason through that, as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で地理のべん強をするのもすきですが、友だちとべん強する方がたのしいです。
example_sentences.english: I like studying geography by myself too, but it’s more fun to study with my friend.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ人の友人は地理が全くのにが手で、さい近まで日本が中国の首とだとおもっていたらしい。
example_sentences.english: My American friend is not good at geography at all, so I heard that she used to think Japan was the capital of China until very recently.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺たちが道に迷ったってどういうことだよ？お前、地理の先公じゃねえのかよ？
example_sentences.english: What do you mean we’re lost? Aren’t you a geography teacher?

notes: "A gold fish is really just gold in color, but it's still called a goldfish." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、五年前の夏まつりの金魚すくいですくった金魚です。
example_sentences.english: I scooped this goldfish at a goldfish scooping booth during a summer festival five years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 金魚もかぜをひくんですか？
example_sentences.english: Can goldfish get colds, too?

example_sentences.japanese: 金魚は、三秒間しか記憶がないので、自分たちがお城に住んでいることに気がづく度に驚いています。
example_sentences.english: Goldfish only have three second memories so they’re always surprised when they realize that they live in a castle.

notes: "The big thing in the sky is the heavens. The heavens where birds and planes soar, not the one you go to after you die if you've been really good." "The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own. Just remember that そら becomes ぞら because of rendaku here."

example_sentences.japanese: 大空を見ていたら、いやな気もちがふきとんだ。
example_sentences.english: The unpleasant feeling vanished when I looked up at the sky.

example_sentences.japanese: アイリちゃんは大空にうかぶお星さまになったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Airi became a star in the firmament.

example_sentences.japanese: 鷲が大空を悠々と飛んでいた。
example_sentences.english: The eagle flew leisurely in the heavens.

notes: "The tall school is for when your kids get about as tall as they're going to get. That's high school, when most people stop growing taller." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 高校まで、車で行けば十分ですよ。
example_sentences.english: It only takes 10 minutes to get to the high school if you drive.

example_sentences.japanese: 高校ではいつも、おひるにどんなものを食べていますか？
example_sentences.english: What kind of food do you guys usually have for lunch in high school?

example_sentences.japanese: 高校に行って初めて話をし始めたんです。そして、今は、話を止めることができません。
example_sentences.english: I didn’t start talking until I went to high school. Now I can’t shut up.

english: How To Make, Way To Make, Way Of Making
notes: "This is the way to make something. This is how to make something. You'll see this for directions on building something." You should know the kun'yomi readings for both of these from lower level vocab. Use that knowledge to remember the reading for this word as well.

example_sentences.japanese: おいしいマカロニチーズの作り方を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach me how to make delicious macaroni and cheese.

example_sentences.japanese: 麦茶の作り方には、おゆでわかしながらに出す方ほう、ふっとうさせたおゆでジワジワおゆ出しする方ほう、つめたい水でジワジワ水出しする方ほうの三しゅるいありますが、それぞれメリットデメリットがあります。
example_sentences.english: There are three ways to make barley tea; steeping it in boiling water, steeping it slowly in boiled water, and steeping it slowly in cold water, and each comes with pros and cons.

example_sentences.japanese: 手裏剣の作り方を知りたいですか？
example_sentences.english: Do you want to know how to make a ninja star?

notes: "A boat's body is called the hull." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 船体にらくがきをしたのはだれだ！？
example_sentences.english: Who graffitied the hull?

example_sentences.japanese: クラーケンがしょく手で船体をつきやぶったんだ。
example_sentences.english: The kraken smashed its tentacles through the ship's hull.

example_sentences.japanese: 船体は思った以上に大きかった。
example_sentences.english: The hull was bigger than I thought.

notes: "The previous week was last week." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 先週は学校はお休みでした。
example_sentences.english: School was out last week.

example_sentences.japanese: 大きくなったねー。先週はまだあんなに小さかったのに。
example_sentences.english: You sure have grown a lot! You were still tiny last week though.

example_sentences.japanese: 先週出席した経済相互援助会議で、喋る犬にインタビューされたんだが、あいつは本当に嫌なやつだった。
example_sentences.english: I was interviewed by a talking dog about the Comecon convention I attended last week. He was so insulting.

english: Less Than, Or Less, Not Exceeding, Below
notes:
"Compared with this, it's below. That's another way to say that what you have is less than it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"Look in the sea and you'll see what looks like a crow moving under the water and it's a thief! It's stealing from all the fish. As it comes closer you see that it isn't a crow, it's a squid. Or a cuttlefish? One or the other." "The reading for this word is an exception. I'd give you a mnemonic to remember it but it looks like the mnemonic for いか is いか! If you've been paying attention, you know this is squid already! "

example_sentences.japanese: 五千円以下の本だなをさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m looking for a bookshelf that’s 5,000 yen or less.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのすきなネコのしゅるいは以下の通りです。
example_sentences.english: The list of cat breeds that Koichi likes is as follows:

example_sentences.japanese: 以下同文です。
example_sentences.english: Those below are the same.

example_sentences.japanese: 烏賊の刺し身が大好物です。
example_sentences.english: Squid sashimi is my favorite food.

notes: "The reasoning that your heart makes decides what you do. Probably when kanji was being made people thought that the heart directed our actions, not our brains. So, if you think about it that way, the reasoning of your heart is your mental state. Nowadays that's known as psychology." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ねこの心理を思うがままにあやつれるようになりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to be able to manipulate cats' minds as much as I want.

example_sentences.japanese: 春人以外の男どもには、女せいのせんさいな心理は分からないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Men, with the exception of Haruto, don't understand the delicate psychology of women.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンと彼女に翻弄される人々の心理を、君の小説で描いてみてもらえないかな？人気が出ると思うんだけど。
example_sentences.english: Can you depict the mental state of Salmon and those she deceives in your novel? I think people would love it.

english: Middle School Student, Junior High School Student, Middle Schooler, Junior High Schooler, Junior High Student
notes: "You've seen 学生 (means student). Now let's look at a student who's in the middle. Perhaps we can call this a middle school student or a junior high school student, depending on where you're from." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 中学生にもなって、まだお母さんといっしょにおふろに入ってるんですか？
example_sentences.english: You are a middle schooler now, but you're still taking baths with your mom?

example_sentences.japanese: かち目のないたたかいはしない方がいいということは、中学生でも知っているよ。
example_sentences.english: Even a junior high student knows that you should choose your battles wisely.

example_sentences.japanese: 中学生の頃、自分自身に、「書かなくても覚えられるから大丈夫」という大法螺をふいてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: "When I was a middle school student, the biggest lie I said to myself was, ""I can remember that without writing it down."""

notes:
"Compared with this, it's more. That's another way to say that what you have is more than it. That's all. ;)" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"It differs from the normal condition of things, making it weird. It is an abnormality. There is something wrong." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このえいがは、十八才以上しか見れません。
example_sentences.english: Only people 18 or older can watch this movie.

example_sentences.japanese: 手つづきは以上です。
example_sentences.english: That's all for the paperwork.

example_sentences.japanese: １００歳以上の人は、必ずブラジャーを着用し無くてはならない。
example_sentences.english: People who are 100 years old or older must wear bras.

example_sentences.japanese: 子宮がん検診の結果が「異状あり」だったのでびびっています。
example_sentences.english: "My Pap test was ""abnormal"" and I’m freaking out."

notes: "The next week is the next week. It isn't last week or this week, it's the next one!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週の日よう日にレストランに行きます。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to a restaurant next Sunday.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週はどれぐらい雪がふるかな？
example_sentences.english: I wonder how much snow we'll get next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲み会は来週に延期になりました。
example_sentences.english: The drinking party was postponed until next week.

hiragana: かいぎょ, うみざかな
notes: "An ocean fish is simply an ocean fish. They also happen to be the most delicious kind of fish." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: さけは海魚ですか？それとも川魚ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is salmon a saltwater fish? Or is it a freshwater fish?

example_sentences.japanese: 海中には、色とりどりの海魚がおよいでいました。
example_sentences.english: In the sea, there were a lot of colorful ocean fish swimming around.

example_sentences.japanese: 水族館には沢山の種類の海魚がいますが、スタッフは僕達に一匹も食べてはいけませんと言いました。
example_sentences.english: There is a wide variety of saltwater fish at the aquarium, but the staff said we’re not allowed to eat any of them.

english: One Loaf of Bread, One Loaf
notes: "One bread loaf counter is counting one loaf of bread." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Be careful of the shortening though!

example_sentences.japanese: 一斤のパンは6枚切りか8枚切りで売られていることが多い。
example_sentences.english: Loaves of bread are often sold in slices of six or eight.

example_sentences.japanese: たった一斤のパンで給料日までを生き延びなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: I need to survive on only one loaf of bread until payday.

example_sentences.japanese: 食パン一斤と、ニュテラがあれば生きていけるよ。
example_sentences.english: I can live off of a loaf of bread and some Nutella.

notes: "Compared with this, it's outside what you wanted. You'll have anything other than that." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビール以外ならなんでもいいです。
example_sentences.english: I’m okay with anything other than beer.

example_sentences.japanese: マンガ以外は何もよみません。
example_sentences.english: I read nothing but manga.

example_sentences.japanese: 式の間中新郎が花嫁の胸元を上から眺めていたこと以外は、とても素敵な結婚式でした。
example_sentences.english: Other than the groom looking down the front of the bride’s dress during the ceremony, it was a nice wedding.

notes: "You have a period of time and it's called a period or era! Simple!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の時代は、インターネットで何でもかうことができます。
example_sentences.english: In this era, you can buy anything on the Internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 明里は、わたしの大学時代の友人です。
example_sentences.english: Akari is my friend from college.

example_sentences.japanese: 紫式部は、平安時代中期の女性作家かつ歌人です。
example_sentences.english: Murasaki Shikibu was a female writer and poet from the mid–Heian period.

notes: "From before, just means previously or before now." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 以前、パーティーで一どお会いしましたよね。
example_sentences.english: I met you once before at a party, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 以前はよく船よいしていたんですが、今はさっぱりなくなりました。
example_sentences.english: I used to get seasick all the time, but not anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の親友は、以前は天文学者に知られていなかった惑星の出身です。
example_sentences.english: My best friend is from a planet that was previously unknown to astronomers.

notes: "The reason your heart does what it does is all psychological. The study of that is psychology." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: えいぎょうをするなら、心理学を学んだ方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You should study psychology if you work in sales.

example_sentences.japanese: 心理学のせつ明によると「あい手にひどいことが言えるということは、その人にいぞんしてるということ」らしいです。
example_sentences.english: According to the psychology explanation, it looks like when you are able to say something mean to a person, you're actually being dependent on them.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は大学で犯罪心理学を専攻していました。
example_sentences.english: My major was criminal psychology in college.

notes: "The reason reason is so reason-ish! That's why this word means reason as well, how could it not? Do you have a reason why it shouldn't be? I thought not." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: とくに理由はありません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t have any specific reason.

example_sentences.japanese: 未だけいひのせいさんをしてないのには、何か理由があるんですか？
example_sentences.english: Do you have any reason for not having settled your business expenses yet?

example_sentences.japanese: 論理的な理由から、彼は行方不明になったゴム手袋の事件の犯人が風船屋であることを導いた。
example_sentences.english: Using logic and reason, he solved the case of the rubber gloves and the culprit was the balloon maker.

english: Shortcoming, Fault, Defect, Flaw, Weakness, Weak Point
notes: "You have a lack of points. These are things about yourself you wish were better. These are your shortcomings." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just watch out because けつ is being shortened to けっ here!"

example_sentences.japanese: だれだって、何かしらの欠点をもってるものさ。
example_sentences.english: Everyone has some sort of weakness.

example_sentences.japanese: そうだ、ちょっと思い出したんだけど、かの女って欠点がないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Oh, I just remembered, she doesn't have any faults.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は欠点がありすぎるので、絶対にプロのサッカー選手にはなれません。たとえば、私には足がありません。
example_sentences.english: I’ll never become a professional soccer player because I have too many shortcomings, for example, I don’t have any legs.

notes: "Not to be confused with 会社, which is a company, this is society. When a company meets together, it's like a bunch of people, who are in groups, who come together to live in one world. That is a society." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今家を出ても、社会のじゅぎょうに間にあわないと思います。
example_sentences.english: Even if I leave home right now, I think I’ll probably be late for social studies.

example_sentences.japanese: 国さい社会の一員として、めしテロにはだんじてくっしません。
example_sentences.english: As a member of the international society, I will not yield to food porn.

example_sentences.japanese: 社会問題として、若者がお葬式で自分撮りをすることについて考える必要がある。
example_sentences.english: As a society, we need to be concerned about youths taking ’selfies’ at funerals.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading you learned with the kanji is the same as the reading for the vocab.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の夏は、さく年よりもあついです。
example_sentences.english: This summer is hotter than last year.

example_sentences.japanese: 近いうちに夏ワンピをかいに行きたいんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I want to go buy some summer dresses sometime soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏にして楽しいことは三つだけだ。映画、ビデオゲーム、それから木彫の鴨を作ること。
example_sentences.english: Summer is only good for three things. Movies, video games, and duck carving.

notes: "There are many white birds out there, for sure, but one really stands out if you ask me. That bird is the swan. It's big, it's white, and it's majestic." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 自どりをするためだけに白鳥をみずうみから引きずり出すなんてひどすぎるよ。
example_sentences.english: Pulling a swan out of the lake just to take a selfie with it is too cruel.

example_sentences.japanese: 白ワインは魚りょうりに合うっていうけど、白鳥りょうりに合うワインは何か知っていますか？
example_sentences.english: They say that white wine goes well with fish, but do you know what kind of wine would go well with swan?

example_sentences.japanese: 白鳥はとても美しいが、汚らしい言葉遣いをする。
example_sentences.english: Swans are so pretty, but they use foul language.

notes: "This word is almost the same as the kanji, but only half of it. It means tag or amulet. They're about the same shape and size as money, but you can't buy a house with them (...probably)." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word:You can't find your tag anywhere. It was on your luggage, you swear, but now it's nowhere to be found. You forget about it for a while, then you eat your dinner (you're at a fancy dinner party). As you finish up your meal you see something. Your label fell into your food (ふだ)!"

example_sentences.japanese: このお札は、げんかんのドアの内がわにはっておいてください。
example_sentences.english: Please put this amulet on the inside of your front door.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の札を見せないようにした方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You should be careful not to show your hand.

example_sentences.japanese: ジェロってほんとにキモい。ドクロマークの絵が描かれた札でも付けておくべきだよ。
example_sentences.english: Jello is really disgusting. There should be a picture of a skull and crossbones on the label.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Throw a ""the"" in there if you'd like, as well." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You've reached the end of the universe. Nothing is there. You step out, and you're surprised because you get greeted by Sue. Imagine meeting this Sue, and talking to them for a while. You should come up with a Sue that you know or a famous Sue that you know. Just pick something you can remember."

example_sentences.japanese: こんなあそびがはやるとは、世も末だな。
example_sentences.english: If this kind of game is popular, then it’s the end of the world.

example_sentences.japanese: おたくのむす子さんは末が本当にたのしみですね。
example_sentences.english: You must be looking forward to seeing what your son might end up being in the future.

example_sentences.japanese: 激しい口論の末、末息子は私の金をどこかに埋めるために出て行ってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: After a heated discussion, my youngest son left to bury my gold somewhere.

notes: "The country peoples are the people of your country. They are the people." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当に国民はわれわれにさんせいしてくれるのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Will the people really give us their approval?

example_sentences.japanese: どうすれば日本国民になれますか。
example_sentences.english: How do you become a citizen of Japan?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨夜、PS4の新ゲームを買うために並んでいた国民たちは、凍って死にました。
example_sentences.english: The people waiting in line for the new PS4 game last night froze to death.

notes: "The now week is this week." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週は仕ごとがたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: There is a lot of work to do this week.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週の火よう日の午前十一じに、しぶ谷のハチ公前でまち合わせをしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's meet up in front of the Hachiko statue at 11 a.m. this Tuesday.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいゲームを４つ買ったので、今週はかなり忙しくなる。
example_sentences.english: This week is going to be really busy because I just bought four new video games.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: What time is it? It's time to key (とき) your enemy's car. Imagine yourself looking at your watch, waiting until the correct time to perform a synchronized keying of someone's car. Who do you hate the most? Whose car would you like to key?"

example_sentences.japanese: れいぼうをつける時は、白いボタンをおしてください。
example_sentences.english: When you want to turn on the air conditioning, please press the white button.

example_sentences.japanese: 時がかい決してくれるのをまつしかないよ。
example_sentences.english: We can do nothing but wait for time to solve this.

example_sentences.japanese: 幸せな時、いつも時が止まればいいのに、と思う。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I’m happy, I always think it would be nice if I could stop time.

notes: "Town peoples are the townspeople!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今すぐ町民をひなんさせるべきです！
example_sentences.english: The townspeople should find shelter right now!

example_sentences.japanese: この町民たちは、みんなちゃんと後かた付けができる。
example_sentences.english: These townspeople are all able to clean up after themselves.

example_sentences.japanese: この町の人達はみんな、この町の町民であることを誇りに思っています。
example_sentences.english: I feel like all the people in this town boast about being townspeople here.

english: Two Loaves of Bread, Two Loaves
notes: "Two bread loaf counters are counting two loaves of bread." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 二斤買えば100円もお得です。
example_sentences.english: If you buy two loaves of bread it will be 100 yen cheaper.

example_sentences.japanese: パンを二斤も焼いたのに、すぐに食べ切ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Even though I baked two loaves of bread, we finished it all.

example_sentences.japanese: 賞味期限が明後日だけど、二斤も食べきれるかな？
example_sentences.english: Do you think we can finish these two loaves of bread even though they're expiring the day after tomorrow?

english: Two Thirty, Half Past Two, Half Two
notes: "When it's two o'clock and a half what time do you think it is? That would be two thirty." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: そのえいがのかいえん時かんは二時半です。
example_sentences.english: The film begins at two-thirty.

example_sentences.japanese: 二時半に大じなやくそくがあるのにねぼうしちゃって、ちょっと今かなりテンパってます。
example_sentences.english: I have an important appointment at 2:30, but I overslept and now I'm freaking out.

example_sentences.japanese: 「私は明日午後二時半に、私のお母さんのお父さんの娘の姪っ子に会います。」「なんで、単にお姉ちゃんとランチに行くって言わないの？ありえないんだけど！」
example_sentences.english: """I’m meeting my mom’s father’s daughter’s niece tomorrow at two-thirty in the afternoon."" ""Why didn’t you just say you’re meeting your older sister for lunch tomorrow? Jeez!"""

notes: "A machine that pumps wind can malfunction and make too much, causing a typhoon. It's a really powerful machine to be able to move that much wind." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. Instead of だい for 台 though, this uses the reading たい. Remember it like this:When a typhoon is coming you have to tie (たい) down all of your stuff. Or, you know, if you already know the word typhoon, that's fine too."

example_sentences.japanese: 今回の台風は弱いので、あまり心ぱいしなくてもよさそうです。
example_sentences.english: This typhoon is weak, so it seems that we don’t have to worry too much.

example_sentences.japanese: ひじょうに強い台風トウフ号が、月よう日、西日本に上りくしました。
example_sentences.english: Strong typhoon Tofu made landfall in western Japan on Monday.

example_sentences.japanese: 大型の台風が日本列島に近づいています。
example_sentences.english: A large typhoon is approaching the Japanese islands.

english: University Student, College Student, Uni Student
notes: "You know that 学生 means ""student"" and you know that 大学 means university/college. Combine the two and you have a university student / college student." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 男の大学生と女の大学生がはなしています。
example_sentences.english: A male university student and a female university student are talking.

example_sentences.japanese: あの大学生の女せいは、ダイエット中です。
example_sentences.english: That college girl is on a diet.

example_sentences.japanese: マカロニチーズしか食べていないっていうのに、いったいどうして大学生は一日中勉強して夜中中お酒を飲む元気があるっていうんだ？
example_sentences.english: How do university students have the energy to study all day and drink all night when all they eat is macaroni and cheese?

notes: "The weak point is your weakpoint." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ついにアイツの弱点を見つけたぜ！
example_sentences.english: I finally discovered his weak point!

example_sentences.japanese: あの体そうせん手の弱点は、せいかくがじゅうなんせいに欠けているところだ。
example_sentences.english: That gymnast's weakness is that her personality lacks flexibility.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の従業員としての弱点は、恐らく弱点が一つも無いことです。
example_sentences.english: My weak point as an employee is probably that I have no weaknesses.

notes: "The end of the week is the weekend... that is, unless you work on the weekend, but we can't cater to everyone here." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は、おきなわにりょ行に行っていました。
example_sentences.english: I was in Okinawa over the weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: せん週末、雪が十センチつもりました。
example_sentences.english: We got 10 centimeters of snow last weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじに当たったんだけど、週末ローマにピザでも食べに行かない？
example_sentences.english: We just won the lottery, so do you want to go to Rome this weekend for pizza?

notes: "This is a good word to know to ask for the time. What is the time? This is how you ask what time it is." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 何時のひ行きにのるんですか？
example_sentences.english: What time will your plane leave?

example_sentences.japanese: 目まいをかんじはじめたのは何時ですか？
example_sentences.english: What time did you start to feel dizzy?

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜何時にボーリングに行くの？
example_sentences.english: What time are you going bowling tonight?

english: Year End, End Of The Year, End Of Year
notes: "The year end is the year end aka the end of the year." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: すみませんが、年末は、ちょっとバタバタしてじかんがとれなさそうです。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry, but I’ll be super busy around the end of the year and I probably can’t make time for it.

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルは、年末にトーフグのだい二えいぎょうぶにいどうになりました。
example_sentences.english: Michael was transferred to Sales Division II of Tofugu at the end of the year.

example_sentences.japanese: 年末までには、氷中毒から立ち直れるといいんだけど。
example_sentences.english: I hope to have gotten over my addiction to ice cubes before the end of the year.

notes: "Your dwelling place is the place you live. How do you identify one's dwelling place? By using the address." This word is made up of the on'yomi readings that you've already learned with the kanji. Have at it!

example_sentences.japanese: こちらにあなたの家の住所をかいてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write down your home address here.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスカードをおくりたいので住所をおしえてくれませんか？
example_sentences.english: Can you please give me your address so I can send you a Christmas card?

example_sentences.japanese: 私が月に購入した土地には、住所はありますか？自分宛に酸素を送りたいので、よろしくお願い致します。
example_sentences.english: Does the land I purchased on the Moon have an address? I want to mail myself some oxygen tanks.

notes: "Do you remember how 米国 can mean ""America?"" That 米 means America sometimes. So, when you see all rice (I mean, America), you can think of this word as meaning All America (sort of like how 全日本 means ""All Japan."")." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、全米がなみだした、大ヒットチョ～大作えいがです。
example_sentences.english: This is a mega-hit blockbuster that brought all of America to tears.

example_sentences.japanese: まつ山ひできは、2017年の全米オープンで二いに入った。
example_sentences.english: Hideki Matsuyama finished second at the 2017 U.S. Open.

example_sentences.japanese: 全米ヒットチャートで今一位の曲は何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What's the No. 1 song on the U.S. hit chart now?

english: Another Place, Somewhere Else, Other Place, Elsewhere
notes: "When you're talking about some other place you're talking about another place." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここじゃなくて、どこか他所の店に行こうよ。
example_sentences.english: Not here, let’s go to another store somewhere else.

example_sentences.japanese: 他所は他所、家は家！
example_sentences.english: Don't compare us to other families.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は暴力夫から逃れるために、他所に移り住んだ。
example_sentences.english: I moved somewhere else to escape from my abusive husband.

notes: "Someone who makes is someone who creates things. Back in the day, a creator like this may have been known as many things, but the big one that stands out is an author." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この小せつの作者の名前がどうしても思い出せません。
example_sentences.english: I just can’t remember this novel’s author’s name.

example_sentences.japanese: ついにテキストフグの作者に会えました。
example_sentences.english: We could finally meet with the writers of TextFugu.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の兄貴がギリシャ神話の作者だったんだが、今は失業している。
example_sentences.english: My brother was an author of Greek mythology, but now he’s unemployed.

notes: "A pond for electricity? May seem weird at first, but if you think of something that's gathering all the electricity into one pond... that thing is like a battery (and is a battery)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このおもちゃの電車は、電池でうごきます。
example_sentences.english: This toy train moves with batteries.

example_sentences.japanese: ママ、見てー！電池が取れちゃった。
example_sentences.english: Mom, look! The battery came off.

example_sentences.japanese: 自作のロボット犬の電池を買いに、ちょっくら町へ行ってくるよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m heading to town to buy a battery for the robot dog I created.

notes: "When you have both someones, you have both people. You'll notice over time that 者 is often used to indicate a person or type of person, so keep that in mind for future words as well!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: それは、両者にひがあると思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I think they’re both at fault for that.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチせん手とマイケルせん手、今のところ両者のじつ力はほぼご角のようです。
example_sentences.english: Player Koichi and Player Michael both seem to be pretty equally matched so far.

example_sentences.japanese: 車両事故に関与している両者は、共に衝突時に携帯電話で話をしていた。
example_sentences.english: Both of the people involved in the car accident were talking on their cell phones at the time of the crash.

notes: "The support bureau is the group that supports a business. It is the branch office. If it helps, this word has the same meaning as 支店 which you will also be learning in this level." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 千ば支局にてんきんすることになりました。
example_sentences.english: I was transferred to the Chiba branch office.

example_sentences.japanese: FBI東京支局の支局員のたこやきパーティーによんでもらった。
example_sentences.english: I got invited to the takoyaki party for the agents of FBI field office in Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビ大阪京都支局の前でくしゃみが出た。
example_sentences.english: I sneezed in front of the Kyoto branch of Television Osaka, Inc.

notes: "The support shop is the branch office. Presumably this is because the regular ""shop"" is the ""shop"" and anything that supports it is the local (branch) office.If it helps, this word has the same meaning as 支局 which you will also be learning in this level." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしのおっとは、大さか支店の支店長をつとめています。
example_sentences.english: My husband is the branch manager of the Osaka branch.

example_sentences.japanese: この支店には、一人で行どうすることがすきな人もはたらいている。
example_sentences.english: In this branch shop, there are workers who like to do things alone as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 支店長の髭は少し長すぎる。
example_sentences.english: Our branch manager’s mustache is a bit too long.

notes: "Noun version of decide? It's a decision." The reading for this word is the same as the kanji!

example_sentences.japanese: それでは、決をとりたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Well then I think that’s the decision I want to make.

example_sentences.japanese: なかなか決が出ないみたいだね。
example_sentences.english: It seems that it's taking a while to make a decision, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ジョン、ホットドッグアイスなんてものを作り始める決を下したのはお前だろう？だから首になったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: John, you made the decision to start making hotdog ice cream and that’s why you got fired.

english: East Exit, East Entrance, Eastern Exit, Eastern Entrance, East Gate
notes: "Remember how 入り口 means entrance and 出口 means exit? This is just the 口 part with a direction on it. That means it can be both entrance or exit. So when you have East up there this word can mean both East exit and East entrance. This is a great word to know if you need to know which side of a train station you need to leave on to go somewhere or meet someone!" "This word uses kun'yomi readings, possibly because of 口, which is a body part (body parts do that quite a bit in words and kanji). You should hopefully have seen both the kun'yomi readings from previous levels meaning you can read this word as well. Just watch out for the rendaku that changes くち to ぐち."

example_sentences.japanese: えきの東口で大道げいをしている人がいたよ。
example_sentences.english: There’s someone doing a street performance at the station’s east exit.

example_sentences.japanese: 東口でとった写しん、たぶん手ブレしたみたいで、ちょっとブレちゃってる。
example_sentences.english: The photo taken at the east gate is a bit blurry, probably from the camera shaking.

example_sentences.japanese: 緊急の際には、このビルの東口から避難してください。そこでは、コーヒーとドーナツが支給される予定です。
example_sentences.english: In the case of an emergency, please evacuate the building through the east exit. There will be coffee and donuts waiting for you there.

notes: "Electricity energy is just a fancy way to say electricity." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電気をつけてください。
example_sentences.english: Please turn on the light.

example_sentences.japanese: 電気をつけっぱなしにしないでって言ったじゃん！かせぎが少ないんだから、ちゃんと電気代せつやくにきょう力してよ。
example_sentences.english: I told you not to leave lights on. You don't earn very much, so you'd better cooperate to save on the electricity bill!

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃は暗闇を恐れていたが、今は電気料金の請求書を受け取る度に、光が怖いと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: When I was little I was afraid of the dark. Now, when I get my electric bill I’m afraid of the light.

notes: "The electricity power of something is its electric power." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 2016年4月から日本でスタートした、電力自由化についてくわしく教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Can you tell me everything you know about the Electricity Liberalization that started in Japan in April of 2016.

example_sentences.japanese: あの電力会社には電気代をはらいたくないよ。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to pay the bill to that electric company.

example_sentences.japanese: 電力が約三時間で復旧したので、私は面接の前に電動バリカンで頭を刈って整えることができました。
example_sentences.english: Power was restored in roughly three hours and I was able to fix my hair with my electric hair clippers before the interview.

notes: "An electricity child. What is a really small part of electricity? What makes up electricity? That would be the electron. This word can also refer to things that are electronic as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電子のおもさはいくらですか？
example_sentences.english: How much does an electron weigh?

example_sentences.japanese: その電子ピアノを直すのに、どれくらい時間がかかると思いますか？
example_sentences.english: How long do you think it will take to fix the electric piano?

example_sentences.japanese: ティラノサウルスは、1万電子ボルトの衝撃を受けた。
example_sentences.english: The Tyrannosaurus Rex was shocked with 10,000 electron volts.

notes: "When you use a drawing to replace your letters to type, you're using emoji! Those are the faces you send when you text or email. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: みなさんは絵文字はつかいますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you all use emoji?

example_sentences.japanese: しいて言えば、この絵文字がすきです。
example_sentences.english: If I had to choose, I like this emoji.

example_sentences.japanese: 一番よく使う絵文字を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Can you tell me which emoji you use the most?

notes: "Do you remember 工学 from a couple levels ago? This is someone who is in 工学. If 工学 is ""engineering"" then 工学者 is an engineer." The readings are just the on'yomi readings of the kanji. All things you should know now.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ルンバ」をはつ明したロボット工学者はだれですか？
example_sentences.english: Who’s the robotics engineer that invented the Roomba?

example_sentences.japanese: あの工学者のことはきらいですが、そうするべきだと思ったから、助けてあげました。
example_sentences.english: I helped that engineer, even though I don't like him, because I thought it was the right thing to do.

example_sentences.japanese: 工学者になるためには、長期間勉強をする必要があります。
example_sentences.english: To become an engineer, you have to put in long hours of studying.

notes: "Every morning is every morning!" The reading is a combination of on'yomi and kun'yomi. That being said, both readings for both kanji are the readings you learned with the kanji so you should be able to read this.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝、シャワーをあびます。
example_sentences.english: I take a shower every morning

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝、本当に楽しかったです。ありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: I had a really great time with you every morning. Thank you so much.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝ラジオ体操をします。
example_sentences.english: I do radio exercises every morning.

hiragana: こうじょう, こうば
notes: "A construction location is a factory. A factory is a place where you or machines do a bunch of construction!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: トヨタの工場に行きたいんですけど、何で行くのがべんりですか。
example_sentences.english: I’d like to go to the Toyota factory - which way would be the most convenient?

example_sentences.japanese: 毎ばん、ベーコン工場のせじょうをするのは、わたしの主人の役目です。
example_sentences.english: It's my husband's job to lock up the bacon factory every night.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が働きたいと思う唯一の工場は、クッキー工場です。
example_sentences.english: The only factory I would want to work in is a factory that makes cookies.

notes: "A famous place is a famous place. When traveling around Japan, you should ask about the 名所 if you can." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ポートランドのかん光名所を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Can you tell me about some Portland tourist spots?

example_sentences.japanese: 名所めぐりの日にちが近くなってきたら、またれんらくするね。
example_sentences.english: I'll get in touch with you when we get closer to the day we're visiting famous places.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、スターバックスやデニーズ、それからニューヨーク郵便局など数々の名所を見るために、ニューヨークへ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to New York to see all the famous places like Starbucks, Denny’s, and the New York City post office.

notes: "Something is versus the outside. Back in the day, everything was a battle with the outside. You had the Mongols... the rebels... and the foreigners. So, when you say something is ""versus the outside"" you're just saying it's something compared to where you are right now. It's something that's foreign or from overseas." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: せん後、日本の対外せいさくはどのようにかわっていったのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: How did Japan’s foreign policy change postwar?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の対外せいさくについてのポッドキャストをレコーディングしています。
example_sentences.english: We are recording a podcast about Japan's foreign policy.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカの対外債務が5000億ドルを突破した時に、俺の個人負債が500万ドルを突破したのは、単なる偶然なのか？
example_sentences.english: Is it just a coincidence that my personal debt shot past $5 million when America’s foreign debt shot past $500 billion?

notes: "The north sea road is the road you take to get to the northern sea. That is an area of Japan, actually. That area is known as Hokkaido. It's a very nice place, be sure to visit it if you can for some of the freshest seafood around." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The ほく does get shortened though, so be careful!"

example_sentences.japanese: ぼくは、北海道で雪合せんをしたことがあります。
example_sentences.english: I’ve gone yukigassen snowball fighting in Hokkaido.

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道についたどー！本もののすしを食べるどー！
example_sentences.english: I've arrived in Hokkaido! Time to eat some real sushi!

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道のお土産といえば、何が有名でしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Speaking of Hokkaido souvenirs, what’s famous?

notes: "This word was probably made pretty recently. A horse's power? That is horsepower." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Take note that the reading for 力 is the りき version of the reading. You can remember this by thinking about how it's Ricky who drives the high horsepower cars. Vroom vroom Ricky!"

example_sentences.japanese: 自どう車の馬力を上げるには、どうすればいいですか。
example_sentences.english: What’s the best way to increase a car’s horsepower?

example_sentences.japanese: アサヒのじいちゃんって、本当に馬力があるよね。
example_sentences.english: Asahi, your grandpa is such an energetic person, isn't he?

example_sentences.japanese: 約四年間いじくり回したおかげで、今俺の芝刈り機は450馬力もあるんだぜ。
example_sentences.english: I tinkered with my lawnmower for about four years and now it has 450 horsepower.

english: Important Task, Great Duty, Important Role
notes: "A big duty is a great duty. It can also be an important task. Think about some kind of big duty you have. Then, think about what an important task it is too. Feel proud of your important task." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この大役をしっかりはたせるよう、一生けんめいがんばります！
example_sentences.english: I will try with all my might to successfully accomplish this important task.

example_sentences.japanese: ずい分とまた大役を買って出たものだね。
example_sentences.english: You volunteered for such a great duty, eh?

example_sentences.japanese: ロード・オブ・ザ・リングでフロドは大役を任されたが、靴も履かずに見事にやってのけた。
example_sentences.english: Frodo, of the Lord of the Rings, was given the most important task and he did it all without putting on shoes.

notes: "The before time was last time." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 前回のじゅぎょうでは、カエルのかいぼうをしました。
example_sentences.english: Last class we dissected a frog.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは、前回のつづきからはじめたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Okay so... we will continue from where we ended last time.

example_sentences.japanese: 前回のレッスンの復習は家でちゃんとやってきましたか？
example_sentences.english: Did you guys review the last lesson at home properly?

notes:
"Life that comes out of the earth is made up of different kinds of materials. Sometimes it's cloth, sometimes it's dough, but everything has to be made out of something." "This word uses the kun'yomi reading for 生 and the on'yomi reading for 地. You haven't learned either of these readings yet, sorry! Here's some mnemonics to help you:If you want the best material to make clothes or pies out of, the key (き)is asking Jesus (じ)! He knows everything, including where to find the materials for whatever weird thing you're making. Just remember: Who's the key? Jesus!"

"When you write down a lot of stuff focusing on one thing it's called an article. If it's on something that just happened it will probably be a news story." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: マリメッコの生地でクッションを作りました。
example_sentences.english: I made a cushion out of Marimekko fabric.

example_sentences.japanese: このカーテンは、パラシュート生地でできています。
example_sentences.english: This curtain is made of parachute material.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷凍のパイ生地を買ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please go buy a frozen piecrust.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは、アメリカの教いくについて、記事をかきました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote an article about American education.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスティンの記事、今月号のナショナル・ジオグラフィックで見たよ！
example_sentences.english: Kristen, I've just found your article in this month's National Geographic magazine!

example_sentences.japanese: この記事はデタラメだ。
example_sentences.english: This news story is nonsense.

notes: "The study of numbers is mathematics (or math)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 川下さんは、石田中学校で数学の先生をしています。
example_sentences.english: Ms. Kawashita is a mathematics teacher at Ishida junior high school.

example_sentences.japanese: 数学のしけん、明日だっていうのに、海人はホントききかんがねーよな。
example_sentences.english: The math exam is tomorrow, but Kaito doesn't seem to have any sense of urgency.

example_sentences.japanese: 数学さんよ、どうか大人になって自分の問題は自分で解決してくれよな。
example_sentences.english: Dear Math, please grow up and solve your own problems by yourself.

notes: "The study of medicine is medical science. It can also be called medicine, but make sure to think of it as the ""medicine"" where it has to do with ""medical science.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: さい近は、医学の本を月に三さつぐらいよんでいます。
example_sentences.english: Lately, I’ve been reading about three medical science books a month.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの兄は、医学ぶを目ざしています。
example_sentences.english: My older brother is trying to get into a medical school.

example_sentences.japanese: 医学はいつも最新の薬を発見し続けている。昨日は、医者が皿洗いをするようになる薬を私にくれたよ。
example_sentences.english: Medical science is always discovering new medications. Just yesterday, my doctor gave me a pill that makes it so I can wash dishes.

english: Medical University, Medical School, Med School
notes: "You've seen 大学 to mean ""college."" So take the 大 and put it with medicine to create ""medicine college,"" or medical university." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは、医大を目ざしてべん強しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m studying to get into medical school.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者のたまごをかれ氏にするため、医大生のふりをして、医大にせん入してみました。
example_sentences.english: I pretended to be a med student and snuck into med school to find a future doctor boyfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、ポケモンコレクションを売って、医大の学費を払った。
example_sentences.english: I paid my tuition for med school by selling my Pokémon collection.

notes: "Earth's middle sea is the Mediterranean Sea. It may not look like it's in the middle of the earth, but a long time ago that's what people thought. It's the sea between Southern Europe and Northern Africa." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: さい近、地中海りょうりにハマっているんですよね。
example_sentences.english: Lately, I’ve been obsessed with Mediterranean cooking.

example_sentences.japanese: ただ今、地中海からきたく中でーす。
example_sentences.english: I'm on my way home from the Mediterranean Sea.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏休みに、家族で地中海をクルーズしてきました。
example_sentences.english: I went on a cruise with my family on the Mediterranean Sea over summer vacation.

notes: "When you're buddy-buddy with the master of a country, you are rewarded splendidly. Why? Because this is a monarchy where being buddies with the master is a very advantageous thing!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 天のうのいる日本は君主国ですか、それとも民主国ですか？
example_sentences.english: Japan has an emperor, so is it a monarchy or a democracy?

example_sentences.japanese: やっとこの君主国にもどって来たぜ！
example_sentences.english: Ah, I'm finally back in this monarchy!

example_sentences.japanese: イギリス君主国は、別のラップ音楽のビデオを作る締め切りをまた大幅に過ぎている。
example_sentences.english: The British Monarchy is long overdue for making another rap music video.

notes:
The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. Hopefully this means you won't have to wake up too early in the morning to study kanji, now.

"The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well, but it also means cannabis as well." "You always smoke your cannabis in the 朝. No other time. Just the 朝."

example_sentences.japanese: 朝のあいさつをしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please say the morning greeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝は毎日、トロトロの半じゅく目玉やきを食べます。
example_sentences.english: Every morning I eat over easy and sunny-side-up eggs.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の朝は早起きをしなくてはいけません。だって、Xboxをプレイしまくるという長い一日が待っているから。
example_sentences.english: I have to wake up early tomorrow morning because I have a long day of Xbox playing to do.

example_sentences.japanese: これは麻の木じゃないって、何回説明したら分かってもらえるんですか？
example_sentences.english: How many times do I have to tell you that this is not a hemp plant?

notes: "The morning sun is not only the morning sun, but it's the rising sun as well (because that's when the sun rises, right?)." "This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji, which is convenient since you've learned both of them by now with the words 朝 (あさ) and 日 (ひ). Put them together and what do you get? あさひ!"

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の朝、一しょに山にのぼって朝日を見ませんか？
example_sentences.english: Would you like to climb a mountain with me tomorrow morning to see the morning sun?

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてあの朝日の絵をかべから外してしまったんですか？
example_sentences.english: Why did you take the picture of the rising sun off of the wall?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は「日出ずる国」として知られているが、それは「朝日国旗」に見事に描写されている。
example_sentences.english: "Japan is known as ""the Land of the Rising Sun,"" which is excellently depicted on its ""Rising Sun"" flag."

notes: "What is the sound of pleasure? What sound puts you at ease? For most people that is some nice music. Just be sure you don't put on any Bieber... that would be like 不音楽 or something... I kid, I kid." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 楽 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:If you play your music too loud, people will come and gawk (がく) at you. But if you try to turn it off and say, ""OH WHAT I DON'T LIKE MUSIC ANYWAY!"" they'll gawk at you even more. Learn proper music etiquette and people won't gawk at you so much, okay?"

example_sentences.japanese: べん強してから音楽をききます。
example_sentences.english: I’ll listen to music after I study.

example_sentences.japanese: 音楽をききながら仕ごとをすることはよくないと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you think it isn't good to work while listening to music?

example_sentences.japanese: 違ったタイプの音楽が創りだされることはもう無いのかなって思ったりするんだよね。あなたは、人類は既に全ジャンルの音楽を全て創りだしちゃったと思う？
example_sentences.english: I wonder if another type of music will be created. Do you think mankind already made every possible genre?

notes: "A number in a series plus a number. You know what happens when two kanji with basically the same meaning get combined into one by now, right? It just turns out to be the same meaning, basically. This word means number." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのじゅけん番号は何番ですか？
example_sentences.english: What is your exam number?

example_sentences.japanese: 三十分で、この番号をおぼえてください。
example_sentences.english: You have 30 minutes to memorize a series of numbers.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、めちゃくちゃ落ち込んでるんだよ。だって、彼女に偽の電話番号を渡されたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m really disappointed right now because she gave me a fake phone number.

notes: "When you're number two in a number in a series you're number two. Not quite as good as being 一番, but take what you can get, you know?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: き末しけんで、学年で二番になりました。
example_sentences.english: I got second place in final exams for my year.

example_sentences.japanese: これは二番目に古いゴジラえいがです。
example_sentences.english: This is the second oldest Godzilla movie.

example_sentences.japanese: カルロス・スリムは、世界大富豪番付けで二番に順位を下げた。
example_sentences.english: Carlos Slim fell to the number two spot on the list of the world’s richest people.

notes: "A number letter isn't a letter like the ones you're reading now, it's more like a numeral, like 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, etc." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 数字がのびるからといって、下ひんなきじをけいさいするのはよした方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of the increase in numbers, you shouldn’t publish vulgar news stories.

example_sentences.japanese: この子は、一万五千六百七十二けたの数字をあん記している天才じです。
example_sentences.english: This child is a genius who memorized a 15,672-digit number.

example_sentences.japanese: 数字の十一は、私がバレーボールをする時にいつも身に付ける背番号です。
example_sentences.english: Eleven is the number I always wear when I play volleyball.

hiragana: わたしじしん, わたくしじしん
notes: """When it comes to somebody like myself... aka I..."" When you say this you're really saying ""personally"" or ""as for me.""" "The readings are a bit weird here. The 私 is わたし and the rest is on'yomi kanji readings. So, it's a mix of both, I'm afraid. ""When it comes to me, I like mixing up on'yomi and kun'yomi because I hate myself."""

example_sentences.japanese: 私自身は、その動物園の問題にはあまり関心がないんです。
example_sentences.english: Personally, I'm indifferent to the zoo's issues.

example_sentences.japanese: 私自身は、そんなにきょくたんなことじゃなければ、どんな食生活でも良いと思っています。
example_sentences.english: As for me, as long as it isn't too extreme, I think any kind of diet is okay.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたがもし私自身よりも私のことを知っていると思っているんだとしたら、 それはとんだ大間違いよ。
example_sentences.english: You’re way off base if you think you know me better than I know myself.

notes: "The number of points is how many points there are (aka the score)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニに百点まん点で点数をつけるなら、何点になると思いますか？
example_sentences.english: If you were to give WaniKani a score out of 100, how many points would you give it?

example_sentences.japanese: この点数は、こないだくれたプレゼントのおかえしだよ。
example_sentences.english: These points are in return for the present you gave me.

example_sentences.japanese: 「どうしてそのテストでこんなに低い点数をとったの？」「欠席のせい。つまり、僕の隣の席の子が休んでたんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Why did you get such a low grade on that test?"" ""Because of absences. I mean, the kid who sits next to me was absent."""

notes: "I have no idea how this one works, admittedly. You mix a number in a series and you get a police box. A police box? Who would want to work in one of those? Think of it this way: all the police have to draw numbers from a hat (they're all mixed up in there). Those who pull out the wrong numbers are on police box duty. That's why mixed numbers in a series = police box. Do you see it?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 交番で、大しかんまでの道をききました。
example_sentences.english: I asked for directions to the embassy at the police box.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しく入って来たヒマリちゃんは、この交番のアイドルです。
example_sentences.english: Himari, the new girl in this police box, is Miss Popular.

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、お巡りさん。一番近い交番はどこですか？ある男が私のことをデブと言ったので、警察を呼ぶ必要があるんです。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, officer. Where is the nearest police box? I need to call the police because some man just called me fat.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "If you fall into a pond, what sound do you make? EEEEK (いけ)! Or maybe you're just afraid of ponds (I don't blame you, there are probably snakes or leeches or alligators in there) and you EEEEK when someone mentions them."

example_sentences.japanese: この池は大きすぎる。
example_sentences.english: This pond is too big.

example_sentences.japanese: 池に竹の矢をおとしたら、中からかみさまがあらわれて、「おまえがおとしたのはこの竹の矢か、それともこの金の矢か。」ときかれたので、正じきに「竹の矢ですが、その金の矢もほしいです。」といった。
example_sentences.english: "When I dropped a bamboo arrow in the pond, God came out of it and asked me, ""Did you drop this bamboo arrow or this gold arrow?"" So I answered honestly, ""I dropped the bamboo arrow, but I want the gold arrow, too."""

example_sentences.japanese: うちのご近所さんは、鳥を撃ち落としては、うちの池に投げ入れる。
example_sentences.english: My neighbor keeps tossing the dead birds that he shoots into my pond.

notes: "You've seen 私立, which is ""private,"" and you've seen 大学, which is ""college"" or ""university."" So, combine them together and you have a private college / private university." "If you know the readings of the words 私立 and 大学 you'll be able to read this. It's also all jukugo on'yomi readings too, so you can read it that way."

example_sentences.japanese: 私立大学は公立大学よりじゅ業料が高いです。
example_sentences.english: Tuition for private universities is more expensive than that of public universities.

example_sentences.japanese: わせ田大学は日本の有名な私立大学です。
example_sentences.english: Waseda University is a famous, private university in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: あの出火した私立大学は、私が通っている学校だよ。
example_sentences.english: The private college that’s on fire is the college I’m currently attending.

notes: "Use a number in a series to group the things you watch and listen to. That makes them your programs. Your TV and radio programs, specifically. If you watch TV you'll hear it a lot!" "This word consists of the on'yomi reading for 番 and the kun'yomi reading for 組. You've learned them both so as long as you remember the rendaku, you should be able to read this word too!"

example_sentences.japanese: この番組はおも白くありませんでしたが、わたしのすきなはいゆうが出ていました。
example_sentences.english: This TV program wasn’t interesting, but my favorite actor was in it.

example_sentences.japanese: きのうの番組で、あの二人はついに両しゃがなっとくするだきょうあんにたどりついたよ。
example_sentences.english: In yesterday's program, those two finally managed to work out a compromise.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はバラエティ番組しか見ません。
example_sentences.english: I haven’t watched anything but variety programs lately.

english: Public Official, Government Official, Public Servant
notes: "A person with duty is someone who works for the government... a government official or public official." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: せいじ家や役人には下手にさからわない方がいい。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn’t carelessly disobey politicians or public officials.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはトーフグの社長であるだけでなく、文ぶ科学しょうの役人でもある。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is not only the president of Tofugu but also an official in the Ministry of Education.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の街の役人の一人が、カメラの前で嘘をついたということで、調べを受けている。
example_sentences.english: One of my city’s public officials is under investigation for lying on camera.

notes: "A person of a dwelling is someone who lives at that dwelling. They are a resident." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなしん夜に大声でけんかをしたら、近りんの住人にめいわくだろう。
example_sentences.english: If you argue loudly so late at night, you’ll bother your neighbors.

example_sentences.japanese: 話し合いの末、森の住人とみずうみの住人は、一しょに百本のけんを買うことにした。
example_sentences.english: After talking it over, forest-dwellers and lake-dwellers agreed to buy 100 swords together.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は地球の住人です。パーティーにようこそ。
example_sentences.english: I am a resident of planet Earth. Welcome to the party.

notes: "When a number of years have passed you say that several years have passed! You don't want to say how many years, so just say several years." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 数年がすぎさった。
example_sentences.english: Several years passed.

example_sentences.japanese: 数年前まで、日本に住んでいました。
example_sentences.english: I lived in Japan until a few years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: この絵が完成するには、あと数年かかります。
example_sentences.english: It will take several years for that painting to be complete.

notes: "The road you walk on is the sidewalk... at least I hope that's where you walk." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして自てん車が歩道を走ってはいけないんですか？
example_sentences.english: Why can’t bicycles travel on sidewalks?

example_sentences.japanese: まもなくうごく歩道がおわりますので、足元にごちゅういください。
example_sentences.english: You are approaching the end of the moving walkway. Please watch your step.

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車は、忙しい車道じゃなく、歩道を走るべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Bicycles should be ridden on sidewalks, not on busy city streets.

notes: "Remember how 米国 can also mean America? That goes for North and South America, actually, not just the United States. So, south America is South America." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 学生時代に、バックパッカーとして南米をりょ行しました。
example_sentences.english: In my school days, I took a backpacking trip through South America.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルの水道水は、南米で今までのんだ水の中で一番おいしい。
example_sentences.english: This hotel's tap water is the best water I’ve ever had in South America.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめんなさい。南米はアメリカの一部だと思っていました。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry. I thought South America was a part of the United States of America.

english: South Exit, South Entrance, Southern Exit, Southern Entrance, South Gate
notes: "The South mouth isn't actually a mouth you find in the south pole or anything, it's an entrance or exit. This is kind of like how 入り口 means entrance (the 口 represents a doorway). You'll see this word a lot in places like train stations or airports. It means both South exit and South entrance." "The reading for these kanji are both kun'yomi. Probably because it's two words put together (South + Exit) rather than a single word. Also, body parts tend to change words into kun'yomi readings as well.
