So, you've seen vocab words that give you the kun'yomi reading of both 南 and 口, right? Now you just need to combine the two vocab readings into one to be able to read this word. Just watch out for the rendaku that changes くち to ぐち."

example_sentences.japanese: そこに行くなら、南口から出るのが一番近いです。
example_sentences.english: If you’re going there, leaving from the south exit is the fastest.

example_sentences.japanese: このモールの南口で今UFOが見られるよ！
example_sentences.english: You can see a UFO at the southern entrance of this mall right now!

example_sentences.japanese: 新宿南口でナンパされた。
example_sentences.english: I was hit on at the south exit of Shinjuku station.

notes: "If you've got an eye on a certain course, it's a subject you really want to take. Maybe you're in school and that means you'll be taking a lot of courses. Maybe you're a teacher and you're planning out your curriculum. Either way, you have your eye on the course-prize." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: とくいな科目とにが手な科目を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Tell me about your strong subjects and weak subjects.

example_sentences.japanese: 多分、その科目、さいじゅこうしないといけないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I probably have to retake that course.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きな科目は何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What subjects do you like?

english: The Number Of People, Number Of People, The Amount Of People, Amount Of People
notes: "The person count is the number of people. Don't confuse this with the ""population"" or something like that, though. This is more like ""how many people are at this event?"" What's the 人数, you know?" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just be sure to take note of the rendaku for the second half, where すう goes to ずう."

example_sentences.japanese: カラオケに行く人数は全ぶで何人ですか。
example_sentences.english: What’s the total number of people going to karaoke?

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのあたらしいライターのぼしゅう人数は何人ですか？
example_sentences.english: What are the recruitment numbers for the new Tofugu writers?

example_sentences.japanese: 沢山の人数の人が、この国の人は同じズボンを履くべきだという私の提案に反対しました。
example_sentences.english: There are a great number of people who disagree with my proposal that everyone in this country must wear the same pants.

hiragana: あした, あす, みょうにち
notes: "A bright day isn't today (because today was terrible), it's tomorrow, because you can always look to tomorrow to be a better, brighter day." "The reading makes no sense at all. You have to learn it straight up, and can't rely on the kanji it's made from. Why is tomorrow going to be such a bright and awesome day? Because you're making ash tacos for dinner, and that's your favorite. Imagine imagining tomorrow, full of ash tacos and deliciousness. Maybe you could use some of those Dorito taco shells?A note about the other two readings あす and みょうにち: あす is used in the news and in weather reports, and みょうにち is really only used in business, so you should really only be using あした for now. But it's good to know that the other two readings exist!"

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、びょういんへ行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s go to the hospital tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は明日の風がふく。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow is another day.

example_sentences.japanese: 一ヶ月イタリアに行くことを知らせるために、明日学校に電話しなくてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: I need to call the school tomorrow to inform them that I’m going to Italy for a month.

notes: "You would think that an electricity car was an electric car, but this word was made before the days of the Prius. This refers to a train, which I guess was electric at some point." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 下のひょうは、「電車の時間」と「バスの時間」です。
example_sentences.english: "As for the chart below, it shows ""train times"" and ""bus times."""

example_sentences.japanese: この電車にのって、トトロえきでおりて、ネコバスにのりかえてください。
example_sentences.english: Get on this train, get off at Totoro Station and transfer to the Catbus.

example_sentences.japanese: ホグワーツ特急は電車じゃなくて汽車です。
example_sentences.english: The Hogwarts Express isn’t an electric train, it’s a steam train.

english: Water Supply, Water Service, Waterworks, Aqueduct, Conduit, Water Line
notes: "A water road carries your water supply. In the old days, these were called aqueducts." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この水道の水は、のんでも平気ですよ。
example_sentences.english: This tap water is safe to drink.

example_sentences.japanese: 水道代がはらえなかったので、水道が止められてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't pay the water bill, so my water was shut off.

example_sentences.japanese: 水道が凍結してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The water line froze.

notes: "One who uses heaven to their advantage is someone from heaven, like an angel." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ニッカちゃん、マジ天使だわー。
example_sentences.english: Nikka really is an angel.

example_sentences.japanese: あの天使と、少しきょりをおきたいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I think I need to distance myself from the angel for a while.

example_sentences.japanese: 天使のように可愛い女の子に会った。
example_sentences.english: I met a girl who was as cute as an angel.

notes: "How heavy is your body? Figure that out and you'll have your body weight." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: アンナさんの体重は、何キロですか？
example_sentences.english: What is Anna’s body weight in kilograms?

example_sentences.japanese: 次の身体そく定で体重をはかるのが待ちきれない。
example_sentences.english: I can’t wait to weigh myself at my next body measuring.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして私があなたの体重を知っているのか聞かないで。ジェシカが口を滑らせたことは絶対に誰にも言わないって、あの子と約束したんだから。
example_sentences.english: Don’t ask me how I know your weight. I promised Jessica that I wouldn’t tell you that she told me.

notes: "A book shop is a shop that sells books. A bookstore." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: よくその本屋に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to that bookstore often.

example_sentences.japanese: この本屋には、ツアーガイドブックがたく山おいてあります。
example_sentences.english: This bookshop has a lot of tourist guidebooks.

example_sentences.japanese: 本屋のレジでアルバイトをしています。
example_sentences.english: I work part time at the bookstore cash register.

english: Butcher Shop, Meat Shop, Meat Store
notes: "A meat shop is a place that sells meat. Who sells meat? A butcher shop." "For 肉 you use the にく reading (which you learned with the kanji). For 屋 you use the kun'yomi, which you learned with the kanji. Basically, if you learned the kanji readings, you can read this word!"

example_sentences.japanese: あそこの肉屋で、合いびき肉を100g買ってきてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Could you buy 100 grams of ground beef and pork from the butcher shop over there?

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのお肉屋さん、新しいあじのビーガンとうふバーガーをかいはつしてるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that butcher shop is creating a new flavor of vegan tofu burgers.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の小さな町には「お肉屋さん」とい名前のレストランがあったんだけど、本当の「お肉屋さん」がどんなものかを知った時にはとてもショックでした。それで、今、私はベジタリアンなんです。
example_sentences.english: My small town had a restaurant called The Butcher Shop, so I was really surprised to learn what a real butcher shop is. I’m a vegetarian now.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the reading you learned with the kanji and uses the on'yomi even though it's a single word. Very strange, but convenient for you so long as you remember this exception reading word.

example_sentences.japanese: 服を引き出しの中に入れてください。
example_sentences.english: Please put your clothes in the drawer.

example_sentences.japanese: かわいい！おそろいの服をきてるんですね。
example_sentences.english: How cute! They are wearing matching clothing.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はチョー暑くて、あなたはあまりにも多くの服を着ているよ。
example_sentences.english: It’s so hot today. You’re wearing too many clothes.

notes: "A club room is a clubroom!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そのまんがなら、部室に全かんそろってるよ。
example_sentences.english: As for that manga, we have the whole series in the clubroom.

example_sentences.japanese: 何ぜか部室に魚を口にくわえたネコがいるんです。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, there is a cat with a fish in its mouth in the clubroom.

example_sentences.japanese: 部室に忘れ物をしちゃった。
example_sentences.english: I forgot something in the clubroom.

notes: "When something happens at every occurrence and at every degree, it's something that happens frequently. It happens each time." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎度おさわがせして、申しわけありません。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry for all the times I’ve troubled you.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎度のことだが、空は今日もちゅう文を決めるのがおそい。
example_sentences.english: Sora can't make up his mind about which one to order, as usual.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎度有難う御座います。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for your continued patronage.

english: Elementary School, Primary School, Grade School
notes: "You've seen 学校 from a couple levels ago. Now we're adding a small to it. What is a ""small school""? That's a school for small people, making it an elementary school." "The reading is the regular on'yomi reading of 小 plus the vocab word 学校 that you've seen previously. Combine these two things for the reading of 小学校."

example_sentences.japanese: 小学校で、小さな子どもたちに、色々な絵本をよんであげています。
example_sentences.english: I'm reading various picture books to little children in elementary schools.

example_sentences.japanese: あの小学校には、コウイチ気取りの六年生の男の子がいます。
example_sentences.english: In that elementary school, there is a sixth grade boy who is a Koichi wannabe.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学校の頃から、君のことずっと気になっていたんだ。
example_sentences.english: I’ve had feelings for you since I was in elementary school.

notes:
"A task action is something you have to do (because 事 is all about actions). What's another way to say ""an action that is a task,"" though? I would say errand or even business." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Children in their infancy are children." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 用事をおねがいしてもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Would you mind if I asked you to do some errands?

example_sentences.japanese: ごめんなさい！ちょっと用事が出来てしまって、今日のレッスンをキャンセルしないといけなくなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Sorry! I have to take care of something and I have to cancel my lesson today.

example_sentences.japanese: 大事な用事があるので、明日は出勤することができません。
example_sentences.english: I have an important matter to attend to so I will not be able to work tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: あの幼児のテディベアの毛はベルベットのように滑らかだった。
example_sentences.english: The fur of that little kid’s teddy bear was as smooth as velvet.

notes:
"Fire is a thing that makes more fire. Basically fire is fire." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"The only action you should be doing in my house is the housework and my chores. This isn't a hotel. Get moving! Clean my dishes!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 火事があった場所は、アパートの五かいです。
example_sentences.english: The fire was on the fifth floor of the apartment.

example_sentences.japanese: 何か臭うんだけど。もしかして、火事じゃない？
example_sentences.english: I smell something strange! Maybe a fire?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、家が火事になる夢を見たんです。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday I had a dream that my house caught on fire.

example_sentences.japanese: 家事、ほんとにめんどくさいけど、がんばる。
example_sentences.english: Housework is really annoying, but I’ll do my best.

example_sentences.japanese: 主人はいつもわたしにばかり家事をおし付けてくるから本当にこまります。
example_sentences.english: My husband has me do chores all the time and I'm not happy about it at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 家事全般が苦手なんですよね。
example_sentences.english: I’m bad at all of the housework.

english: Fish Shop, Fish Market, Fish Dealer, Fish Store, Fishmonger
notes: "A fish shop is a fish shop, a place from which you buy fish. Especially in Japan, very important." "The kun'yomi reading is used for the 魚 (so it's さかな) and the kun'yomi reading is used for 屋 (や). You'll have to use the reading of 魚 from the vocabulary from a couple levels ago to remember the reading of this one."

example_sentences.japanese: 魚屋で金目だいを買ってきたの。
example_sentences.english: We went to buy splendid red bream at the fish store.

example_sentences.japanese: この魚屋のゆかはすべりやすいから気を付けてね。
example_sentences.english: This fish shop floor is very slippery, so be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: あの魚屋さんは百円おまけをしてくれた。
example_sentences.english: The fish shop gave me a 100 yen discount.

english: Front, Surface, Exterior, Face, Outside, Appearance
notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji express. If you want to understand what something is trying to express you usually look at its front or its exterior. This word is usually used for the exterior face of buildings." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet though, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You're standing in front of a building, staring at its front. You spend some time gazing at it before you realize what it is. ""Oh, motel (おもて)"", you say aloud. A little time looking at the exterior and you're able to figure it out."

example_sentences.japanese: 表はピンク色にぬってください。
example_sentences.english: Please paint the front pink.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの表のかおはトーフグ社長であるが、うらのかおは世界でも有数のジャグリングせん手である。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's public face is the president of Tofugu, but his private face is the most well-known juggler in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 十円玉の表はどちらですか？
example_sentences.english: Which side of a ten yen coin is the face?

notes: "Your house tools aren't the tools you use to build a house. They're more like the things that are a part of your house that you use like tools. Those things would be your furniture. So, remember, your house tools are just furniture." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週末は、新きょの家具を買いに行く予定です。
example_sentences.english: I plan to go buy furniture for my new house this weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: 王女の家具は本当にすばらしいですね！さすがです！
example_sentences.english: You have such wonderful furniture, Princess! Very impressive.

example_sentences.japanese: 家具はあなたの家にお運びしましたが、もう少し腰を軽くして扉と窓を早く取り付ける方がいいのではないかと思います。
example_sentences.english: We moved the furniture to your new house but you should act quickly to get the doors and windows installed.

notes: "A guest's room is the guest room (the room you put guests in, duh!)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大すきなアイドルと、ろ天ぶろ付の客室にとまることがゆめなんです。
example_sentences.english: My dream is to stay in a guest room attached to an open air bath with the idol I love.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルでは全ての客室にコンシェルジュサービスが付いてきます。
example_sentences.english: In this hotel, all the guest rooms have concierge service.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうど客室のリフォームが終わったところなんですの。是非うちにいらして、ご意見を聞かせてくださいな。
example_sentences.english: I just finished renovating the guest room. Come over and tell me what you think.

hiragana: はーとがた, ハートがた
notes: "ハート is of course ""heart"" and you know that 形 means shape. You've probably already figured this one out. It's heart shaped. You can add this kanji to all sorts of other things too to say ""____ shaped."" Give it a try!" "The reading for the kanji portion uses the kun'yomi reading. This is kind of like the reading you already learned for 形 just without the ち part. And rendaku happens too, so it becomes がた. If you can remember that, you should be able to remember this reading too!"

example_sentences.japanese: ネイル用に、ハート形のストーンをさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m looking for a heart shaped stone to use on my fake nails.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスティンは、くぎをくわえながら、ハート形のハンマーをふり回していた。
example_sentences.english: Kristen was swinging a heart shaped hammer around while holding nails in her mouth.

example_sentences.japanese: フラミンゴがキスをする時、二羽の頭と首がハート形を描く。
example_sentences.english: When flamingos kiss, their heads and necks form a heart shape.

notes: "You know 高校 means ""high school."" So, a ""life"" that does high school is a high school student. This is like how 中学生 are middle school students and 小学生 are elementary school students!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Use the reading of 高校 from before to learn the reading of this word as well, if it helps."

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は、高校生たちが、このパン工場の見学に来ます。
example_sentences.english: Today, high school students are coming to this bread factory on a field trip.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは高校生の時、毎日のように海に行っては魚をとって食べていました。
example_sentences.english: When I was a high school student, I would go to the sea every day to catch fish and eat them.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつはただの高校生デビューだよ。
example_sentences.english: He's just trying to look cool because he’s in high school now.

english: How Many Times, How Often, What Temperature
notes: "If someone asks you what occurrence or what degrees they're really trying to ask you how many times something happened. Sometimes they're asking what temperature it is too." The reading is a combination of kun'yomi and on'yomi readings. That being said, both readings for both kanji are the readings you learned already, so you should be able to read this.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生には本当に大切なしゅん間が何度かおとずれる。
example_sentences.english: We all have really important moments, a few times in our lives.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは、おなかが空いたサメに食べられそうになったことが何度もある。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu has almost been eaten by the hungry shark many times.

example_sentences.japanese: 何度同じことを言えば分かるんだ？
example_sentences.english: How many times do I have to say the same thing before you understand?

notes: "The Japanese style style. The Japanese often like to think they're very unique and have a very special kind of style (and often times they do). So, you'll hear this word used when someone wants to describe this unique sense of style. Wafuuuu! Note that this word uses alternative kanji meanings in both of the kanji. They're in the kanji explanation, but they're not the primaries, so it may take a little extra effort to learn this word depending on what you studied!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 和風のあじ付けがすきなんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I do like Japanese flavors.

example_sentences.japanese: かえりにスーパーで、和風ごまドレッシングを買ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Can you get Japanese sesame dressing from a grocery store on the way back?

example_sentences.japanese: これが和風ホットドッグです。
example_sentences.english: This is the Japanese style hotdog.

english: Japanese Style Clothes, Japanese Clothing, Japanese Style Clothing, Japanese Clothes
notes: "Japanese style clothes (Japanese Style Clothes). We're talking kimonos and yukata and things like that. Basically, this differentiates Japanese clothing from Western clothing. What kind of clothes will you wear to the festival tonight? Oh, probably some 和服." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 和服もに合ってるね。
example_sentences.english: You look good in Japanese style clothes too.

example_sentences.japanese: 何ちゃく和服をもっていますか？
example_sentences.english: How many Japanese style clothes do you have?

example_sentences.japanese: 和服でマラソンをする日本人を見たことがありますか？
example_sentences.english: Have you seen Japanese people running marathons in Japanese style clothes?

notes: "Japanese style eat ... well, let's change ""eat"" to ""food"" and you have Japanese style food. This is a good way to differentiate between an American style restaurant and a Japanese style restaurant. What kind of food you feeling like tonight? Oh, how about some 和食?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ごはんは、和食がいいですね。
example_sentences.english: Well I like having Japanese style food for breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ人の中にもさい近、よう食よりも和食がすきな人がふえている。
example_sentences.english: There's been an increase in Americans who prefer Japanese cuisine to Western cuisine.

example_sentences.japanese: 和食イコール寿司ってわけじゃない。
example_sentences.english: Japanese style food doesn’t always mean sushi.

notes: "A Japanese style room tends to be pretty small. This mainly refers to the kind of room that's covered in tatami mats, though. If you're looking for places to stay in Japan, a 和室 will be something like that. You'll pull the futon out of the closet and sleep on the floor. So comfy, these Japanese style rooms!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 和室でねるのは、これがはじめてです。
example_sentences.english: This is my first time sleeping in a Japanese-style room.

example_sentences.japanese: この和室、ドッグフードとコウイチの足のにおいがまざったようなにおいがしない？
example_sentences.english: Don't you think this Japanese-style room smells like a mix of dog food and your feet, Koichi?

example_sentences.japanese: 私のお兄ちゃんは、和室で大きな蜘蛛を飼っています。
example_sentences.english: My older brother has a huge pet spider in his Japanese-style room.

notes: "The temporary names. These are the kana (that's hiragana and katakana). Why are the ""temporary names"" kana, though? Perhaps they were never meant to be a main way to write the names of the kanji... They are just a temporary way to write the name of kanji you don't know how to write the ""correct"" way (aka kanji)? That's just a guess, but it should help you to remember that this word means ""kana,"" at least." "The reading for 仮 is the one you learned with the kanji. The 名 portion is not, however, and uses its kun'yomi reading (な), which you saw with the kanji 名 (な). How to remember all this, though? Think of it this way: The people who made kanji really don't want you to know kana. It's bad for business. They want anyone who uses the word ""kana"" to suffer, so they decided to make one part on'yomi and another part kun'yomi. Don't let them get you!"

example_sentences.japanese: まずは、仮名をかくれんしゅうから始めましょう。
example_sentences.english: First, let’s begin by practicing writing kana.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニでかん字をべん強するのに、まずは仮名を全部知っている必要がある。
example_sentences.english: In order to study kanji on WaniKani, you must first know all of the kana.

example_sentences.japanese: この書類の漢字全部に、振り仮名を振ってもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: Could you add kana to all the kanji in this document, please?

notes: "A Life guarantee is something you get on someone else. If their life ends, it's guaranteed with money. That's a life insurance policy, for yah!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 生保はもちろんつみ立てですよね？
example_sentences.english: Well of course your life insurance is the reserve type, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本ではけんこう保険のせい度が整っているんだから、わざわざ生保に入る必要はあまりないよ。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, the health insurance system is all-inclusive, so you don't really need to purchase life insurance separately.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では、女性の生命保険販売員は「生保レディ」と呼ばれますが、彼女たちの中には大きなコミッションや昇進のために枕営業をする人がいるという噂があります。
example_sentences.english: "Life insurance saleswomen are called ""seiho ladies"" in Japan and there are rumors that some of them sleep their ways into big commissions or promotions."

notes: "A thing that has life is a living thing! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: かわらでなぞの生物を発見した。
example_sentences.english: A mysterious creature was discovered at a dry river bed.

example_sentences.japanese: 地きゅう上でもっとも大きい生物はシロナガスクジラではなく、シロナガスフグです。
example_sentences.english: The largest living thing on the planet isn't blue whale but blue blowfish.

example_sentences.japanese: こないだの生物の授業のノート、見せてくれないかな。
example_sentences.english: Can I see your notes from the other day in Bio?

english: Local Specialty, Famous Product, Specialty, Famous Goods
notes: "The famous thing of an area is their famous product, but it sounds better in English if you say it's the local specialty. When you're traveling around Japan, be sure to be on the lookout for the 名物! It's always fun." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ポートランドの名物は何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What is Portland’s specialty?

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの名物社長から、東京名物の東京ばななをおみやげにもらいました。
example_sentences.english: "I got Tokyo's famous ""Tokyo Banana"" from the Tofugu's famous-for-being-unique president."

example_sentences.japanese: たこ焼きは絶対に大阪名物の一つです。
example_sentences.english: Takoyaki is definitely one of the most famous foods in Osaka.

english: Main Point, Gist, Main Idea, Essence
notes: "The needed point is the main point. It's the gist of what you're trying to say." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少し要点をせいりしてからいけんをのべてください。
example_sentences.english: Please state your opinion after rearranging your main point a bit more.

example_sentences.japanese: ユウサクが要点をはあくしているとは思えないんだけど。
example_sentences.english: I don't think Yusaku got the gist.

example_sentences.japanese: いいから！早く要点を言ってよ！
example_sentences.english: Come on! Get to the point!

notes: "You know that 学校 means school. So, people who are in the middle school are in... wait for it... middle school. And, of course, if you're one of those people that call it junior high school you can do that too." "The reading is a combination of 学校 and 中. Really, it's all on'yomi too, so you should be able to read this one. Take note of the がく turning to がっ, though."

example_sentences.japanese: それより、中学校の前でとった写しんがいいよ。
example_sentences.english: All that aside, you should choose the photo taken in front of the junior high school.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっとまってて。その中学校のば所を今しらべてあげる。
example_sentences.english: Give me a sec, I'll look up the location of the middle school for you.

example_sentences.japanese: ええっと、私は中学校の教師ですよね。そこで、時間を無駄にしないためにも、とりあえず私は絶対に間違ったことを言わない、ということにしておいてください。
example_sentences.english: I’m a middle school teacher, right? To save time, let’s just always assume that I am never wrong, okay?

notes: "The place that's famous for old roofs. I don't know why, but it's the city of Nagoya. Just associate the two things together and it'll be hard to forget (so long as you've heard of Nagoya before - if not, read up about it!)." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji (except for 名 and 屋, which are kun'yomi here). If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. For な just think to 名前 (なまえ) which uses the な reading. The ""name"" (名前) of this city is what? It's Nagoya. Watch out for rendaku changing こ to ご too."

example_sentences.japanese: 名古屋にはおいしいものがたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: Nagoya has a lot of delicious food.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日も名古屋で仕事があった。
example_sentences.english: I had work in Nagoya today again.

example_sentences.japanese: 名古屋にいる友人を訪れた際、矢場とんというとても美味しいトンカツをご馳走してもらいました。
example_sentences.english: When I visited my friend in Nagoya, I was treated to a delicious pork cutlet called yabaton.

notes:
"If you attach things near you, they end up being in the same neighborhood as you. They're attached nearby so they can't go much further. " "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 付 though, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Your neighborhood is full of fools (ふ). Fools everywhere. You're probably one too, since you live nearby."

"A cloth towel is just a cloth towel. Essentially it's known as a dish cloth or tea towel." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この付近に、コンビニはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Does this neighborhood have a convenience store?

example_sentences.japanese: 付近には、外国人見物客もたくさんいました。
example_sentences.english: There are many foreign viewers nearby as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この付近に公衆便所はありますか。
example_sentences.english: Is there a public restroom in this neighborhood?

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かが棒のてっぺんに、日の丸の代わりに布巾をはためかせたみたいですね。
example_sentences.english: It seems that somebody put a dish cloth on top of the pole instead of the national flag of Japan.

notes: "A new year is a new year. Hope you had / have / are having a good one, depending on when you read this." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 新年、明けましておめでとうございます。
example_sentences.english: Happy New Year!

example_sentences.japanese: 新年のほうふはもう決めましたか？
example_sentences.english: Have you decided your New Year's resolution yet?

example_sentences.japanese: 新年の挨拶に、親戚の家を回りました。
example_sentences.english: We went around to our relatives houses exchanging New Year’s greetings.

notes: "Picture the part of your body that makes up your neck. Are you picturing it? That's a building block that makes up your body. A really important one. If you didn't have that neck, you wouldn't look like a person at all. Sound familiar? It should! Because that part of your neck is a radical! Just like part of your neck is a building block of your body, the radical is a building block of kanji. Get it? I sure hope so!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 首 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:When you need a radical to make a new kanji, you just press a button and the radical comes tumbling down the radical chute (しゅ). There's definitely no rhyme or reason to radical picking, it's just whatever pops out of the ol' chute. "

example_sentences.japanese: このかん字の部首は何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What is this kanji’s radical?

example_sentences.japanese: 部首をわらうものは部首になく。
example_sentences.english: Someone who laughs over radicals will eventually cry over radicals.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は全部の部首を覚えています。
example_sentences.english: I remember all of the radicals.

notes: "The peoples who make their dwelling here are the residents." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 市はひなん所をかいせつして、住民にひなんをよびかけています。
example_sentences.english: The city established a shelter and appealed to the citizens to take refuge.

example_sentences.japanese: 住民たちは、みんなすぐに打ちとけました。
example_sentences.english: The residents got along with each other right away.

example_sentences.japanese: あのアパートの住民には無料のエアコンが与えられるが、何故か冬の間だけなのである。
example_sentences.english: The residents of that apartment are given free air-conditioning, but only in winter for some reason.

english: Sure Victory, Certain Victory, Sure Win, Certain Win
notes: "A certain win sounds like a great thing. When these two kanji are put together, a certain victory is inevitable." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Take note that the つ in ひつ is turned into a small っ, though."

example_sentences.japanese: じん社で必勝をきがんしてきました。
example_sentences.english: I prayed for certain victory at a shrine.

example_sentences.japanese: 空手のし合で、「必勝」とかかれたハチマキをしている人を見ました。
example_sentences.english: "I saw a person wearing a headband that said ""Sure Victory"" at the karate match."

example_sentences.japanese: もし虎と七面鳥が戦争することになったら、それはもう虎の必勝になるだろうね。それから、ついでに、養鶏所で働く人も喜ぶだろうね。
example_sentences.english: If tigers were to go to war against turkeys, it would mean certain victory for the tigers. Chicken farmers would be happy, as well.

notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji swim, so it means swimming." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading already so you should be able to read it!

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルは魚よりも泳ぎが上手です。
example_sentences.english: Michael's swimming is better than the fish's!

example_sentences.japanese: カエルの泳ぎにあこがれて必死に平泳ぎをれんしゅうしていたら、手と足がほそ長くなりました。
example_sentences.english: I admired frogs' swimming so I frantically practiced the breaststroke until my arms and legs got longer.

example_sentences.japanese: 泳ぎはあまり得意ではありません。
example_sentences.english: I’m not very good at swimming.

english: Tea Shop, Tea Store, Tea House
notes: "A tea shop is a tea shop. Mmm, delicious, delicious tea." This word uses the readings you learned with the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ポートランドでは、トーフグ茶屋の、ふぐもちが人気です。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu tea shop in Portland has popular fugu mochi.

example_sentences.japanese: きょうとにりょ行したとき、コウイチは毎ばん茶屋あそびを楽しみました。
example_sentences.english: When Koichi traveled to Kyoto, he enjoyed teahouse entertainment every night.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人は現代的なカフェを「カフェ」、昭和の香りのするコーヒーラウンジを「喫茶店」、伝統的なお茶屋さんを「茶屋」と呼びます。
example_sentences.english: "Japanese people call modern cafes ""Cafe,"" slightly old fashioned coffee lounges ""Kissaten,"" and traditional tea shops ""Chaya."""

notes: "In the now  occurrence you'll learn your kanji, no? This word means this time (same like ""now occurrence""). Despite being ""this time"" it has the feeling of next time, though. It's like saying ""okay, this time we'll get it"" where ""this time"" really means ""next time,"" making it a little bit different from 今回." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: じゃあ、やっぱり今度にしよう。
example_sentences.english: Okay, then let’s do it next time.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度は本当に本気の本気で日本ごをべんきょうします！
example_sentences.english: I'm really, really serious about studying Japanese this time.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度俺がお前を泣かせる時は、嬉し泣きだ。
example_sentences.english: The next time I make you cry it will be because you are happy.

english: Thousand Yen Bill, Thousand Yen Note, One Thousand Yen Note, One Thousand Yen Bill
notes: "You know what 千円 is (1000 yen). So if you add a bill to that you get a thousand yen bill. That's just the little rectangular piece of money that is worth 1000 yen." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 千円札のおつりが不足しています。
example_sentences.english: I don’t have change for a thousand yen bill.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、水そうから紙のひしゃくで千円札をすくうゲームです。
example_sentences.english: This is a game in which you scoop thousand yen bills with a paper scoop from a water tank.

example_sentences.japanese: 「千ドル札を燃やしてるの？」「いや、ただの千円札だよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Are you burning a thousand dollar bill?"" ""No, it’s just a thousand yen bill."""

notes: "The tools you use on the road of life are important to have. What is your most important tool?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これが、ロブさんがかりたいと言っていた道具です。
example_sentences.english: This is the tool that you told me you wanted to borrow, Rob.

example_sentences.japanese: ドラえもんの道具の中で一番使ってみたい道具は何ですか。やっぱりどこでもドアですか？
example_sentences.english: Out of all of Doraemon's tools, which one would you want to use the most? Obviously the Anywhere Door, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日買った道具入れの中に、なんとベイブ・ルースのルーキーカードが一枚入っていたんだ！
example_sentences.english: I bought a tool pouch yesterday that had a Babe Ruth rookie card hidden inside it.

english: True Strength, True Ability, True Power
notes: "The truth behind someone's strength is their true strength. It is also their true ability." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのフラダンスの実力は本物です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's hula dancing abilities are genuine.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトが本気の実力を出した所を見た人はまだだれもいません。
example_sentences.english: There is no one who has witnessed Viet's true power yet.

example_sentences.japanese: 運も実力のうちってよく言うだろ。
example_sentences.english: "They usually say, ""luck is what you make of it."""

notes: "The action of truth is just truth itself, though it's also facts and reality as well. Really, it's the idea of ""truth"" in a way." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 事実かもしれないけど、なっとくはできないな。
example_sentences.english: That may be true, but I'm still not convinced.

example_sentences.japanese: あのせいじ家の言っていることは、事実に反します。
example_sentences.english: What that politician has been saying contradicts the facts.

example_sentences.japanese: 口髭を生やした男が気味悪く見えるのは、科学的な事実です。
example_sentences.english: It is a scientific fact that a man with a mustache looks creepy.

notes:
"Someone who wins is the winner / victor." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Someone who has a wound is someone who is wounded. They are an injured person." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 勝者だけが次のステージにすすめます。
example_sentences.english: Only the winner will advance to the next stage.

example_sentences.japanese: せんそうに勝者はいないのですから、どうかそんなむいみなたたかいは止めてください。
example_sentences.english: There are no winners in wars, so please stop such a meaningless fight.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは、72時間耐久スクラブルゲームの勝者となった。
example_sentences.english: Viet emerged the victor in the 72 hour Scrabble game.

example_sentences.japanese: その事故による死者は三名、傷者は二百人以上にのぼるという。
example_sentences.english: It’s said that there were three killed and more than 200 wounded in that accident.

notes: "A study institution is an academy. That's where all the fancy people study, anyways." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 2014年に、トーフグ学院をそつぎょうしました。
example_sentences.english: I graduated from Tofugu Academy in 2014.

example_sentences.japanese: かん西学院大学の多くの学生はざい学中にりゅう学をけいけんします。
example_sentences.english: Many students from Kwansei Gakuin University get to study abroad while at college.

example_sentences.japanese: やあ！こいつはワニカニ。あだ名はクラビゲーターだよ。トーフグ工業学院で働いてるんだ。
example_sentences.english: Hey! This guy is WaniKani, a.k.a. the Crabigator. He works for Tofugu Institute for Industrial Education.

notes: "Remember how 足す means ""to add?"" Add calculate to that and you'll have addition! It's the type of calculation you're doing when you add." "This is the kun'yomi reading for 足 and the on'yomi for 算. And the さん reading is rendaku'd into ざん. This is the same for all the math-ish words (addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division), so try to remember that, because you'll see it again!"

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは足し算ができない。
example_sentences.english: I can’t do addition.

example_sentences.japanese: その足し算コンテストに、かん客としてさんかすることはできますか？
example_sentences.english: Can I participate in the addition contest as a spectator?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、学校で足し算の勉強をしました。
example_sentences.english: Today we studied addition in school.

notes: "If you think about it, an earth road isn't going to be the main road. It will be the road less traveled. You could call it a path (you know, like a dirt path!). Alternatively, another less traveled street that would probably be made out of dirt back in the day (before everything was paved) would be an alley. Imagine yourself walking down a dirt alley at night with no shoes. Scary!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You've learned these readings already, so you should be able to read this word too! And remember, that it's the じ reading that you learned with 生地 here. "

example_sentences.japanese: うちのお店は、ウェスタン通りから、少し路地に入ったところにあります。
example_sentences.english: Our store is in a small alley off of Western Street.

example_sentences.japanese: その路地は、夜は少しきけんだから気を付けてね。
example_sentences.english: That path is a bit sketchy at night, so be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官は、路地まで苺泥棒を追いかけた。
example_sentences.english: The policeman chased the mugger who stole the strawberries down the alley.

notes: "Someone who gives you a helping hand is an assistant." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ワトソンはかせは、シャーロック・ホームズの助手ではなく、あくまで友人です。
example_sentences.english: Dr. Watson isn’t just Sherlock Holmes’ assistant, he’s his friend till the end.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの助手は、年末に肉ばなれになりました。
example_sentences.english: My aide got a torn muscle at the end of the year.

example_sentences.japanese: もし私が今首になった助手の助手だとしたら、それってつまり私も首になっちゃったってこと？
example_sentences.english: If I’m the assistant to an assistant who was just fired, does that mean that I’m fired too?

notes: "A self revolving car. You'd think this would be a regular car, but bicycles were probably introduced before cars were, meaning the self revolving car is the bicycle, not the car. Just imagine yourself on a bike, and you don't even have to move the pedals. They revolve themselves, but now you're going too fast and it's scary." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは自転車で会社に行っています。
example_sentences.english: I go to work by bike.

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車を買ってあげるよ。お返しは要らないからね！
example_sentences.english: I'll buy you a new bicycle, no strings attached.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ごめん。てっきり君が僕の自転車を壊したのかと思ってたよ。」 「何それ！ひどい。私がそんなことするはずないでしょ。」
example_sentences.english: """I’m sorry. I thought for sure you were the one who broke my bike."" ""What? That’s awful. You know me better than that."""

notes: "There is only one place in Japan that has a thousand leaves and that's Chiba. Picture all of those leaves swirling around you on your vacation to Chiba. Beautiful." "This is a place name and it uses the kun'yomi. You haven't learned kun'yomi for 千 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember it:While you're admiring all of the leaves in Chiba, you realize you're craving something. What goes well with watching leaves? Why, cheese (ち) of course. Delicious Chiba cheese."

example_sentences.japanese: かれは千葉県人です。
example_sentences.english: He’s from Chiba.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの母は、千葉県さんの落花生が大すきです。
example_sentences.english: My mom loves peanuts made in Chiba.

example_sentences.japanese: ここから千葉までだと、片道1時間30分から2時間はぐらいかかりますね。
example_sentences.english: It usually takes an hour and a half to two hours for a one way trip from here to Chiba.

english: Close Friend, Best Friend, Good Friend
notes: "A friend who is like one of your parents is someone who will look out for you. They are like family, in fact! That's why this word means best friend or close friend. Just imagine someone who watches over you like a parent would. This is the way to describe them." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ま、親友には反対されたんですけどね。
example_sentences.english: Well, I was objected to by a close friend.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとビエトは親友で、友だち以上、こい人未まんのかんけいです。
example_sentences.english: Koichi and Viet are good friends. They are more than friends, but not lovers.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ねぇ、知ってる？サラがベスと付き合ってるのよ。」「え、知らなかった。サラのこと親友だと思ってたけど、私そのこと何も聞いてないわ。」
example_sentences.english: """Hey, you know what? Sara is going out with Beth."" ""What? I didn’t know that. I thought she was my best friend but she never told me about that."""

notes: "A bend in a line is merely a curve." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このドレスは、曲線を美しく出してくれます。
example_sentences.english: This dress gives me beautiful curves.

example_sentences.japanese: ブーメランパンツから出てるコウイチのおしりの曲線…いいね！
example_sentences.english: The curve of Koichi's butt protruding from the speedo is very... nice!

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが怒った時の、ほおの柔らかく歪んだ曲線が好きよ。
example_sentences.english: I really love the soft, slanted curve of your cheek when you get mad.

notes: "The electricity iron sounds scary, but if you think to back in the day and to where iron was used a lot, you probably think of the railway systems... big hunky pieces of iron on the ground to make the railway. So, you can advance this by adding electricity instead of coal, creating an electric railway." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 東きゅう電鉄によりますと、東きゅう東よこ線は人身じこのえいきょうで、げんざい運転を見合わせています。
example_sentences.english: According to the Tokyu Corporation, the Tokyu Toyoko line has currently suspended operations due to an accident involving personal injury.

example_sentences.japanese: 電鉄会社ではたらくのがゆめです。
example_sentences.english: My dream is to work for an electric railroad company.

example_sentences.japanese: 「はい、どうぞ。あなたが好きな阪急電鉄の写真よ。」「うわぁ！やったぁ！俺の大好きな阪急電鉄じゃん！」
example_sentences.english: """Here you are, dear. Some of those Hankyu Railway pictures you like."" ""Oh wow, I absolutely love the Hankyu Railway!"""

notes: "Do you remember 医者 (doctor)? What happens when you add eye on there? You have yourself an eye doctor." "The reading is just the vocab word 医者 (いしゃ) plus the reading 目 (め), the same as the reading you learned with the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: きのう目がいたくなって、目医者に行ったら、ものもらいだった。
example_sentences.english: My eye started hurting yesterday, I went to the eye doctor, and it was a sty.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末も開いている目医者をさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for an eye doctor who is open on weekends.

example_sentences.japanese: 「よお、目医者さん。もう何もかもばれているんだよ。だから、目について何も知らないふりをする必要はないぜ。」
example_sentences.english: Listen, Mr. Eye Doctor. The cat's out of the bag, so there's no need to pretend you don’t know anything about eyes.

notes: "The place you do your farming is a farm!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日よう日、小麦のしゅうかくを体けんしに、農場へ行ってきました。
example_sentences.english: I went to a farm on Sunday to experience the wheat harvest.

example_sentences.japanese: 農場で、引きつづきはたらかないかと聞かれました。
example_sentences.english: I was asked if I'd like to keep working at the farm.

example_sentences.japanese: オーガニック農場を始めるつもりです。
example_sentences.english: I’m planning to start an organic farm.

notes: "You've seen 一番 (number one), so what in the world is this eye on the end? This eye (目) signifies the order. So, add this to ""number one"" and you have the first thing / the first." "The reading for this word is just the vocab word 一番 plus the word 目. If you know both of those readings you'll be able to read this one as well."

example_sentences.japanese: このごうかな朝食を食べ終わって、一番目のかんそうは、やっぱりベーコンはおいしい、です。
example_sentences.english: The first thing that comes to mind after finishing this wonderful breakfast is that bacon is delicious, as we all know.

example_sentences.japanese: 一番目のらんには、すきな人の名前をかいてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write down the name of the person you like in the first column.

example_sentences.japanese: 「僕は毎朝一番目に、5キロのランニングをするんだぜ。」「大したことないよ！僕は10キロ走るよ。」
example_sentences.english: """The first thing I do every morning is run five kilometers."" ""Big deal! I run ten!"""

notes: "You know the word 外来 to mean ""imported."" So, combine that with the kanji for language and you have an imported word, aka a borrowed word. There are a lot of these in Japanese, which makes this word important. Almost everything in katakana is a 外来語, in fact." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: げんざいの中国語では、たくさんの日本語が外来語として使われています。
example_sentences.english: Many Japanese words are used as loanwords in modern day Chinese.

example_sentences.japanese: リュックサックは、外来語ですか？それとも和せいえい語ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is rucksack a foreign word, or Engrish?

example_sentences.japanese: ねえ、煙草って外来語なのに漢字があるって知ってた？
example_sentences.english: Hey, did you know that there's kanji for the word tobacco even though it’s a loanword?

hiragana: ふらんすご, フランスご
notes: "I bet you can guess that フランス means ""France."" So what happens when you add language to it? You get the ""France Language"" aka the French Language." "The reading is just the on'yomi reading for 語 which is the reading you learned with the kanji. This is probably because it gets added onto a lot of other words so it's treated like a jukugo. For example: 日本語 = ""Japanese Language."" 中国語 = ""Chinese Language."" スペイン語 = ""Spanish Language."""

example_sentences.japanese: わたしのむすめは、フランス語もえい語も話せます。
example_sentences.english: My daughter can speak both French and English.

example_sentences.japanese: アフリカの多くの国では公用語にえい語とフランス語が使用されています。
example_sentences.english: In many African countries, both English and French are used as their official languages.

example_sentences.japanese: フランス語の学習は僕には難しすぎるよ。もうたく山だ！勘弁してくれよ！
example_sentences.english: Learning French is too difficult! I can’t take it anymore. Give me a break!

notes: "So there's this weird thing with Japanese people. Many things that most people would consider ""green"" are actually ""blue"" in their eyes. So, things like plants and street lights are ""blue"" even though you may think of them as green. Remember that for this word, where we talk about a blue leaf. In your head, though, think ""green leaf."" Now think of all things that have green leaves. This is greenery." "The readings for the kanji in this word are the kun'yomi readings. Since you've already seen the word 青, hopefully you can just combine it with 葉 (you learned the reading for this part with the kanji). Be sure to pay attention to the rendaku, though. は goes to ば in this word, making it あおば."

example_sentences.japanese: 青葉が目にしみるきせつとなりました。
example_sentences.english: It's that time of year again when the leaves make my eyes burn.

example_sentences.japanese: 家のにわの青葉に虫がいっぱい付いてる！
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of bugs on the young leaves in our garden!

example_sentences.japanese: お前の頭、ちょっと変なにおいがするぞ。 乾燥した青葉か何かみたいな。
example_sentences.english: Your head smells a little weird. It’s like dried up leaves or something.

notes:
"Remember how you learned that 大学 means ""college?"" Well the institution you go to after college is graduate school!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"Remember how you learned that 大学院 means ""graduate school"" and 大学生 means ""college student?"" Well smush them together and you have a  graduate student!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院をそつぎょうしたんだけど、仕事が見つからないんだ。
example_sentences.english: I graduated from grad school, but I can’t find a job.

example_sentences.japanese: この大学院の自どうはん売きは、つめたい飲み物しか売っていません。
example_sentences.english: You can only buy cold drinks from the vending machines at this grad school.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は大学院進学を考えております。
example_sentences.english: I’m thinking about going to graduate school.

example_sentences.japanese: この大学院生は、えんげいが上手だ。
example_sentences.english: This graduate student has a green thumb.

example_sentences.japanese: あのまんるいホームランを打ったせん手、げん役の大学院生らしいよ。
example_sentences.english: That player who hit a grand slam is apparently an actual grad student.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院生ってどんなことをするんですか？
example_sentences.english: What kinds of things do graduate students do?

notes:
"The business of industry is... well... industry." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"The mineral business is the mining industry." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では工業が発たつしています。
example_sentences.english: Japan has an advanced industry.

example_sentences.japanese: 工業デザイナーの中山さんは、ワニカニをストレス発さんに使っています。
example_sentences.english: The industrial designer, Mr. Nakayama, uses WaniKani for stress relief.

example_sentences.japanese: 「工業技術プロジェクトの進み具合はどう？」「今のところは順調だよ。」
example_sentences.english: """How is your industrial technology project going? "" ""So far, so good."""

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は鉱業の過去十年間を振り返りました。
example_sentences.english: He looked back on the past 10 years of the mining industry.

hiragana: にほんしゅ, にっぽんしゅ
english: Japanese Style Alcohol, Japanese Alcohol, Sake
notes: "You know that 日本 is ""Japan"" so when you add alcohol onto the end of that you have Japanese Style Alcohol (what's the big Japanese style alcohol that everyone knows? That's sake)." "The reading is just the vocab 日本's reading plus the reading you learned for 酒, put together."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本酒はあまりすきではないんです。
example_sentences.english: I don’t really like Japanese alcohol.

example_sentences.japanese: その日本酒のボトルから、値札を外してもらってもいいですか？
example_sentences.english: Could you remove the price tag from the Japanese sake bottle for me?

example_sentences.japanese: 「何飲んでるの？」「日本酒だよ。一口飲んでみる？」「それじゃ、お言葉に甘えて一口もらってみようかな。」
example_sentences.english: """What are you drinking?"" ""Japanese rice wine. Would you like a sip?"" ""Well, I suppose I’ll give it a try."""

english: "Laboratory, Lab, Study Room, Professor's Office, Teacher's Office"
notes: "Remember how 研究 means “research?” Well the room where you do research is a laboratory! " This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは子どもの時、研究室ではたらくのがゆめでした。
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, my dream was to work at a laboratory.

example_sentences.japanese: くどいようですが、山田さんのかつらについて話すのは、この研究室ではタブーですからね。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me for repeating myself, but talking about Mr.Yamada's wig is a big no no in this study room, okay?

example_sentences.japanese: 蛙の解剖を始めるので、皆さんには研究室に移動して頂きたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I’d like everyone to move into the laboratory now so that we can start dissecting the frogs.

notes: "When you say words in a language, you are speaking a language. Not sure what that language is, but since you're saying it it must be real." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今人気のプログラミング言語は何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What are the popular programming languages right now?

example_sentences.japanese: 言語オタクたちが朝まで言語について語りつくすオフ会にさんかしてきました。
example_sentences.english: I joined an offline gathering where language geeks got together and talk about language all night long.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいコンピュータ言語の勉強を始めました。
example_sentences.english: I started to study a new computer language.

notes: "The end point is where everything ends... but for this example, think of a map with a route on it. The last spot on the route is the ""last point."" It is the last stop." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車でばくすいしてしまって、終点でうん転手さんに起こされたことはよくありますね。
example_sentences.english: I often fall asleep on the train and have to be woken up by the driver at the last stop.

example_sentences.japanese: このシカゴ発のアムトラックの終点の駅は何て言う名前ですか。
example_sentences.english: What's the name of the last stop on the Amtrak leaving from Chicago?

example_sentences.japanese: お願いがあるの。私がたとえ何と言っても、何をしようとも、終点に着くまで私が電車から降りないようにして。分かった？
example_sentences.english: You have to do me a favor. No matter what I say, no matter what I do, please do not let me get out of the train until it gets to the last stop. Okay?

notes: "You know 番号 means ""number"" so add a tag to it and you have a numbered tag." "This is a jukugo word (番号) with a single-word kanji added. That means you have two on'yomi readings from the jukugo word and the kun'yomi reading from the single kanji (ふだ). Put them all together and you have the reading of this kanji!"

example_sentences.japanese: 番号札をとって、お待ちください。
example_sentences.english: Please take a numbered ticket and wait your turn.

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、この辺りに番号札は落ちていませんでしたか？
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, wasn't there a number tag left around here?

example_sentences.japanese: こちらがお客様のお荷物の番号札となります。
example_sentences.english: Here is the numbered tag for your luggage.

notes: "A road road is obviously the best kind of road. It's double road, after all. So, what is this ultimate road? It is a paved road." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大雪で、高速道路が通行止めになっているそうですよ。
example_sentences.english: It looks like the highway is closed because of the heavy snow.

example_sentences.japanese: ミネソタ州は夏に道路工事ばかりしています。
example_sentences.english: So many roads are under construction in Minnesota during the summer.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は本当につまらない。基本的に道路と家しかないし。あぁ〜もう！どこか楽しいところはないのかな？
example_sentences.english: This town is really dull. There are basically only paved roads and houses. Ugh! Where can I get some action?

english: Private College, Private University, Private Uni
notes: "You know how 私 can mean private and how 大 is the first half of 大学? Well, combine those together and you have the shortened version of private college or private university." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私大の授業料は高いもんね。
example_sentences.english: Private college tuition sure is expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: とある大阪の私大で英語を教えています。
example_sentences.english: I'm teaching English at a private uni in Osaka.

example_sentences.japanese: こないだ言ってた私大の学園祭の件なんだけど、今回は私の事数にいれないで。ごめん。でも悪く思わないでね。時間ができたら連絡するから。
example_sentences.english: As for the school festival at the private university you told me about the other day, could you count me out this time? I’m sorry, don’t get mad at me. I’ll contact you when I have free time.

notes: "A private iron (remember how 鉄 often has to do with railroad tracks and the like? Same goes here) is a private railway. There are a good number of these in Japan." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京の私鉄はふくざつでよく分かりません。
example_sentences.english: Private railways in Tokyo are too complicated to understand.

example_sentences.japanese: JRで新宿駅まで行ったら私鉄に乗りかえてください。
example_sentences.english: When you arrive at Shinjuku Station by JR, please transfer to a private railway.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、とある日本の大手私鉄会社で働いております。
example_sentences.english: I work for one of the major private railway companies in Japan.

english: Railroad Track, Train Track, Railway Track, Track, Line
notes: "A line that runs on a road is a railroad track. First you have to get into your mind that the ""line"" in question is a railway line. Then, what railway line runs on a road and what kind of road is it? It's a railroad track." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大雨で、線路わきの土しゃがくずれ、線路が土しゃでうまってしまっているもよう。
example_sentences.english: It seems that the earth beside the train track collapsed from the heavy rain and covered the tracks.

example_sentences.japanese: だれかが線路に立ち入ったため、電車が止まってしまった。
example_sentences.english: The train has stopped since somebody trespassed on the train tracks.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あぁ、ごめん。今はあんまりそういう気分じゃないんだ。」「あなた、どうしたの？」「実は、さっきそこの線路で男が飛び込み自殺をするのを目撃したんだ。」
example_sentences.english: """Well, sorry. I’m not really in that kind of mood right now."" ""Honey, what’s going on? "" ""Well, I just saw a guy commit suicide on the railroad track over there."""

hiragana: けんきゅうしょ, けんきゅうじょ
english: Research Institute, Research Laboratory, Research Establishment, Research Lab, Research Facility
notes: "You've seen that 研究 is research from previous vocab. So, a ""place"" that is a research place could be many things, though mainly a research institute or research laboratory." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will also help if you know the reading of 研究 already. Also note that 所 is normal for one reading, but also gets the rendaku treatment, meaning しょ becomes じょ, for the secondary reading."

example_sentences.japanese: とあるアメリカの研究所が、日本語がペラペラになるくすりを開発したそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that a certain American lab has made a pill that will make you fluent in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は、みそしる研究所で、ぼうさいくんれんがあります。
example_sentences.english: There is an emergency drill in the Miso Soup Research Facility today.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はバーガーキング研究所で働いています。私の仕事は、フライドポテトを食べ、その後自分の体重を測ることです。
example_sentences.english: I work for the Burger King Research Institute. My job consists of eating french fries and then having my body weighed.

notes: "This is just the noun version of the kanji 酒 - it has an お there to be nice. This word can mean both alcohol (same like the parent kanji) or sake (the main kind of Japanese alcohol, at least back in the kanji days)." "The reading is kun'yomi, which isn't what you learned with the kanji. But, it should be pretty easy. You know what Japanese alcohol is called already, right? It's さけ, simple as that. So long as you've heard of sake you should be A-Okay with this reading."

example_sentences.japanese: わたしはパーティーでお酒を飲んだ。
example_sentences.english: I drank alcohol at the party.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、そのお酒はシーズンではないので、申しわけありませんがご用いできません。
example_sentences.english: That sake is out of season now, so I'm afraid it's not available.

example_sentences.japanese: 「割り勘にしよう。」「いや。今日は俺の奢りだよ。しかも、俺はお酒をたくさん飲んだけど、お前は一滴も飲まなかったじゃないか。」
example_sentences.english: """Let’s split the bill."" ""No, it’s on me this time. I drank a lot of alcohol, but you didn’t drink anything"""

notes: "A person who is sick is a sick person. They are also a patient, at least we can hope they are, for their sake." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that this uses the にん reading for 人. This is because every sick person enjoys laying in bed playing nintendo."

example_sentences.japanese: うつったらいやだから、病人には近よりたくない。
example_sentences.english: If you don’t want to catch something, you shouldn’t go near sick people.

example_sentences.japanese: うらないしに、前世は病人だったと言われました。
example_sentences.english: The fortuneteller told me that my previous life was as a sick person.

example_sentences.japanese: 「調子はどうだい？」「絶好調だよ。」「それは良かった。病人からその言葉を聞けるとは思ってもみなかったがな。」
example_sentences.english: """How’s it going?"" ""Couldn’t be better."" ""Good. I’m surprised to hear that from a sick person though."""

notes: "Remember how 手 can sometimes refer to a person? In this case, we have a song person (or perhaps a ""person who handles songs""). What is a song person also known as? A singer." "The readings are on'yomi readings. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this like a singer sings with a bunch of cashews かしゅ in their mouth. FAST AND LOUD!"

example_sentences.japanese: 歌手になったのは、母のえいきょうが大きいです。
example_sentences.english: My mother had a large influence in my becoming a singer.

example_sentences.japanese: あの歌手、かなり日やけしたね。
example_sentences.english: That singer got quite a tan, didn't she?

example_sentences.japanese: 子どもの頃は、歌手だったのよ。なんちゃってね。今でも歌手なんですけど。
example_sentences.english: I used to be a singer when I was kid. Well, who am I kidding, I’m still a singer now.

hiragana: すぺいんご, スペインご
notes: "You can probably figure out that スペイン is ""Spain"" just by reading it. Add the kanji language on there and you have the Spanish language (or just Spanish), if you'd like." The reading for the kanji portion is just the reading you learned with the kanji. Since it's attached to something, it's like a jukugo word.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日はスペイン語の小テストだぜ！
example_sentences.english: There’s a Spanish quiz tomorrow!

example_sentences.japanese: そのスペイン語のテキストは今売り切れているので、ご用いできません。
example_sentences.english: That Spanish textbook is currently sold out, so it's not available.

example_sentences.japanese: ニンニクはスペイン語で「ajo」っていうんだけど、「アホ」って発音されるんだよ。「アホ」は日本語で「stupid」って意味だよ。
example_sentences.english: "Garlic in Spanish is ""ajo,"" which is pronounced ""aho."" ""Aho"" means ""stupid"" in Japanese."

english: Strong Man, Badass, Iron Man, Macho Man, Tough Guy
notes: "A man made of iron is a strong man... aka a huge badass. Have you seen ""Iron Chef?"" The Japanese translation is 料理の鉄人, which means ""Chef Iron Man"" aka ""Chef Badass,"" at least in my book." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの社長は、鉄人すぎます。
example_sentences.english: My company president is way too much of a macho man.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしが一番すきな番組はりょうりの鉄人です。
example_sentences.english: The TV program I like most is Iron Chef.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はスーパーで赤ちゃんに「いないいないばぁ」をしている鉄人を見た。
example_sentences.english: I saw a tough guy playing peak-a-boo with a baby in a grocery store.

english: Subway, The Underground, The Metro, The Tube
notes: "The iron below ground isn't a deposit of iron. It's man made. And what is made of iron? Trains and subways. In this case, because it's underground, it's definitely a subway, though." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 地下鉄に乗って行きます。
example_sentences.english: I’ll go on the subway.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京の地下鉄はかなりふくざつです。
example_sentences.english: Tokyo's subway is extremely complex.

example_sentences.japanese: ああ、よかった！地下鉄に乗り遅れちゃうかと思ったよ。
example_sentences.english: What a relief! I thought I missed the subway train.

notes: "Now morning is just another way of saying this morning. It's the closest morning to right now!" "This reading is an exception. Let's use this mnemonic to remember it:This morning you want a quesadilla (けさ) for breakfast. You can't wait until tomorrow morning, you NEED it this morning! Imagine eating a delicious quesadilla first thing this morning. Mmm!"

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝、くすりを飲むのをわすれました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to take my medicine this morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝から両足がいたくて思うように歩けません。
example_sentences.english: My legs have been hurting since I woke up this morning, so I can't move as much as I'd like.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝ここで玉突き事故があったんだ。
example_sentences.english: This morning there was a multi-vehicle accident here.

english: Tone, Tone Of Voice, Verbal Expression
notes: "When your mouth makes tones we call it your tone or tone of voice. They're different kinds of sounds you make with your mouth that make you sound happy, sad, mean, etc." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 口 yet. Remember when you learned the vocabulary word 口? Just take the ち off and you get its other on'yomi reading く. That's easy, right?"

example_sentences.japanese: かの女は口調がキツイのでちょっと苦手です。
example_sentences.english: I don’t really like her because of her harsh tone.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、とてもきびしい口調で、「うんも実力のうちだ」と言った。
example_sentences.english: Koichi said, in a very stern voice, that luck is just part of his talents.

example_sentences.japanese: 厳しい口調で責め立てられた。
example_sentences.english: She scolded me violently in a severe tone.

english: Town Hall, Town Office, Public Office
notes: "A service location is a place that people go when they're in need of a service. The best place for this is the town hall. Everyone goes to this one location to voice their complaints and in return their needs are serviced by the officials in the town hall." This word uses the on'yomi reading for the first kanji and the kun'yomi reading for the second kanji. That's all you have to remember, though, because you've seen both of these readings before!

example_sentences.japanese: 役場でしょう明しょをもらってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please get the certificate from the town hall.

example_sentences.japanese: 役場のかべ紙は、かべからはがれてきています。
example_sentences.english: The town hall's wallpaper is peeling off the wall.

example_sentences.japanese: 役場に行って転出届を出してきたよ。
example_sentences.english: I went to the town hall and submitted my change of address information.

english: Advanced Level, High Grade, Advanced Grade, High Level
notes: "When you are at an above rank, you are at an advanced level. This is referring to things like proficiency in Japanese, or things like that." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 上級クラスについていけずにこまっています。
example_sentences.english: I have trouble following the advanced level class.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ子ちゃん、上級生からいじめられているみたいなんです。
example_sentences.english: Koichiko seems to have been bullied by high level students.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語が母国語でない人で、ネイティブレベルや上級の英語を話す人もいれば、そうでない人もいます。
example_sentences.english: Some non-native speakers speak English at a native or advanced level, while others do not.

notes: "The selling that you've raised (上げ) is the amount sold or number of sales. Think of a graph going upward, where it's rising as you sell more things." "The reading for 売 is the one you learned with 売る. The reading for 上げ is the same as the reading for 上げる, a word you learned previously. If you know those two separate things, you should be able to combine them into one awesome vocab thing."

example_sentences.japanese: だんだん売り上げがへってきた。
example_sentences.english: Sales gradually decreased.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ人人気はいゆうが主えんしたハリウッドえいがのDVDは、日本だけで売り上げが八百万まいになった。
example_sentences.english: The DVD of the Hollywood movie in which a popular American actor played the main character has sold eight million copies in Japan alone.

example_sentences.japanese: あの性差別の広告のせいで、売り上げが激減した。
example_sentences.english: Sales have decreased rapidly because of that sexist advertisement.

notes: "Don't let this word confuse you. It may end in い, but it's not an adjective, it's a noun. There are no rules in war, after all. This word describes what happens in war. Those things are battles, fights, and conflicts." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: In a fierce battle, there's always a lot of collateral damage. One of the things that gets destroyed is your car. But you can't do anything about it, it's battle time! So you wave goodbye to your car saying, ""Ta ta car (たたか)!"" as you punch some jerk in the face."

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のコウイチ、なんだか戦いにくたびれてしまったへいしみたいだね。
example_sentences.english: Koichi looks like a battle-weary soldier today.

example_sentences.japanese: しずかだろうがさわがしかろうが、戦いはきらいなんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Whether it's quiet or noisy, I still don't like conflict.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はマクドナルドに行く途中、血みどろの戦いに遭遇したが、その後そのままビッグマックを食べに行った。
example_sentences.english: On the way to McDonald’s he got in a bloody fight but that didn’t stop him from getting his Big Mac.

notes: "A war location is the battlefield. That's where the wars are fought, anyways." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 戦場にいたって、そりゃあだれだって命はおしいさ。
example_sentences.english: Nobody wants to be killed, even on the battleground.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトのせいで、トーフグのオフィスはヤクザの戦場と化した。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu office turned into a Yakuza battlefield because of Viet.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは頼れるやつだ。たとえ戦場にいたとしても、俺達を決して見捨てやしないよ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is a dependable guy. He would never let us down even if we were on a battlefield.

notes: "Remember how 生物 means ""living things?"" Well when you study living things you're studying biology. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの一番すきな科目は生物学と生化学です。
example_sentences.english: Two of my favorite subjects are biology and biochemistry.

example_sentences.japanese: 川田さんのお兄さんは生物学をせんもんとする学者さんです。
example_sentences.english: Ms. Kawada's older brother is a scholar who specializes in biology.

example_sentences.japanese: デザイナーになりたいなら、生物学も学んだ方がいい。
example_sentences.english: If you want to become a designer, you should also study biology.

english: Bus Stop, Taxi Stand, Train Platform, Place For Boarding Vehicles
notes: "You've seen the word 乗る by now, hopefully, and know it means ""to ride."" So this word has to do with a ""riding location."" Where do you go to get a ride somewhere? Most likely, it's a bus stop or taxi stand." "This word uses the kun'yomi readings, which you've learned already. Also, use 乗る to help you to remember the reading for 乗り."

example_sentences.japanese: ゴンドラ乗り場はどこですか？
example_sentences.english: Where is the gondola terminal?

example_sentences.japanese: 空港のタクシー乗り場でタクシーを待っているところです。
example_sentences.english: I'm waiting for a taxi in the airport taxi stand right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、家の前のバス乗り場で通り過ぎる車を見ながらダラダラしているよ。
example_sentences.english: At the moment, I’m chilling at the bus stop in front of my house looking at cars passing by.

english: Clothes, Western Clothing, Western Style Clothes
notes: "Western style clothes is just Western clothing (or Western style clothes). But nowadays, because Japanese people wear Western clothing all the time, we use it to just mean clothes. We're talking things that aren't kimonos, etc." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 洋服を貸してくれて有難う。
example_sentences.english: Thanks for lending me your clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: 和服にしようか洋服にしようかまよってます。
example_sentences.english: I have trouble deciding which clothes to wear, Japanese-style or Western-style.

example_sentences.japanese: 早く洋服を着ないと、学校に遅れるわよ。
example_sentences.english: You should get dressed really quickly or you’ll be late for school.

notes: "We pass through this point together. This point is our common point. It is where our ideas, philosophies, and bodies pass through each other." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとは共通点が全くないから、何を話せばいいか分からないよ。
example_sentences.english: I don't know what to talk about because Koichi and I have nothing in common.

example_sentences.japanese: トウフとフグの、おどろくべき共通点を発見しました。
example_sentences.english: We discovered an amazing similarity between Tofu and Fugu.

example_sentences.japanese: 「コウイチが熟女好きっていう噂を聞いたんだけど。」「マジかよ！もしそれが本当なら、俺とコウイチに共通点ができるってことになるぜ。」
example_sentences.english: """I heard a rumor that Koichi likes older women."" ""Seriously? If that was true it would mean that he and I have something in common."""

english: Different Person, Changed Person, Changed Man
notes: "A separate person is someone who is different from who they were before. I saw you a year ago and you were someone else. Now you're a different person, in a good way! You're a changed man." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはお酒を止めてから、すっかり別人になったね。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is a changed man ever since he quit drinking.

example_sentences.japanese: 友だちだと思って声をかけたら、かん全に別人だった。
example_sentences.english: I thought it was my friend and said hi, but it was a completely different person.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは昔はAKB48をよくディスっていたのに、今はすっかり大ファンになっちまった。まるで別人のようだよ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi used to diss AKB48 pretty often, but now he's a crazed AKB48 fan. It’s as though he's a different person.

english: Entrance Exam, Entrance Examination, Admission Test, Admission Exam, Admission Examination, Entrance Test
notes: "For school admission (入学) you're taking an examination (試験). What exams do you have to take to get into a school? How about entrance exams? The Japanese ones are pretty hard.
