Another word for them is ""hell tests.""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It'll also help if you know the two separate words that make up this longer word.

example_sentences.japanese: 入学試験を終えた息子が、ニコニコしながら飛んで帰ってきました。
example_sentences.english: My son flew back home smiling after finishing the entrance exam.

example_sentences.japanese: えーっ！入学試験代ってこんなにかかるの？は産しちゃうよ〜。
example_sentences.english: What? The entrance examination fees are that expensive? I'm gonna go bankrupt!

example_sentences.japanese: ええっ！入学試験に落ちちゃったの？
example_sentences.english: What! She’s failed the entrance exam?

notes: "Everyone has to carry their fate. So what is the thing you're carrying? It's your fate." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 運命をしんじますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you believe in destiny?

example_sentences.japanese: 二人は運命の赤い糸でむすばれているって思ってたけど、だんだん心がはなれていってるみたい。
example_sentences.english: I thought those two were tied together by the red thread of fate, but it seems that their hearts are growing ever distant.

example_sentences.japanese: iPhoneさん天国行き。用を足した後のトイレに落としちゃいました。まぁ、これがiPhoneさんの運命だったのかもしれないけどさ。でも、猛烈に悲しいぜよ...。
example_sentences.english: Rest in peace iPhone. I just dropped it in a toilet filled with more than just water. Maybe this was just fate but I am so sad right now.

english: Folk Tale, Legend, Old Story, Folklore
notes: "Long ago people used to talk about all sorts of things. Most of them weren't true. Long ago people liked to lie a lot. Now we call those things they talked about folk tales and legends. " "The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them both already, so you should be able to read this on your own. Just watch out for the rendaku of はなし to ばなし."

example_sentences.japanese: これは日本の昔話ですか。
example_sentences.english: Is this a Japanese folk tale?

example_sentences.japanese: まるで昔話の中に出てくるおひめさまみたいね。
example_sentences.english: That's like a princess in a legend.

example_sentences.japanese: バス待合所でバスを待ちながら、昔話の絵本を子どもに読み聞かせた。
example_sentences.english: While waiting for a bus in the bus shelter, I read a folk tale picture book for my child.

notes: "If you have a friend you like, well, that's true friendship!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このやきいもは、友好のしるしです。
example_sentences.english: This baked sweet potato is a sign of our friendship.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは、日米の友好をそくしんする役わりをはたした。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu played a role in promoting Japan-U.S. friendship.

example_sentences.japanese: カナさんって、とても友好的で経験豊富な日本語教師じゃない？でもそれだけじゃなく、実はヤクザの隠れメンバーでもあるんだよ。
example_sentences.english:
Kana is a very friendly and experienced Japanese teacher, right?
Actually, she is also a secret member of the Yakuza.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 仮名 means ""kana?"" Well this is flat kana. Flat kana is just hiragana." You should know the reading for this word because it's the same as the English meaning.

example_sentences.japanese: 平仮名は読めるけど書けません。
example_sentences.english: I can read hiragana but I can’t write it.

example_sentences.japanese: 平仮名でかいていただけませんか？
example_sentences.english: Could you write it in hiragana, please?

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトが、平仮名を五分で全部おぼえられるアプリを開発しました。
example_sentences.english: Viet developed an app that make it so people can memorize all hiragana in five minutes.

english: How To Use, Way Of Using
notes: "You've seen the word 使う hopefully by now. If you have, you know it means ""to use."" So, the way to use something is the way of using (aka how to use). This will be a word you see when you're looking at directions for how to use something." "The readings come from the vocab words 使う and 方. So long as you're okay with those you can apply that knowledge over here."

example_sentences.japanese: もう少し、言葉の使い方に気を付けた方がいいでしょ。
example_sentences.english: You should be more careful about how you use language.

example_sentences.japanese: アイフォンの使い方が分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't know how to use iPhones.

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒に仕事ができるように、俺の犬に金槌の使い方を訓練してみようと思うんだ。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to train my dog how to use a hammer and bring him to work with me.

english: Laborer, Blue Collar Worker, Manual Laborer
notes: "Someone who does labor for work is a laborer." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ社長は、肉体労働者の不足についてどうお考えなんですか？
example_sentences.english: What does president Koichi think about the shortage of blue-collar workers?

example_sentences.japanese: 一体、お前と労働者たちの間に、何があったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: What happened between you and all the laborers?

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっとコピー機使わせてもらってもいい？新しい労働者を雇うために、チラシを作ってるんだけど。
example_sentences.english: Can I use the photocopier? I’m making up flyers to try to get new laborers.

notes: "The fat flat ocean is the Pacific Ocean. I guess it's fatter than the Atlantic? Whatever it is, it's the ocean that China/Japan would have known the most about when they were coming up with words and kanji, which is why this is the Pacific, not the Atlantic." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグチームは、ごうか客せんで太平洋をわたる社いんりょ行をけいかくしています。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu team is planning a company retreat to travel across the Pacific Ocean on a luxury cruise.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷ぞうこの中の太平洋クロマグロは、カナエちゃんのお土産です。
example_sentences.english: That Pacific bluefin tuna in the fridge is Kanae's souvenir.

example_sentences.japanese: 現在、ほとんどの河豚は繁殖期である春に収穫され、太平洋に浮かぶ籠の中で養殖されます。
example_sentences.english: Nowadays, most pufferfish are harvested in the spring during the spawning season, then farmed in floating cages in the Pacific Ocean.

notes: "The electricity wave is a wave of electricity going through the air. There are many words one can use to describe this, but the easiest one is reception (aka the reception on your phone, for example). Other more technical meanings are radio wave and electromagnetic waves. Which one you like is up to you, but reception is going to be the most common meaning on the street. Luckily people in Japan don't have AT&T otherwise you'd hear this word a lot more..." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The は from 波 rendakus to ぱ, so be careful. Maybe it's your pa who has bad reception every time you try to call him?"

example_sentences.japanese: このビルはコンクリでできてるので、む線の電波はとどきません。
example_sentences.english: This building is made of concrete, so it can't be penetrated by radio waves.

example_sentences.japanese: 公きょうの電波でそんな事言うなんて、最低だね。
example_sentences.english: How could he say such things on public radio! Nasty jerk.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん、よく聞こえないよ。ここは電波が悪いみたい。
example_sentences.english: Sorry, you sound kind of choppy. It seems like I’ve got bad reception here.

notes: "Imagine someone accepting something and then attaching something. This person is a receptionist, because they are accepting the call, writing down the information, and then attaching said information to a sticky note for you to read. You say, ""No, I'm not available.""" "For this reading you have to think back to the verb words that get used with this kanji, namely 受ける and 付ける. Then just drop off the るs and put them together. 受 becomes うけ and 付 becomes つけ and you're left with うけつけ. This is what's called a compound word. And now you know it. Nice!"

example_sentences.japanese: あの受付の女せい、左足に大きな魚の目があるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that receptionist lady has a big corn on her left foot.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から、シュワちゃんがトーフグの受付をしてくれます。
example_sentences.english: Arnold Schwarzenegger will be Tofugu's receptionist starting tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: え？知らない。受付で聞いてない？
example_sentences.english: Huh? I don’t know. Didn't someone at reception explain it to you?

notes: "Above the roof is the rooftop. What else would be up there?" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 屋 though, so here's a mnemonic to help you:One place in the world has more rooftops than any where else, and that's Oklahoma (おく). They get so many tornadoes that they need extra rooftops for when the first few blow off."

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、屋上でバーベキューをします。
example_sentences.english: We're doing a rooftop barbecue today.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜きん明けにもかかわらず、屋上できんトレをしました。
example_sentences.english: I worked out on the rooftop in the morning even though I work the night shift.

example_sentences.japanese: 屋上に上がって、天からふり注ぐ星の光を一緒にあびないかい？
example_sentences.english: Why don't we go up to the housetop and catch the star light shining down from the heavens?

notes: "The hand that sells the items is connected to a person who is known as the seller or the vendor." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji, but you know them both now, so you should be able to read this too! One hint that this is a kun'yomi reading word is the hiragana in the center. It's like two separate words combined together, and when a word is a single kanji / a single kanji with hiragana attached it is usually kun'yomi. This is like two of those, combined.

example_sentences.japanese: あの売り手にだまされました。
example_sentences.english: I was cheated by that vendor.

example_sentences.japanese: 空ぜんの売り手市場ですね。
example_sentences.english: This's the hottest seller's market ever.

example_sentences.japanese: その家の売り手は、「近所の人が本当にひどいやつなので、家を手放すことにしたんだ」と、私に話してくれました。
example_sentences.english: The guy selling that house told me he’s selling it because his neighbor is a real jerk.

notes: "The way/road of the god(s) is, as you can probably guess, a big Japanese religion. There's two, and I'll give you a hint, this one isn't Buddhism (that would probably have the kanji for Buddha in it, no?). So what's the other big one? It's Shinto. If you're having trouble remembering this because you've never heard of it before, skip to the reading. The reading will help." "The reading is a bit wonky. 神 should be no problem. 道 on the other hand is almost the one you learned (どう) but now it's とう for some reason. Perhaps the gods took away the dakuten to make it とう, who knows. All I know is that it's best not to question said gods. If you already know of Shinto in English, though, this reading should be really easy. If you don't, perhaps you can use this reading to help you to remember Shinto the religion."

example_sentences.japanese: これは、神道のぎしきの一つです。
example_sentences.english: This is one Shinto ritual.

example_sentences.japanese: きのうの夜、ひたすら神道についてコウイチに語るゆめを見ました。
example_sentences.english: Last night, I had a dream that I was just explaining Shinto to Koichi forever.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして神道には絶対的な神がいないのですか。
example_sentences.english: Why doesn’t Shinto have an absolute God?

notes: "A God company... think of this as ""what 'company' does the god's work?"" Well, the answer to that is a shrine, probably. In this case a Shinto Shrine because of the しん in the 神." "But wait! 神 is read じん in this word for some reason. Darn them gods, always messing around, adding dakuten. Maybe this will help, though: Imagine yourself at a Shinto Shrine. You are praying to the Gods, asking for food. Out from the sky rains Ginger (じんじゃ). You are pelted with it and not sure if you should be happy or upset."

example_sentences.japanese: 神社に初もうでに行ったら、コウイチとビエトがなぐり合いのけんかをしていた。
example_sentences.english: When I visited a shinto shrine at the beginning of the new year, I saw Koichi and Viet having a fist fight.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の神社で買ったおまもりのこと、すっかりわすれてた。
example_sentences.english: I totally forgot about the charm I bought at a shinto shrine in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: よぉ、中々イケてる自撮りじゃん。でも、お前、なんで学校じゃなくて神社になんていたんだよ？
example_sentences.english: Yo! Very cool selfie, but why were you in a shinto shrine instead of at school?

notes: "A war car is probably a little more dangerous than the Honda you drive. No, a war car is a tank." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの市では、ゴミしゅう集車の代わりに戦車が使われることになりました。
example_sentences.english: Our city decided to use a tank instead of a garbage truck.

example_sentences.japanese: この戦車、そろそろせん車しないとなぁ。
example_sentences.english: We have to wash this tank soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 「俺の戦車のタイヤ、どう？」「もう少し空気を入れるか、戦車用の履帯に換えた方がいいと思いますよ。」
example_sentences.english: """How are the tires on my tank?"" ""I think you should either pump them up a lot more or switch to tank treads."""

notes: "The first of something you'll do several or many times is the first time." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの新曲の、初回げん定ばんのCDを手に入れました。
example_sentences.english: I got the first-press limited edition of Koichi's new song.

example_sentences.japanese: 初回のお客さまには、特別かかくでごていきょうしています。
example_sentences.english: We have a special offer for first time customers!

example_sentences.japanese: えっ、君が日本語学習クラブに参加するのは今回が初回なんだ？よし、みんな。彼は初心者だから手加減してあげようぜ。
example_sentences.english: Oh, is this your first time attending our Japanese language club? Okay everyone, he’s a newbie, so let’s go easy on him.

notes: "*Ahem.* This is the place of convenience. What place above all others do you want to be convenient? Just in case, you know... that would be the toilet." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: へをこく時は便所に行けよ。
example_sentences.english: You should go to the bathroom when you fart.

example_sentences.japanese: サトシ、ようやく便所そうじのスイッチが入ったみたいだね。
example_sentences.english: It seems that Satoshi finally got serious about cleaning the bathroom.

example_sentences.japanese: よっしゃ！完璧なシュートが決まったぜ！俺、ここの便所のバスケットゴール付きのゴミ箱めっちゃ好きだわ。
example_sentences.english: Oh yeah! Nothing but net! I really love that this restroom’s trashcan has a basketball net on it.

notes: "You know that 乗り has something to do with riding and that 物 is a thing. So what is a ""riding thing?"" Nowadays, at least, that would be a vehicle." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji, but you know them both now, so you should be able to read this too!

example_sentences.japanese: 乗り物の中でタバコをすわないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don’t smoke in vehicles.

example_sentences.japanese: 乗り物よいしちゃった。
example_sentences.english: I got motion sickness.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あの乗り物、どうだった？」「ああ、怖かったさ！小便チビっちゃうくらい怖かったぜ。」
example_sentences.english: """How was the ride?"" ""Oh, it was terrifying! I spent the whole time trying not to pee my pants."""

notes: "The Western eats are Western food. Mmmm, 'dem hamburgers." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この洋食レストランは、有名なすし屋が共同して立ち上げたものです。
example_sentences.english: The Western food restaurant was made in cooperation with famous sushi restaurants.

example_sentences.japanese: いわゆる昔ながらの洋食屋さんで、バイトをしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm working part-time at a so-called old fashioned Western family restaurant.

example_sentences.japanese: ええっ！あそこのレストランで洋食ランチセットを食べたの？ははは。どおりでまだお腹がいっぱいなはずだわ。
example_sentences.english: Oh, did you eat the western-style lunch set at that restaurant? Hahaha. No wonder you still feel full.

notes: "A Western style room is a Western style room. We're talking something that's not a tatami mat filled room. Good to know this word if you're staying in hotels or ryokans and prefer not to sleep on a futon, etc." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの発言で、洋室にいた全いんがこおりついてしまった。
example_sentences.english: When Koichi made that comment, everybody in the western style room froze.

example_sentences.japanese: この洋室、はじめて来た場所なのに、なんだかよく知ってる部屋のような気がする。
example_sentences.english: This western style room looks strangely familiar, though I know I've never been here before.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の部屋は六畳の洋室で、壁の色は私の好きな水色です。
example_sentences.english: My room is a western style room, about ten square meters, with my favorite color of light blue on the walls.

notes: "Put aside your steampunk blimp fantasies for a moment. A sky harbor is an airport, nothing more." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この間、成田空港で大げんかをしているカップルを見ました。
example_sentences.english: I saw a couple having a huge fight at Narita Airport the other day.

example_sentences.japanese: おむつがえシートのあるトイレはこの空港にありますか？
example_sentences.english: Are there bathrooms with changing tables in this airport?

example_sentences.japanese: 空港で借りた車の中に、パスポートを忘れた気がする。
example_sentences.english: I think I left my passport in the car I rented at the airport.

notes: "A moving thing... think about the ""things"" that move. Technically it could be a lot of things (aka basically anything), but in this case we are talking about moving living things. We won't include humans, because humans are too good to be called things. This refers to animals instead." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物は苦手なんです。
example_sentences.english: I don't like animals.

example_sentences.japanese: 何か動物はかっていますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you have any animals?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチがトーフグ動物園に100匹の重要な動物を集めてパーティーを開催したんだけど、何故か私は招待されなかったんだよね。私もコウイチにとっての重要動物の一匹だと思っていたんだけど。
example_sentences.english: Koichi hosted a party at the Tofugu Zoo for one hundred very important animals and for some reason, I wasn’t invited. I thought I was one of the VIA to him too.

notes: "Field Sphere! The greatest sport to grace this earth since a very similar (aka the same) sport, baseball. Think about it, you play on a field and you use a little sphere. Awesome!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これから、プロ野球のし合を見に行くところなんです。
example_sentences.english: We are just about to go to a professional baseball game.

example_sentences.japanese: 野球は好きだけど、野球部は体育会けいって聞いたから入りたくないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I like baseball, but I heard you have to act like you're in the army if you belong to the baseball club, so I don't want to join it.

example_sentences.japanese: 野球をしている時に膝を骨折しちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I fractured my knee while playing baseball.

notes: "Who is part parent to you? Your boss! They make it so you can take care of yourself by paying you, don't they? They'll break the legs of someone who crosses you. But they won't help you get back to sleep after you have nightmares. So they're only part like a parent." "This word consists of the kun'yomi reading for 親 and the on'yomi reading for 分. You've learned both of these so you should be able to read this already!"

example_sentences.japanese: 地下道でヤクザの親分とすれちがったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I walked by a yakuza kingpin in the underpass.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチとビエトではどちらが親分でどちらが子分ですか。
example_sentences.english: Between Koichi and Viet, which is the boss and which is the henchman?

example_sentences.japanese: 親分にバレたら大目玉を食らうぞ。
example_sentences.english: The chief will chew us out if we let it slip.

notes: "The actions and things you have to 心配 about are your cares and worries." "The reading is the reading of 心配 (which you've hopefully gotten down okay by now) and 事 using the (こと) reading. It is rendaku'd, as well, so beware of the ごと (just another 心配事, ammiright?)."

example_sentences.japanese: 心配事をわらいとばしてくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for laughing my cares away.

example_sentences.japanese: なんだか心配事があるみたいだよ。
example_sentences.english: Apparently he's got some worries.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の一番の心配事は、町に降り落ちる火山灰です。
example_sentences.english: My biggest worry is volcanic ash falling over the city.

notes: "Don't think of this as a juvenile talk. Think of 話 the vocab word, which means ""story."" If you do that, you get a ""juvenile story."" What's a juvenile story? It's a children's story." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この童話、意外と泣けるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: This fairy tale will actually make you cry.

example_sentences.japanese: やっと、童話のしっぴつに、本気モードになってきました。
example_sentences.english: I'm finally getting serious about writing children's stories.

example_sentences.japanese: 宮沢賢治の童話「祭の晩」は、私が子供の頃大好きなお話でした。
example_sentences.english: "Miyazawa Kenji’s fairy tale ""Night of the Festival"" was my favorite story when I was a child."

notes: "A ""company"" (会社) member is someone who works at a company. This is a company employee. There are many of these in Japan. Most of them are drunk." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの夫は、ごくふ通の会社員です。
example_sentences.english: My husband is just an ordinary office worker.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしたちはみんな、会社員である前に、一人の人間なんですよ。
example_sentences.english: We're people before we are employees.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社員は麻薬所持で逮捕された。
example_sentences.english: That employee got busted for drug possession.

notes:
"You know that a 医者 is a doctor. So what is a tooth doctor? A dentist. Seriously, don't forget to floss. 歯医者 hate when you forget to floss." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"The failure someone (person) is the loser or the defeated." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 半年に一度は歯医者に行った方がいい。
example_sentences.english: It's better to go see a dentist at least once every six months.

example_sentences.japanese: 花田さんは、この歯医者にはもっ体ないよ。
example_sentences.english: Ms. Handa is too good for this dentist.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はただ不良に憧れてるだけだと思うよ。絶対に本物の不良にはならないね。だって、歯医者さんに行くのですら怖がってるんだよ！
example_sentences.english: I think he’s just a wannabe delinquent. I doubt he’ll end up being a real one because he’s still afraid of going to the dentist.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ敗者ふっ活戦が残っていますよ。
example_sentences.english: We still have a consolation match left for the defeated.

example_sentences.japanese: その歯医者は、生まれながらの敗者であった。
example_sentences.english: That dentist was born to be a loser.

example_sentences.japanese: スポーツを見るとき、全力を尽くした負け犬と自分を重ね合わせてみなよ。それって楽しい？達成感はある？何か意味はあるの？意味無いよね？敗者から勝者に生まれ変わらなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: Whenever you watch sports, you identify with the underdog that tried their best. Is that fun? Do you feel like you achieve something? What’s the point? No point, right? You have to change yourself from a loser to a winner.

notes: "Something that is two times is double (or it is just simply two times). Of course, this all works with things like 三倍, 百倍, and 四十二倍 as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このかぶのかぶかはたったの二日で二倍になった。
example_sentences.english: This stock's price doubled just in two days.

example_sentences.japanese: めんつゆを二倍にうすめるのを忘れないでください。
example_sentences.english: Don't forget to dilute the noodle soup base two times.

example_sentences.japanese: うわ！君のお兄さんって、君の二倍の体重があるんだね！
example_sentences.english: Wow! Your brother weighs twice as much as you, huh?

notes: "You know that 運転 has to do with driving, right? And you know that 手 often has to do with a person doing something in words like these. So, a person who does driving is what? A driver." "The reading is all on'yomi, because it's jukugo. You should know the on'yomi reading of 手 by now just by seeing similar word patterns to this one."

example_sentences.japanese: タクシーに乗ったら運転手がトーフグのコウイチだった。
example_sentences.english: When I took the taxi, the driver happened to be Tofugu's Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: バスの運転手と言い争いになってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I ended up getting in an argument with the bus driver.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転手は大丈夫だったみたいだけど、車は事故でめちゃくちゃになっていたよ。
example_sentences.english: The driver seemed okay but his car was totaled in the accident.

english: Employee, Staff, Company Employee, Company Staff
notes: "The company members are the employees and the staff." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 全社員がコウイチと仲良くするためのイロハを心えている。
example_sentences.english: All of the staff know the ABCs of getting along with Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: れいの社員さんとは最近どうなの？仲直りはできた？
example_sentences.english: How are things with that employee lately? Patch things up yet?

example_sentences.japanese: この会社の社員は、全員奇抜で素晴らしい。
example_sentences.english: The employees in this company are all weird and wonderful.

english: Evil Woman, Wicked Woman, Bad Woman
notes: "A bad woman is an evil woman. Surprisingly, ""mother in law"" is not one of the meanings for this word." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの悪女、耳だけはいいんだよな。
example_sentences.english: That bitch sure has good ears!

example_sentences.japanese: かの女は悪女だが、いつも時間はきっちり守る。
example_sentences.english: She is a wicked woman, but is always on time.

example_sentences.japanese: その悪女は息をのむほど美しかった。僕は彼女に夢中だった。
example_sentences.english: The evil woman took my breath away. I was crazy about her.

notes: "The ordinal number prefix one rank. Basically, this means ""first rank"" or first place." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグはユニークな日本語学習教ざいとして、五年れんぞく第一位のざをかくとくしています。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu got first place five consecutive times in tournaments for unique Japanese learning tools.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグチームの中で一番げん付乗りまわしていてほしい人第一位はわたしてきにはクリステンなんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Out of the whole Tofugu team, I personally want Kristen to drive around in a moped the most.

example_sentences.japanese: あきらが入社するまで、ヒロは五年続けて、社内で売り上げ第一位だった。
example_sentences.english: Hiro had been the top sales person in the company for five consecutive years until Akira joined the company.

english: Gathering, Meeting, Assembly, Party, Collection, Get Together
notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji gather, so it means gathering." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading already so you should be able to read it!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は研究室の集まりがある。
example_sentences.english: There’s a get-together with people from the lab today.

example_sentences.japanese: なんか今日の飲み会、集まりも悪かったし、グダグダだったね。
example_sentences.english: Not many people showed up at today's drinking party and it was also very disorganized, eh?

example_sentences.japanese: 正月の集まりに弟が彼女を連れてきやがった。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother brought his girlfriend to our New Year's gathering.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "This is a single kanji with no okurigana, so it's using the kun'yomi reading. You don't know this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You go down to the harbor and speak the secret password me natto (みなと) to buy some fresh natto. Imagine the salty air hitting your face as you whisper, ""me natto."" Now eat that yummy natto by the water! Mmmm!"

example_sentences.japanese: ベラクルスという港町に行ってみたいです。
example_sentences.english: I would like to visit the port city of Veracruz.

example_sentences.japanese: ごう雨のため、港への道は通行止めになっています。
example_sentences.english: Due to heavy rain, the road to the harbor is closed.

example_sentences.japanese: 不思議な船が港に漂着した。
example_sentences.english: There was a mysterious ship drifting in the harbor.

notes: "The wide island... this isn't helpful on its own, but this wide island is Hiroshima (heard of it?). When you do the reading it will make more sense." The reading is the kun'yomi readings of both of these which is what you learned with the individual kanji. Just make sure you know those readings and you'll be able to read this.

example_sentences.japanese: 広島に、登山にいい山はありますか？
example_sentences.english: Are there good mountains to climb in Hiroshima?

example_sentences.japanese: 広島空港から市バスで市内に向かってるところです。
example_sentences.english: I'm heading into the city from Hiroshima airport by city bus.

example_sentences.japanese: 広島と長崎に投下された原爆は、一瞬で十万人以上の人々の命を奪った。
example_sentences.english: The atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki instantly killed more than 100,000 people.

notes: "A warm spring (like the water kind of spring) is a hot spring. These are really nice. You should go to them in Japan." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この温泉は、タトゥーのある人も入よくできます。
example_sentences.english: This onsen is open for people with tattoos too.

example_sentences.japanese: かるく運動してあせを流した後、温泉に入ろう。
example_sentences.english: Let's go to hot spring after sweating a little bit from some light exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の父も母も温泉が好きじゃありません。
example_sentences.english: Neither my dad nor mom likes hot springs.

notes: "You receive profit at every breath. What kind of profit is this? It's interest. As time goes by and as you take more breaths you gain more bank interest." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: もし利息の支はらいがおくれたら、ビエトがヤクザの友だちをつれてお前のところにやって来ると思うぜ。
example_sentences.english: If you miss the interest payment, Viet will probably bring some of his yakuza friends to your place.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは利息で生活できるぐらい十分なお金をぎん行にちょ金しています。
example_sentences.english: Koichi has enough money in the bank to live on his interest.

example_sentences.japanese: あいにく今、その質問に答えられる者がいないのですが、もしインターネットにアクセス可能なら利息のレートはそちらでもご確認頂けますよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m afraid there is no one here who can answer your question right now, but you can also check your interest rate online, if you can connect to the Internet.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 文字 can mean ""characters?"" Well make a face out of those characters and you've made a kaomoji! ʅ(◔౪◔ ) ʃ" "This word consists of the kun'yomi reading for 顔 added to the jukugo word 文字 that you already learned. You've learned these readings before, so reading this word should be nice and easy!"

example_sentences.japanese: 今の気持ちを顔文字で表してください。
example_sentences.english: Please express your current feelings with kaomoji.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトがコウイチにあてた手紙を内しょで読んだら、全てが顔文字でかかれていた。
example_sentences.english: I secretly read Viet's letter to Koichi, but everything was written in kaomoji.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司へのメールに顔文字を使うんじゃない！
example_sentences.english: Don’t use kaomoji when you’re emailing a superior!

notes: "The capital metropolis back in the day was Kyoto. Now of course the capital is Tokyo, but kanji doesn't know this. That's why Kyoto is the capital metropolis!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: JRの「そうだ、京都行こう」の広告を見て京都に行きたくなったが、そんなお金はなかった。
example_sentences.english: "The JR ad ""That's it! Let's go to Kyoto."" made me want to go to Kyoto, but I didn't have that kind of money."

example_sentences.japanese: 京都に行ったら、湯葉を食べたいです。
example_sentences.english: When I go to Kyoto, I want to eat tofu skin.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは本日は既に京都へ発ってしまいました。明日の朝一番に折り返しお電話をさせましょうか？
example_sentences.english: Koichi has already left for Kyoto today. Shall I have him call you back first thing tomorrow morning?

notes: "We've seen a few times where 電 refers to a train. They're big deals, after all, and use a ton of electricity. So, the end train for this word would refer to the last train." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 終電、何時だっけ？
example_sentences.english: What time was the last train?

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐ終電だから、そろそろかえらなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: I've gotta go because it's almost time for the last train.

example_sentences.japanese: 「もし終電に乗り遅れたら、いつでも電話してくれていいよ。」「有難う。覚えておくよ。」
example_sentences.english: """If you ever miss the last train, you can always call me."" ""Thanks, I’ll keep that in mind."""

notes: "If you meet enough members you will become a member yourself!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会員はかなり心配しょうのようなんです。
example_sentences.english: That member seems to be a huge worrywart.

example_sentences.japanese: 見えないかもしれませんが、そこにもう一人小さな会員がいるんですよ。
example_sentences.english: You may not be able to see it, but there's one more little member over there.

example_sentences.japanese: 会員カードはお持ちですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you have a membership card?

english: Middle Of The Night, Late At Night
notes: "The deep night is the middle of the night. It doesn't get any deeper than that before you start coming out of the night to start the next day." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな深夜に、どうしたの？
example_sentences.english: What's up this late at night?

example_sentences.japanese: 深夜に小ばらが空いてきた。
example_sentences.english: I got a bit hungry in the middle of the night.

example_sentences.japanese: 環境難民となった熊たちは、新しい国で食べ物を探すため、深夜、国境を越えた。
example_sentences.english: The environmental refugee bears crossed the border late in the night to find something to eat in a new country.

notes: "The root of your energy. You have to dig deep into your energy, all the way to the origin and source of it, to have enough patience to deal with this dumb kid who's eating away at your not-root energy. It's all you have, and you need to use it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これは根気のいる仕事だよな。
example_sentences.english: This job requires patience, huh?

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんどの失ぱいのげんいんは、根気のなさなんだよね。
example_sentences.english: The reason for failure in most cases is a lack of perseverance.

example_sentences.japanese: 根気よく日本語の勉強を続けていれば、いつかはペラペラになれるさ。
example_sentences.english: Keep studying Japanese persistently and you’ll be fluent someday.

notes: "Plant things are plants or vegetation." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You'll need to remember the 物 reading as ぶつ, though. Why? Because you like looking at plant butts. You get off on it. You're weird like that. Imagine this."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは植物の言っている事が分かるらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently Koichi can understand what plants are saying.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、植物でできたふ葉土です。
example_sentences.english: This is mulch from the vegetation.

example_sentences.japanese: 園芸の才能は無いけど植物を育てるのは好きなんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t have a green thumb but I like to grow plants.

notes: "The root of your roof is still your roof. If it helps, imagine roots growing out of your roof. They protect you from the rain." "This word uses the kun'yomi readings. The kun'yomi for 根 is ね. For a mnemonic, we'll use the sound a horse makes, neigh (ね). Why is the horse neigh-ing? It's stuck on the roof."

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、屋根をしゅう理する必要があります。
example_sentences.english: We have to fix our roof next year.

example_sentences.japanese: 屋根にあなが開いているので、雨もりしてるんですよ。
example_sentences.english: It's leaking because we have a hole in our roof.

example_sentences.japanese: お昼までに屋根の雪を取り除いて下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please clear the snow off the roof by noon.

english: Second Floor, Floor Two, Second Story
notes: "The two floor is the second floor. Going up!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯医者さんなら、このビルの二階にあります。
example_sentences.english: The dentist is on the second floor of this building.

example_sentences.japanese: 二階だてのマイホームを買いました。
example_sentences.english: We bought a second story home.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日午後に二階にある同じ教室に行って、英語を二時間教えます。
example_sentences.english: Every afternoon I go to the same classroom on the second floor and teach two hours of English.

notes: "The short sword is the short sword. What's another word for a short sword? It's a dagger." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その短刀、どこで買ったの？
example_sentences.english: Where did you buy that tanto?

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは、短刀を使ってとても上手にりょう理をします。
example_sentences.english: Viet cooks very well with a short sword.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の父は、母に短刀で刺されて死にました。
example_sentences.english: My mother stabbed my father with a dagger and he died.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Another meaning I'm going to add is sports ball because this is the word used for balls in various sports (soccer, baseball, etc)." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You're holding onto a sports ball in your hand, let's say it's a baseball for this mnemonic's sake. You throw it at your friend who's going to catch it. As it flies through the air, though, it transforms into a tomahawk (たま). Imagine your shock and fear as you see this happening, flying towards your friend! It's going to stick in his forehead. He can't catch this with his glove! Also notice that it has the same reading as the vocab word 玉. So, if you know that one, you may know this one too! They're kind of similar.This can be read きゅう too, if you're talking about more of a globe sphere than the ball sphere you throw."

example_sentences.japanese: ああっ！球がバンカーに入っちゃったよ。
example_sentences.english: Dammit! I hit the ball into a bunker.

example_sentences.japanese: 球の体せきをもとめる公しきって何だっけ？
example_sentences.english: What was the formula for the volume of a sphere?

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、新しい野球の球を買ったんだけど、一緒にキャッチボールしない？
example_sentences.english: Hey, I got a new baseball. Do you want to play catch with me?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You're looking at a natural spring in the ground. Water is bubbling up, but then something changes. It looks a bit clogged... something is poking out. Then, all of a sudden, Mario flies out of the springs, falls in front of you and yells: ""izumeeeee (いずみ), Mario!"""

example_sentences.japanese: わたしたちは、泉からのわき水を飲んでいます。
example_sentences.english: We're drinking water from the spring.

example_sentences.japanese: その泉にはがちょうがたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of geese in that spring.

example_sentences.japanese: わぁ！すごく綺麗。何か特別なダイエットでもしたの？それとも、若返りの泉でも見つけたとか？
example_sentences.english: Wow! You look beautiful! Did you go on a special diet? Or did you find the Fountain of Youth?

notes: "Hot water's energy isn't the hot water itself, it's what comes out of it (when it's boiling, for example). This is the steam and vapor." "The ゆ part of the reading makes sense. The げ part for 気 is a bit of an exception. Just think of yourself standing in the steams and vapors. You're getting all hot and sweaty, but the feeling makes you incredibly happy and gay (げ). Then someone asks, as they look at you in the steam: ""Hey, you gay?"" (ゆげ). You answer however you want to answer."

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトのおでこから出ている湯気、なんだかいいにおいがするんだよね。
example_sentences.english: This vapors coming out of Viet's forehead smell nice for some reason.

example_sentences.japanese: それ、まだ湯気が立つほどあついから、気を付けてね。
example_sentences.english: That's still steaming hot, so be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しい寿司飯を作るには、しゃもじを使って、湯気が立つ炊きたての熱いごはんに酢を混ぜる必要があります。信じられないかもしれませんが、実際に米一粒一粒を潰さずに酢を混ぜるには技術が必要です。
example_sentences.english: To make good sushi rice, you need to mix vinegar into steaming hot, freshly cooked rice, using a paddle. Believe it or not, it actually takes skill to mix the vinegar into the rice without crushing the individual grains.

notes: "The fat sunshine thing up in the sky... what is it called? Oh, that's right. It's the sun." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽のようなコウイチのえ顔に、こいに落ちてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I fell in love with Koichi's sunshine-like smile.

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽の温度って何度ぐらいあるか知っていますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you happen to know what the sun's temperature is?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本万国博覧会のシンボルは、岡本太郎が作った「太陽の塔」で、それは今も日本の大阪の吹田にある万博公園にそびえ立っています。
example_sentences.english: The symbol of Expo ’70 was the Tower of the Sun, created by Taro Okamoto, and it’s still standing in the Expo Commemoration Park in Suita, Osaka, Japan.

notes: "It's an island where they use cats as a substitute for rice! Lovely Tashirojima. Don't worry, they don't eat them! ...or, wait, do they?" "This is a place name and it uses the kun'yomi. You haven't learned this particular kun'yomi for 代 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember it:When you go to Tashirojima, make sure you visit the old woman. You know what woman I'm talking about, the one who starred on Murder she wrote (しろ). She writes a lot about cats now, I guess."

example_sentences.japanese: 田代島の人口は百人以下です。
example_sentences.english: The population of Tashirojima is less than one hundred.

example_sentences.japanese: 田代島にはガソリンスタンドがありません。
example_sentences.english: There are no gas stations on Tashirojima.

example_sentences.japanese: 最も有名な「猫島」といえば、日本の宮城県にある田代島という島です。
example_sentences.english: "The most famous ""cat island"" is the island Tashirojima in Japan's Miyagi prefecture."

notes: "The hot water of tea. That is part of the ceremony that goes into the tea ceremony." The readings are both the readings you learned with the kanji. Now you can spend a little more time drinking tea at a tea ceremony and a little less time trying to remember kanji readings.

example_sentences.japanese: 茶の湯の道具が買えるお店をさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for a shop where I can buy tools for tea ceremonies.

example_sentences.japanese: この水は、茶の湯にてきした水として知られています。
example_sentences.english: This water is known to be good for tea ceremony.

example_sentences.japanese: 茶の湯の世界には、「一つ一つの出会いを大切に」という意味の「一期一会」という言葉があります。この言葉は、映画「フォレスト・ガンプ」の副タイトルとしても使われました。
example_sentences.english: "In the world of tea ceremonies there is a saying, ""Ichi-go ichi-e,"" which means ""to treasure every encounter."" This saying was also used as the subtitle for Japan’s release of Forrest Gump."

notes: "The warm degrees is how many degrees warm it is in here. Of course, there can be very few warm degrees as well, making it very cold. What is all this? It's the temperature." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ人と日本人って、温度のかんじ方がちがうと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you think American and Japanese people feel temperature differently?

example_sentences.japanese: エアコンの温度を二十四度まで上げてもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: Can you raise the temperature on the AC up to 24℃?

example_sentences.japanese: 醸造中に天気や温度がほんの少し変化しただけで、酒の味に影響することがあるため、酒を作ることは非常に難しいと言われています。
example_sentences.english: It’s said to be very difficult to make sake because the slightest change in the weather or temperature during brewing can affect its taste.

notes: "The energy of the warmth will cause the temperature to go up and down. Energy goes up? Higher temperature because of more movement and activity. Energy goes down? Well, temperature gets colder and slower." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 気温が急に下がった。
example_sentences.english: The temperature fell suddenly.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の最高気温は四十度です。
example_sentences.english: Today's highest temperature will be 40 degrees.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ばんの気温のさがはげしいんです。
example_sentences.english: There is a large temperature gap between morning and night.

english: The End, End, The Finish, Finish
notes: "By now you should know that 終わる means ""to end"" or ""to finish."" So what is this noun-version of that word? It would be the end or the finish." "The reading comes from 終わる. So long as you know that word, you can learn this word's reading as well!"

example_sentences.japanese: これで終わりだ。
example_sentences.english: This is the end.

example_sentences.japanese: 終わり良ければ全て良し、でしょ？
example_sentences.english: All is well that ends well, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 今週で仕事も終わりで、来週からはクリスマス休暇だー！あー、待ちきれない。
example_sentences.english: Work ends this week and Christmas holidays starts next week! Aww I can't wait for that.

notes: "Remember 一番目? This is just like that, but with three, making it the third thing or simply the third." "Use your knowledge of the reading for 一番目 to remember the reading for this word as well."

example_sentences.japanese: この曲、ビートルズの中で三番目くらいにすき。
example_sentences.english: This is probably my third favorite Beatles's song.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチなら左から三番目のトイレでハリーポッターを読んでるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are looking for Koichi, he's reading Harry Potter on the third toilet from the left.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の有人島の多さは、インドネシア、フィリピンに次いで、世界で三番目だってこと、知ってた？
example_sentences.english: Did you know that Japan has the third highest number of inhabited islands in the world, after Indonesia and the Philippines?

english: Time, Season, Period, Time Period, Period Of Time
notes:
"The time period of time is a period of time of time. If anything, just notice how many times the word ""time"" is used and you'll remember this word means time. The meaning is a specific type of time, though. This is talking about a season or period of time, not the concept of time itself. That would be 時間 or something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Magnetic energy is when magnetism occurs." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 時期が来るまで、見守ってやらないか？
example_sentences.english: Why don't we just wait and see until the time is right?

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐハリケーンの時期ですね。
example_sentences.english: Hurricane season is just around the corner.

example_sentences.japanese: タケシは単によくあるフェーズにさしかかっているだけだよ。ほら、外国で暮らす人はたいてい、カルチャーショックの時期を経験するっていうじゃない？
example_sentences.english: It’s just a phase Takeshi is going through. Don’t they say people living in a foreign country usually experience a period of culture shock?

example_sentences.japanese: 磁気カードと磁石を一緒にしない方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn’t put magnetic cards and magnets together.

english: Tokyo Metropolis, Tokyo Metro, Tokyo Metropolitan Area, Tokyo Metro Area
notes: "The Tokyo Metropolis is, of course, the Tokyo Metropolis. Technically this is one of Japan's prefectures, but it's called a ""Metropolis"" instead. It's the capital and the largest city in all of Japan! " "The reading is just 東京 and 都 (と). Really it's all just the reading you learned with the kanji, too, so you can think of it that way as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 東京都には、一流のレストランがたくさんある。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of first-rate restaurants in the Tokyo Metropolitan Area.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京都の３０代会社員、山田太ろうさん（仮名）は、げきむと長時間ろうどうで知られるぎょうかいで働いています。
example_sentences.english: Taro Yamada (pseudonym), who is in his 30s and a salaryman in the Tokyo Metropolis, is working in an industry that is notorious for its hard work and long working hours.

example_sentences.japanese: スカイツリーがそびえ立つ東京都墨田区では、今年は昨年よりも早く木の葉が落ち始めた。
example_sentences.english: The leaves started falling earlier this year than last year in Tokyo Metro’s Sumida Ward, where the Tokyo Sky Tree stands.

notes: "The water deepness is the water depth. You should check this before diving into the water so you don't hit your face." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 水深100フィートまでもぐったことがあります。
example_sentences.english: I've dived to depths of one hundred feet before.

example_sentences.japanese: このプールの水深はあさいから、心配しなくていいよ。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to worry because this pool is very shallow.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイビングをしている際に、水深十メートルのところで虹色の海藻を見つけました。
example_sentences.english: While diving at a depth of ten meters, I found rainbow-colored seaweed.

english: Way Of Speaking, Speaking Style, Way Of Talking, Talking Style
notes: "The way of speaking is your way of speaking (or it could be your speaking style). This is how someone talks. Some people have an interesting speaking style, after all." "The readings come from 話す and 方. By now you should have seen these words separately and should be able to read this word too."

example_sentences.japanese: 話し方が本当にイライラするのよね。
example_sentences.english: The way he talks makes me really annoyed.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの話し方って、かなりしぶいよね。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's style of conversation is very cultured, eh?

example_sentences.japanese: うわぁ！君の話し方、まるで母国語が日本語の人みたいだね。
example_sentences.english: Wow! The way you talk sounds just like a native Japanese person.

notes: "The writing chapter on its own is more like an article or something like that. Even if it's a sentence long. So it covers just about every type of writing there is." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この文章をかいたのはだれですか？
example_sentences.english: Who wrote this article?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは文章が本当に上手だ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is such a good writer.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、村上春樹の気障で気取った文章があまり好きではありません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t like Haruki Murakami’s cheesy, pompous writing style very much.

english: Admission Fee, Entrance Fee, Entry Fee
notes: "The fee for entering a public building is the admission fee. Gotta pay it if you want to get inside." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 入口で入館料をはらってください。
example_sentences.english: Please pay the admission fee at the entrance.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグはく物館の入館料は高すぎます。
example_sentences.english: The entrance fee for the Tofugu Museum is too expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 入館料、もう10％値引きしていただけませんかねぇ？
example_sentences.english: Could you give us an additional ten percent off of the entry fee?

notes:
"A foster child you bring into your family is your adopted child." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"The parts we need. The point of that. That is the point. That is the essentials. It's what we need and it's to the point, you know?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの駅長の子は、どうやら養子らしいです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that station master's kid is actually an adopted child.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの友人は九月に養子をむかえいれることにした。
example_sentences.english: My friend decided to adopt a child in September.

example_sentences.japanese: 養子の態度が悪いから、叱ってやったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I scolded my adopted child because he has such a bad attitude.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業前にその本の要旨を理解しておくと、プラスになると思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I think it would be a plus to understand the fundamentals of the book before the lesson.

notes: "A prize of gold is so old fashioned. We use cash now, which is why this word means cash prize." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 実はコウイチの首には賞金がかけられているって知っていましたか。
example_sentences.english: Did you know that the prize money is actually on Koichi's head?

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは今回の日本旅行で当てたけい馬の賞金が一億円もあるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Viet won a one-hundred-million yen cash prize from a horse race during his Japan trip this time.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は変顔コンテストの賞金をいつもらえるんですか？
example_sentences.english: When do we get our prize money from the funny face competition?

notes: "The feeling of the actions going on around you are the circumstances. For example: you feel like things are going pretty poorly right now, which is why the circumstances are looking pretty dire for you." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人には大人の事情があるんですよ。
example_sentences.english: Adults have adult circumstances.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察はすべての事情を考慮しなければならない。
example_sentences.english: The police must take all circumstances into account.

example_sentences.japanese: サマンサが母親の入院ひのためにワニカニのサービス利用代金がはらえなかったという事情はむしされてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Samantha neglected the fact that her mother's hospitalization was the reason she couldn't pay to use WaniKani.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Also, you can call this a bowl, too, if you want." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You have this container. It's upside down with a stick holding it up and a string on the stick. You're going to catch some U2s (like, the band). You put some food under it and wait. Then, out of the bushes comes Bono. He sniffs around for a bit and then goes under the container. You pull! U2 walked (うつわ) right into the trap! Haha!"

example_sentences.japanese: この器は母の形見なんです。
example_sentences.english: This vessel is a relic of my mom's.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしよう？コウイチが大切にしていたフグの器をわってしまった。
example_sentences.english: What should I do? I accidentally broke the container of blowfish that Koichi cherishes.

example_sentences.japanese: まず最初にごはんを器に入れて、次にハンバーグをのせて、それからグレービーソースをかけて、最後に卵をのせたら…ジャーン！ロコモコの出来上がり！
example_sentences.english: First you put some rice in a bowl, then you put a hamburger patty on the rice, followed by some gravy, and then an egg on top. Then, ta-da! Now, your Loco-moco is done!

notes: "When you express a feeling it shows on your face. This is called a facial expression. " This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなこわい表情をしないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't make such a scary facial expression.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニの売り上げレポートを見たコウイチの表情はとてもうれしそうだった。
example_sentences.english: After looking at WaniKani's revenue report, Koichi's face looked very happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供達の表情は、みんなとても活き活きとしていた。
example_sentences.english: The children’s faces all looked very lively.

notes: "The fee gold (or money, if you will) that you have to pay are your fees and bills." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本はガスの料金は高いですか。
example_sentences.english: Are gas bills expensive in Japan?

example_sentences.japanese: けいたい電話の料金プランがふくざつすぎて分かりません。分かりやすくせつ明してくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: It's too hard to understand cell phone service fee plans. Could you explain them in a way that's clear and easy to understand?

example_sentences.japanese: 「申し訳ありませんが、この料金が精一杯です。」「うーん。まぁ、妥当な値段のようですね。分かりました。これで手を打ちましょう。」
example_sentences.english: """I’m afraid this price is the best we can offer."" ""Well, that sounds fair. Okay, let’s finalize the deal."""

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, so don't get all feverish over this one.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は少し熱があるので外出できません。
example_sentences.english: I have a bit of a fever today so I can’t go out.

example_sentences.japanese: なんてこった！ちょっと熱っぽいだけだと思ってたら、体温40度以上あるじゃん！
example_sentences.english: OMG! I thought I was just a little feverish but my temperature is over 40 degrees!

example_sentences.japanese: この五百度の熱を持った鉄をさわってみて、その体験を感想文に書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Touch this 500-degree-heat iron and write about your experience.

english: Front Of Station, In Front Of Station, Front Of The Station, In Front Of The Station, Station Front
notes: "The station front is the front of station. This word is great for telling people where you want to meet, by the way." "This is like two separate words put together into one, so you can imagine it's the kun'yomi readings. You learned the right reading for 駅 in the kanji, and you should know the vocab word 前 by now. Combine the two together and you have yourself front of station."

example_sentences.japanese: 駅前のマンションをさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for an apartment in front of the station.

example_sentences.japanese: せんきょの期間は多くのせいじ家が駅前でスピーチをする。
example_sentences.english: During the election period, lots of politicians make speeches in front of stations.

example_sentences.japanese: なんで私に、駅前で撮ったこんな変な自撮り写メを送ってきたの？
example_sentences.english: Why did you just send that weird looking selfie taken in front of the station to me?

notes: "The luck island wasn't actually too lucky. This is Fukushima where the nuclear meltdown happened after the 2011 earthquake. So, when you think of ""luck island"" this is where you should think." The readings are the readings you learned with the kanji. If one thing is lucky, it's probably that.

example_sentences.japanese: このバンドのボーカルは、福島の出身です。
example_sentences.english: This band's vocalist is from Fukushima.

example_sentences.japanese: 福島の子どもたちがかいた絵の中の、この銀色の星空を見て下さい。
example_sentences.english: Look at the silver, starry sky in this drawing from a kid in Fukushima.

example_sentences.japanese: 福島問題に関するメールは、全て私をCCに入れてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Please CC me on all emails concerning the problems of Fukushima.

notes: "The signpost you have your eye on is your goal and target. Just imagine looking at this signpost in the distance. You know you have to get to it from where you are. That is the goal of your hike and journey." "You've had the on'yomi reading of 目 with 目次 way back in level 6. For this vocab, you're trying to get to your goal, that signpost in the distance. As you're trekking towards it there are people standing to the side mocking you, telling you you'll never make it to your goal. Imagine this happening."

example_sentences.japanese: 川村さんの人生の目標はなんですか。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Kawamura, what is your life's goal?

example_sentences.japanese: 五十メートル先の目標に向かって矢を放ちました。
example_sentences.english: I fired an arrow toward the target 50m ahead of me.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの目標について、もう少し具体的に話をして頂けませんか？
example_sentences.english: Could you be a little more specific about Tofugu’s goals, please?

notes: "A woman who is also a god is a goddess." "The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You haven't learned this reading for 女 yet so here's a mnemonic to help you:This goddess has the most beautiful 目 (め) you've ever seen. You can't stop staring into them. This must be how people know they've met a god."

example_sentences.japanese: この女神の人形の前がみを少し短くしてください。
example_sentences.english: Can you cut this goddess doll's bangs kinda short?

example_sentences.japanese: あの女神の身勝手さには、開いた口がふさがらなかったね。
example_sentences.english: My jaw dropped from the female deity's selfish attitude.

example_sentences.japanese: 女神のように美しい女声に出会った。
example_sentences.english: I came across a beautiful woman’s voice that sounded like a goddess’.

english: "Heartfelt Desire, Heartfelt Wish, Prayer, Heart's Desire"
notes: "The thing your heart requests is what your heart wants. This is your heartfelt desire." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンの心願には心が打たれますね。
example_sentences.english: We are touched by Salmon's prayer.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のハリケーンのひがいが少なくてすむようにというのがわたしの心願です。
example_sentences.english: My heartfelt wish is that the damage caused by the hurricane is less this time.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はその神社で心願成就の御札を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a charm at the shrine to help fulfill my heart’s desires.

notes: "The lodge you're staying in has a topic around it. Think of it as a theme. This theme is doing your homework. So yeah, you just went to a nice lodge for vacation only to have to do homework everywhere." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ななめから見てるから、宿題の答えが見えづらいんだよね。
example_sentences.english: It's hard to see the answers to your homework because I'm looking at it from an angle.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のわたしの宿題、ちょっと見てもらえないかな？
example_sentences.english: Can you take a quick look at my homework from today, please?

example_sentences.japanese: 「でも、ママ！僕…」「つべこべ言わないの。さあ、自分の部屋へ行って、宿題をしなさい。」
example_sentences.english: """But, Mom! I..."" ""No buts. Now go to your room and do your homework."""

english: Humanity, Human Feelings, Empathy, Kindness, Sympathy
notes: "The person (people) feelings are human feelings. That is what humanity is all about." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 人情のあたたかさに生かされています。
example_sentences.english: I survive on the warmth of humanity.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ様は人情味にあふれているすばらしいお方ですが、ビエト様はひとかけらの人情もないごく悪ヤクザです。
example_sentences.english: Koichi-sama is such a wonderful person with deep empathy, but Viet is such a devilish yakuza with not one atom of humanity.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達はTofuguの毎日のブログ記事を通して、日本人の生き方や人情を描き出すことを目指しています。
example_sentences.english: Our goal with the daily Tofugu articles is to depict human nature, emotions, and the everyday lives of Japanese individuals.

notes:
The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, presumably because it's normally attached onto other numbers to signify how many hundred millions of ____ there are.

"Something that is in the interior of something else is inside of it, deep, and far back / in the back. Just imagine something interior to something else, it's probably in the back." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: このおく歯までしっかりとどく歯ブラシで、今年は五億円を売り上げました。
example_sentences.english: We sold five hundred million yen worth of this reach toothbrush this year.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに小さかった子がこんなに大きくなって、今や毎年三億ドルをかせぐ大物になっているなんて、本当にしんじられないよ。
example_sentences.english: I really can't believe that little kid has gotten so big and now earns three hundred million dollars every year.

example_sentences.japanese: 出張の領収書は全部とっておいてください。経費は二億円までなら後で精算されますので。
example_sentences.english: Please keep all the receipts from your business trip. You will be reimbursed for your business expenses later, as long as they’re under two hundred million yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 奥にもっと小さいサイズのものも置いてますよ。
example_sentences.english: We have ones in smaller sizes in the back.

notes: "A drawing of an image is an image. Back in the day images were usually drawn. This is also portrait or picture, too." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 勝手にわたしの画像を使わないでくださいよ！
example_sentences.english: Don't use my picture without my permission!

example_sentences.japanese: けいさつにコウイチの暗殺事けんにかんするしょうこ画像をてい出しました。
example_sentences.english: I submitted images as evidence to the police regarding Koichi's assassination case.

example_sentences.japanese: 残念。この画像はちょっとボケてるので使えないよ。
example_sentences.english: What a shame. This picture is a little out of focus so you can’t use it.

english: Japanese Inn, Japanese Hotel, Inn, Ryokan, Japanese Style Inn, Japanese Style Hotel
notes: "A public building for taking trips is a place you stay when you are taking a trip. Back in the day that would just be an inn or something. Now, this specifies that the inn is a Japanese inn or Japanese hotel. A lot of people even just call it by its Japanese name: ryokan." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に旅行に行ったら旅館にとまってみたいです。
example_sentences.english: When I travel to Japan, I would like to stay at a Japanese-style hotel.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月日本に旅行に行くんだけど、旅館とホテルとどっちにとまった方がいいと思う？
example_sentences.english: I'm traveling to Japan next month. Where do you think I should stay: a Japanese-style inn or a hotel?

example_sentences.japanese: 「なんでこの旅館、こんなにゴキブリが出るの？」「最近雨ばっかり降ってるからじゃない？」
example_sentences.english: """Why are there so many cockroaches in this Japanese inn?"" ""I think it’s because of all the rain we’ve been getting."""

notes: "Wind of the Gods. These are divine winds. More popularly, this is a word known as Kamikaze, which became known because of the kamikaze pilots during WWII. This was used before WWII, though, when the entire Mongol fleet was destroyed by a storm, preventing an invasion of Japan. How lucky." "The readings are kun'yomi readings for both, probably because this is two words put together into one. You know the reading of 風 from previous levels, hopefully. Now all you need to do is apply your knowledge of the word 神 to be able to read the rest."

example_sentences.japanese: この神社には神風がふいています。
example_sentences.english: Divine winds blow on this shrine.

example_sentences.japanese: 第二次世界大戦の末期には日本ぐんは神風とっこうたいを使ってアメリカぐんをこうげきしました。
example_sentences.english: At the end of WWII, the Japanese army used the kamikaze corps to attack the American army.

example_sentences.japanese: 五年前、神風が吹き、コウイチはビエトの軍隊を海岸から後退させた。
example_sentences.english: Five years ago, Koichi drove Viet’s troops back from his shores where they were swallowed up by a divine wind.

english: Little Finger, Pinky Finger, Pinky, Little Toe, Pinky Toe
notes: "The small finger is your little finger or pinky finger. Makes sense, but it's also used for the pinky on your feet. You know, your pinky toe." This word uses the kun'yomi readings from both kanji, probably because it includes body parts. You know them both already, so now you know this too!

example_sentences.japanese: なんでグラスで飲み物を飲む時に小指を立てるの？
example_sentences.english: Why do you extend your pinky when you drink from a glass?

example_sentences.japanese: いってぇー、そこのタンスの角に右足の小指ぶつけた。
example_sentences.english: Ouch! I just hit my right pinky toe on the corner of the dresser.

example_sentences.japanese: またシュートミスっちまったぜ。突き指してる小指のせいで今日はまじでダメだわ。
example_sentences.english: That’s another air ball. I’m doing badly today because of this jammed pinky finger.

notes: "A lodge is a form of lodging. It is also considered to be an inn or hotel." "Yah do (やど) what you must to get lodgings for the night. Whether that's an inn or hotel or whatever. Yah do what you gotta do."

example_sentences.japanese: 十年前にそこをおとずれた時には、こんな宿は全くありませんでした。
example_sentences.english: When I went there ten years ago, there weren't any lodgings like this at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿がまだ決まってないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: We still haven’t decided on a hotel yet.

example_sentences.japanese: この宿は歴史的にも有名で、宿泊客だけでなく見物客も訪れる。
example_sentences.english: This inn is historically famous as well, so not only do inn guests visit but sightseers do as well.

notes: "One of the meanings of 本 is main (which is what we're using here). The main public building is the main building." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 本館には、ようじ教室の部屋がへいせつされています。
example_sentences.english: The main building has a classroom for pre-school children.

example_sentences.japanese: 本館のれきしをゼロから教える本を作ります。
example_sentences.english: We are going to make a book that teaches the history of the main building from scratch.

example_sentences.japanese: あの百貨店の本館で働いている店員は、別館で働いている人たちに比べて、なんか働かされてるって感じだった。愛想がやけに悪いっていうかさ。
example_sentences.english: Lots of the people working in the main building of the department store act like someone is forcing them to work, compared to those working at the annex. They have awfully bad attitudes.

english: Middle Finger, Second Finger, Middle Toe
notes: "The middle finger is the middle finger, of course! And because we don't see the difference, it's your middle toe too. Stick that up the next time someone makes you mad." This word uses the kun'yomi readings from both kanji, probably because it includes body parts. You know them both already, so now you know this too!

example_sentences.japanese: の良犬に中指をかまれました。
example_sentences.english: A stray dog bit my second finger.

example_sentences.japanese: 右手の中指に出来たタコが、かなりかたくなってきてます。
example_sentences.english: My callus on the middle finger on my right hand is getting pretty hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 中指を立てるんじゃない！
example_sentences.english: Don’t stick out your middle finger!

notes: "One hundred million is one hundred million. That's a lot of zeros." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは東京に一億円のマンションを持っています。
example_sentences.english: Koichi has a one hundred million yen condo in Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本という小さな島国に一億もの人が住んでいることがしんじられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't believe that Japan, a tiny island country, has one hundred million people living on it.

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじで一億ドル当たったけど、私は既に兆万長者なので全部慈善活動に寄付したよ。
example_sentences.english: I won a hundred million dollars in the lottery, but I donated it all to charity because I’m a trillionaire.

notes: "One hundred million yen! So rich! You have one hundred million yen!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 一億円とか大きな注文は入ってないけど、コンスタントに注文はあるよ。
example_sentences.english: We don't get big orders of like one hundred million yen, but we do get steady orders.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグがわたしに一億円をめぐんでくれることが決定したというお知らせを受けとりました。
example_sentences.english: I received a notification saying Tofugu had decided to donate one hundred million yen to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 「さっき一億円が入ったスーツケースを無くしちゃったんだけど。」「えぇっ！見つかるといいね。」
example_sentences.english: """I just lost a suitcase that had one hundred million yen in it.” ""What! I hope you find it."""

english: PE Class, PE, Physical Education, Gym Class
notes: "Remember how 教育 means ""education?"" Well, the 育 here is referring to the education word, but this time it's a body education. What do you call the body education at school? Physical education or PE." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学校の時、体育のマラソンが大きらいでした。
example_sentences.english: I hated that time in elementary school when we had to do long-distance running in gym.

example_sentences.japanese: 次の体育のじゅ業の前に、つめを切ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Before the next PE class, please clip your fingernails.

example_sentences.japanese: 「体育の日に、一緒にバレーボールしない？」「ああ、確か祝日だったよね。十月十日とかだっけ？」「そうそう。祝日。でも、もう十月十日じゃないよ。ハッピー・マンデー制度ができてから、十月の第二月曜日になったんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you want to play volleyball with us on Physical Education Day?"" ""Oh, it’s a national holiday, right? Isn’t it October 10th or something?"" ""Yes, it’s a holiday, but is not October 10th anymore. Now it’s the second Monday of October because of the Happy Monday system."""

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the kanji as well! You are so happy that you could write a poem all about this...The vocab readingIs the same as the kanjiCrabigator loveHow was that?

example_sentences.japanese: 詩が大好きで、毎日詩を読んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I like poems a lot, so I read them every day.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの心のやみを詩で表げんしてみたんだけど、ちょっと読んでみてくれない？
example_sentences.english: I expressed the darkness of my mind in a poem. Can you take a look?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の宿題は、日本語で詩を書くことです。
example_sentences.english: Today’s homework is to write a poem in Japanese.

notes: "A person who does poems is a poet." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンは今世紀を代表する詩人です。
example_sentences.english: Salmon is a poet who represents the current century.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの友人に詩人が一人いるんですが、かれの家の中はかべ中詩でおおわれているんです。
example_sentences.english: One of my friends is a poet, and poems take up space all over the walls in his house.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は詩人で、暗喩を使うことが好きなのかもしれないけど、もっと分かりやすく話さないと相手はわからないよ。
example_sentences.english: Even though you’re a poet and you like using metaphors, you have to speak clearer or people won’t understand you.

english: Pro Athlete, Sports Player, Professional Athlete
notes: "This is a strange one, but in one way it makes sense. Just make sure you're thinking of 手 as the word for ""person,"" kind of like 運転手 or something along those lines. If you do that, you can say ""the person that you choose."" One situation in which you'd choose a person to do something is in sports. That's why this is a pro athlete or sports player." "The reading for 選 is what you'd expect. 手 is the on'yomi reading as it is every once in a while, especially when it has to do with representing a person, so you'll have to remember that. I think you've seen 手 using this reading enough to be able to remember it, though."

example_sentences.japanese: あのハンサムな選手はだれですか。
example_sentences.english: Who is that handsome pro athlete?

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、日本人のプロ野球選手がメジャーリーグでもプレイするすがたがよく見られます。
example_sentences.english: These days, we can often see Japanese professional baseball players play in the major leagues.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは素晴らしい剣道の選手です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is magnificent pro kendo player.

notes:
The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You put on the ring you found, hoping it will be the one ring to rule them all (invisibility!). Instead, it turns out it's a special Walken ring, made out of Christopher Walken's bones. It talks up to you, telling you how he kept this ring in his (*ahem*) butt during the war so he could get it to you. First of all, why is this ring talking? Second, why is it talking like Walken. Third, eww, gross, it was in his anus."

"The kanji refers to a bundle, but this refers to a counter for bundles. Put this on a number, and you have ""1 bundle"" or ""2 bundles"" or even three, oh my!" "Saying ""1 bundle"" and ""2 bundle"" takes too long, so you decide to call these bundles what they look like: わ for walrus (わ)!"

example_sentences.japanese: 早くこの輪投げの輪をなげてくださいよ！
example_sentences.english: Please throw this Quoits ring quickly!

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーに行くと、友だちの輪が広がります。
example_sentences.english: If I go to parties, my circle of friends expands.

example_sentences.japanese: うわっ！コウイチ、なんで金の輪っかのイヤリングなんて付けてるの？
example_sentences.english: Ew! Why are you wearing gold hoop earrings, Koichi?

example_sentences.japanese: わっ！ほうれん草一把で九十八円だって。
example_sentences.english: Wow! A bunch of spinach is only ninety-eight yen!

notes: "The new lodge area is Shinjuku, a popular district in Tokyo. Perhaps there are many places to stay in Shinjuku. Either way, you should visit, it's fun! It will help if you've heard of Shinjuku before, too. Do some research about Shinjuku if you've never heard of it." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji.
