If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just be careful of the しゅく changing to じゅく. Once again, will help if you've heard of Shinjuku."

example_sentences.japanese: この新宿のホテルのシャワーは、水かぬるま湯しか出ない。
example_sentences.english: This Shinjuku hotel's shower only has cold or lukewarm water.

example_sentences.japanese: 新宿は毎年、わたしの行ってみたい場所ランキングの中で最下位です。
example_sentences.english: Shinjuku is always dead last on my personal list of places I want to visit each year.

example_sentences.japanese: 新宿二丁目は今はゲイタウンとして知られていますが、昔は危険な香りのする赤線地区でした。
example_sentences.english: Shinjuku 2-chome is now known as a gay town but it used to be a sketchy red light district.

english: Station Master, Stationmaster, Train Station Master, Train Stationmaster
notes: "This word uses 長 in the same way as 社長, where it means something like ""boss"" or ""manager."" So, this 長 is the boss of the station, right? What do you call someone like that? You call them the stationmaster (that is, unless you want to be thrown to the trains)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: すきなアイドルが一日駅長にえらばれました。
example_sentences.english: My favorite idol was selected to be a one-day train station master.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅長と川田さんは親友だからこっそりと切ぷ代をわり引してもらっているんだって。
example_sentences.english: Because the stationmaster and Mr. Kawada are best friends, I heard that he secretly gets discount on fares.

example_sentences.japanese: うわっ！あの駅長、今電車に唾はかなかったか？お前、見たか？
example_sentences.english: Oh my God! Did the station master just spit on the train? Did you see that?

notes: "A power samurai isn't a samurai at all. A Samurai's all about precision, after all. So, imagine someone that's a huge mass of muscle (and fat). This Japanese warrior is all about power... ramming into people as hard as they can to knock them over. This person is a sumo wrestler." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 力士のサインがほしいなら両国に行ってみたら？
example_sentences.english: If you want a sumo wrestler's autograph, why don't you go to Ryogoku?

example_sentences.japanese: 初デートで、力士はずっと前がみをなでつけてたんだよね。
example_sentences.english: The sumo wrestler kept patting down his bangs on our first date.

example_sentences.japanese: お集まりの皆さん、本日は度重なる力士の不祥事に関する会議にご出席いただき有難うございます。
example_sentences.english: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for attending today’s conference regarding the repeated misconduct of our sumo wrestlers.

notes: "Your eating containers can be a lot of things. For a more general meaning, this can be your tableware. But, more specifically it can also mean your eating utensils or your utensils. Basically, it's stuff you use to eat your food." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just be sure to note the shortened しょく."

example_sentences.japanese: この食器をテーブルの上にならべてくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Can you arrange these utensils on the table, please?

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが池に落としたのはこの金の食器ですか、それともこの銀の食器ですか。
example_sentences.english: Which utensils did you drop in the pond, the gold ones or the silver ones?

example_sentences.japanese: 「どうして、食器が一式多いの？」「お前がフグを招待したからだろ。」「あぁ、そっか。 ごめんなさい。 フグは来ないのよ。 数日前に元カノが街に遊びにやってきて、よりを戻したから、サンクスギビングは彼女と一緒に過ごすんだって。」
example_sentences.english: """How come we have one extra place setting?"" ""Because you invited Fugu."" ""Oh, right. Sorry, but Fugu’s not coming anymore. His ex-girlfriend came to town the other day and they got back together, so he’s spending Thanksgiving with her."""

notes: "The five feelings that you have are what? Sight, sound, taste, touch, and smell (don't count the sixth one where you see dead people). These are the five senses that you probably have." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 五感のうちどれか一つを失ってしまうとしたら、どれを選びますか？また、その理由も教えてください。
example_sentences.english: If you had to lose one of your five senses, which one would you give up and why?

example_sentences.japanese: さく夜のゆめで、今までにかいだことのないにおいを感じました。五感ってねている間も働いているんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: In my dream last night, there was a smell I didn't notice before... do all five senses work in dreams?

example_sentences.japanese: 五感に関する日本語の単語と動詞の他に、第六感に関する語彙も学習してください。
example_sentences.english: Please study Japanese words and verbs related to the five senses, as well as some Japanese vocabulary related to the sixth sense.

notes: "The concept you think about is your thoughts. It is your ideas." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの思想にはついていけません。
example_sentences.english: I can't follow Koichi's thoughts.

example_sentences.japanese: きのう、ニュースを見ていたら、ビエトが思想犯としてたいほされたニュースが出て本当にびっくりしたよ。
example_sentences.english: When I was watching the news yesterday, I was so shocked that it said Viet was arrested for thoughtcrimes.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはトーフグの創始者であり、近代日本を代表する啓蒙思想家である。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is the founder of Tofugu and one of the great modern Japanese thinkers.

notes: "Your parent finger is your thumb! It's bigger than your other fingers, so that means it's in charge too! This goes for the fingers on your feet too, I mean, your toes. So the parent toe is your big toe." This word uses the kun'yomi readings from both kanji, probably because it includes body parts. You know them both already, so now you know this too!

example_sentences.japanese: 親指を放してくれ！
example_sentences.english: Let go of my thumb!

example_sentences.japanese: きんちょうすると、親指がふるえます。
example_sentences.english: When I'm nervous, my thumbs shake.

example_sentences.japanese: 親指にタコができました。
example_sentences.english: I’ve got a callus on my thumb.

notes: "The car rings are what part of your car? What's round and ringy? Those are your tires. So, a car ring is a tire." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: バイクの車輪が外れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: My motorcycle's tire came off.

example_sentences.japanese: 暗殺のきょうきには車輪が使われたそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that a car wheel was used in the assassination.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、ちょっと自転車貸してもらえないかな？今、車輪を取り替えてもらっているので、自分のが無いんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Could I borrow your bike today? I don’t have mine right now because I’m having a tire replaced.

english: Train Station Employee, Train Station Staff, Train Station Attendant, Station Attendant, Station Employee
notes: "A train station member is someone who works at the train station. They are a train station employee. Feel free to ask them if you need help knowing which direction to train in." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その駅員の黒目は普通の人よりも大きいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that train station attendant's irises are larger than most people's.

example_sentences.japanese: この駅の駅員は、みんなお昼に一杯二百八十円のかけそばを食べる。
example_sentences.english: All the station employees here eat bowls of 280 yen kake soba for lunch.

example_sentences.japanese: あの駅員、こう見えてすっごくお金持ちなのよ。
example_sentences.english: You couldn’t tell from looking at him, but that station attendant is a really rich guy.

notes: "Your ability power is what you can do. This is your ability. It is also your capability." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしには、グーグルをとてもこうりつてきに使う能力があります。
example_sentences.english: I have the ability to use Google very efficiently.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニの例文作りには、へんな文章をかく能力が求められる。
example_sentences.english: The ability to write weird sentences is required to create WaniKani example sentences.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は英語のネイティブスピーカーだが、日本語でテレパシーをする能力がある。
example_sentences.english: I’m a native English speaker, but my telepathic abilities are in Japanese.

notes: "You've probably seen the words 知る and 合う by now. This is someone you ""know"" because you had the chance to ""meet"" them, but that's pretty much it. You don't really know them, you just met them a couple times so you know who they are. This person is an acquaintance." "The readings are that of 知る and 合う. So long as you know those words, you should be able to read this one too."

example_sentences.japanese: 知り合いにたのんで、トーフグのコウイチからサインをもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I asked an acquaintance if they could get me Koichi’s autograph from Tofugu.

example_sentences.japanese: 今知り合いにれんあい相だんしてるから、カラオケには行けないかも。ごめんね！
example_sentences.english: I’m consulting my acquaintance about my relationship with my boyfriend right now, so I probably won’t be able to join the karaoke party. Sorry!

example_sentences.japanese: ここだけの話なんだけど、上司が知り合いの人妻と浮気しているのよね。
example_sentences.english: Don’t tell a soul but my boss is having an affair with a married woman who is an acquaintance of mine.

notes: "The acting arts are the greatest arts of all. Back in the day they were the only arts, which is why the art of acting is just art itself. In fact, it's THE arts." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: おか本太ろうは、「芸術はばく発だ」って言ってたけど、あれってどういう意味？
example_sentences.english: "Taro Okamoto said, ""Art is an explosion,"" but what the heck does that mean?"

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの妹は、芸大でタイ芸術を学んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister is learning Thai art at a university of fine arts.

example_sentences.japanese: アヤは、芸術と音楽への愛をもっと多くの人に伝えるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Aya should share her love of art and music to more people.

notes: "A bad example is a bad example and is something you don't want." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を学ぶ時には、いい例だけでなく、悪例を学ぶことも必要です。
example_sentences.english: When learning Japanese, it is necessary to learn from good examples as well as bad examples.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは悪例のかたまりだ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is a cluster of bad examples.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の両親は、今後の寝る時間に悪例を残すことになるからって、絶対に夜更かしさせてくれないんだ。
example_sentences.english: My parents never let me stay up late because they believed it would set a bad precedent for future bedtimes.

notes: "This meaning is a little weird, but I'm going to try my best to help you remember. Every person has to participate in eating carrots. I don't care if you don't like them, if you don't eat at least one carrot in your life you'll die. So if you're a person you better participate in the eating of at least a single carrot." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 参 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You're craving a carrot, but you can't seem to find any. You look in your fridge, in your garden, and even in the trash. Finally you give up your carrot search and sit down when... ouch! The carrot was in your jeans (じん) the whole time!"

example_sentences.japanese: この人参スープには失望しました。
example_sentences.english: I was disappointed with this carrot soup.

example_sentences.japanese: 酒好きの王様に、人参リキュールをプレゼントしたが、よろこばれなかった。
example_sentences.english: I gifted some carrot liqueur to the King, who loves alcohol, but he didn't like it.

example_sentences.japanese: お願いします。何でも食べるので、人参だけは勘弁してください。
example_sentences.english: Please. I'll eat anything else, just not the carrot. Please.

notes: "What suits a location? Or, another way to think about it, what happens when everything fits for that location? You have yourself a case or circumstance that happens because of the location and its suitability." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji, but you know them both now, so you should be able to read this too!

example_sentences.japanese: タオルや石けん、おかし、おそばなどをもっていく場合が多いです。
example_sentences.english: In many circumstances, we take things like towels, soap, snacks, or noodles.

example_sentences.japanese: 出来るかぎり早くEメールにへんしんできるよう努めておりますが、すぐにへんしんできない場合もありますのでごりゅういください。
example_sentences.english: We try our best to respond your emails as soon as possible, but please note that we may not be able to respond immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: その場合には警察を呼んだ方がいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: In this case, I think it would be good to call the police.

notes: "Your person status is where you, yourself, are a person. This is more than skin deep, though, this is your status after all. This is your character and personality. What's the status of your character? Good? Bad? Getting there?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトの人格を疑います！
example_sentences.english: I question Viet's character!

example_sentences.japanese: フグってとっても温こうな人格の持ち主だね。
example_sentences.english: Fugu has a very gentle personality, doesn't he?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは人格者です。毎週日曜日に孤児院に出向いて、ベーコンを寄付しているのです。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is a person of integrity. Every Sunday he goes to the orphanage and donates bacon.

notes: "A person who does humorous acting is a comedian. You might think that this would be actor, but it's usually a comedian. Just think of them like more of a performer!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その芸人は、まるでねむれる森の美女のようにねむっています。
example_sentences.english: That comedian is sleeping like sleeping beauty.

example_sentences.japanese: あの芸人、いつもおしい所まで行くんだけど、ゆう勝はできないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: That comedian always almost makes it to the top, but never wins.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は根っからの芸人かもしれない。
example_sentences.english: He might be a natural-born performer.

notes: "You have to find the right tool to suit your condition. If you have a health condition, the tool is a pill, or exercise, or real life friends. But it always depends on the condition you're in." "This word consists of the on'yomi reading for 具 and the kun'yomi reading for 合. You've learned them both, so you should be able to read this word too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 母の具合があまりよくないんです。
example_sentences.english: My mother’s condition isn’t very good.

example_sentences.japanese: なんかめっちゃ具合わるそうだけど、大じょうぶ?
example_sentences.english: You don't look great at all. Are you okay?

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと昨日から具合が良くなくて。
example_sentences.english: I was a little under the weather yesterday.

notes: "If you follow the circumference of a period of time, you end up back at the beginning and it makes a full cycle. Events in history always repeat, right?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ふり子の周期についてのお返事、お待ちいたしております。
example_sentences.english: I await your response regarding the cycle of a pendulum.

example_sentences.japanese: 実はさぁ、クリステンにきいてもらいたくて、「月の周期」っていう曲を練習してるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: "Actually, I've been practicing a song called ""The Moon Cycle"" because I wanted to play it for you, Kristen."

example_sentences.japanese: 東北の天気は短い周期で変わる。
example_sentences.english: Tohoku’s weather changes in short cycles.

notes: "Someone with bad energy is someone who has evil intent. Hopefully you don't have too much 悪気." "The reading itself has a lot of 悪気 with all the exceptions it has. The 悪 part is read like 悪い. Then, 気 is rendaku'd. What an evil reading. Just think ""what's the most evil reading I can come up with?"" when you see this word. Then you should hopefully be able to read it."

example_sentences.japanese: 悪気がないのは知ってるけど、そういうことを言われるとこっちもきずつくんだよ？
example_sentences.english: I know you don't have any evil intent, but please understand that we could get hurt if you say something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪気があってしたわけじゃないんですが、けっかてきにそういう風に感じさせてしまう事になって本当にごめんなさい。
example_sentences.english: I didn't do it out of malice, but I'm really sorry that I made you feel that way.

example_sentences.japanese: ところで、そもそも、何の経験もなくて、どうやってその職を得たの？あ、悪気は無いよ。
example_sentences.english: By the way, how did you get the job without any experience in the first place? No offense, of course.

english: Example Sentence, Model Sentence, Sample Sentence
notes: "Example writing is a piece of writing that is an example for maybe a word or a kanji or something like that. This is an example sentence." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 例文という語いを使ったいい例文が思いつきません。
example_sentences.english: "I can't come up with a good sample sentence that uses the word ""sample sentence."""

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニの例文の中で一番好きな文章を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please let us know which WaniKani example sentence is your favorite.

example_sentences.japanese: 何故だか分からないんだけど、僕の先生は例文を作る時にいつも僕の名前を使うんだよね。
example_sentences.english: For some reason my teacher always uses my name when she makes model sentences.

notes: "You'd think that someone who does acting is an actor or something... but think about the reading for this kanji. What is it? Do you recognize the word? It's geisha." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの芸者とわたしの間には、何一つ共通点がありません。
example_sentences.english: That geisha and I have nothing in common.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に旅行に行ったらぜひ芸者のかっ好をして京都の町を練り歩いてみたいです。
example_sentences.english: When I travel to Japan, I would certainly like to dress like a geisha and parade around Kyoto.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ、昨日は私達が芸者遊びをしている間、フグと私の子どもを見ててくれてありがとう。再度お礼が言いたくて。
example_sentences.english: Koichi, I just wanted to say thank you again for taking care of Fugu and my kid yesterday while we were drinking with geisha.

notes: "You have to pay a fee for the material you use to make food. Those are the ingredients you're paying for! Imagine making a list of all of the materials you need to make a stew, then making sure you have enough to pay the fees, so you'll have all the ingredients you need to make it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: かれが材料調たつのたん当者です。
example_sentences.english: He's the person in charge of material prep.

example_sentences.japanese: 材料の二倍の水を入れてください。
example_sentences.english: Please pour two parts water for one part of the ingredient.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の好きな食べ物は饂飩ですが、麺の材料は、小麦粉と塩と水だけなんですよ。
example_sentences.english: My favorite food is udon noodles and the ingredients are just wheat flour, salt, and water.

notes: "One example is just an instance of what you're describing. Just one example." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: これはほんの一例にすぎません。
example_sentences.english: This is just one example.

example_sentences.japanese: 一例としては、ごはんやじゃがいもを食べるりょうをへらしたからといって、やせられるわけではないということがあげられます。
example_sentences.english: As an example, you can't get skinnier by simply eating less rice and potatoes.

example_sentences.japanese: 秘書としてサーモンを迎え入れた後で、彼女が職場で突然感情を爆発させる性格であることが判明したのです。例えば、自分のデスクの電話を引き抜いて、粉々にブチ壊しちゃったりとか、まあ、ほんの一例を挙げればそんな感じです。
example_sentences.english: After I hired Salmon as secretary, I found out that she was the type of person who has sudden emotional outbursts in the office. For example, she ripped the telephone from her desk and smashed it to pieces, just to name one small incident.

notes: "The things you wear are your clothes. Oh, and Japanese clothes count too. We're talking kimonos. Way back when, these could just be called clothes because it's all people really wore, but nowadays we know they're specific to the stereotypical kimono you think of when you think ""Japan.""" "The reading is a bit strange using kun'yomi readings. Luckily, we taught you these already, so go put on that kimono of yours and relax at the 温泉 for a bit."

example_sentences.japanese: カオリさんは、着物のどこがすきですか？
example_sentences.english: What do you like about kimono, Kaori?

example_sentences.japanese: お着物が汚れていますよ。
example_sentences.english: Your clothes got a bit dirty.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親に、既婚女性か未婚女性かで着物の種類が異なると教えてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: My mom told me that married women and unmarried women wear different kimonos.

notes: "Lumber trees are what you use to make lumber and timber." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: なんで材木にクイックルワイパーをかけてるの？
example_sentences.english: Why are you mopping that wood with a Quickle wiper?

example_sentences.japanese: あの材木おき場に夜の八時に行くと、神様に会えるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that if you go to the lumber yard at 8 p.m. you'll be able to meet God.

example_sentences.japanese: 材木が来たらすぐに犬小屋作りに取り掛からないとな。
example_sentences.english: We should get started building the doghouse as soon as the lumber gets here.

notes: "For some reason the status of your gender is what dictates your personality. Think of it this way: What kind of personality does someone of the female gender usually have? What about the personality of a male gender? Their personality status always seems to fit into gender roles, which is why the status of the gender dictates the personality. Make sense?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは性格はおっとりとしているが、頭の回転が速いだけに、よくしたが回る。
example_sentences.english: Koichi has a level-headed personality, but he is quick-witted and talks a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: かれ、性格はそんなに悪くないんだけど、一しょにいても会話が広がらないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: His personality isn't that bad, but it's hard to have deeper conversations.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の旦那さんの性格はのんびり屋で、忘れっぽくて、優柔不断です。彼のことは大好きだけど、たまにイラッとくるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: My husband is really easy going, but forgetful and indecisive. I love him but sometimes it drives me nuts.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, so no need to think too hard.

example_sentences.japanese: その松買うのに、二十分間も待ったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I bought that pine tree and yet I had to wait twenty minutes to get it.

example_sentences.japanese: 松の木から松ぼっくりが落ちてきてわたしの頭に当たった。
example_sentences.english: A pine cone fell off a pine tree and hit my head.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの小学校では、クラスを一組、二組、とは分けずに、松組、竹組で分けていました。
example_sentences.english: "In my elementary school, classrooms were labeled ""pine class"" and ""bamboo class"" rather than ""1st class,"" ""2nd class,"" and so on."

notes: "The leaves of a pine are not really leaves, they're more like needles, thus making this word pine needle." "If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The 葉 gets rendaku'd to ば though, so watch out for that."

example_sentences.japanese: かんそうした松葉が一本私の部屋のゆかに落ちていました。
example_sentences.english: One dried pine needle was laying on the floor of my room.

example_sentences.japanese: その松葉は、クルクルと十回転した後、水たまりへ落ちました。
example_sentences.english: The pine needle spun ten times and fell into a puddle.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度の昇給が得られれば、ようやく両親に松葉ガニを買ってやることができる。
example_sentences.english: Getting this raise will finally enable me to buy a Matsuba crab for my parents.

notes: "The stream go language. This is language that goes down the stream with everything else. Imagine this language being carried away quite quickly so everyone standing on the edge of the stream can grab some of this language. This thing streaming down it is a popular phrase. Yolo!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どの流行語が、今年の流行語大賞にえらばれると思う？
example_sentences.english: Which popular phrase do you think will be chosen for this year's buzzword of the year?

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年ほんとに色んな流行語が生まれるよね。
example_sentences.english: A lot of new catchphrases are born every year, huh?

example_sentences.japanese: ここ数年の間に、「ミーム」はインターネットでの流行語となりました。
example_sentences.english: "In the past few years, ""meme"" has become a popular word on the internet."

notes: "You know that 流行 refers to a ""trend."" So, a ""trend"" song is a popular song." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今時は「流行りの歌」って言うよね。「流行歌」っていうとなんかしょう和の歌よう曲って感じがする。
example_sentences.english: "We say ""pop song"" these days, so when I hear ""popular song,"" it reminds me of popular songs from the Showa period."

example_sentences.japanese: ツイッターでフォローして、最新の流行歌情ほうをチェックしてね。
example_sentences.english: Follow our Twitter for updates on the latest popular songs.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、流行歌ではないけど良い曲を見つけるのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like finding good music, but not necessarily popular songs.

notes: "The nature of reason is still reason." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を飲みすぎて、完全に理性を失ってしまっていました。
example_sentences.english: I had too much drink and I lost all sense of reason.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは、今時は、ヤクザもぼう力にたよるんじゃなく、理性にうったえなくっちゃダメだって言ってたよ。
example_sentences.english: Viet said that nowadays even yakuza have to appeal to intellect instead of resorting to violence.

example_sentences.japanese: ダメだと分かっていたが、理性を保てなかったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I understood it was hopeless, but I couldn’t hold on to reason.

english: School Festival, Culture Festival, Arts Festival
notes: "Remember how 文化 means ""culture?"" Well add festival to it and you end up with a culture festival! These happen all the time at Japanese schools, so sometimes they're called school festivals too." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned all of these readings already, good for you!

example_sentences.japanese: うちの学校の文化祭にもあそびに来てくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Please come visit my school’s culture festival!

example_sentences.japanese: 「文化祭の練習、何時にする？」「おれは一日中ひまだから、そっちの都合の良い時なら何時でもいいよ。」
example_sentences.english: """What time should we start the school festival rehearsal?"" ""I'm available all day long, so anytime that suits you best."""

example_sentences.japanese: 文化祭の管理諸経費は全体の約三十五パーセントになると見積っています。
example_sentences.english: We've assessed administrative and overhead fees at about 35 percent of the total culture festival costs.

notes: "The world of acting ability is the world of showbusiness. Save yourself some letters, honey, and call it showbiz." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 折角東京まで行ったのに、芸能界には入れなかった。
example_sentences.english: I went all the way to Tokyo, but I couldn't get in to the showbiz industry.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしのむすめは思いつきで物事を決めがちなんですが、今度は芸能界で働きたいって言い出してるんですよね。
example_sentences.english: My daughter tends to make decisions on the fly, and now she's saying that she wants to work in show business.

example_sentences.japanese: 芸能界のゴシップなんて全然興味ねーよ。どうでもいいっつーの。
example_sentences.english: I’m not interested in the gossip of the world of show business. I couldn’t care less.

notes: "Your skill and ability are kind of similar things. That's why this word means either or. Your skill ability is your skill and ability." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: カナエは、先月末にウェブデザイン技能検定に合格した。
example_sentences.english: Kanae passed the technical skill test for web design at the end of last month.

example_sentences.japanese: リーディング、ライティング、リスニング、スピーキングの四つの技能をバランスよく上たつさせるのはむずかしい。
example_sentences.english: It's difficult to improve the four abilities of reading, writing, listening, and speaking, so that they're balanced well.

example_sentences.japanese: 逃走するために、俺はCIA諜報員としての年月で習得した技能を駆使した。
example_sentences.english: To escape, I used the skills that I had acquired in my years as a CIA agent.

notes: "Your special skill is your specialty. So, what is your 特技?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの特技は、お湯をわかすことです。それ以外の特技は何一つありません。
example_sentences.english: My specialty is boiling water. I don't have a single skill outside of that.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の六人ぐらい後ろにならんでる青い服の男の子、高校の同級生なんだけど、なんとオナラでセーラームーンのテーマをかなでるという特技を持ってるのよ。
example_sentences.english: The guy in the blue shirt about six people behind me in the line was one of my classmates in high school and he has a specialty where he can play the Sailor Moon theme song with his farts.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの特技はお菓子作りです。お菓子作りが好きな理由は、みんなの嬉しそうな顔を見るのが好きだからだそうです。
example_sentences.english: Koichi’s specialty is making desserts. He said he likes making them because he likes seeing everyone’s happy faces.

notes: "Remember how 運動 means ""exercise?"" When you meet with a bunch of other people to exercise it's called Sports Day! This is a day at schools in Japan where everybody does physical stuff together! It's fun and also very tiring! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪天こうで、折角楽しみにしていた運動会が中止になってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The bad weather spoiled Sports Day, which we had really been looking forward to.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動会の日、晴れるといいですね。
example_sentences.english: I hope it’s sunny on the day of the sports festival.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動会の日の朝に、今日は都合が悪いから運動会を明日に変えることはできないかって聞いてきた親がいて、びっくりしたよ。
example_sentences.english: We were surprised that on the morning of Sports Day, there were parents asking if we could change it to tomorrow just because they couldn't make it that day.

notes: "She who has genius ability has quite the talent." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画に出えんしているはいゆうたちは、みんな才能があります。
example_sentences.english: The actors in this movie are all talented.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国語を勉強するのに才能がいると思いますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you think you need to be talented to study a foreign language?

example_sentences.japanese: 君はゴミをゴミ箱に投げ入れる才能があるね。
example_sentences.english: You have a talent for throwing garbage into trash bins.

notes: "What is a skill? It's something you can do, and do quite well. It is a technique that you can make happen with ease." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You do your technique on a bad guy, coming at you. You flip him over and knock him out. He was (わざ) a threat, but now he's not. You look closer at the bad guy. Turns out it's Woz, the Apple Co-founder. He was just trying to hand you an iPhone12, not grab your wrist. Whoops!"

example_sentences.japanese: これはまたきわどい技をマスターしたね！
example_sentences.english: You've mastered tricky art like that one, have you?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはニッカに新しい技を仕こんでいるんですか？
example_sentences.english: Is Koichi teaching Nikka a new trick?

example_sentences.japanese: 柔道では力より技のほうが大切であります。
example_sentences.english: In judo, technique is more important than strength.

notes: "You've seen that 旅行 is ""trip."" So who is someone who goes on trips? That is a tourist or traveler." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help if you know the reading of 旅行 already."

example_sentences.japanese: 最初、ぶあい想な旅行者だなぁと思ったんだけど、話をしてみると意外におも白い人だったのよね。
example_sentences.english: At first, I thought the traveler was unsociable, but when I tried talking to her, I discovered she was actually very interesting.

example_sentences.japanese: ふだんはこういった対おうはいたしませんが、旅行者でいらっしゃるということですので、今回は特別に対おうさせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: Normally we would not do this, but since you are a tourist, we'll comply with your request.

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、見て見て。あの旅行者の服装、全然年相応じゃないと思わない？
example_sentences.english: Hey, look, look. Don’t you think that tourist is wearing clothes that are completely unsuitable for her age?

notes:
"When you meet for cooperation, you're coming together to help each other. One form of this is when people form unions. They're all cooperating and coming together to help each other and themselves." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"The boundary separates worlds. It is a boundary." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が折角コツコツためたお金は、協会ひの支はらいに消えてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: All the money my son worked so hard to slowly save up was used to pay his union membership fees.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は協会の集まりがあるので、六時に起こしてください。
example_sentences.english: I have to attend an organization meeting tomorrow, so please wake me up at six.

example_sentences.japanese: こんにちは。僕はコウイチといいます。オレゴン州ポートランド市のポートランド剣道協会で、イベントマネージャーをしています。
example_sentences.english: Hello. My name is Koichi and I am the events manager for the Portland Kendo Association here in Portland, Oregon.

example_sentences.japanese: 母と私は、いつもお互いの個人的な境界線のようなものを気にしています。
example_sentences.english: My mom and I are always cautious of each other’s personal boundaries.

hiragana: わるくち, わるぐち, あっこう
english: Verbal Abuse, Saying Bad Things, Insult, Slander, Bad Mouth
notes: "Your bad mouth is saying bad things (as usual!). Everything that comes out of this bad mouth of yours is verbal abuse. One day someone's going to pop you in that bad mouth of yours." "The reading is the kun'yomi vocab readings for these two kanji, probably because this word is just two words put together into one (bad + mouth). Use your knowledge of the vocab words 悪い and 口 to learn the reading of this word.Okay, I lied. You can also do わるぐち if you want. Sorry to say such bad things before."

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは意地悪なえみをうかべながらコウイチに大声で悪口を言い始めた。
example_sentences.english: Viet started shouting verbal abuse at Koichi with a malicious grin.

example_sentences.japanese: 子どもの前では、おっとの悪口を言ったことがありません。
example_sentences.english: I've never bad mouthed my husband in front of my kids.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達がみんなで私の悪口を言っているのを聞いちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I heard that all of my friends were saying bad things about me.

notes: "Wood that is lumber is lumber wood." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ひまだったら、木材をはこぶのを手伝ってくれない？
example_sentences.english: If you have nothing to do, can you help me carry some wood?

example_sentences.japanese: 「木材」は、まだほとんど加工されていない原料としての木のことを指し、「材木」は、その木材を加工してすぐ使える状態に仕上げたものを指します。
example_sentences.english: """Mokuzai"" refers to raw wood material that is not yet processed, and ""zaimoku"" refers to wood that is a finished product and can be used immediately."

example_sentences.japanese: 二日なら時間を作れるよ。いつもの木材置き場で話さない？
example_sentences.english: I can make time on the second. Why don’t we meet up at the lumberyard and talk?

english: AD, Anno Domini, After Death, CE, Common Era
notes: "The origin is after the narrative. What narrative was this? It's THE narrative, to many. This is the narrative of Jesus. This was so important that they decided to start a new era after it, making this era after death* or AD.*Yes, I know it's not actually ""After Death"" but it's so commonly misconceived as such that I put it in there as the definition. You understand the meaning still, right? Anno Domini is also available as a definition too, so don't fret!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この原始人は、紀元後にようやくスランプをだっ出するまで、あせらずじっとたえていました。
example_sentences.english: This caveman just calmly waited until he could finally get out of his slump in Common Era.

example_sentences.japanese: 力ずくでネジをしめるとななめになりやすいってこと、紀元後になるまで知らなかったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I didn't know that the screw wouldn't go in straight if you do it forcefully until Anno Domini.

example_sentences.japanese: 紀元前五十年から紀元後二十年の間に作られたとされるこの地域の土器に、同じようなフグの模様が見られるんです。
example_sentences.english: Similar Fugu patterns can be seen on local earthenware made between 50 B.C. and 20 A.D.

notes: "A strange person is an eccentric. They are also an oddball." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの変人のクローゼット、見た？
example_sentences.english: Did you see what's in that weirdo's closet?

example_sentences.japanese: 変人的なふるまいをしつづける世界記ろくにちょう戦したが、おしくも世界記ろくにはあと十分足りなかった。
example_sentences.english: I challenged myself to set a new world record for acting like an oddball, but I was ten minutes shy.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの上司はちょっと変人ですが、すぐに馴染めると思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: Your boss is a little eccentric but I think you’re going to fit right in.

notes: "The director who is above you is your boss or superior." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その上司のコートは、とても丈夫な生地で出来ていました。
example_sentences.english: That boss' coat was made of very durable material.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの上司は、日本のれきしに大変きょう味があるようです。
example_sentences.english: It seems that my superior is very interested in Japanese history.

example_sentences.japanese: シャークがあなたのこと、名ばかりの上司だと言ってましたよ。
example_sentences.english: Shark said you are the boss in name only.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, so you can read this one!

example_sentences.japanese: あの岩のところまでどっちが先に着けるか競争しよう！
example_sentences.english: Let's race and see which one of us can make it to that boulder first.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグにはコウイチが岩みたいなかおをしている時は、話しかけないでそっとしておくという決まりがあります。
example_sentences.english: At Tofugu, there is a rule that people should leave Koichi alone when his face looks like a boulder.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、夢の中で大きな岩が頭上に落ちてくるところで、目が覚めた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi woke up as a huge boulder fell toward him in a dream.

notes: "The England country is where England is. This word can refer to Britain, the United Kingdom and England!Note that イギリス is more common for ""England"" - but, since this is a kanji learning website you should learn this word." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの頑固な英国首相をせっとくするのはとても大変だったでしょう？
example_sentences.english: It was very tough work persuading the stubborn British prime minister, wasn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年、大変な数の人たちが、ゴルフをしに英国をおとずれます。
example_sentences.english: A great number of people visit United Kingdom to golf every year.

example_sentences.japanese: 英国と米国は敵対関係にある。
example_sentences.english: The UK has an antagonistic relationship with the US.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You go up to Buddha. You want to rub his head for good luck, because that's what you hear is good to do. Right before you touch him, he backs off and says, ""Whoa! I'm hot, okay?"" (ほとけ). You touch him and it burns your hand clean off. Imagine saying ""hot, okay?"" in a strange accent to help you to remember."

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはヤクザをやめて、仏の道に入ることを決意しました。
example_sentences.english: Viet has decided to leave the Yakuza group and follow the teachings of Buddha.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、いつも仏のようにれいせいで、えんま大王のようにきびしい。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is always as cool as Buddha and as strict as Yama, the King of Hell.

example_sentences.japanese: 「知らぬが仏」や「仏の顔も三度まで」など、仏に関する諺はいくつかありますね。
example_sentences.english: "There are some proverbs related to Buddha like, ""what you don’t know can’t hurt you,"" and, ""the crushed worm will turn."""

notes: "The buddha teachings are what you have to learn when you're studying Buddhism." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that 仏 gets changed to ぶっ for this one."

example_sentences.japanese: 仏教とヒンドゥー教のちがいを正かくにせつ明できますか？
example_sentences.english: Can you explain the differences between Buddhism and Hinduism accurately?

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに信心深い人間じゃないんですが、一おう神道と仏教を信こうしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m not a deeply religious person, but I practice both Shintoism and Buddhism.

example_sentences.japanese: 仏教に伴って、お香は六世紀に日本に伝来しました。
example_sentences.english: Along with Buddhism, incense was brought to Japan in the 6th century.

notes: "The account of a generation... this covers a whole generation, and considering how long Japanese people live, this account totals a whole century." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今って何世紀だっけ？」「二十一世紀だよ。」
example_sentences.english: """What century is it right now?"" ""It's the 21st century."""

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは少なくとも一世紀は生きたいと思っている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi wants to live at least a century.

example_sentences.japanese: あいにく、その日のスケジュールは少しきついですね。今世紀最大の日本語学習祭り関連の会議がいくつか入っているんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m afraid my schedule is a little tight that day. I have several meetings related to a Japanese learning festival, which will be the largest one this century.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji!

example_sentences.japanese: 私のおじは、中央区の区役所で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My uncle works at the ward office of Chuo-ku.

example_sentences.english: You cannot park here because this is a no-parking district.

example_sentences.japanese: ここ最近、横浜の外国人居留区では、暴力行為がかつてないほど横行している。
example_sentences.english: Recently, the foreign quarter of Yokohama has suffered from an unprecedented level of violence.

notes: "English meeting and talking with each other. This is English Conversation. This is used a lot when talking about ""speaking in English"" for studying English and whatnot." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の兄は、英会話は上手だけど、計算は下手なんです。
example_sentences.english: My older brother is good at English conversations, but bad at calculations.

example_sentences.japanese: まさか。また英会話のテストに落ちちゃったよ。ショックすぎる。
example_sentences.english: Oh no, I can’t believe I failed another English conversation test. I’m so shocked.

example_sentences.japanese: 英会話の試験でミスをしたことで動揺してしまい、さらに別のミスを誘発することになってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I knew I made one mistake on the English conversation exam and I was so flustered that it ended up setting off another mistake.

notes: "This is seen on things like dictionaries. When you have an English and Japanese (style) dictionary, for example. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 英和ほんやくの仕事をしています。
example_sentences.english: I work as an English-Japanese translator.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい英和対やくの本が出ました。
example_sentences.english: A new English Japanese parallel translation book came out.

example_sentences.japanese: おっと、キャメロンが泣きそうだ！ちょっとあの英和辞典を探して来て、キャメロンに渡してあげてくれない？
example_sentences.english: Uh-oh, Cameron's about to cry! Can you go to find the English-Japanese dictionary and hand it to him?

notes: "England writing is English Writing (or if you want to be fancy, English Composition)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに日本語で文をかいて、その下に英文でやくを付けてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write the sentence in Japanese here and add its English translation below it.

example_sentences.english: I heard that my mother graduated from the Department of English Compositions in college in order to become a high school English teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、忙しいところ悪いんだけどさ、この英文の翻訳にちょっと手こずっちゃってるんだよね。手伝ってもらえないかな？
example_sentences.english: Hey, sorry to bother you, but I am kind of stuck on these English sentence translations. Could you help me?

notes: "Every night is simply every night. What do you do every night?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 体を丈夫にするために、毎晩やく用酒を飲んでいます。
example_sentences.english: In order to improve my health, I drink medicinal alcohol every night.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の夫は、毎晩五時に夕食を食べて、十時には寝ます。
example_sentences.english: Every night my husband eats dinner at 5 o’clock and goes to bed by 10 o’clock.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎晩泣く子を抱きながら、子供の世話をするには大変な忍耐が必要だということを学びました。
example_sentences.english: While holding a crying baby every night, I learned that you need a lot of patience to take care of children.

notes: "Poison inside the food is food poisoning. No fun when you get this :(" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 食中毒で会社を休んでしまい、大変申しわけありません。
example_sentences.english: I'm terribly sorry that I took a day off because of food poisoning.

example_sentences.japanese: ハーゲンダッツを食べて食中毒を乗りこえるというとても役立つ情ほうを教えてくれて、本当にありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much for your helpful information on how to get over food poisoning from eating Häagen-Dazs.

example_sentences.japanese: フグが私に食中毒の危険性をレクチャーしてくれたんだけどさぁ、説明がすっごく分かりにくかったんだよね。

english: Giant Buddha Statue, Daibutsu, Giant Statue Of Buddha, Large Buddha Statue, Large Statue Of Buddha
notes: "A large Buddha doesn't make sense if you don't know the context. There are giant statues of Buddha, and these are called Daibutsu, making this word translate to Giant Buddha Statue." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、ならの大仏をおとずれました。
example_sentences.english: I visited the Great Buddha at Nara yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 大仏をすんげーしんけんに見つめてるあの男、だれ？
example_sentences.english: Who is that guy staring at the giant Buddha statue so seriously?

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼女、大仏さんと付き合っているのよ。」「とても信じられないわね。だって、彼女の父親と言ってもいいくらい年上でしょ？」
example_sentences.english: """She’s dating Mr. Giant Buddha Statue."" ""You could have fooled me. He's old enough to be her father."""

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: Think about your husband even if you don't have one. What's his name? It's Otto (おっと), and he's always leaving you at home because he's working at the auto (おっと) shop."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の夫の歯は、とても丈夫です。
example_sentences.english: My husband has very healthy teeth.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の夫は、大変すばらしい男性です。
example_sentences.english: My husband is such a wonderful man.

example_sentences.japanese: ほら、また始まった。あんたって本当にいつも自分の夫の不満ばかり言っているよね。
example_sentences.english: There you go again, always complaining about your husband.

notes: "An action that takes place that could change the locale or even the world has got to be a big incident. You'll sometimes see this on the ends of ""incident"" names, like the ""Manshuu Jihen"" (満州事変), aka the ""Manshuu Incident."" You know that it isn't an unusual or strange incident (like 変事) because the ""strange"" kanji (変) doesn't come first with this word. Instead, it comes after and means ""change"" in this case." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 上海事変は何年に起こりましたか。
example_sentences.english: What year did Shanghai Incident occur?

example_sentences.japanese: 事変という言葉を使った例文をさがしていたら、東京事変というバンドがあることを知りました。
example_sentences.english: When I was looking for an example sentence with the word incident, I came across a band called Tokyo Incident.

example_sentences.japanese: 満州事変について説明をしてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Can you explain what the Manchurian Incident is?

notes: "When you get someone to transmit information, they're a type of intermediary, a go-between, if you will." "When a vocab word is a single kanji with no okurigana, it takes the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn this one yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember: When the go-between gets back and is about to tell you everything the other group said, it takes him two takes (つて) to get it all right. The other group had a lot to say and he had trouble getting it all on the first take, but he totally nailed it on the second."

example_sentences.japanese: 母が亡くなったことを伝えたいんですが、おじさんにはれんらくする伝がないんです。
example_sentences.english: I want to tell my uncle that my mom passed away, but I don't have a way to get in touch with him.

example_sentences.japanese: 伝をたよって、トーフグにしゅうしょくしました。
example_sentences.english: I got a job at Tofugu through my connections.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かの伝があるといいんだけど。
example_sentences.english: But I think some kind of intermediary would be good.

notes: "A child cat is an adorable kitten. D'awww!" "The reading is the vocab word 子 (こ) and the reading for cat (ねこ)."

example_sentences.japanese: その子猫は、えだからえだを軽かいにとびうつりました。
example_sentences.english: The kitten jumped nimbly from branch to branch.

example_sentences.japanese: 子猫が時計回りにクルクル歩き回っている動画をYoutubeにアップロードしました。
example_sentences.english: I uploaded a video to Youtube of a kitty walking clockwise, round and round.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達、ちょうどこの子猫を見つけて、飼い主をさがしているんです。
example_sentences.english: We just found this kitten and we’re looking for the owner.

notes: "Yesterday's year was actually last year. Today must be New Years then!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この二十四時間スーパーは、昨年オープンしました。
example_sentences.english: This 24-hour supermarket was opened last year.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨年は旅行でグアムに行きました。
example_sentences.english: I went on a trip to Guam last year.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨年、医者から中性しぼうのあたいが高いと言われちゃったんですよ。
example_sentences.english: Last year, my doctor told me that I have a high level of triglycerides.

english: Line, Line Of Things, Line Of People, Queue
notes: "When things are put in a row they end up forming a line. This can be a line of people or a line of random stuff." This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 「列の最後びはここですか？」「いいえ、私は列の先頭です。」
example_sentences.english: """Is this the end of the line? "" ""No. I'm at the front of the line."""

example_sentences.japanese: 私のせきは、前から二列目でした。
example_sentences.english: My seat was in the second row.

example_sentences.japanese: ベーコンショップの前には長い列ができていた。
example_sentences.english: There was a long line in front of the bacon shop.

notes: "The way method or the method way is the method or way. This is a good word for talking about how to do something. What's the 方法? Well, first you..." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトには、その方法はきかないっていうか、むしろぎゃくこうかですよ。
example_sentences.english: That method doesn't work on Viet. It actually works the other way around.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんをぐっすりベッドでねむらせる方法が知りたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to know the way to make a baby sleep very well in a bed.

example_sentences.japanese: シャーロック・ホームズって、古びた犯罪調査方法を使っているよね？
example_sentences.english: Sherlock Holmes has an old method of investigating crimes, doesn’t he?

notes: "You've hopefully seen 映画 in level 13. A public building for movies (映画) is a movie theater." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 次にこの町にくる時には、この映画館が完成して町なみもずいぶん変わってるんだろうね。
example_sentences.english: When I come back to this town next time, I guess this movie theater will be completed and it will change the townscape quite a bit.

example_sentences.japanese: れん休も終わったし、あの映画館多分しばらくガラガラだろうね。
example_sentences.english: The long holiday is over now, so the movie theater will probably be very quiet for a while.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今夜、映画館に行かない？」「そうできればいいんだけど、このレポートを仕上げなくちゃいけないんだ。」
example_sentences.english: """Would you like to go to the movie theater tonight?"" ""I wish I could but I have to finish this paper."""

notes: "You've hopefully seen 殺人 (murder) from level 13. So, someone who does murder is what? A murderer." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その殺人者は、とう走中に大変な失ぱいをおかしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: That killer made a terrible mistake while running away.

example_sentences.japanese: 殺人者とうたわがわれていましたが、ついにようぎが晴れました。
example_sentences.english: I'd been suspected of murderer, but I was finally cleared.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の今まで、俺の友達の人生は信じられない苦難の連続でした。彼の人生は殺人者の子どもとして始まりました。
example_sentences.english: Up until now, my friend’s life has been an epic struggle. He began his life as the baby of a murderer.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading for this word is the same as the kanji it comes from, so you should be able to read it!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の昼、あそこの定食屋でお昼一しょに食べようよ。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we eat lunch together at that diner during our lunch break today?

example_sentences.japanese: 目ざまし時計が鳴らなくて、起きたらすでに昼だった。
example_sentences.english: My alarm didn't go off and it was already noon when I woke up.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から一時間昼休憩を取るので、電話は取り次がないようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to take a one hour lunch break, so please hold my calls.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading for this word is the same as the kanji's reading.

example_sentences.japanese: 働きすぎは体に毒ですよ。
example_sentences.english: Working too much is harmful to your body.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトのつくえの引き出しには、コウイチをいつでも暗殺できるように毒の矢が仕こんである。
example_sentences.english: Viet is hiding a poison arrow in his desk drawer so that he can assassinate Koichi any time.

example_sentences.japanese: フグはとても美味しく、食べる人の心を豊かにしてくれますが、一方で猛毒も持っています。
example_sentences.english: While puffer fish is very delicious and provides a deeply satisfying culinary experience, it also carries a deadly poison.

hiragana: どくがす, どくガス
notes: "Poison Gas is a nasty thing. It is poison gas." "The reading is the same as the kanji it comes from. The ガス is of course ""gas."""

example_sentences.japanese: 毒ガスは第一次世界大戦で使われ始めたらしいです。
example_sentences.english: I read that poison gas was first used in World War I.

example_sentences.japanese: 午前十時からの毒ガスの使い方のレッスンを取っていたはずなんですが、もう一度かくにんしてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry, but I'm pretty sure that I took the lesson on how to use the poisonous gas at 10:00 a.m. Can you recheck that, please?

example_sentences.japanese: 「この野郎！また屁をこきやがったな！毒ガスのように臭いじゃねえか。」「すみません。もう二度とおならはしません。」「いいや、きっとまたこくさ。もう堪忍袋の緒が切れた。お前は首だ。」「そんな〜。」
example_sentences.english: """You bastard! You’ve farted again. It’s as stinky as poison gas!"" ""I’m sorry. I will never do it again."" ""No, I’m sure you will. That’s the last straw. You’re fired."" ""Oh no~!"""

notes: "A finger ring is the kind of ring you'd put on your finger. That's just simply a ""ring"" though, so you'll have to know what ""ring"" this is via context." "The readings come from the individual vocab readings, 指 and 輪. In English we don't distinguish some other ring from a ""finger ring"" but in Japanese, you can think of this as two separate words coming together to form one word, which is why it uses the kun'yomi vocab readings like this. So, if you know the individual words, you should be able to figure out this word is read as ゆびわ."

example_sentences.japanese: 大事な指輪を失くしてしまい、気分が晴れません。
example_sentences.english: I lost my precious ring and I feel awful.

example_sentences.japanese: 指輪が指から外れなくなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I can't get this ring off of my finger.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ボーナスが出たら、ダイヤモンドの指輪を買ってやるよ。」「あなたはいつも口先ばかりでしょ。」
example_sentences.english: """When I get a bonus, I’ll buy you a diamond ring."" ""You always say that, but words are just words."""

notes: "A ring of gum (ゴム) (which is what Japanese people call rubber quite often) is a ring of rubber. What is a ring of rubber that people use often? It's a rubber band." "The reading for 輪 is the kun'yomi vocab reading, which is わ, making this word わゴム."

example_sentences.japanese: この輪ゴムはとても丈夫です。
example_sentences.english: This elastic band is very durable.

example_sentences.japanese: 輪ゴムどろぼうのうたがいをかけられていたが、ついに晴れの身となりました。
example_sentences.english: They suspected I was the rubber band robber, but I've now been cleared of all charges.

example_sentences.japanese: わぁ！そのワンピマジで可愛い！カラフルな輪ゴムの絵がたくさんプリントしてあるんだね！そんなワンピ初めてみたよ。
example_sentences.english: Oh my God, I just totally love your dress! So many colorful rubber band pictures printed on it, eh? I’ve never seen a dress like this before.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading you learned with the kanji is the same as this one.

example_sentences.japanese: その寺なら、この坂を上ったところにありますよ。
example_sentences.english: That temple stands at the top of this hill.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは自転車でゆるやかな坂を下るのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: Viet likes going down gentle slopes on his bicycle.

example_sentences.japanese: スター選手であったフグを失ってから、Tofugu野球チームの調子は下り坂となってしまった。
example_sentences.english: The Tofugu baseball team has been on a downward slope since it lost its star player, Fugu.

notes: "An army person is someone in the army. What are those people called? They're soldiers." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: おきなわにはアメリカ軍のき地があるから、軍人さんがたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: Because there are American military bases in Okinawa, there are a lot of soldiers.

example_sentences.japanese: その軍人の勇気ある行動が、多くの人の命をすくいました。
example_sentences.english: That soldier's brave acts saved a lot of lives.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、上司に俺はリストラで首になるって言われちゃってさ。だから、今、軍人になることを真剣に考えてるんだ。
example_sentences.english: My boss told me yesterday that I am going to be fired, so now I’m seriously thinking about becoming a soldier.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading for this word is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. Ah, the beauty of spring! Err... はる, I mean."

example_sentences.japanese: わたしは虫が苦手だから春はきらいです。
example_sentences.english: I don't like bugs, so I don't like spring.

example_sentences.japanese: 「お前のチーム、春の大会ではどうだったの？」「へへ。大勝したっての！」
example_sentences.english: """How did your team do in the spring tournament?"" ""Hehe. Epic win."""

example_sentences.japanese: 春巻きという料理に「春」の字が使われているのは、春に芽が出る野菜を使って作る食べ物だかららしいですよ。
example_sentences.english: "I heard the reason the character for ""spring"" is used for spring roll is because people used to make spring rolls with vegetables that sprout in spring."

notes: "Something is making one thing the same as another inside a period of time. You'll see this word on computer-ish things a lot. This is syncing." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: iPhone同期中に電源が切れて軽くあせった。
example_sentences.english: When I was syncing my iPhone, it turned off and I was a little freaked out.

example_sentences.japanese: Dropbox、いつも写しん同期中にフリーズしてしまうのはなぜ。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why Dropbox always freezes while syncing photos.

example_sentences.japanese: たぶんもうすぐ反映されると思う。私のエバーノート今同期中だし。
example_sentences.english: It will probably show up soon. My Evernote is syncing right now.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is the same as the kanji too! You must have been praying to the kanji Gods at the local お寺."

example_sentences.japanese: 昨夜、あのお寺で変死体が発見されたらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Apparently, the body of someone who died accidentally was found at the temple last night.

example_sentences.japanese: 子どものころ、寺のとなりに住んでいたので、仏教の勉強には大変都合が良かったんです。
example_sentences.english: I lived next to a temple when I was a child and it was really convenient for studying Buddhism.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の地元のお寺で誕生日会を開いたんだけど、すぐに追い出されちゃった。お寺ってロック・コンサートをやる場所じゃないってこと、知っておけばよかったんだけど。
example_sentences.english: I held a birthday party at one of the local temples in Japan. We got kicked out pretty quickly. I should have known that a temple wasn’t a good place to have a rock concert.

notes: "Previous from now are the times around now. They're these days." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just note that さく changes to さっ as many K-column sounds do in situations like this."

example_sentences.japanese: 昨今はあなたの様な大物にお目にかかれることはめったになくなりましたよ、コウイチさん。
example_sentences.english: Nowadays it is very rare to meet somebody big like you, Mr. Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨今の流行りにあやかって、コウイチはオフィスでしば犬とチンド犬をかうことに決めました。
example_sentences.english: Owing to recent trends, Koichi decided to have a Shiba-inu and a Jindo in our office.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨今は就職氷河期だと言われているが、会社を選ばなければどこかには就職できるはずである。
example_sentences.english: They say it's been a hard time for job seekers these days, but I'm sure you should be able to find a job if you're not picky about the company you work for.

notes: "A thing that gives you time measurements is a watch or clock. Most people have these in their phones instead of on their wrists now." "The reading for this is pretty weird. 計 is all nice and normal, but 時 is と for some reason. It probably is coming from the vocab word 時 (とき), is my guess. But even if it is, it's shortened, making it a step more complicated. Maybe it's just better to imagine that your watch is a walky talky (とけい) and run with that?"

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはビエトにもらった時計を船から落としてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi dropped the clock Viet had given him from the ship.

example_sentences.japanese: 時計台の下で、三時に待ち合わせね！
example_sentences.english: We're gonna meet at the clock tower at 3 p.m., okay?

example_sentences.japanese: ねぇ、あなたの時計に唾が着いてない？
example_sentences.english: Hey, isn’t that spit on your watch?

notes: "The yesterday day is yesterday. What a blast from the past!" "Oof. The reading for this word makes no sense. You'll have to forget everything you've learned about the readings of the kanji and just go straight up mnemonic for the word on its own. Okay. Think about what you did yesterday, all day. You played keno (きのう), gambling away your grandmother's money. Yesterday was the worst day ever because you lost everything playing Keno. Today is different, not like yesterday, right?"

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の夜は、よくねむれた？
example_sentences.english: Did you sleep well last night?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日はアメリカとカナダで労働者の日でした。
example_sentences.english: It was Labor Day in the U.S. and Canada yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は、大学の課題で、沢山の叙事詩を読まなくてはいけませんでした。
example_sentences.english: We had to read many epic poems yesterday for a university assignment.

notes: "You've seen 料理 and probably know it means ""cooking."" So, what is a person who does cooking? That is a cook or chef." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチからの手紙を読んで、料理人になる決意を固めました。
example_sentences.english: My position as cook was confirmed by Koichi's letter.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理人は、「料理が気に入らなかったら、残してくださっていいですよ」と悲しそうに言いました。
example_sentences.english: "The chef ruefully said, ""If you don't like my food, just leave it."""

example_sentences.japanese: その料理人は、冷凍庫のドアから栓抜きを剥ぎ取った。
example_sentences.english: The chef grabbed the bottle opener hanging from the freezer door.

notes: "You've seen 技 as a vocab word meaning ""technique."" This is sort of using that meaning. So, a technique of art is still art, but it's also your craft, your technique." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は医者ではありませんが、ある医者から、心ぞういしょくの技術を学びました。
example_sentences.english: I'm not a doctor but I learned heart transplant techniques from a doctor.

example_sentences.japanese: 以前に働いていた会社で、えい業技術を身につけました。
example_sentences.english: I learned the art of selling from the company I used to work for.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は技術的に優れたボクサーと結婚した。
example_sentences.english: I married a technically brilliant boxer.

notes: "This is the same as the kanji, at least in regards to the article or goods meaning, which means you can use this word to mean article or goods." The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: この品は、まとめ買いがおとくですよ。
example_sentences.english: You can get a discount if you buy this item in bulk.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は男らしくて良い人だけど、品のないしゃべり方をするので少し苦手です。
example_sentences.english: He is a nice, manly person but he uses coarse language, so I find it a bit difficult to get along with him.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチさんから開業祝いの品が届いたので、机の上に置いておいたよ。ちなみにメッセージカードには、「あまりにも早く独立開業を成し遂げたあなたのパワーに圧倒されています」って書いあるよ。
example_sentences.english: A congratulatory gift for the new business’s opening arrived from Mr. Koichi and I put it on your desk. On the card he wrote that you overwhelmed him with your power and how fast you were able to open your business.

notes: "You know that 芸術 is art so you'd think that 芸術家 would be something like ""art house."" Well, it's not. Think of it this way: Who is the person who works for ""House Art""? It's the artist." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この芸術家の作品には、苦笑いがかくせません。
example_sentences.english: I can't hide my wry smile at this artist's works.

example_sentences.japanese: その芸術家は、弟子に留守番をたのんで、ヨーロッパに留学しました。
example_sentences.english: The artist asked his disciple to look after his house while he was away and left for Europe to study.

example_sentences.japanese: 再来月のマラソン大会、芸術家達と一緒に参加するってのはどう？
example_sentences.english: How about running a marathon with a bunch of artists the month after next?

notes: "You know that 自動 is automatic. So what is an automatic car? That is an automobile." "The reading comes from 自動 and the kanji 車's readings, combined."

example_sentences.japanese: あの自動車ディーラーにうら切られた気分です。
example_sentences.english: I feel betrayed by that car dealership.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい自動車を買うために、お金をためるようにしています。
example_sentences.english: We are trying to set some money aside for a new car.

example_sentences.japanese: 自動車の運転免許を失くしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I lost my driver’s license.

notes: "A product you make is a fine work. It is a work you made. It is of your production." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この箱庭の作品は、マッチ箱で作られています。
example_sentences.english: This miniature garden work is made from a matchbox.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグオフィスの入り口にあるヘンテコな像は、コウイチの十五才の時の作品ですよ。
example_sentences.english: The strange statue at the entrance of Tofugu office is a work of Koichi's from when he was fifteen.

example_sentences.japanese: 久々にいい作品に出会ったわ。進撃の巨人は、私の好きなアニメの歴代三位に入るんじゃないかってくらい良かったよ。マジでお薦めするわ。
example_sentences.english: It’s been a while since I came across a work I like. Attack on Titan is so good that it might be one of my top three anime. I highly recommend it.

notes: "You know how 弁 means dialect and 当 means success? Well, this isn't going to help you much, because this means bento or box lunch. Chances are, though, you know the word ""bento"" from English. So, if you read this word (which you should be able to) you can figure out it's べんとう. If you do that, you can realize this word means bento too!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のかばんの中には、さいふと、弁当と、タバコが一箱入っています。
example_sentences.english: In my bag, there's a wallet, a bento, and a pack of cigarettes.

example_sentences.japanese: お弁当のおかずを少し残しておいて、子猫にあげました。
example_sentences.english: I left some sides in my box lunch and gave them to a kitten.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日あなたにお弁当作ってあげようと思うんだけど、何か苦手なものとかあるの？
example_sentences.english: I think I’ll make a bento box for you tomorrow. Is there anything you’d prefer not to have?

notes: "The Buddha rules are the rules Buddha made for Buddhists. These can be found in the Buddhist Scriptures and Buddhist Writings." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that ぶつ gets shortened to ぶっ."

example_sentences.japanese: その仏典はこの箱の中にしまってもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Can you put the Buddhist scriptures in this box?

example_sentences.japanese: こんざつ時は、ゆずり合って仏典をご利用ください。
example_sentences.english: During peak hours, please be considerate of others waiting to use the Buddhist writings.

example_sentences.japanese: 仏典がどのようにしてサンスクリット語から漢語に訳されたのかご存じですか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know how the Buddhist scriptures were translated from Sanskrit to Chinese?

notes:
"The rules for letters can be found in a character dictionary. In Japanese, one ""letter"" or ""character"" can have a lot of information (we're talking kanji here). That means you need dictionaries for these individual letters as well! That's what this is." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"You need to know the word rules of the language you're learning, don't you? Then you need a good dictionary that can explain its lexicon!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"Something filled with the rules of various actions is something that contains a ton of knowledge. It contains all things and actions, right? What kind of ""thing"" is filled with all this information (that existed during the creation of words and kanji?)? One thing would be an encyclopedia." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、ぬれた字典について、ビエトにせつ明を要求しました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi demanded an explanation about the wet character dictionary from Viet.

example_sentences.japanese: とつ然大雨になったので、手でもっていた字典がびしょぬれになっちゃったんです。
example_sentences.english: It suddenly started pouring rain and the kanji dictionary I was holding got soaking wet.

example_sentences.japanese: この書道字典はあそこの古本屋で買ったんです。
example_sentences.english: I bought this calligraphy dictionary at a secondhand bookstore over there.

example_sentences.japanese: その辞典、使い終わったらちゃんと箱の中にもどしておいてね。
example_sentences.english: Can you put the dictionary back in the box after you use it?

example_sentences.japanese: 電子辞書には色んな辞典が入っています。
example_sentences.english: An electronic dictionary has various dictionaries in it.

example_sentences.japanese: 辞典の使い方が分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know how to use a dictionary.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチなら、サンルームの日光浴用のイスで事典とにらめっこしていますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are looking for Koichi, he is staring at an encyclopedia on the lounge chair in the sunroom.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが事典を万引きしたしゅん間がカメラに映っているんですよ。
example_sentences.english: The camera showed that you shoplifted an encyclopedia.

example_sentences.japanese: 本としてはちょっと大きすぎたので、私は百科事典を枕として使っていました。
example_sentences.english: I used my encyclopedia as a pillow because it was too big to be a book.

notes: "The things related to your heart are the things that concern and interest you the most." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本のアニメの声ゆうは好きですが、海外のアニメの声ゆうには関心がありません。
example_sentences.english: I like Japanese anime voice actors but I have no interest in foreign ones.

example_sentences.japanese: げんざいの最大の関心は何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What is your greatest concern at the moment?

example_sentences.japanese: 当社トーフグ、ならびに当社製品に関心をお寄せいただき、有難うございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for your interest in our company, Tofugu, and our products.

notes: "The weekday day is the day of the week, as in ""Monday"" or ""Tuesday."" You'll be learning those on level 18, but first you should learn 曜日 to get you prepared." "This word uses the on'yomi reading for 曜 and the kun'yomi reading for 日. You've learned both of these already, but be careful because ひ of 日 changes to び here."

example_sentences.japanese: 水曜日は、ネイティブが話すスピードで日本語を話す日にしませんか？
example_sentences.english: Why don't we make Wednesday the day we try speaking Japanese at the speed of native speakers?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日って何曜日だっけ？
example_sentences.english: What day of the week is today?

example_sentences.japanese: 肝心なのは、この日本語の課題を金曜日までに終わらせなければならないということだ。
example_sentences.english: The bottom line is that we have to finish this Japanese assignment by Friday.

notes: "Take all the words you use in writing, put them together and you have a dictionary!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、トーフグにたくさんの辞書を残して死んだ。
example_sentences.english: When Koichi died, he left Tofugu a ton of dictionaries.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、世界で一番売れている辞書です。
example_sentences.english: This is the best selling dictionary in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 「愛」という字を辞書で引いて、その意味の上に彼氏の名前を書いておいたの。そしたら、彼に見つかっちゃって、それで振られちゃったのさ。
example_sentences.english: "I looked up the word ""love"" in my dictionary and wrote my boyfriend’s name on top of the definition, but he dumped me when he saw it."

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: Someone left some evidence behind at the crime scene. You pick it up, it's a kashi (あかし) bar. It has genetic evidence on it, because the criminal was eating it at the crime scene."

example_sentences.japanese: 友情の証として、このふじ山のキーホルダーをあげます。
example_sentences.english: As proof of our friendship, I'll give you this Mt. Fuji keychain.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつの身の証を立てるのはそうかん単なことじゃないかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: It might not be easy to show the evidence of his innocence.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の両親だって本当は叱りたくないけど、叱っているんだよ。愛の証だよ。
example_sentences.english: Your parents tell you off, even though they don't actually want to. It's proof of their love.

notes: "Suppose that life is in existence on this planet... What would that say about life and survival in such an unforgiving place?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: われわれの肉体は、生存のためにつねに水分を必要としている。
example_sentences.english: Our bodies always need water for survival.

example_sentences.japanese: その世界では、きょ人たちが人るい生存のきょういとなっていた。
example_sentences.english: In that world, titans were threatening the existence of humanity.

example_sentences.japanese: FBIは、生存者を求めて、夜通しTofuguオフィスの中を捜索した。
example_sentences.english: The FBI searched all night for the survivor in the Tofugu office.

hiragana: がいめん, そとづら
notes: "The outside face to something is the exterior of that thing." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. This reading is usually for building exteriors and outside surfaces.
