The other reading そとづら is used when a person's personality comes to the surface and is a bit of an exception, so you'll probably see it less often. Just keep those differences in mind!"

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは外面はいい人そうですが、実はとてもおそろしい一面を持っています。
example_sentences.english: On the surface, Viet looks like a nice guy, but he actually has a scary side.

example_sentences.japanese: 外面だけがいい男性とけっこんし、外面は立ぱだけど内面はボロボロの中古住たくを買ってしまい、今とても苦労しているんです。
example_sentences.english: I'm married to a man who is an angel outside and a devil at home, and we bought an older home that has a fine exterior, but the interior is worn out, so I'm having a tough time right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の外面に騙されない方がいいですよ。私がインストラクターのことが嫌いだったのは、上司にはいい顔をして陰で後輩のことを小突き回していたからです。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn’t be fooled by his outward appearance. I hated my instructor because he showed his superiors a nice face while he bullied subordinates, including me, behind their backs.

english: Fail A Test, Failure, Fail An Exam
notes: "You know that 合格する is ""to pass a test,"" so what's the opposite of that? Fail a test or failure." "If you know the reading for 合格, all you have to do is add 不 to it! You've learned all these readings, yay!"

example_sentences.japanese: カンニングしたのがバレて不合格になってしまった。
example_sentences.english: They found out that I'd cheated and I was rejected.

example_sentences.japanese: 本命の公立大学の入学しけんは不合格だったが、すべり止めで受けた私立大学に合格しました。
example_sentences.english: I failed the entrance exam for a public university, which was my first choice, but I passed for a private college, which was my second choice.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに簡単な試験が不合格だったなんて本当に恥ずかしいよ。穴があったら入りたいぐらいだ。
example_sentences.english: I’m so embarrassed I failed such an easy test. I wish I could sink through the floor.

notes: "When you quit your current generation to join an older one you need all the flattery you can get because you're starting to feel old. People probably still won't like you though, ya old fart." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは心にもないお世辞を言うのが下手です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is not good at giving insincere compliments.

example_sentences.japanese: お世辞で日本語が上手だと言われるのは好きではありません。
example_sentences.english: I don't like being complimented on my Japanese speaking.

example_sentences.japanese: 「わぉ！今夜の君はとてもきれいだね。まるで、お姫様みたいだよ。」「パパ、お世辞を言っても何も出ないわよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Oh wow! You look so beautiful tonight. Like a princess!"" ""Flattery will get you nowhere, daddy.”"

notes: "A fold you can see with your eye is a fold or crease in something." "The readings are both kun'yomi vocab readings. You should have seen 折る by now which should help you to read 折り. Then there's 目, which I'm guessing you won't have a problem with."

example_sentences.japanese: このズボンには、折り目がなかったということを、ここに証明いたします。
example_sentences.english: I hereby certify that these pants are without a single fold.

example_sentences.japanese: 折り紙を半分に折って、折り目をつけてからまた開いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please open the origami again after you fold it in half to add the crease.

example_sentences.japanese: ズボンには折り目を付けてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Could you put a crease in my trousers?

notes: "The front face of something is the front or the front side of it (kind of like how 外面 is the exterior because it's the outside face)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはいつもいい人さを前面に出している。
example_sentences.english: Viet always puts his good man-ness to the front.

example_sentences.japanese: 前面も後面も両方とも緑色の箱をさがしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please find a box that has green on both the front and back sides.

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙や小包を送る時には、いつも前面にTofuguのステッカーを貼ります。
example_sentences.english: Whenever we send a letter or a package, we put the Tofugu sticker on the front of it.

hiragana: ごみばこ, ゴミばこ
english: Garbage Can, Garbage Bin, Trash Can, Trash Bin, Waste Can, Waste Bin, Rubbish Bin
notes: "ゴミ means ""garbage."" Add a box to it and you have a garbage box aka a garbage can or garbage bin." "The reading is just the kun'yomi reading, the one you learned with the kanji. Be sure to pay attention to the rendaku though. はこ changes to ばこ."

example_sentences.japanese: ゴミ箱に、新せんな箱づめの魚がすてられていました。
example_sentences.english: There were boxed fresh fish in the garbage can.

example_sentences.japanese: そのゴミ箱の中にけっこん指輪があるかもしれないというかすかな希望がありました。
example_sentences.english: I had weakly hoped to find the wedding ring in the trash can.

example_sentences.japanese: ゴミ箱のゴミを捨てる時のあなたってとってもセクシーだと思うのよね。だから、ちょっと私のためにゴミ箱のゴミを捨ててくれないかな？
example_sentences.english: I think you are so sexy when you empty the garbage can— could you empty the garbage can for me please?

notes: "Politics and government. They are needed to keep the government rolling." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ政府は、国きょうのぼうびを固めなくてはいけないと言っています。
example_sentences.english: The U.S. government says that we must strengthen our defenses on the border.

example_sentences.japanese: 政府は、自分たちのひみつは固く守るが、国民との約束はちっとも守らない。
example_sentences.english: The government keeps their secrets very well, but they don't keep their promises to the people at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達の記事が政府から出版を禁止されているなんて信じられません。Tofuguには政府を批判する権利があります。
example_sentences.english: We can’t believe that the government has prohibited our articles from being published. Tofugu has the right to criticize the government.

notes: "You know that 卒業 is graduation so what about when you add ceremony to it? That makes it a graduation ceremony." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help if you know how to read 卒業 already as a word, too."

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業式の後で、橋の上で一しょに写真をとろうよ！
example_sentences.english: After the graduation ceremony, let's take a photo on the bridge together!

example_sentences.japanese: はあ？卒業式にビヨンセが来て歌を歌ってくれた？まさか！冗談でしょう？
example_sentences.english: Huh? Did you say that Beyoncé came to the graduation and sang for you guys? No way! You must be joking!

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業式の後の旅行超楽しみだよ〜！ゆっくり露天風呂に入って、山の幸をいっぱい食べ尽くそうね。ところで、念のため確認だけど、宿の予約してくれたんだよね？
example_sentences.english: I’m so excited for the trip after our graduation ceremony! Let’s relax in the hot springs and eat a lot of local delicious food. By the way, just making sure but you made a reservation at the cottage, right?

notes: "Products you're paying a fee to eat later are your groceries. Buy them now, eat them later, yum!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 食料品コーナーで働いている人たちが、ちん上げを要求しているらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the workers at the grocery section are making demands for higher wages.

example_sentences.japanese: 「サーモン、万が一にそなえて、食料品を買っておかなくちゃ。」「フグ、買わなくても大丈夫よ！食料品ならここにあるじゃない。」「え、どこに？」「食料にこまったら共食いすればいいだけじゃない。」
example_sentences.english: """Salmon, we should buy some groceries in case of emergency."" ""Fugu, we don't need to buy them. We have food here!"" ""Where?"" ""If we have trouble with food, we just need to prey on each other."""

example_sentences.japanese: 食料品売場はどこにありますか。
example_sentences.english: Could you tell me where the grocery section is?

notes: "The slopes of the gods! What could this be? Well, it's mainly just a company, known as Hanshin. They're based in the area between Osaka and Kobe. Think of it this way: 大阪 + 神戸 = 阪神! They're everywhere, though, and even have a baseball team (the Hanshin Tigers), so it's good to know." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 阪神電車カラーのゼリーを氷でひやして固めているところです。
example_sentences.english: I'm setting the Hanshin Electric Railway colored jelly by cooling it with ice.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度、阪神地区に新築の家を買おうと思ってるんですが、相場はいくらぐらいなんですか。
example_sentences.english: I am thinking about buying a newly-built house in the Hanshin district. About how much is the market price?

example_sentences.japanese: うわぁ、阪神タイガースのファンたち、恵比寿橋からあの汚い川にダイブしたんだって？すげぇな、あいつらの頭大丈夫かよ！
example_sentences.english: Oh my God! Hanshin Tigers fans dived off the Ebisu bridge down into the dirty river? Wow, they are nuts!

notes: "Some days are so special that you have to write down all your thoughts when they're done. These are special days like holidays and your anniversary." "The reading is a combination of on'yomi for the first two and kun'yomi for the last one. That being said, all of the readings for all of the kanji are the readings you've learned already, so you should be able to read this word too. Just watch out because ひ is rendaku'd into び."

example_sentences.japanese: 記念日をわすれるなんて、最低よ！
example_sentences.english: Forgetting something like a Memorial Day is the worst!

example_sentences.japanese: 今年のけっこん記念日には、夫から全自動せんたくきをもらいました。
example_sentences.english: My husband gave me a fully automatic washing machine for our wedding anniversary this year.

example_sentences.japanese: どく立記念日は、フリマで服を売っています。
example_sentences.english: On Independence Day, I'm selling clothes at a flea market.

english: Image Of Buddha, Statue Of Buddha
notes: "You have Buddha's image. What is that? It's an image of Buddha." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で仏像を買ったら、申告しないといけませんか？
example_sentences.english: Do I have to declare if I buy a statue of Buddha in Japan?

example_sentences.japanese: 仏像はよく金色に作られています。
example_sentences.english: Buddha statues are often made gold.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かがうちのオフィスに毎月仏像を一体ずつ送ってくるんです。心当たりのある方は、どうか名乗り出て下さい。
example_sentences.english: Someone sends a Buddhist statue to our office every month. If you are that person, please come forward and identify yourself.

notes: "The Kansai region of Japan is the Southern Central part of Japan. It actually connects the East side of Japan (at least back in the day) to the West side, making it the ""connection to the west."" For our purposes, though, we should call it ""Kansai.""" "Urgh, what a confusing reading! The 西 is さい instead of せい. Readings like this just make you want to sigh (さい), no?"

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルは、関西一の芸人としての地位を固めつつある。
example_sentences.english: Michael has been consolidating his position as the number one comedian in Kansai.

example_sentences.japanese: 関東の人と関西の人って折が合わないって聞いたんですが、本当ですか。
example_sentences.english: I heard that people from Kanto and people from Kansai are not getting along well. Is it true?

example_sentences.japanese: こいつは関西は完全に初心者だから、俺らが案内してやらないとな。
example_sentences.english: This guy is a total noob in Kansai, so we’ll have to show him around.

notes: "Something that's special and in a hurry must be special indeed. This refers to limited express trains in Japan. They go fast, they stop at fewer stops (because they're special!) and they hurry. Look out for these if you want to get somewhere in a jiffy." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just note that the とく goes to とっ."

example_sentences.japanese: ノリで特急に乗ることに決めました。
example_sentences.english: We decided, spur of the moment, to take the limited express.

example_sentences.japanese: けんこうしんだんで、心電図に異常があったので、月曜日に特急に乗って大阪の大学病院まで行って、せいみつけんさを受けなければいけません。
example_sentences.english: When I had my checkup, they found something unusual in my EKG, so I have to go back for a complete physical at a university hospital in Osaka via the limited express train on Monday.

example_sentences.japanese: 特急券を先に買っておいたので、今出れば三時五十分の特急に間に合うよ。
example_sentences.english: I already got an express ticket for you, so if you leave now you can still catch the 3:50 express train.

notes: "A luggage thing is your luggage. It's also your baggage and load too." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You'll need to remember the 物 reading as もつ, though. Why? Because all your luggage just got thrown into various moats along the countryside. It's going to take you forever to collect your luggage from these moats and by then it'll be all soggy. Dangit..."

example_sentences.japanese: ぜい関で荷物を調べられないか心配です。
example_sentences.english: I'm worried about my baggage being examined in customs.

example_sentences.japanese: 荷物でいっぱいのベビーカーが公園におきっ放しになっていました。
example_sentences.english: A stroller full of luggage was left in the park.

example_sentences.japanese: 「誰かが車から荷物を降ろさないといけないんだけど…。」 「わかったから、それ以上言わなくていいよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Someone ought to unpack the luggage from the car…"" ""Alright. Say no more."""

notes: "A temporary face is something you put over your face to cover it. It's a mask." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ハロウィンの日の夜、仮面ライダーのコスプレをしながら、チョコレートを一箱平らげたビエトを見ました。
example_sentences.english: On the Halloween night, I saw Viet wearing the Masked Rider costume and eating a whole box of chocolates.

example_sentences.japanese: わぁ、びっくりした！何で仮面なんてかぶってるの？
example_sentences.english: Ah, you startled me! Why are you wearing that mask?

example_sentences.japanese: ヴェネツィアの仮面舞踏会に行って白馬の王子様に会うことが私の夢です。
example_sentences.english: My dream is to go to the masquerade in Venice and meet a knight on a white horse.

notes: "It’s the era of Bright Rule! If this doesn't make sense, don't worry about it. Focus more on the reading, which is めいじ. Sound familiar? This is the famous Meiji Era or Meiji Emperor. If you don't know about it consider reading up, it's interesting history!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 明治生まれのそ母は、生前は仏教の教えをちゅう実に守っていました。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother was born in the Meiji era, and she devotedly practiced the Buddhist teachings when she was alive.

example_sentences.japanese: 明治い新についてのろん文を書いています。
example_sentences.english: I'm writing a paper about the Meiji Restoration.

example_sentences.japanese: 明治時代の生活を描いたドラマを見ているんですが、当時は一万円が大金だったということに驚きました。
example_sentences.english: I was watching a drama series about life in the Meiji period and I was surprised that ten thousand yen was a large amount of money back then.

notes: "Articles of merchandise are still merchandise." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニは、トーフグのヒット商品です。
example_sentences.english: WaniKani is Tofugu's hit product.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社の商品にはいつも保証がついてるから、私はそこで買うことが多いかな。
example_sentences.english: Their merchandise is always guaranteed, so I tend to buy things from them.

example_sentences.japanese: この新商品は大成功を収めると信じているんだ。そして、君にはこの商品の店内キャンペーンでの販売促進に取り組んでもらいたいと思っているんだ。頼りにしているよ。
example_sentences.english: I believe this new product will be a big success and I’d like you to work on promoting it through in-store campaigns. I’m really counting on you.

notes: "You know 美術 is fine art. So what is a public building that contains said fine art? It's a museum." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その美術館にかざられていたノアの箱ぶねの絵が好きでした。
example_sentences.english: I liked the picture of Noah's ark that was displayed at the art gallery.

example_sentences.japanese: 母が残してくれた指輪を、美術館にき付しました。
example_sentences.english: I donated the ring handed down to me from my mother to the museum.

example_sentences.japanese: 「どうやって美術館のツアーガイドになれるの？芸術の専門家か何かじゃなくちゃいけないんじゃないの？」「いいや、そうでもないよ。 美術館が情報を全部くれるから、まぁ、台詞を覚えるようなもんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """How can you be a tour guide in the museum? Don’t you have to be an art expert or something?"" ""No, not really. They give you all the information, it’s like memorizing a script."""

notes: "You know that 折る is ""to fold,"" so what about ""to fold paper""? Ever heard of something that involves lots of folding of paper that is Japanese? Most likely you have. This is origami, aka the art of paper folding." "The reading comes from 折る and the vocab word 紙. As long as you know those you should be able to read this. Also, you probably already know this reading because it's an English word, too."

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のコウイチの弁当箱の中には、なぜか食べ物の代わりに折り紙が入っていました。
example_sentences.english: Today, in Koichi's bento box, there were some origami instead of food.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はプロの折り紙アーティストです。
example_sentences.english: I'm a professional origami artist.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のことをこの数年間支えてくれたみなさん、本当に有難うございます。お陰様で、ついに折り紙で河豚が折れるようになりました。
example_sentences.english: I want to thank everyone who has shown me support over the years. Thankfully, I’ve finally mastered how to make an origami Fugu.

notes: "The big heights. What a nice area to be, it's where everyone wants to live! This magical place is Osaka. Heard of it before? It's a city, and kind of the rival to Tokyo." "The reading is pretty weird, but then again so are people from Osaka (just kidding, Osakazens!). The 大 reads like おお from おおきい. Then, 阪 uses the kun'yomi reading as well, which you didn't learn. That being said, doesn't this kanji look like 坂, which also means slope? Well, it shares a kun'yomi reading as well, so if you've seen 坂 you can apply that reading over to here, making おおさか. Then again, if you know this word means Osaka you probably can figure out how to write it too. Don't forget the double おお though!"

example_sentences.japanese: 大阪では、せいげん速度を守って走る車は少ないと聞いたんですが、本当ですか？
example_sentences.english: I heard that not many cars obey the speed limit in Osaka, is that true?

example_sentences.japanese: 大阪旅行が楽しみすぎて、勉強がすっかりお留守になってしまっていました。
example_sentences.english: I was so excited about the Osaka trip that I totally neglected my studies.

example_sentences.japanese: あいにくですが、来週の水曜日はちょっと都合がつかないんです。代わりに来週の木曜日に大阪に行くってのはどうでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: I’m afraid I won’t be able to make it next Wednesday. What about going to Osaka next Thursday instead?

notes: "A copy of reality is a lot like magic. How do you make a copy of reality, though? You take a photo." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの高校時代の写真が流出してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's picture from high school was leaked.

example_sentences.japanese: この写真、見て！お父さん、昔のまんま。変わったことと言えば、ちょっと太ったことくらいじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Look at this photo. Dad hasn't changed at all since then. Well, he's gained some weight, but nothing else has changed, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ご依頼のフグのヌード写真集を同封いたします。
example_sentences.english: Enclosed are the nude photos of Fugu you requested.

notes: "If you want to cure the government, you have to get into politics. Gotta join 'em to fix them... but can you survive that long without being corrupted yourself?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ついに、大学で政治を学ぶという私の長年の希望がかないました。
example_sentences.english: My long held hope, which was to study politics in university, finally came true.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンの政治に対する考えはとても保守的です。
example_sentences.english: Salmon's attitude toward the government is very conservative.

example_sentences.japanese: ワシントンDCで起きている政治騒動なんてお構いなしに、トーフグは共和党と民主党の両地域で雇用を生み出している。
example_sentences.english: Being mindful of the political turmoil occurring in Washington D.C., Tofugu has been creating employment for both the Republican and Democratic dominated regions.

english: Public Order, Public Safety, Public Peace
notes: "If your people can relax because you rule over them so well, there is public order. You don't want the people you rule being upset or stressed out, you want public safety and public peace for all!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺りは治安も悪くないけど、あの辺りは治安が良くないからね。
example_sentences.english: This area doesn’t have bad public safety, but that area does.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトの親分は、治安ぼうがいでたいほされた。
example_sentences.english: Viet's boss was arrested for disturbing the peace.

example_sentences.japanese: こないだ、酔っ払ったコウイチが、「俺は実はスーパーマンなんだ。この辺りの治安を守っているのはこの俺様なんだ」って豪語していたよ。
example_sentences.english: The other day I saw Koichi, drunk, boastfully telling people that he's actually Superman and he's the one who keeps the peace around here.

notes: "A public park is a park that is public. It's a public park." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この通りを真っ直ぐ行くと、公園があります。
example_sentences.english: If you go straight down this road, there’s a park.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園ですなあそびをしていたら、手が真っ黒になってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I was playing with sand at a public park and it turned my hands as black as coal.

example_sentences.japanese: 「フグと一緒にいった公園、どうだった？」「正直今までに行った公園の中で一番楽しかったよ。」
example_sentences.english: """So, how was the park you and Fugu went to?"" ""That was actually the most enjoyable park we’ve ever been to."""

notes: "A luggage tag is a tag you put on luggage. It's also a label you can put pricing and information on in stores or any other place with packaging." This word uses the kun'yomi reading for both kanji. You've learned both of these readings already, so you should be able to read this word too.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行かばんに付ける荷札をさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for a tag to put on my suitcase.

example_sentences.japanese: 荷札の書き方を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me how to write a package label.

example_sentences.japanese: 加茂錦の「荷札酒」の荷札を集めるのが趣味なんです。
example_sentences.english: "My hobby is collecting the labels of Kamonishiki's ""Labeled Sake."""

notes: "The thing you use to teach a course with writings is a textbook. It's a book of writings you use to teach your course!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その日本語の教科書は高すぎて買えません。
example_sentences.english: I can't buy the Japanese textbook because it's too expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 教科書はシェアしないで一人一さつ買ってくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Please don't share the textbook. Each person must buy their own.

example_sentences.japanese: 教科書を持ってくるのを忘れたせいで、放課後一時間学校に残されました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to bring my textbook and I was kept an hour after school.

notes: "You know that 東京 is Tokyo, and you know that 弁 is dialect, so you have yourself Tokyo dialect." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know how to read 東京 already, which you should."

example_sentences.japanese: 東京弁は共通語とほとんど同じですよ。
example_sentences.english: Tokyo dialect is almost the same as standard Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京弁でしゃべってほしいというコウイチの要求をしりぞけました。
example_sentences.english: I rejected Koichi's request that I speak in Tokyo dialect.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ねえ、無料で東京弁のレッスンを受けたいんだけど。」「コウイチに聞けよ。アイツは何でもするぞ。」
example_sentences.english: """I need to get some free Tokyo dialect lessons."" ""Ask Koichi. He’ll do anything."""

english: Unsold Merchandise, Remaining Stock, Unsold Stock, Remaining Merchandise, Unsold Product, Remaining Product
notes: "The remainder products are the things that haven't been sold. It's the unsold merchandise. It's the remaining stock." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note that ひん changes to ぴん."

example_sentences.japanese: 残品は半がくでしょ分しました。
example_sentences.english: We sold the remaining goods at half price.

example_sentences.japanese: 残品はこちらで引き取るので、こちらのお店ではん売させてもらえませんか。
example_sentences.english: You can return any unsold stock, so would you let us sell our products here?

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜店を出発する前に残品を数えておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Before we leave the store tonight, let’s go ahead and count the remaining stock.

notes: "A room where you join other people to wait. This is a waiting room." "Remember how you learned 待合 already? Well throw the on'yomi for 室 on the end of that and you have your reading!"

example_sentences.japanese: 今、歯医者の待合室にいます。
example_sentences.english: I'm in the dentist's waiting room now.

example_sentences.japanese: 空港には、団体で旅行するグループのための待合室があります。
example_sentences.english: There are waiting rooms for tourist groups in airports.

example_sentences.japanese: 数日前、病院の待合室で経済についての本を読んだんだけど、結構良かったよ。
example_sentences.english: I read an economics book the other day in the hospital waiting room and it was pretty interesting.

notes: "An evidence person is a witness, because witnesses are people who provide evidence (you know, with their mouths or something)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 証人が、ビエトが有ざいであることを証明してくれました。
example_sentences.english: The witness proved that Viet was guilty.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の夫のさいばんでは、夫の口座がある銀行の行員の人たちが証人として出ていしてくれました。
example_sentences.english: In my husband's court case, the clerks of the bank where he has his accounts appeared in court as witnesses for him.

example_sentences.japanese: 証人として、遠回しに言わずに率直に君の質問に答えさせてもらうよ。ああ、あのフグが確かに君のプリンを食べていたね。
example_sentences.english: As a witness, I won’t beat around the bush, I’ll answer your question frankly. Yeah, that Fugu was absolutely eating your pudding.

notes: "Remember how 動物 means animal? Well when you add park it becomes a zoo. It's a park for animals. Except the animals can't leave. Ever." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ヤクザだって動物園に来ることもあるさ。
example_sentences.english: Even yakuza can come to the zoo.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物園で間近で見たフラミンゴは、とてもきれいでした。
example_sentences.english: The flamingos looked so beautiful when I saw them up close at a zoological garden.

example_sentences.japanese: 多くのコアラはコアラレトロウィルスというウイルスを先天的に保持しており、ストレスなどを受けると、リンパ腫など死につながる病気を発症してしまいます。ですので、動物園に行かれた際は、カメラのフラッシュや大声を出すなどしないよう、十分気をつけてください。
example_sentences.english: Many koala bears have an innate virus called koala retrovirus and it often causes a life-threatening diseases like lymphoma when they get stressed out, so please make sure not to use your camera's flash or speak loudly when you go to the menagerie.

notes: "The Love Know Prefecture! I want to live here, because people must know love! Of course, we don't call it that in English. You'll have to know the reading of the kanji to know the reading of this prefecture, which is Aichi Prefecture (jump to the reading to figure this out)." "The reading here is all the on'yomi jukugo madness you can handle. If you learned the kanji, you should be able to read this. If you can read it, you can translate it to ""English"" even though only half of it is English."

example_sentences.japanese: 愛知県には、美しい梅林があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a beautiful ume grove in Aichi Prefecture.

example_sentences.japanese: 愛知県は、そろそろ梅雨入りです。
example_sentences.english: Aichi Prefecture is gradually entering the rainy season.

example_sentences.japanese: フグが日本の愛知県に引っ越した後、サーモンが切ない思いをしていることを、誰一人知らなかった。
example_sentences.english: After Fugu moved to Japan’s Aichi Prefecture, no one knew of Salmon’s hopeless longing for him.

notes: "You know that 建築 is architecture. So, someone of house architecture is someone who does architecture. They are an architect." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will also help if you know how to read 建築 already."

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、あんたが建築家になったから、鼻が高いのよ。
example_sentences.english: Dad is very proud of you because you became an architect.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者は、その建築家をあやまって胃がんだとしんだんしました。
example_sentences.english: The doctor incorrectly diagnosed the architect with stomach cancer.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家は有名な建築家によって設計されたんですよ。
example_sentences.english: My house was designed by a famous architect.

notes: "The original child of everything is the atom. It is the child from which everything else is created, for it was the original child. Atoms are the building blocks of all things!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: しょう来は、原子エネルギーの勉強をしたいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: In the future, I think I want to study atomic energy.

example_sentences.japanese: この原子の原子番号と原子記号は何だったっけ？
example_sentences.english: What was the atomic number and atomic symbol of this atom?

example_sentences.japanese: 老朽化した原子力発電所は、多くの国々にとって悩みの種です。
example_sentences.english: Aging nuclear power plants are a problem for many countries.

english: Before Christ, Bc, Bce, Before Common Era
notes: "Remember how 紀元後 is ""After death"" or ""AD""? Well, this is the opposite because it has a before (前) in it. It's BC or Before Christ." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will also help if you know how to read 紀元後 already, because then you'll just have to remember the 前."

example_sentences.japanese: きょうりゅうがいたのは、紀元前何年ごろまでですか。
example_sentences.english: Until about what year before Christ did the dinosaurs exist?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のコウイチは、自分は紀元前の古代ローマからタイムスリップしてきた男だって言いはってきかないんです。
example_sentences.english: This Kochi keeps insisting that he's a man who time traveled from pre-Christian, Ancient Rome.

example_sentences.japanese: もしタイムマシーンがあったなら、紀元前三千年紀に行ってみたいな。
example_sentences.english: If time machines existed, I would want to go to 3000 B.C.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This vocab uses the same reading as the one you learned with the kanji. Well played!

example_sentences.japanese: くつの底にガムがついてるよ。
example_sentences.english: There’s gum stuck to the bottom of your shoe.

example_sentences.japanese: 底無しぬまに泳ぎに行くなんて、無茶だよ。
example_sentences.english: It's ridiculous to go swimming in the bottomless swamp.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのお陰で、日本語がペラペラになりました。心の底から感謝しています。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to Tofugu, I'm now fluent in Japanese. I thank them from the bottom of my heart.

hiragana: いぎりすじん, イギリスじん
notes: "You've probably seen 英国 for ""England"" already. This is just another version I wanted to make sure you knew about. Not kanji, sure, but it's a little more common than 英国 so I wanted to make sure you got it here. To stay with the spirit of ""learning kanji"" though, we've added 人 to the end. I bet you can guess the meaning of this already. English + Person = English Person or British Person." "The first part's reading is just in katakana. The second part is the じん from 人."

example_sentences.japanese: あの鼻すじの通ったイギリス人は、鼻にかかった声で話します。
example_sentences.english: That British person with the straight nose speaks in a nasal voice.

example_sentences.japanese: このイギリス人は、梅ずを飲んだことがないそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently, this English person hasn't tried ume vinegar before.

example_sentences.japanese: 知らないイギリス人から友達申請が来たよ。
example_sentences.english: I got a friend request from some English person I don't know.

notes: "An eating hall is a big room in which you eat. What big rooms do you eat in? How about a cafeteria or dining hall?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この食堂の店主は、古くさい男で、男は家庭のことに干渉すべきではないと主ちょうするんです。
example_sentences.english: The owner of this diner is so old fashioned that he insists that men shouldn't interfere in domestic matters.

example_sentences.japanese: さっきトーフグ食堂に行ったんだけど、無名の歌手が無料のワンマンライブをしてたよ。
example_sentences.english: When I went to the Tofugu dining hall a while ago, there was free live music from some singer I didn't know.

example_sentences.japanese: お昼ごはん、食堂で食べない？もしよければ、私二限目のクラスが無いから、席取っておけるよ。
example_sentences.english: Do you want to eat lunch in the cafeteria? If so, I don’t have a second period class, so I could find some seats for us.

hiragana: おととい, いっさくじつ, おとつい
english: Day Before Last, Day Before Yesterday
notes: "Remember how you learned that 昨日 means ""yesterday?"" Well one day previous to that day is the day before last. " "This reading is an exception. Let's use this mnemonic to remember it:The day before last you bought an ""O"" toe toy (おととい). It's a kid's toy in the shape of the letter O that you put on your toe. You know it was the day before last because you wore it all yesterday, and now today your toe is sore. If only you could go back to the day before yesterday to tell yourself not to buy that O toe toy! Or at least not to wear it for the whole next day!"

example_sentences.japanese: 今さらですが一昨日の5月5日はルフィのたん生日でした。
example_sentences.english: It's a bit late, but the day before yesterday, May 5, was Luffy's birthday.

example_sentences.japanese: 一昨日だったら空いてたんだけど、今月は他の日は全てうまってしまってるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I was available the day before last, but this month all of my other days are entirely full already.

example_sentences.japanese: 一昨日、夫の不倫現場を見てしまったんです。
example_sentences.english: The day before last I caught my husband cheating on me.

notes: "Someone from the outside who comes in to mix with the government is a diplomat. Really, that's what diplomats do, right? They come from the outside (country). They mix with the government, and they do what they're there to do!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの外交官は、どうしてけっこんして身を固めないんだろう。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why that diplomat doesn't get married and settle down.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のおじは外交官で、世界に数台しかないギターを他の国の外交官からプレゼントされました。
example_sentences.english: My uncle is a diplomat and a diplomat from another country gave him a rare guitar, which is one of only a few that exist in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は外交官で、どうしても今日日本に飛ばなければいけないんです。空席待ちをさせてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: I’m a diplomat and I really need to fly to Japan today, so could you put me on the waiting list?

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well (drama). Can also mean play or show as well." The reading is the same as the kanji. No more drama from you, okay?

example_sentences.japanese: オペラ劇を観劇しに行く天皇へい下をお見送りしました。
example_sentences.english: I saw off the emperor, who was going to see the opera.

example_sentences.japanese: この劇の第2幕第3場で馬の役をしているのがオレの兄貴なんだ。
example_sentences.english: The person who plays the role of the horse in Act II Scene III of this play is my older brother.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の席の人が劇の最中にずっと指をポキポキ鳴らしてて、すっごく苛々しました。
example_sentences.english: The person next to me was constantly cracking their knuckles during the show and it was so annoying.

notes: "Remember how 天気 is weather (and how 天 often refers to sky things?). Well, when those sky things are dry, you have dry weather." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: れんぞく干天日数が二十九日をむかえ、フグは干からびるすん前だった。
example_sentences.english: Because of the continuous, twenty-nine day drought, Fugu is about to dry out.

example_sentences.japanese: 無じ悲な干天がつづき、はたけのやさいが全てかれてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The long, cruel dry weather killed all the vegetables in my field.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチから腹ペコの社員への差し入れのベーコンは、まさに干天の慈雨だった。
example_sentences.english: The supply of bacon Koichi got for the starving workers was like a welcome rain after a drought.

notes: "The East side is the East side." "Remember how 東口 read as ひがしぐち? This word is like that too, with 東 being read as ひがし. 側 is read like you learned it with the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: 寒天工場なら、その道路の東側にあります。
example_sentences.english: The agar factory is on the east side of that street.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらは、地中海東側の地いきで食べられている料理です。
example_sentences.english: This is a dish that's eaten in the Eastern region of the Mediterranean.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行場の東側なので、ダンダス通りを真っ直ぐ東側に三十分ぐらい行くと着きますよ。
example_sentences.english: It’s on the east side of the airport, so just go east on Dundas for about thirty minutes.

english: Evil Breeds Evil, Evil Begets Evil
notes: "Things that cause evil are the fruits of evil. This is a nice little saying. In English, you might say it as evil breeds evil. Remember that." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The last 悪果 gets the 悪 shortened a little bit."

example_sentences.japanese: ぜん因ぜん果悪因悪果って言うだろ？当然のむくいだよ。
example_sentences.english: "They say ""evil begets evil"" right? So they just got properly punished."

example_sentences.japanese: 悪いことをしたら、悪因悪果で後々ひどい目にあうよ。
example_sentences.english: If you do something bad, you'll get in trouble later because evil breeds evil.

example_sentences.japanese: 聖書には、業について何て書いてあるんだっけ？悪因悪果とかだっけか？
example_sentences.english: "What does the Bible say about karma? Was it like ""evil begets evil"" or something?"

notes: "A fruit thing is just fruit." "The reading for this is an exception, at least for the 果 portion. To remember this part, imagine yourself asking for some fruit. Could I (くだ) have some fruit, please?"

example_sentences.japanese: 果物の中では、無花果が一番好きです。
example_sentences.english: Out of all fruit, I like figs the best.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子は野さいはきらいですが、トマトだけは果物だと思っているようで食べてくれるんです。
example_sentences.english: My kid doesn't like veggies, but apparently he thinks the tomato is a fruit so he eats them.

example_sentences.japanese: 「果物屋さんが閉まるまでに、仕事終わりそう？」「大丈夫。もし終わらなかったら明日に回すよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you think you’ll finish your work before the fruit shop closes?"" ""Don’t worry. If I can’t finish, I’ll just leave it for tomorrow."""

notes: "You helped your city prosper, and a light shines out of you, so that the entire city can bask in your glory." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回、勝利の栄光にかがやいたのは、トーフグチームです！
example_sentences.english: The team that won a glorious victory this time is Team Tofugu!

example_sentences.japanese: か去の栄光をなつかしそうに語る大人にだけはなりたくありません。
example_sentences.english: I never want to be an adult who speaks nostalgically of the glory days.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの栄光の瞬間は、二十二歳でブロガーのチャンピオンになった時にやって来た。
example_sentences.english: At twenty-two, Koichi’s moment of glory came when he became a champion blogger.

notes: "Government gold (aka money) is what makes up government funds." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 間違っても官金に手を出んじゃないぞ！
example_sentences.english: No matter what happens, never misuse government money!

example_sentences.japanese: 保育園まで公用車に子どもを乗せて行くことは、ある意味で官金の私消に当たると思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you think dropping off a child at a daycare using a public car is a misuse of government money in any way?

example_sentences.japanese: 金曜日に親友が一万ドルの公的資金を濫用したとして官金私消罪で逮捕されたのだが、私には彼女がそんなことをしたとは思えない。
example_sentences.english: My best friend was arrested on Friday for the embezzlement of over $10,000 of government funds, but I doubt she actually did it.

notes: "You have memorized an illusion. You see it there, as if it's real, as if it's in your memory and brain. But it's not real. It's a hallucination." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは時々、ポッドキャストをレコーディングしている時に幻覚を起こしてしまうんだ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi sometimes has hallucinations while recording podcasts.

example_sentences.japanese: この映像を見る時は、部屋を明るくしてはなれて見ないと、幻覚が見えてくるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: When you watch this video, you have to watch in a well-lit place, not too close to the screen, otherwise I heard you'll have hallucinations.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは幻覚作用のあるキノコを食べたせいで、幻覚に襲われていたに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Fugu must have been hallucinating from the hallucinogenic mushrooms he ate.

notes: "Try singing a nose song. How does it sound? Like humming perhaps?" "The readings are both kun'yomi vocab readings, probably because a 鼻 is a body part, and body parts do that to jukugo words. You know 鼻's reading from the kanji (はな) and you know 歌's reading from the vocabulary word 歌 (うた). Combine them together and you have a very nice humming tune and reading, はなうた."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、鼻をふくらませながら、鼻歌を歌っていた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi was humming while making his nose swell.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは鼻歌まじりで楽しそうに自転車に乗っていました。
example_sentences.english: Viet was happily riding his bicycle while humming.

example_sentences.japanese: 爆笑！お前鼻歌下手すぎだっつーの。
example_sentences.english: LMAO! You are just terrible at humming.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. You can add phantom to the meanings as well, because phantoms are kind of like illusions." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You look up to see a crazy illusion. You can't believe it's real. Master Roshi, from Dragonball, is standing in front of you (you thought he was a cartoon!). Then, he splits into a million versions of himself, creating a mob of Roshis (まぼろし). This mob goes on to train many people to fight."

example_sentences.japanese: この薬を飲むと、幻が見えますよ。
example_sentences.english: You'll be able to see apparitions if you take this drug.

example_sentences.japanese: 幻の魚をつかまえたぞ！
example_sentences.english: I caught a phantom fish!

example_sentences.japanese: 恍惚状態の中でサーモンの幻を何度も見た後に、フグはようやく彼女が12年前に死んだことを思い出し、自分が幻を見ていたことに気づいた。
example_sentences.english: After a series of ecstasy filled visions of Salmon, Fugu finally remembered she had been dead for 12 years, and he realized he was seeing an illusion.

notes: "A diagram theory is an illustration that is used as an explanatory diagram. Just imagine a chalk board with all sorts of drawings of things, showing how they work, at least in theory." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 図説付きの参考書をさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for a textbook with illustrations.

example_sentences.japanese: アヤが、トーフグ社内の人間関係の図説を作ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: Aya made an explanatory diagram of the in-house Tofugu relationships.

example_sentences.japanese: もし解説と共に図説があれば、より分かりやすくなるかと思うんですが、如何でしょうか？
example_sentences.english: I think it would be easier to understand if there was an illustration with an explanation, what do you think?

english: Internal Cause, Actual Reason, Intrinsic, Endogenous
notes: "The inside cause is an internal cause. Internal causes are usually the nastiest causes, if you ask me." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 内因性ぜんそくだとしんだんされました。
example_sentences.english: I was diagnosed with intrinsic asthma.

example_sentences.japanese: トラウマになる出来事が起きると、その苦しみを和らげるために、内因性オピオイドというのう内ま薬が分ぴつされます。
example_sentences.english: When a traumatic thing happens, endogenous opioids, which are morphine-like substances, will be secreted.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は長い間内因性精神疾患に悩まされています。
example_sentences.english: For a long time the actual reason I’ve been suffering was a mental disorder.

notes: "Let me transmit to you a theory... a theory that perhaps a great legend is true." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You just have to remember that 伝 is read as でん in this case. Just imagine yourself sitting in your den (でん) as you get cozy and listen to this theory about a great legend."

example_sentences.japanese: アイルランドの伝説の英ゆうと言われれば、だれを思いうかべますか？
example_sentences.english: "When you hear ""a legendary Irish hero,"" who comes to mind?"

example_sentences.japanese: お前めちゃくちゃモテるな！マジで伝説的だよ。
example_sentences.english: Girls love you, man. You are legendary, seriously!

example_sentences.japanese: 伝説によると、この海には豆腐を食べるフグが住んでいるそうです。
example_sentences.english: According to a legend, there is a fugu eating tofu in this ocean.

notes:
"When you have romance you also have love! The romantic kind of mushy, gushy love. Be careful though. This word doesn't share its meaning with its kanji. But, that's how romance is. It gets all crazy and turns to love really fast." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: Your love isn't toward a person, it's toward this giant Koi (こい) fish you met the other day. The fish is just so... so... handsome! You get hearts popping above your head every time you think about this koi!"

"The circumstance was caused by the idea I had. Because I had this idea before the circumstance, it shows I had intention of doing it. I did it on purpose." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 今まで、恋に恋したことはあっても、本当にだれかに恋したことは無かったんです。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to fall in love, but I'd never actually fallen for anyone until now.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンちゃん、なんかかわいくなったよな。恋する女って感じじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Don't you think Salmon got prettier? I think it's because she's a woman in love, don't you?

example_sentences.japanese: フグのことが頭から離れないの。これって恋の始まりなのかな？
example_sentences.english: I can’t get Fugu out of my head! Is there love in the air?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの秘密のベーコンを故意に食べた罪を認めます。
example_sentences.english: I plead guilty to intentionally eating Koichi’s secret bacon.

example_sentences.japanese: 鯉に餌をあげないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please do not feed the carp.

notes: "The person you make love to is your lover. Woooh! Don't worry I won't tell. Have fun and be safe, kids." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの愛人は、少し鼻にかかったみ力的な声をしていました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's lover had an attractive, slightly nasal voice.

example_sentences.japanese: お前は愛人にすらなれなかったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: You couldn’t even be his lover!

example_sentences.japanese: 愛人の是非については、判断しかねますね。
example_sentences.english: I'm ambivalent about whether a mistress is acceptable or not.

notes:
"The main cause is the main cause or the primary cause." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"A vermillion colored seal is a red seal. Just look up the (Japanese) word in Google Image search and you'll see what this is." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 下りの主因はおそらくさっき食べたソフトクリームです。
example_sentences.english: The primary cause of my diarrhea is probably the soft serve I ate just now.

example_sentences.japanese: ニアミスの主因は、この電車がスピードを上げるべきではないタイミングで上げたことです。
example_sentences.english: The main cause behind the near-miss is that the train sped up when it wasn't supposed to.

example_sentences.japanese: 癌や自閉症など、多くの病気の主因は未だに分かっていません。
example_sentences.english: The main causes behind many conditions like cancer and autism are still unknown.

example_sentences.japanese: この紙に御朱印を押してもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Could I get the red seal of the shogun on this paper?

notes: "Medicine things are medicines and drugs. Try not to take too many of these, now!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今すぐ薬物をやめろ！」とさけびながら、コウイチはビエトの鼻を人さし指で指した。
example_sentences.english: "Koichi screamed, ""Stop doing drugs right now!"" and pointed at Viet's nose with his index finger."

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは、ヤクザの世界からも、薬物からも、完全に足をあらった。
example_sentences.english: Viet made a clean break from both the yakuza world and drugs.

example_sentences.japanese: 今までに何か薬物によってアレルギー反応が引き起こされたことはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Have you ever had an allergic reaction to any medicines?

notes: "A soldier member (or a member of the soldiers) is a person that is of the military personnel. It also shows the amount of military strength an army has. The more soldier members, the more military strength and military personnel it has!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 兵員たちはみんな、かぜにかかって鼻がつまっている。
example_sentences.english: All of the military personnel have colds and stuffy noses.

example_sentences.japanese: 兵員がにげ出さないよう、ドアには外側からかぎがかけられていた。
example_sentences.english: The door was locked from the outside so that the military personnel wouldn't run away.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグ軍の改革のため、コウイチは兵員の数を削減をしなくてはならなかった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of the Tofugu army reform, Koichi had to reduce the amount of military strength they had.

notes: "A water soldier is a soldier that is out to sea. That is a navy soldier." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの水兵が、船長にふるえ声で何かを話しているのを見てしまったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I happened to see the seaman saying something to the captain in a shaky voice.

example_sentences.japanese: かわいい水兵服と水兵ぼうが売っていたので、まごに買ってあげました。
example_sentences.english: I found a cute sailor uniform and a sailor cap, so I bought them for my grandchild.

example_sentences.japanese: その演劇で水兵を演じた素晴らしい俳優は、観客を大いに沸かせた。
example_sentences.english: The brilliant actor who played a navy soldier in the play really wow’d the audience.

notes: "If rest is nothing then there are no holidays. If there are no holidays, then that means a place is always open." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは大てい無休で働いている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi usually works without taking holidays.

example_sentences.japanese: カナとマミは、無休でワニカニの例文を作っています。
example_sentences.english: Kana and Mami are making WaniKani example sentences without any breaks.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguのウェブサイトは、24時間年中無休で開いております。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu’s website is always open, twenty-four hours a day, every day of the year.

notes: "A nose with blood is a nose with a nosebleed. It is a bloody nose." "The readings are the kun'yomi vocab readings. You already know 鼻's reading from the kanji and vocab, and you should know the vocab reading of 血 as well. Put them together and you have はなち, though you want to change the ち to ぢ. Alternatively, it's possible (though less common, but it doesn't matter if you're turning it to kanji via an IME anyways) to write it as はなじ. I guess that blood added a little tenten (it represents the blood coming out of that nose!). Spurt spurt spurt."

example_sentences.japanese: 鼻の下にひげをはやしていると、鼻血が出た時に大変ですね。
example_sentences.english: If you have a mustache it'll be a pain if your nose bleeds, right?

example_sentences.japanese: すみません。ちょっと一言、言わせてもらいたいんだけど、あなた、鼻血が出てますよ。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me. I just need a quick word with you. Your nose is bleeding.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車に駆け込み乗車をしようとして鼻が挟まれて、鼻血が出ました。
example_sentences.english: I tried to rush onto the train, but the doors closed, squished my nose and made it bleed.

notes: "You know that an お願い is a request, and that 事 is a ""thing"" or ""action."" So, this is a ""request action,"" in a sense. A better way to say that is one's wish or a prayer, because that's what you're doing when you do the action of requesting something." "The readings come from the words お願い and 事. If you know how to read those you should be able to read this word too."

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの願い事は、きっとすぐにかなうと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think your prayers will be answered soon.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはいつも、願い事を書いた紙をそばにおいてねます。
example_sentences.english: When Koichi goes to sleep he always keeps a piece of paper with his wishes written on it nearby.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人は、人生の節目節目に、願い事だけでなく感謝の気持ちを伝えるために、神社を訪れます。
example_sentences.english: Japanese people visit shrines on important occasions not only to make wishes but also to offer thanks.

notes: "When you have love for your country deep within your heart, that is patriotism." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 愛国心がやたらに強い男が、トーフグに入社しました。
example_sentences.english: A very patriotic man entered Tofugu.

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルが、愛国心あふれるチップチューンの曲を作曲しました。
example_sentences.english: Michael composed a very patriotic 8-bit song.

example_sentences.japanese: あの国が、誤った教育を通じて子どもたちに愛国心を植え付けようとしているのは好ましくないと思います。
example_sentences.english: I don’t like that the country is trying to instill patriotism in children through misguided education.

notes: "When medicine is sent to your direction it's going to you. That's your  prescription." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者にもらった薬方を失くしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I lost the prescription that the doctor had given me.

example_sentences.japanese: 字がきたなすぎて、薬方に何が書いてあるのかさっぱり分かりません。
example_sentences.english: The handwriting is so messy that I don't understand what's written on the prescription at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い薬方の中には、危険であるということで現代医療からは除かれているものもある。
example_sentences.english: Some of the old prescriptions were considered to be dangerous and have been removed from use in modern medicine.

english: Public Behavior, Public Behaviour, Official Stance, Public Position, Public Face, Tatemae
notes: "What you build up in front of other people is your public image. This is your public behavior, how you act around others you don't really know. This concept is surprisingly important in Japan, so you'll hear it often enough despite being such a strange concept in other places. You'll have to think of this like you're building buildings of personality in front of you. These show off who you are on the outside, but it protects what's on the inside." "The reading is pretty strange. It's a lot like 建物 in that it's read as たて, which is like the word 建てる even though the て isn't showing here. So, you'll have to remember it's read like 建てる but the て gets pushed into the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトは本音と建前を使い分けるのが上手い。
example_sentences.english: Viet is good at separating his public and private selves.

example_sentences.japanese: しょうかいじょうが無いとここの医者にみてもらえないというのは建前です。
example_sentences.english: Our official stance is that you can't see a doctor here without a letter of reference.

example_sentences.japanese: よく「本音と建前」は日本独特の文化だと言われますが、実際は世界中に存在します。
example_sentences.english: "It’s often said that ""the contrast between one’s personal feelings and public behavior"" is a characteristic unique to Japanese culture, but that exists all over the world."

notes: "The river bottom is the river bottom, also known as the riverbed. " "The readings are the readings you learned with the kanji. Just don't forget the rendaku for 底!"

example_sentences.japanese: あの辺りは川底が深いので気を付けてください。
example_sentences.english: The river is deep around there, so be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: この川は、川底にかなりのすながたまってしまっています。
example_sentences.english: There's a lot of sand on the bed in this river.

example_sentences.japanese: 「サーモンはゴールデンウィーク期間中何してたの？」「結婚指輪を川で無くしちゃって、ずっと探してたの。三日もかかったけど、ようやく川底に沈んでいる指輪を見つけたわ。」
example_sentences.english: """What did you do during Golden Week, Salmon?"" ""I lost my wedding ring in a river, so I was looking for it. It took me three days, but I finally found it buried in the riverbed."""

notes:
The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, no extra salt needed.

The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: If you think of the tide, you think of the ocean. If you think of the ocean and what it's filled with (besides water) you think of salt (しお)."

example_sentences.japanese: もう少し塩が多い方が良いかもしれませんね。
example_sentences.english: It might be better with a little more salt.

example_sentences.japanese: 一才になるまで赤ちゃんには塩をあげない方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: Until your baby turns one, you shouldn't give them any salt.

example_sentences.japanese: けしからん！一体どうやってそんなに馬鹿なことが出来るんだ？砂糖と塩を入れ替えるなんて、いくら今日がエイプリルフールだからといっても、ちっともおもしろくないぞ。お前が馬鹿者だ！
example_sentences.english: Oh my God! I can’t believe you could be so stupid! Replacing salt and sugar is not funny at all, even if it’s April Fool’s Day today. You are the fool!

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットで調べたら潮の満ち引きの時刻が分かるんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Can’t we find out when the tide rises by looking online?

hiragana: しおみず, えんすい
notes: "Water with salt in it is salt water. Best not to drink 塩水." "The readings are the kun'yomi vocab readings. You know 塩's from the kanji and you know 水's from the vocab word 水. Combine them together and you have しおみず."

example_sentences.japanese: 鼻が利く方だと思っていたんだが、どちらが塩水か分からなかった。
example_sentences.english: I thought I had a good nose, but I couldn't tell which one was salt water.

example_sentences.japanese: 塩水につけて天日干ししたフグってきっと美味しくなると思うんだけどなあ。
example_sentences.english: I think puffer fish dipped in salt water and dried in the sun would be pretty tasty.

example_sentences.japanese: 気温はそんなに高くないけど、日差しは強いから、熱射病対策で塩水を持って行った方がいいんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: The temperature itself isn't that high, but the sun's rays are really strong, so why don't you take some salt water to prevent heatstroke?

notes: "Gender love is that kind of love that has to do with gender parts. That's sexual love." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学で、性愛学について勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm studying sexual love at university.

example_sentences.japanese: 他人の夫婦の性愛に口出しするなんて、下品にもほどがあるよ。
example_sentences.english: Interfering with another married couple's sexual love is just indecent.

example_sentences.japanese: 性欲が無いのか性愛恐怖症なのか自分では判断できません。
example_sentences.english: I’m not sure if I’m asexual or have erotophobia.

notes: "A soldier samurai is still just another soldier." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの兵士の泣き声が頭からはなれません。
example_sentences.english: I cannot get the soldier's cry out of my head.

example_sentences.japanese: その兵士はコウイチの車に火を付けた。
example_sentences.english: The soldier set Koichi’s car on fire.

example_sentences.japanese: 仲間がいないといつもの道が遠く感じると思いながら、兵士は足早に歩いた。
example_sentences.english: The soldier walked at a brisk pace thinking about how long distances feel much longer without any companions.
