The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: あの兵が、無力な子供たちにドーナツを投げつけたんだ！
example_sentences.english: That soldier threw donuts at helpless children!

example_sentences.japanese: たくさんの兵たちが、梅毒に苦しんでいました。
example_sentences.english: Many troops suffered from syphilis.

example_sentences.japanese: ここで、アメリカ兵たちがよく屯しています。
example_sentences.english: The American army frequently gathers here.

example_sentences.japanese: ブロック塀の取付け費用がいくらかかるのかが知りたいんですが。
example_sentences.english: I want to know how much concrete-block wall installation will cost.

english: Tip Of The Nose, Tip Of Nose, Nose Tip
notes: "You know the previous part of your nose? The part of your nose I just chopped off? Well, you were lucky, as that was only the tip of the nose. Time to cut off the rest, next!" "The readings are the kun'yomi vocab readings. With 鼻 you learned that with the kanji. With 先 you learned that with the vocab. So, you should have all the pieces to be able to read this. Remember, body parts tend to change words into kun'yomi readings for some reason, no exception here."

example_sentences.japanese: 鼻先にマスタードがついてるよ。
example_sentences.english: You got mustard at the tip of your nose.

example_sentences.japanese: その警察犬は、鼻先をひくひくさせて、見知らぬ人のにおいをかぎ始めた。
example_sentences.english: That police dog started twitching his the tip of its nose and sniffing at the stranger.

example_sentences.japanese: フグはサーモンの鼻先が赤くなってるのを見て、とても可愛いと感じた。
example_sentences.english: When Fugu saw that the tip of Salmon’s nose was so red, he found it very cute.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji. It's also the same as the meaning of the kanji / vocab, though you can think of this as  Japanese plum as well if you want."

example_sentences.japanese: 梅の花がさき始めました。
example_sentences.english: Japanese plum trees started to bloom.

example_sentences.japanese: 「こんなにたくさんの梅の実、どうしたの？」「今日、梅園に行ってきたんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Where did you get this many ume?"" ""I visited an ume orchard today."""

example_sentences.japanese: 給料日が来たら、一粒一万円もする高級梅干を買ってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: As soon as payday comes, I’ll buy the high grade, pickled Japanese plums that costs 10,000 yen a piece.

english: Ume Wine, Plum Wine, Plum Liquor, Umeshu
notes: "Alcohol that comes from ume is ume wine. It can also be called plum wine or plum liquor. If you're of age give it a taste, it's quite nice!" The reading is just the readings of the kanji that you learned. How about a toast to easy to read words!

example_sentences.japanese: 風ろ上がりに梅酒を開けると、一本飲み切るまで止まりません。
example_sentences.english: When I open a can of ume wine after taking a bath, I can't stop until I've finished it.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では、電車の中で梅酒を飲んでもいいんですか？
example_sentences.english: Is that okay to drink plum wine on the trains in Japan?

example_sentences.japanese: よっしゃ〜花金だ〜。今夜の自家製梅酒が待ち遠しい。
example_sentences.english: Thank God it’s Friday! I’m looking forward to drinking homemade plum wine tonight.

notes: "Remember how 米国 is ""America."" Well, more of that again. With 米 representing ""America"" you can combine that with 兵 (soldier) to have yourself a US soldier / American soldier." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの米兵は、どうして鼻めがねをかけているの？
example_sentences.english: Why is that US soldier wearing pince-nez glasses?

example_sentences.japanese: ここは米兵がたくさん通るから、通行のじゃまをしないようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: Lots of American soldiers walk through here, so please make sure you're not in their way.

example_sentences.japanese: 「すごい。今日は本当にいいお天気だね！今日こそ腹筋三百回が出来そうな気がする。」と、米兵は言った。
example_sentences.english: """Wow. What beautiful weather! I feel like I'll finally be able to do 300 sit ups today,"" said an American soldier."

notes: "When how much you prosper goes into your heart and just enters a void, it will rarely mean anything to you. A person who has this trait is going to have extreme vanity because he/she just needs to suck more and more prosperity into their bottomless pit of a heart. It's like a black hole. They need more and more and more so then they have to become vain." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 虚栄心の強い人は、男でも女でも苦手です。
example_sentences.english: I don't like vain people, regardless of their gender.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の虚栄心に度々きずつけられます。
example_sentences.english: I get hurt by my own vanity from time to time.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguソフトボールチームに入る際の第一規則は、虚栄心をベンチに置いておくことです。
example_sentences.english: The first rule of Tofugu’s softball team is that you have to leave your vanity on the bench.

english: Victory Or Defeat, Win Or Lose, Outcome
notes: "You have win and you have failure. When you are talking about both in one word, you have victory or defeat." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その戦いの勝敗なら、一昨日の朝決まりましたよ。
example_sentences.english: The game's outcome was decided on the morning of the day before last.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのその一言が、勝敗の分かれ目になったんです。
example_sentences.english: That one word Koichi said made the difference between victory and defeat.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の両親はいつも、全力を尽くしさえすれば、勝敗は問題ではないと言っていたけれど、私はそれが好きじゃありませんでした。もちろん、私は勝敗をとても気にします。だって、ベストを尽くした後に負けるなんて、意味が無いじゃないですか。
example_sentences.english: My parents always told me that it doesn’t matter if I win or lose, as long as I try my best, but I didn’t like that. Of course, I care very much about winning and losing. If I lose after doing my best, then there’s no point.

notes: "You know that 笑う is ""to laugh."" This is the noun version, because the う in 笑う turns to い (so don't confuse this as an adjective). What is the noun version of ""to laugh""? It's a laugh." "The reading is the same as 笑う, so just make sure you know that so you can know this as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本ではクリスマスディナーにケンタッキーを食べると言ったら、なぜか笑いが起きました。
example_sentences.english: Everybody laughed for some reason when I said that people eat KFC for Christmas dinner.

example_sentences.japanese: もうかれ自身多分何を笑ってるのか分からないけどただ笑いが止まらないっていうじょうたいなんだと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I feel like he probably doesn't even know what he's laughing at anymore, but he just can't help it.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画を見て泣くなんて、お前らしくないじゃないか。いつもどの映画のどんな深刻なシーンにも大笑いしてるのに。
example_sentences.english: It’s not like you to cry at movies. You always laugh really hard when there are any serious scenes in them.

notes: "The path of the bow. This is archery." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 弓道はむずかしいという結ろんに達しました。
example_sentences.english: I came to the conclusion that kyudo is difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の弓道の弓って、どうしてそんなに強いの？
example_sentences.english: Why are Japanese bows for kyudo so powerful?

example_sentences.japanese: 「一生懸命何しているの？」「弓道だよ。」
example_sentences.english: """What are you working on?"" ""Japanese Archery."""

hiragana: こくえん, くろけむり
notes: "Black smoke is black smoke. It's also something you should avoid if you can." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 黒煙のせいで、熱気がこもって息苦しかった。
example_sentences.english: The air was hot and stuffy from the black smoke.

example_sentences.japanese: あなただけがあの黒煙をすいこんだわけじゃないのよ。
example_sentences.english: You're not the only person who inhaled the black smoke.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はバスの運転手になるのを楽しみにしていたんですが、息子から、「バスが黒煙をまき散らしていることを知りながら、それでもバスの運転手を続けたいなら、排気管からの黒煙を少し吸ってみるといい」と言われました。
example_sentences.english: I was looking forward to being a bus driver but then my son told me buses spread black smoke, and that if I still want to be a bus driver, then I should try inhaling some of that black smoke that comes out of my exhaust pipe.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You have your bow and you use it to shoot things, sure, but you've also covered it in candy so you can eat it when you're waiting out in the woods waiting for a buck to come by. You lick your candy bow and say: ""yummy!"" (ゆみ). Imagine the taste of your bow. What taste would make you say yummy?"

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの弓がどこにも見当たらないんだ。
example_sentences.english: We can't find Koichi's bow anywhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 弓を引くには、まず上半身を安定させなくてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You have to stabilize your upper body to draw the bow.

example_sentences.japanese: うん、ローソンは確かに二十四時間営業だよ。でもさぁ、あのー、多分弓と矢は置いてないと思うよ？
example_sentences.english: Yeah, Lawson is open 24/7, but, you know, I don’t think they carry bows and arrows.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji. Don't have to use your brain for that."

example_sentences.japanese: アイツは本当に脳が弱いよな。
example_sentences.english: He has no brains.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっとは脳を使って考えろよ！
example_sentences.english: Use your brain when you think!

example_sentences.japanese: この国の人たちは脳を食べるってこと、知ってる？珍味なんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Did you know that people eat brains in this country? It’s a delicacy.

notes: "A Buddha priest is a Buddhist Priest." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの仏僧は、あと一ヶ月で九十九才に達します。
example_sentences.english: That Buddhist priest will reach the age of ninety-nine in one month.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのダジャレがつまらなさすぎて、仏僧ははとがまめ鉄っぽうを食ったような顔をしていた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's pun was so lame that the Buddhist priest looked like a deer in headlights.

example_sentences.japanese: その魔女は仏僧の心をも燃え上がらせた。
example_sentences.english: The witch set even the Buddhist priest’s heart on fire.

notes: "You hopefully know that 証明 means ""proof."" So, when the proof is written down, what kind of proof is it? It's a certificate of some kind. I'm going to need to see some 証明書 if you want to get in here, sir." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Knowing 証明's reading will also be helpful."

example_sentences.japanese: 電車の中に証明書が入ったかばんを忘れてきてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I forgot my bag with the certificate on the train.

example_sentences.japanese: 証明書のていじは必要ですか？
example_sentences.english: Do I have to show my credentials?

example_sentences.japanese: 身分証明書をご提示頂けますか？
example_sentences.english: Could I check your ID?

notes: "You know how 守る is ""to protect,"" right? This is like that, but it's the noun version. It's not really ""a protection,"" though it kind of is. What things can you wear to protect you from things like bad luck, demons, and ancient aliens? That would be a charm or an amulet. You'll see these kinds of things sold at temples and such." "The reading is like that of 守る, so if you know the reading of that word you should be able to read this one as well."

example_sentences.japanese: このお守り、どのぐらいお借りしていてもいいですか？
example_sentences.english: How long can I have this charm for?

example_sentences.japanese: お守りを入れるのを忘れちゃったみたい。
example_sentences.english: It seems I forgot to pack my amulet.

example_sentences.japanese: たくさんのお守りを同時に付けない方がいいですよ。逆に不幸をもたらすかもしれないですからね。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn’t wear multiple lucky amulets at the same time. It could bring you bad luck instead.

notes: "You know that 笑う is ""to laugh."" This is a noun version of that, though it's not ""a laugh,"" (that's 笑い). Add お to that and you have the thing that makes you laugh. It's comedy. It's the joke that's elevated with お because it made you laugh SOOOOO much. Haha!" "The reading is the same 笑う or 笑い. It's also the same as what you learned with the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルがトーフグに入る時に間ちがえてメイン州のポートランドに引っこしてしまったことは、今でもみんなのお笑い草です。
example_sentences.english: When Michael got a job at Tofugu, he moved to Portland, Maine by mistake. It's still a funny story we laugh about to this day.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは毎日、マイケルからお笑いの特くんを受けています。
example_sentences.english: Koichi gets intensive comedy training from Michael every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢の中で、私はお笑い芸人で、テレビでお客さんの前でオナラをしなくちゃいけなかったんだけど、うまくできなかったの。それで、その番組の司会を務めてた先輩芸人にすごく怒られたのよね。
example_sentences.english: In my dream, I was a comedian and I had to fart on purpose in front of the TV audience, but I couldn’t do it. Then I was scolded by the experienced comedians who hosted the show.

notes: "A paragraph in writing is what you send someone when you want to submit a complaint. You want to make sure these are in writing, though, otherwise you don't have proof of your complaint. Also, don't make it longer than a paragraph, because that's too long and nobody cares about how you think the shop staff mistreated your dog Fluffy." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、トーフグ社員のJLPTの試験結果に文句タラタラだった。
example_sentences.english: Koichi complained incessantly about the Tofugu employee's JLPT results.

example_sentences.japanese: オンラインの日本語学習教材の中では、トーフグが文句無しで一番いいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I think Tofugu is, without a doubt, the best of the online Japanese learning tools.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語で、文句という言葉が、英語の僧侶という単語と発音が似ているということは面白いですね。
example_sentences.english: It’s funny that the Japanese word for complaint is pronounced like the English word monk.

notes: "This is a combination of the word 辞書 ""dictionary"" and the suffix 〜形 or ""form."" Put them together and you get dictionary form!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べたの辞書形は食べるです。
example_sentences.english: The dictionary form of ate is eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 辞書形は分かるんですが、活用形がよく分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I'm fine with dictionary form, but I have trouble with conjugated form.

example_sentences.japanese: この言葉の辞書形を書きなさい。
example_sentences.english: Write the dictionary form of this word.

notes: "When it's possible to separate something, it's divisible. Just imagine separating things into parts. It's possible. So, if that's possible, it's divisible. Now think of something that's nothing (i.e. ""no candy bars""). That is not possible to separate into parts. That is not divisible." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のトーフグポッドキャストのテーマは、生と死の不可分性です。
example_sentences.english: The theme of today's Tofugu podcast is the inseparability of life and death.

example_sentences.japanese: 英文けい約書には、一ぱんじょうこうの一つに、可分性というじょうこうがよくあります。
example_sentences.english: English contracts often have a severability clause as one of general provisions.

example_sentences.japanese: 預貯金などの可分債権は、原則として遺産分割の対象にはなりません。
example_sentences.english: As a general rule, divisible claims, like savings accounts, do not become the target of divisions of inherited property.

notes: "If you put writing into a category, you'd have to write it down after you've chosen what category it is in. Where would you write that down? Into a document, probably." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この書類は不びがあります。
example_sentences.english: This document is incomplete.

example_sentences.japanese: 書類を家のつくえの上においてきてしまったっぽい！
example_sentences.english: I think the document is on my desk at home.

example_sentences.japanese: 「いつTofuguの機密書類が欲しい？」「早ければ早いに越したことはないな。」
example_sentences.english: """When do you want Tofugu’s secret documents?"" ""The sooner, the better."""

notes: "How do you represent an equal number? With an equal sign." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに等号を書き忘れているよ。
example_sentences.english: You forgot to write an equal sign here.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは等号の上と下の線が同じ長さじゃないとげきどする。
example_sentences.english: Koichi gets furious if the top and bottom lines of an equal sign are not the same length.

example_sentences.japanese: 等号の右側の数式が正か負かについて、注意する必要があります。
example_sentences.english: You have to pay attention to whether the formula to the right of the equal sign is plus or minus.

english: Exchange Student, International Student, Foreign Student
notes: "Remember 留学, which means ""study abroad""? Do you also remember 学生, which is ""student""? This word is like those two words mashed together (they share a 学), making it a ""study abroad student."" What's a better way to say that? How about exchange student!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その留学生は、くつひもを結ぶのをいつも忘れてしまいます。
example_sentences.english: That international student always forgets to tie his shoes.

example_sentences.japanese: あのクラスの留学生、何だかあどけない感じがするよね。
example_sentences.english: That class's foreign students look kind of innocent, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: あの留学生、いつも私と彼氏の写真に変顔とか変なポーズで写り込んでくるんだけど。ちょっとうざいんだよね。
example_sentences.english: That exchange student is always photobombing pictures of my boyfriend and me. It’s kind of annoying.

notes: "You know that 枚 is a flat objects counter. So, now we're counting! You have five flat objects." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

english: Flat Object, Clothing Items, Sheets, Flat Object Counter
notes:
"This is a counter that can be used with various ""flat"" things, which is why it is referring to a flat object. Other things it can refer to include clothing items, sheets, paper, stamps, dishes, and more. Notice how they're all kind of flat shaped?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: People think you're dancing, but you're really jumping from the mice (まい) running on your floor. You don't want the mice running up your legs so you have to hop from one to the other, making it look like you're dancing."

notes: "You have flat objects but what amount of flat objects? This word is asking that question: ""how many flat objects are there?"" notes: "The body part that lives between your throat and your head is your larynx. Otherwise known as the voice box, because your vocal cords live in there." You also know 18 levels of kanji and you really want to shout them all out, which makes your voice box tired (but makes you happy)."

notes: "When you sit and do zen you are probably doing zen meditation. Hummmmm." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

The てら gets changed to でら, though.In terms of when it's pronounced ぜんじ, if you put this word onto the end of the name of a 禅寺 the pronunciation changes to ぜんじ. It makes sense - it's more like a jukugo word that way (not that the original isn't, but you can see the separation of words coming together which gives the hint that it's a kun'yomi combo reading). english: Aiueo Order, In Aiueo Order, Syllabary Order
notes: "This is a little confusing for someone who didn't grow up with the Japanese language. You have fifty sounds. Then, they're in a certain order. So, these fifty sounds are the Japanese syllabary. That's hiragana / katakana, probably from back in the day when there were more sounds than there are now. So, the ""fifty sounds in order"" makes up aiueo order, where the ""aiueo"" is あいうえお representing the five columns." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. notes: "An automatic part of speech is an intransitive verb. Intransitive verbs are actions that just happen, aka you're not the one doing the action or thing. These are words like 付く or 消える, where you aren't doing the action. That's why they're automatic!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 自動詞「進む」の可能形は、「進める」です。
example_sentences.english: "The potential form of the intransitive verb ""to advance"" is ""something advances."""

example_sentences.japanese: 私が大の苦手としていることの一つに、他動詞と自動詞の使い分けがあります。
example_sentences.english: One of the things I really dread is using transitive and intransitive verbs properly.

example_sentences.english: You can easily judge if it's an intransitive verb or a transitive verb when you think about whether or not you can change it to the passive form.

example_sentences.english: Nikka expresses joy by wagging her tail.

example_sentences.english: Koichi beamed with delight as he officially launched WaniKani at last.

example_sentences.japanese: 喜びを表す、面白い顔文字を探しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m looking for a funny kaomoji to express my joy.

english: Konbu, Kombu, Konbu Seaweed, Kombu Seaweed
notes: "This one is pretty weird. The cloth of our descendants is konbu. This is a type of seaweed that is very common in Japan. It is used in foods and in broths. It is everywhere, and delicious. If you're not familiar with it already this may be a hard word to learn, but I believe in you. Maybe if you read up on konbu for a bit it will help you to remember your descendants' cloth." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The 布 part gets changed to ぶ, probably because if a food doesn't have konbu you say boo (ぶ)."

example_sentences.english: I made broth with kombu.

example_sentences.english: Please tell me the difference between wakame seaweed and konbu seaweed.

example_sentences.english: """How dare you throw konbu seaweed at me!"" ""I’m sorry. I didn’t think it would be that big of a deal."""

notes: "A riot of war is where things go nuts. This is a melee! A free for all!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.english: On the first day of the sale, the mall became super crowded, like it was some kind of battle royal.

"Take your name and stab someone with it... using your business card. Your business card has your name on it. Also, you ""stab"" it at people who are willing to take it and read it. notes: "This is a food pretty specific to Japan, making it a slightly weird one to learn. You have a Japanese Plum. Then you have dry. So when the Japanese plum is dried, it's not a dried plum (that would be too easy), it is a pickled plum or pickled ume. If you know the name of this food, you can call it by that too: umeboshi." "The reading for this one, like the meaning, is kind of strange. It's the kun'yomi readings, so apologies in advance for that. You have うめ plus ぼし, which comes from 干す though the し is stuffed inside the 干 for some reason. It's also rendaku'd. Basically, everything is all screwed up, so you know, deal with it. This food is awesome, and common, so you have to learn it. I guess the pickling process has mangled the reading of this word. At least it tastes good."

example_sentences.english: Umeboshi is good for motion sickness.

example_sentences.english: Excuse me. May I get through? I’d like to buy that jar of pickled plums.
