example_sentences.japanese: 新しいゲームをする時に説明書を読んでから始めるタイプですか。それとも、説明書は読まずにいきなり始めるタイプですか。
example_sentences.english: When you play a new game, are you the type of person who reads the instructions first or do you start playing without reading them?

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は現在、日本語で書かれた説明書を英語に翻訳してくださる方を探しています。
example_sentences.english: We are currently looking for someone who can translate some instructions written in Japanese into English.

notes: "Someone who does crime together with you is your accomplice in crime. It's best to ""take care of these"" before the coppers get to him/her." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの共犯者は、まさに飛んで火にいる夏の虫だったな。
example_sentences.english: The accomplice was indeed like a bug that flew into the fire in summer.

example_sentences.japanese: 共犯者は国外に飛んでしまった可能性が高い。
example_sentences.english: There is high probability that the accomplice has already fled the country.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はとても素晴らしい犯罪者で、自分一人でも、いとも簡単にとても危ない状態から抜け出すことが出来ました。そして、共犯者は一生必要ないとも豪語していました。
example_sentences.english: He was a really wonderful criminal who could easily get out of the most dangerous situations by himself. He boasted that he would never need an accomplice.

notes: "A surplus (that's an extra!) earthquake is a quake that  comes after the main (non-surplus) quake. That's an aftershock." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ余震が続いているので、予だんは許されない。
example_sentences.english: The aftershocks are still coming so we need to be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は何回ぐらい余震を感じましたか？
example_sentences.english: How many aftershocks have you felt today?

example_sentences.japanese: その地震の後に、余震が相次ぎました。
example_sentences.english: The earthquake was followed by aftershocks.

notes: "The fly and go machine is some machine you get into that flies and goes places. It's an airplane." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機のチケット、もう取っちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I've already booked the airplane tickets.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機でコウイチのとなりの席になった時、めちゃくちゃこうふんしました。
example_sentences.english: I was super excited when Koichi sat down next to me on the plane.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は飛行機が苦手なので、一生日本に行けることはないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I dislike airplanes, so I would never be able to go to Japan.

notes: "You hopefully know that this has something to do with housesitting (留守番). So, a telephone (電話) that does housesitting for you is what? It's your answering machine." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 留守番電話にコウイチから明日飛行機でハワイに行くというメッセージが入っていました。
example_sentences.english: On my answering machine, I got a message from Koichi saying he's flying to Hawaii tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: あっちが留守番電話で議論をふかっけてきたんだぜ。
example_sentences.english: He challenged me to a debate on my answering machine.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguのオフィスに何度も何度も電話をしていますが、いつも留守番電話です。
example_sentences.english: I've been calling the Tofugu office over and over again, but I always get the answering machine.

notes: "The study of mankind (人類) is known as anthropology." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチのお父さんの専門は文化人類学です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's father's specialty is cultural anthropology.

example_sentences.japanese: 研究対しょうのアフリカの民族に気に入ってもらうために、その人類学者ははだかになって村人と交流を始めた。
example_sentences.english: In order to get along with the African ethnic group that she wants to research, she started interacting with the villagers naked.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてあなたの妹は人類学の授業を受けたかったのかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why your sister wanted to take an anthropology course.

notes: "Check the pressure of your blood. It's your blood pressure." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: お互い年だし血圧が上がっちゃうから、もう非難し合うのは止めにしない？
example_sentences.english: Let's not play the blame game because we are both old and our blood pressure might go up.

example_sentences.japanese: 低血圧だから朝起きられなくて困っているんです。今日は血圧をはかってもらったら、上が85で下が30でした。コウイチ先生、何とかしてもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: I am having trouble getting up in the morning because I have low blood pressure. When I had my blood pressure taken today, it was 85 over 30. Can you do something for me, Dr. Koichi?

example_sentences.japanese: 血圧の薬を飲んでも血圧が高いままであることを医者に言うと、血圧を抑えるにはストレスを減らすことが重要だよと教えられました。
example_sentences.english: When I told my doctor that I still have high blood pressure, even after taking blood pressure meds, he told me the importance of reducing stress to control it.

notes: "The hand who borrows is the borrower." "You'll want to know the words 借りる and 手 to be able to read this one. Combine them to know the reading."

example_sentences.japanese: そうは言っても、借り手が見つからない可能性もありますよね？
example_sentences.english: Regardless of what you say, there's still a possibility that we won't be able to find a tenant, right?

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが昔住んでいた部屋だと言ったら、すぐに借り手が見つかりました。
example_sentences.english: When we advertised that Koichi used to live here, the house went right away.

example_sentences.japanese: あのマンションは、幽霊屋敷であるという評判のせいで借り手がつかない。
example_sentences.english: That apartment still doesn’t have any tenants because it’s rumored to be haunted.

notes: "A bow and an arrow. Put them together and you have a bow and arrow." "The reading is the vocab readings, 弓 and 矢, put together. This is probably because this word is like two separate words put together, thus the ""and"" in the middle of the English translation."

example_sentences.japanese: 弓矢でシカを仕留めるには、にんたいがいります。
example_sentences.english: You need to be patient if you want to shoot a deer with a bow and arrow.

example_sentences.japanese: その夜、両親は、弓矢を売るべきかどうか議論しました。
example_sentences.english: That night, my parents discussed whether or not to sell the bow and arrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔はうさぎ狩りに弓矢を使っていました。
example_sentences.english: We used to use bows and arrows for hunting rabbits.

notes: "The お is just there to be nice to your butt. This word simply means butt." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 高いところに行くと、お尻がかゆくなるんです。
example_sentences.english: When I go to high places, my butt itches.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんのお尻ほど可愛いものはこの世に無い。
example_sentences.english: There's nothing in the world that's cuter than a baby's butt.

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんどの日本人が誕生日にお尻を叩くなんて聞いた事がないと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I bet most Japanese people have never heard of a birthday spanking.

notes: "The person in charge of long discussions is the chairman, or the speaker. They also say who gets to talk and for how long." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 議長は危機をだっしました。
example_sentences.english: The chairman got through the crisis.

example_sentences.japanese: あのバスの最後尾の席に座っている黒いスーツの男性が議長です。
example_sentences.english: The man in the black suit sitting in the last row of the bus is the speaker.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がこの会議の議長を務めさせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: I am acting as chairperson of this meeting.

english: Conference Room, Council Room, Meeting Room
notes: "A room where you meet for discussions is known as a conference room." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、ビエトを助けるために、会議室まで飛んで行きました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi hurried to the conference room to help Viet.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトとコウイチが会議室に入ったまんまずっと出てこないんだ。
example_sentences.english: Viet and Koichi went in the meeting room and still haven't come out.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は会議室で寝泊まりしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m staying in the conference room now.

notes: "A hole child isn't some kind of creepy hole child (not sure how else to describe it). It's a conger eel, a type of tasty eel eaten in Japan. It might be easier to learn the reading first, though, and use that, because the second meaning option is anago, the Japanese word for it (also used in English)." "The reading is the two kun'yomi vocab readings combined. So, 穴 and 子 to make あなご."

example_sentences.japanese: 穴子が減ってきたから、そろそろ注文しないといけないな。
example_sentences.english: We are running short on conger eel, so we need to place an order for them soon.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカでは穴子は手に入りにくいので、代わりにウナギが使われています。
example_sentences.english: Since it is difficult to get conger eel in America, freshwater eel is used instead.

example_sentences.japanese: 「穴子の握り、もう一貫頼む？」「うん！あたり前田のクラッカーだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you want another piece of conger eel nigiri?"" ""Sure. Why not?"""

notes: "Throat candy is the kind of candy that should make your throat feel better. That's right, it's a cough drop or a throat lozenge. Don't just eat regular candy when your throat hurts! Use the right kind." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji. You've learned them both already, so you should be able to read this already!

example_sentences.japanese: マヨネーズ味の喉飴があったら良いのになあ。
example_sentences.english: I wish mayonnaise flavored cough drops existed.

example_sentences.japanese: 喉飴持ってない？
example_sentences.english: Do you happen to have a throat lozenge?

example_sentences.japanese: 喉飴って理科室みたいな味がすると思わない？
example_sentences.english: Don't you think cough drops taste like the science room?

notes: "When you incur damage you are doing damage and harm." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: オフィスにどろぼうが入ってしまい、トーフグは大きな被害を受けました。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu suffered a great loss from an office burglary.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は、山火事の被害は受けませんでした。
example_sentences.english: This town wasn't damaged by the wildfire.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は、洪水の被害があった地域に、今日の利益を募金としてお送りします。
example_sentences.english: We are going to send our profits from today's business to the area with flood damage.

english: Diet, The Diet, Congress, Parliament, Assembly
notes: "The place you meet for deliberation in Japan is called the Diet. It's their version of congress." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつら、何とかして議会の進行を妨害するつもりだぞ。
example_sentences.english: They are trying to obstruct the proceedings of Parliament by any means necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 正直、そのことについて議会で説明するのはかなり面倒です。
example_sentences.english: To be honest, it's extremely troublesome having to explain it at Congress.

example_sentences.japanese: もう議会で決定したことなんだ。
example_sentences.english: The Diet has already come to a decision.

english: Dishwashing, Doing Dishes, Washing The Dishes, Washing Dishes
notes: "You know the word 皿 (plate) and the word 洗う (to wash), right? You can probably guess dish washing is happening here, but this is a noun, so it's the idea of dishwashing or doing dishes." "The readings are the individual vocab words (you can tell because there's a bit of hiragana stuck on there). It's the reading for 皿 and 洗う combined."

example_sentences.japanese: 皿洗いをしているクリステンが可愛すぎて、穴があくほど見つめてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Kristen was just so cute when she was doing dishes and I couldn't help staring holes into her.

example_sentences.japanese: 皿洗いをしている時は、時間が経つのがおそく感じます。
example_sentences.english: I feel that time passes slowly when I'm washing dishes.

example_sentences.japanese: 食事代を支払う代わりに皿洗いをすることができるラーメン屋さんが日本にあるって本当ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is it true that there is a ramen restaurant in Japan where you can wash dishes to pay your bill?

notes: "An earthquake disaster is just that, an earthquake disaster. These are no good." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The reading for 災 is the さい reading because *sigh* earthquakes suck man."

example_sentences.japanese: 震災で、地面が穴ぼこだらけになってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Because of the earthquake disaster, there are a lot of potholes on the ground now.

example_sentences.japanese: 震災にあった日のことが、今でもわすれられないトラウマになっています。
example_sentences.english: I still can't forget the trauma I experienced from the day of the earthquake disaster.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に行く時に、2011年の東北大震災の大津波に耐えた一本の松の木を見に行きたいです。
example_sentences.english: When I go to Japan, I want to see the single pine tree that withstood the giant tsunami caused by the Great Tōhoku Earthquake in 2011.

english: Earthquake Intensity, Earthquake Magnitude, Magnitude, Seismic Scale
notes: "The earthquake degrees is how you measure an earthquake. The 震度 is the earthquake intensity." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 震度は3でしたがけっこうゆれました。
example_sentences.english: The earthquake's magnitude was at a three, but it felt quite strong.

example_sentences.japanese: マグニチュードと震度って、何が違うの？
example_sentences.english: What’s the difference between magnitude and seismic scale?

example_sentences.japanese: 2011年に震度七を記録した東日本大震災の余震は、今後百年程は続き、巨大余震もあるだろうと言われています。
example_sentences.english: They say the aftershocks from the 2011 Tohoku Earthquake hit a magnitude of seven, and that they'll continue for the next hundred years, even the big ones.

notes: "You have an electronic (電子) container machine. This is just a machine that contains electricity and electric parts. It is, basically, just electronic equipment. Though, you can say electronics if that's easier for you." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 機内ではお手持ちの電子機器の電げんはお切りになるか機内モードにごせっ定くださいますよう、ご協力お願い申し上げます。
example_sentences.english: Please turn off all personal electronic devices or set them to airplane mode on this plane. Thank you for your cooperation.

example_sentences.japanese: 電子機器に欠かんが無いか、一個ずつ手作業で確認しています。
example_sentences.english: We manually check electronic equipment one by one to make sure there are no defects.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしていくつかの航空会社は、飛行中の電子機器の使用についての規制を緩和し始めたんでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: Why did some airlines start relaxing their rules about the use of electronics during flights?

notes: "You already know that  最後 means ""end"" so the tail end is the end of a line." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. It isn't the same as 最後 though, so watch out for that! It uses the other on'yomi reading you learned with the kanji!"

example_sentences.japanese: 大人気のゲームを発売日に買うために開店前にお店に行ったけど、すでにお店の前から列の最後尾まで200mぐらいあった。
example_sentences.english: To buy a very popular game on the release day, I went to a store before they opened, but there was already a line from the store that was about 200-meters long to the end.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日通りかかったお店の列の最後尾にクリステンがいたよ。仕事をサボって何買いに行ってたんだろう？
example_sentences.english: I saw Kristen at the end of a line for a shop I passed by yesterday. I wonder what she was playing hooky from work to get.

example_sentences.japanese: 行列の最後尾はこちらです。
example_sentences.english: The end of the line is this way.

notes: "A fire disaster is a fire disaster. Maybe you'll get to meet a sexy firefighter if things go well..." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやって火災が大水害を引き起こしたの？
example_sentences.english: How did a fire disaster cause heavy floods?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日中に火災で空いた穴をふさがなくてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: I have to fill the hole made by the fire disaster by the end of today.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は深夜二時に換気扇を回さずにフライパンでステーキを焼いて、火災警報装置を鳴らした。
example_sentences.english: He cooked a steak in a frying pan without running the ventilation fan at 2AM and the fire alarm went off.

notes: "Water damage is so bad they call it water damage. Doesn't get any clearer than this." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトとダリンが、水害で飛んだデータをふく元しています。
example_sentences.english: Viet and Darin are recovering the data that was lost from the water damage.

example_sentences.japanese: その水害で、5,000びきの猫が家を失いました。
example_sentences.english: The flood left 5,000 cats homeless.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、水害の起きやすい島で育ちました。
example_sentences.english: I grew up on a flood-prone island.

english: Forgotten Item, Something Forgotten, Forgotten Thing, Lost Property
notes: "Remember how 忘れる is ""to forget""? Well, a thing you've forgotten is a forgotten item." "Since you didn't learn this reading for 忘 with the kanji, here's a mnemonic to help you out. If you study this vocabulary out the wazoo わす, it'll never become a forgotten item!"

example_sentences.japanese: 単に忘れ物をしたことを非難してるわけじゃないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I'm not blaming you just because you forgot to bring something.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの飛行機が成田空港に着いた時、コウイチは忘れ物に気づいたのでそのまま同じ飛行機でポートランドへと引き返しました。
example_sentences.english: When Koichi's plane arrived at Narita Airport, Koichi realized that he forgot something, so he returned Portland on the same airplane.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日何か忘れ物をしたような気がするんだけど、それが何だったかをどうしても思い出せないんだよな。
example_sentences.english: I feel like I forgot something today, but I just can’t remember what it is.

english: Hand Washing, Bathroom, Restroom, Lavatory, Washing The Hands
notes: "You remember how 洗う is ""to wash""? Well, when you wash your hands you're doing hand washing." "The readings are the vocab readings 手 and 洗う put together."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは何度言っても社員達が手洗い、うがいをしないので機嫌が悪い。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is angry with his workers because they don't wash their hands and gargle, regardless of how many times he's told them to do so.

example_sentences.japanese: お手洗いをお借りしてもいいですか？
example_sentences.english: Can I borrow your bathroom?

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグTシャツに洗濯機は使えません。手洗いをしなくてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You can’t use a washing machine for Tofugu T-shirts. You have to wash them by hand.

english: Hole In The Wall, Little Known Good Place
notes: "A hole place is what's known as a hole in the wall. This is a place that looks small, hidden and dingy, but probably has awesome food." The readings are the readings you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは、フグ料理の穴場なんですよ。
example_sentences.english: This is a good blowfish restaurant, which isn't known to the public.

example_sentences.japanese: このい酒屋、カガヤって言うんだけど、東京でも穴場中の穴場だよ。
example_sentences.english: This Izakaya restaurant is called Kagaya and this is one of the best holes in the wall in Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: あのことがあって以来、もう二度とああいう思いをしたくないし、周りにも迷惑をかけたくないので、フグ釣りの穴場に行くことは止めました。
example_sentences.english: Ever since then I’ve never wanted to have that kind of experience again, or to cause trouble for others, so I’ve stopped going to the little-known place where you can fish for fugu.

notes: "You have a husband and a wife. Combine them together and they're husband and wife." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その夫妻は、良い夫ふ関係には議論が必要かどうかについて、はげしく議論していました。
example_sentences.english: That husband and wife had a long, heated argument on whether discussions are indispensable for a good married relationship.

example_sentences.japanese: みんながコウイチ夫妻のことを非難がましい顔で見ていました。
example_sentences.english: Everybody looked at Mr. and Mrs. Koichi with disapproval.

example_sentences.japanese: フグ夫妻はともにとても口が達者で、近所の人達に大量の海藻を売りつけた。
example_sentences.english: Mr. and Mrs. Fugu were such smooth operators that they sold tons of seaweed to their neighbors.

notes: "Using theory and reason, you are one who uses much logic. Imagine this type of person, I bet you know at least one." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その論理でいくと意味が通じないよ。
example_sentences.english: It won't make sense if we go by that logic.

example_sentences.japanese: 三だん論法の論理についてだれか教えてくれる人はいますか？
example_sentences.english: Can anyone teach me about the logic of syllogism?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の不満は理解できたんだけど、私はただ論理的に私達の問題を考えてほしかっただけなんだよね。そしたら今度は、私がいつも誰のせいかってことを決めたがるとか言ってきて。全然そんな事ないのに。
example_sentences.english: I understood her frustration, but I just wanted her to think about the issues between us logically. Then she told me that I’m always trying to find out whose fault things are, which was not true at all.

notes:
"A machine contraption is just a machine" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"When the machines meet, you finally have the opportunity to take them all out at once. DIE MACHINES!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらは、地面に穴をほる機械で、そちらは、はりの穴に糸を通す機械です。
example_sentences.english: This is a machine for digging holes in the ground and that's a machine for threading needles.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は機械の調子があんまり良くないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Today the machine is not working very smoothly.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは会社用にバッティングセンターの機械を買ったの？
example_sentences.english: Did Koichi buy a batting cage machine for the office?

example_sentences.japanese: 「土曜日に夕食にいらっしゃいませんか？河豚のパイ生地包み焼きを作る予定なんですよ。」「喜んで行きたいのですが、会議がありますので。またの機会にお願いします。」
example_sentences.english: """Would you like to come to dinner on Saturday? I’m going to make Fugu-wellington."" “I’d like to, but I have a meeting. I’ll take a rain check."""

english: Member Of The Diet, Diet Member, Legislator, Assembly Member
notes: "A discussion member talks about all the really important things that need to be discussed for the sake of the country. They are a member of the Diet. The Diet is Japan's version of congress. Diet members discuss really important matters." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 国会議員になるのがマイケルの長年の夢でした。
example_sentences.english: Becoming a member of the diet is Michael's longterm dream.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生の時にある市議会議員のところでインターンをしていました。とてもいい経験でした。
example_sentences.english: When I was a college student, I was interning for a city council Diet member. It was a good experience.

example_sentences.japanese: 議員バッヂを失くしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I lost my Diet member badge.

notes: "A disaster that is difficult is particularly difficult, making it more of a misfortune. Obviously a disaster that wasn't difficult wouldn't really be that bad, so a difficult one gets the ""misfortune"" or calamity label." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、運良く海外にいたので、その災難をまぬがれることができました。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, I was overseas at the time, so I was able to escape the disaster.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日学校で、「災難は勇気を試す試金石である。」ということわざを習いました。
example_sentences.english: "Today at school I learned a proverb that goes, ""calamity is the touchstone of a brave mind."""

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてあいつはあんなに災難に見舞われてばかりいるのかな？本当に偶然なのか、それともあいつ自体に何か問題があるんだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why misfortune is always following that guy? Is it just by chance or is there something wrong with him?

notes: "A disaster that does damage. Usually these are natural disasters, though they could also just be regular disasters as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 自然災害ほどおそろしいものはありません。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing scarier than natural disasters.

example_sentences.japanese: そもそも、どうして災害が起こる可能性の高い場所に原子力発電所を建てたのかが理かいできません。
example_sentences.english: I can't understand why they built the nuclear power plant on a potential disaster site to begin with.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれの部屋には、災害の場合に備えて懐中電灯とペットボトルのお水が何本か用意してあります。
example_sentences.english: Each room has been prepared with flashlights and water bottles in case of a natural disaster.

notes: "A bad dream is also known as a nightmare. Ah! Noooooo!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 主役が急病になったんだけど、代役が見つからなくてね。まさに悪夢だったよ。
example_sentences.english: The lead actor got sick all of a sudden and we couldn't find another actor to fill in for him. It was such a nightmare.

example_sentences.japanese: 太った猫になって歩けないという悪夢を見た。
example_sentences.english: I had a bad dream that I turned into a fat cat that couldn’t walk.

example_sentences.japanese: 腕を胸の前で組んで寝ると悪夢が見れるって聞いたから試したら、朝から晩までひたすらトイレ掃除をずっとしているという夢を見たよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard you can make yourself have nightmares if you sleep with your arms folded across your chest, so I tried it and I had a dream that I was cleaning a toilet nonstop from morning to night.

notes: "What's your nose's hole? How about your nostril?" "The reading is the readings for 鼻 and 穴. Smell that fresh air through your nose hole."

example_sentences.japanese: 「コウイチの鼻の穴の形ってちょっと変じゃない？」「そう？私はかわいいと思うけど。」
example_sentences.english: """Aren't the shapes of Koichi's nose holes a bit weird?"" ""Really? I think they are cute."""

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、鼻血が出てくる時は鼻の穴にチクワをさしこんで止血します。
example_sentences.english: When Koichi has a nose bleed, he sticks a tube-shaped fish paste cake in there to stop it.

example_sentences.japanese: 「君の鼻の穴…。」「何？聞こえないわ。」「ええっと、やっぱり何でもないよ。大したことじゃないから。」「教えてくれなきゃだめよ。何を言おうとしてたの？」
example_sentences.english: """Your nostril..."" ""What? I can’t hear you."" ""Well never mind. It’s nothing."" ""Now you have to tell me. What were you saying?"""

english: One Small Thing, One Thing, One Small Object, One Object
notes: "The counter 個, which means individual on its own, refers to ""an individual thing."" This is usually a small thing, so it's used to count small things. This word here talks about one individual. A better way to translate that would be to call it one small thing." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The いち gets shortened, but I bet you knew that already."

example_sentences.japanese: おく歯に一個、大きな穴が空いているね。
example_sentences.english: You've got one big hole in your back teeth.

example_sentences.japanese: そのイチゴは、一個百円にもかかわらず、飛ぶように売れました。
example_sentences.english: Those strawberries were one hundred yen each, but they flew off the shelves.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはシュークリームがとっても好きなので、毎日少なくとも一個は食べます。
example_sentences.english: Viet likes cream puffs so much that he eats at least one every single day.

english: "On'yomi And Kun'yomi, Chinese And Japanese Readings"
notes: "You've seen (hopefully) 音読み and 訓読み. This is a combination of the two. This is on'yomi and kun'yomi, aka the Chinese and Japanese readings." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: かん字の音訓の見分け方を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach me how to differentiate between on'yomi and kun'yomi.

example_sentences.japanese: これは常用かん字の音訓表です。
example_sentences.english: This is a Chinese and Japanese reading chart of commonly used kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字の音訓ってすごく紛らわしいので嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: The Japanese and Chinese readings for kanji are so confusing, I hate them.

notes: "The kanji 達 pluralizes things sometimes. So, when you have a plural amount of a person you have more than one person, you have people.Take note! When using this word, you want to attach it to the type of ""people"" you are talking about. For example, あの人達 (those people over there). Other examples: 男の人達, その人達, 向こうの人達, etc. You don't use this by itself, instead you use it with something describing what kind of people you're talking about." "The readings are both kun'yomi readings of the kanji. The readings come from the word 人 and the だち of 友達, though now it's たち because it hasn't been rendaku'd. You like to touch (たち) people, you perv."

example_sentences.japanese: この人達、みんな本当によく舌が回るよね。
example_sentences.english: These people are really talkative, eh?

example_sentences.japanese: テキサスの人達ってとっても親切だね！
example_sentences.english: People in Texas are very friendly, aren't they!

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんがピザの配達人であることを笑う人達もいますが、僕はお父さんのことをとても誇りに思っています。
example_sentences.english: There are some people who make fun of my dad for being a pizza delivery man, but I’m very proud of him.

notes: "You compare the percent and by doing that figure out the percentage and ratio of something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 機械ほんやくにはどれぐらいの比率でたよっていますか？
example_sentences.english: What percent relies on machine translations?

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのオフィスの男女比率は、5:2です。
example_sentences.english: The ratio of boys and girls in the Tofugu office is 5 to 2.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの自己資本比率は100％だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think Tofugu has a capital-to-asset ratio of 100%.

notes: "This is the noun form of disaster, though it is more like a personal disaster or personal misfortune. Just picture that flood from the kanji sweeping you up into your own personal disaster—one only you experience." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: When a personal disaster strikes, you start moaning and groaning. Say it along with me: ""Wahhhhh! Zaahhhh! Waahhhh!"" (わざわ). Be careful of the い on the end, it can be tricky and make you think it's an adjective when it's a noun."

example_sentences.japanese: これは、災いを防いでくれるお守りです。
example_sentences.english: This is a lucky charm that protects you from misfortune.

example_sentences.japanese: 災い転じて福となすという言葉を信じてがんばりました。
example_sentences.english: "I believed in the phrase, ""turn disaster into advantage,"" and it really worked."

example_sentences.japanese: シャークは他人の災いを願っているようだね。
example_sentences.english: It seems like Shark wishes misfortune upon other people.

notes: "Your possible (可能) gender is one of two things. This means there's a possibility you'll either be a boy or a girl. Or maybe something else! Who knows?! " "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to be able to read 可能 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 戦争になる可能性は低いと思うけど、心配だよね。
example_sentences.english: I think the possibility of a war breaking out is low, but I'm worried.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年のクリスマスは雪になる可能性が高いみたいです。
example_sentences.english: It seems like the likelihood of it snowing on Christmas Day is very high.

example_sentences.japanese: 思いついた考えは、どれも実現の可能性は無さそうでしたが、私達はそう簡単には諦めませんでした。
example_sentences.english: None of the ideas we came up with sounded likely, but we didn’t give up easily.

notes: "The pressure power is the pressure. This can also be stress as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 圧力なべをばく発させてしまいましたが、幸いケガはありませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I made the pressure cooker explode, but luckily I didn't get injured.

example_sentences.japanese: ロケットが大気にとつ入するときの圧力は相当なものだ。
example_sentences.english: The pressure that a rocket is under when it's entering the atmosphere is very strong.

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニがベータ版から脱するよう、我々はコウイチに圧力をかけ続けなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: We must keep the pressure on Koichi to get WaniKani out of beta.

notes: "An individual room just for you is your own private room. How nice!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さい子がいると個室い酒屋の存在はありがたいです。
example_sentences.english: When you have small kids, the existence of izakaya with private rooms is appreciated.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはシェアハウスで自分の個室がないという生活をもう五年も続けている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's been living in a shared house without his own room for more than five years now.

example_sentences.japanese: 忘年会に個室を予約しました。
example_sentences.english: I reserved a private room for our year-end party.

notes: "You're certain there is this percent chance it will happen? You know that this is the probability?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチがあやまってこの穴に落ちる確率は、20%ぐらいだろうね。
example_sentences.english: The probability of Koichi accidentally falling into this pit is at about 20%.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが友情に厚い人である確率はどのぐらいだと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: What's the likelihood of Koichi being someone who's kind to his friends?

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトはコウイチに、Tofuguが成功する確率は二百パーセントだと言いきった。
example_sentences.english: Viet told Koichi that the chances of Tofugu succeeding were 200%.

notes: "The reading someone is someone who is reading. They are the reader (of a book, blog, article, etc)." "The reading for 読 is the on'yomi reading, which you didn't learn with the kanji. This reading is どく, and you can remember it by thinking about how you are the reader, and as the reader you choose where to read. For you, the best place to read is a peaceful dock (どく). Sit on the dock and relax. Be the reader."

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグの読者が、飛行機代を出してくれたんです。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu readers paid for my plane tickets.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグには世界中にたくさんの読者がいます。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu has many readers all over the world.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの読者のうち、日本語学習者はどのくらいいますか？
example_sentences.english: Among Tofugu readers, how many are Japanese language learners?

notes: "Remember when you learned that 高等 means ""high class"" and 学校 means ""school?"" Well put them together and you have senior high school! It's the most high class school you've got (unless you go to university, but that's considered to be separate). Fun fact: 高校 is the abbreviation of this word. Neat, right?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは高等学校を卒業してすぐ海軍に入りました。
example_sentences.english: Right after graduating from his senior high school, Koichi joined the navy.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がまだ小さかった時に住んでいたマンションの近くに芸能人が通うことで有名な高等学校がありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a senior high school, that was famous for celebrities going there, near the condo I used to live in when I was little.

example_sentences.japanese: 高等学校で教頭をしております。
example_sentences.english: I’m the vice principal of a senior high school.

notes: "You have an abundant surplus! How nice it must be to have a surplus with so much leeway." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは今年は予算にかなりの余裕があります。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu has quite a bit of room in the budget this year.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ二、三人分ぐらい余裕があるよ。
example_sentences.english: We still have enough room for a few people.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいパソコンとAKB48のフィギュアを買いたいが、今は余裕が無い。
example_sentences.english: I’d love to buy a new computer and some AKB48 figures, but I can’t afford to right now.

notes: "I dislike him and I have doubts about him. I therefore have much suspicion against him as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトがヤクザだという嫌疑がぬぐえません。
example_sentences.english: Our suspicion that Viet is a yakuza cannot be wiped away.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察に嫌疑をかけられているんだ。
example_sentences.english: I'm under suspicion from the police.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトがコウイチにかかった殺人の嫌疑を晴らした。
example_sentences.english: Viet dispelled suspicions of Koichi being a murderer.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet though, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You look down and you've sprouted a tail! You're so shocked that all you can say is ""Oh. (お) Oh okay..."" This your life now. A life with a tail."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、魚の尾を見ただけで魚の種類を言うのが特技です。
example_sentences.english: Koichi can look at a fish's tail and tell you what kind it is based on that alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 尾が無いと、鳥は上手く着りく出来ません。
example_sentences.english: Without tails, birds would have difficulty landing.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして犬の尾を短くする習慣が産まれたのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Why do you think the custom of shortening dog’s tails started?

notes: "A writing of your theory is usually a thesis. Remember how school teachers always wanted you to present theories in writing? And to make sure you have a thesis in that paper? I do." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この論文、終わりの方で五ページぐらい飛んでたよ。
example_sentences.english: There are about five pages missing near the end of this thesis.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は大学院在学中に論文をたくさん出ぱんしたツワモノです。
example_sentences.english: My friend is a warrior who published many essays during her graduate school years.

example_sentences.japanese: うまくいけば、大学の卒業論文今日中に書き終わるかなって感じ。
example_sentences.english: If things work out well, I’ll be able to finish writing my college graduation thesis today.

english: Three Small Things, Three Things, Three Objects, Three Small Objects
notes: "Three individuals is three small things. The kanji 個 can be used to count small objects, just like this! Try other numbers as well." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーにはミルクとシロップを三個ずつ入れます。
example_sentences.english: I put three milks and three syrup cups in my coffee.

example_sentences.japanese: 三個入りの石けんを一箱買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a box of soap that comes with three bars.

example_sentences.japanese: チーズバーガー三個と照り焼きバーガー三個とナゲットをいくつか食べたので、今とても気持ちが悪い。
example_sentences.english: After eating three cheeseburgers, three teriyaki burgers, and several nuggets, I feel really awful.

notes: "This is a combination of the words 天気, meaning ""weather,"" and 予報 meaning ""forecast."" Put them together and you get the weather forecast!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報を事前にチェックするのが面倒くさかったんです。
example_sentences.english: I just felt that it was troublesome to check the weather forecast beforehand.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報では午後から雨になってたよ。
example_sentences.english: The weather forecast said it would rain this afternoon.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報は見事に外れた。
example_sentences.english: The weather forecast was crazy off.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This is used to refer to your own wife, though, for the most part. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: Your wife does everything for you. She feeds you, she bathes you, she cleans up after you and even wipes your butt when you poop. Really, she is doing too much (つま), and you should stop being a baby."

example_sentences.japanese: 妻のたん生日に、水上飛行機をプレゼントしました。
example_sentences.english: For my wife's birthday, I got her a seaplane.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻がコウイチのコンサートに行ってきたんですが、最後尾の席だったけど、すごく良かったと言ってましたよ。
example_sentences.english: My wife went to Koichi's concert and she said it was fantastic, though her seat was in the last row.

example_sentences.japanese: 元妻が、「私みたいな女にはもう巡り合わないわよ」とか言うんだけどさ…っていうか、それが俺の計画なんですけど、みたいな？
example_sentences.english: "My ex-wife says, ""You’ll never find someone like me."" Well exactly! That’s the plan!"

english: Wife And Kids, Wife And Children
notes: "You have your wife and you have your child. These are your wife and kids." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 家では妻子がおなかをすらせて待っているんです。
example_sentences.english: My hungry wife and children are waiting for me at home.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは妻子ある身なのに毎晩行きつけのホステスのところに通っているんだよ。ひどいと思わない？
example_sentences.english: Even though Koichi has a wife and kids, he visits his favorite hostess every night. Don't you think he's terrible?

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい支店に転勤になって、やる気満々だよ〜。イイ男探しを日課に頑張ってます。妻子持ちだろうが関係ないかんね。笑
example_sentences.english: Now that I’ve been transferred to the new branch store, I’m feeling really motivated. Working hard to find a good man has become one of my daily routines. I don’t care whether he has a wife and kids, you know? lol

notes: "You know how 宇宙 is space? Well, a person from space is an alien." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will also help to know how to read the word 宇宙 on its own, too."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの写真は、火星で干ばつと大恐慌の犠牲となった宇宙人たちを正直に、かつ同情を込めてとらえている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi’s photographs honestly and sympathetically portray aliens who were victims of drought and the Great Depression on Mars.

notes: "Your big enemy is your worst enemy. Your arch enemy." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 分かっていると思うけど、油断大敵だよ。「猿も木から落ちる」って言うだろう？
example_sentences.english: "As you all know, overconfidence is man’s greatest enemy. People say ""even monkeys fall from trees,"" right?"

notes: "You have rights to profit! This is a right you have!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: フェミニストの中には、生理中に血を垂れ流しにすることが女性の権利だと主張する人まで出てきました。
example_sentences.english: Some feminists started claiming that free-bleeding during their period is a women’s right.

english: Biker Gang, Motorcycle Gang, Japanese Bikers, Bosozoku
notes: "A tribe that runs wild (暴走) is what the Japanese call a biker gang. Just imagine them riding around on their bikes, running wild. They're also close, like a family. How nice!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエトさん、あなたが暴走族をしていた頃のエピソードについて、早急にお返事いただけると幸いです。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Viet, I would be grateful if you could reply as soon as possible about your time spent in a biker gang.

notes: "With time your body will acquire a certain type of character. It shows your true nature as a person.Note: We almost always use this word in the phrases 得体が知れない/得体の知れない, so check out the context sentences to see what kind of ""character"" we're talking about." The reading is a combination of kun'yomi and on'yomi readings. That being said, both readings for both kanji are the readings you learned already, so you should be able to read this.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな得体の知れないもの、食べられないよ。
example_sentences.english: I can’t eat something so strange.

example_sentences.japanese: 得体の知れない男がさっきからこっちを見ていると思ったら、トーフグのコウイチだった。
example_sentences.english: I thought a mysterious man was looking at me, but it turned out to be Koichi from Tofugu.

example_sentences.japanese: 得体の知れない何かが、猛スピードで迫ってくるような感覚に襲われ、冷や汗が止まらなくなりました。
example_sentences.english: I suddenly felt as if something unidentifiable was coming towards me at furious speeds and I started sweating with fear.

notes: "Cloth from the earth is still cloth, just a little dirty." The reading is a combination of kun'yomi and on'yomi readings. That being said, you've learned them both already!

example_sentences.japanese: レースを布地にたたきつける。
example_sentences.english: I stitched lace into cloth.

english: Crime Syndicate, Yakuza, Gangster Organization, Gangster Organisation
notes: "A group that has power using violence? Sounds like some kind of crime syndicate to me." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 暴力団と関東連合の違いは何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What’s the difference between the Yakuza and Kanto RENGO?

notes: "You have a duty. You have a task. You have both a duty and a task to do." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 任務完了前に撤退することは許されないとコウイチに言われました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi told me that I’m not allowed to leave before the job is done.

notes: "The main resources are the funds and capital we're getting. Everything else can be gotten using said funds, which is why they're the main resources we have!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ベンチャー・キャピタル、いわゆる冒険資本が不足するには、訳があります。
example_sentences.english: There’s a reason for the venture capital shortage.

notes: "The resources of gold that we have are our current funds. If the resources include a lot of gold, then we have a lot of funds. If they don't, then we don't have a lot of funds." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 資金が底をつき始めたときに、パリでホテル代を払ってくれるというあの素晴らしいお方にお会いしたのです。
example_sentences.english: When we started running out of funds, we met a wonderful person in Paris who offered to pay for our hotel bills.

notes: "The correct righteousness is always your righteousness. It is your form of justice." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguチームは正義の味方です。
example_sentences.english: Team Tofugu takes the side of justice.

notes: "What does your heart want to acquire above all other things? Knowledge! That's why you're here isn't it? Dig deep and see that all your heart wants is more information and understanding of Japanese to be happy." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が就職活動の心得を教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: My senpai passed on his knowledge about job hunting.

english: Member Of A Committee, Committee Member
notes: "A committee member is a member of a committee (or a committee member)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 風紀委員は、保健体育の授業で教師が夢精について生徒たちに教える必要は無いと判断した。
example_sentences.english: The school’s disciplinary committee decided that teachers don’t need to teach students about wet dreams in the physical education class anymore.

notes: "A 形容詞 is an adjective. So what about an adjective with a 動詞 (verb) in there? How does that make sense? I'm not entirely sure either, but an adjective with movement in it is a na adjective. These are the adjectives that can end with な (便利な, for example). In fact, they're more like nouns than they are verbs, so what gives? Whatever it is, just decide you don't want to deal with this craziness. Just say nah, I don't care about this anymore." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. It will help to know 形容詞 and 動詞 as well, since they're both parts of this word."

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の授業は形容動詞でした。
example_sentences.english: Today’s class was on na-adjectives.

notes: "The place where actions and tasks happen is the office. None of that happens at home. The office is more of an action / task place." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 当社トフグの事務所を簡単にご案内させてください。
example_sentences.english: Let me quickly show you around the Tofugu office.

notes: "Okayama (岡山) Prefecture is a prefecture in Japan. Learning the reading will help you to remember the meaning of this word since half of it is in Japanese." "The reading is the kun'yomi readings of the first two kanji. Luckily you learned them when you learned the kanji. Then, stick 県 on there and you should be good to go!"

example_sentences.japanese: 岡山県には、土地特有の建築物はありますか？
example_sentences.english: Is there any vernacular architecture in Okayama prefecture?

notes: "The child of a judge is the thing he puts on his judgements. What does he put on his judgments? His seal, you know, to make it all official and stuff." "判 is the reading you learned. 子 is the kun'yomi vocab reading, which I bet you know pretty well by now as well. You just have to remember to use it here."

example_sentences.japanese: この書類には、コウイチによって公的な判子が押されています。
example_sentences.english: This document was officially sealed by Koichi.

notes: "You know that 参加 is participation, so someone who does participation is a participant." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画好きのパーティーの最年長参加者は、なんと百歳だった。
example_sentences.english: Surprisingly, the oldest participant of the moviegoer party was 100 years old.

notes: "The police (警察) government is full of police officers. This is a nice way to say ""police officer."" Don't confuse it with 警察署, though." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官が容疑者を発見した際、男は丘の上で美しい風景画を描いていました。
example_sentences.english: When the police officer found the suspect, he was painting a beautiful landscape on a hilltop.

notes: "He's the whole reason this country is still running. If it wasn't for the prime minister here we'd all be doomed I say. DOOMED!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofugu.comは総理大臣賞を受賞した。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu.com won the Prime Minister’s Prize.

notes: "The credible resources that determine your professional status are your qualifications. You need some good ones if you want to get into a good school or land a sweet job." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 一流の資格を持っていたって、食いっぱぐれることはあるさ。
example_sentences.english: You can have the best qualifications and still lose the ability to make a living.

notes: "When you want to use the most basic elements of a material, you end up with raw materials. Maybe it's the raw materials you're going to use to build a house. Maybe it's the raw materials you need to make a good soup. Either way, they haven't been touched much (yet)." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The reading for 素 is the そ reading, so be careful. You can remember by thinking how you have to sew the building together using these raw materials."

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランでは、素材そのものの味を楽しんでもらうために味付けは控えめにしています。
example_sentences.english: In this restaurant, seasoning is kept to a minimum for you to enjoy the natural taste of the ingredients.

english: Space Ship, Space Shuttle, Starship, Star Ship, Ufo, Spacecraft, Space Craft, Flying Saucer
notes: "You know how 宇宙 is outer space and how 船 is ship, right? Well, put those together and you have an outer space ship (better known as a space ship)." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know the word 宇宙 beforehand as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 十六台の宇宙船のほとんど全てが、保持され改装されました。
example_sentences.english: Nearly all of the sixteen space ships were retained and refurbished.

notes: "I have a suspicion (容疑) about someone. That someone is my main suspect." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help to be able to read 容疑 first, though."

example_sentences.japanese: その容疑者は、どういう訳か十代の若者たちに大志と楽観主義のメッセージを伝えた。
example_sentences.english: The suspect somehow conveyed a message of ambition and optimism to teenagers.

notes: "The tax gold is what you have to pay when you have to pay a tax." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の両親があなたを養子縁組したのは、ただ税金の控除を受けたかったのが理由です。
example_sentences.english: My parents only adopted you because they needed the tax deduction.

notes: "Remember how 自動詞 was ""intransitive verb""? Intransitive verbs are when something just happens. You aren't doing the action to them. This word, however, is the other kind. A transitive verb is when you are directly doing something to something else. That's why it has other in there, because it's a verb (動詞) you do to another thing, directly." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その動詞が他動詞か自動詞かを学ぶには、まる暗記するしかないのかな。
example_sentences.english: Is memorization the only way to learn if the verb is transitive or intransitive?

notes: "There are many clauses about the promises you make in this contract considering it's supposed to be a treaty." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの今年の抱負は、ベルサイユ条約の全文を暗記することです。
example_sentences.english: Koichi’s New Year’s resolution is memorizing the entire text of the Treaty of Versailles.

notes: "If you control people, you make them wear the same clothes. That's a uniform." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: アヤに、制服を着た女の子の絵を、立体派の画風を取り込みながら描いてもらいたいんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I want Aya to draw girls in school uniforms and integrate cubism style into it.

notes: "A mouth flute... Normal flutes you blow air through to make a sound. How do you blow air through your mouth to make a sound? By whistling." "The reading is the kun'yomi readings put together. Thank 口 for being a body part, which tends to cause this to happen. So, you have 口 (くち) and 笛 (ふえ) put together, though ふえ changes to ぶえ, maybe because you can't whistle properly? Buuuweeee. Buwwweee."

example_sentences.japanese: 口笛が下手くそなので、私が口笛を吹いても犬が来てくれません。
example_sentences.english: My dog doesn’t come to my whistle because I’m bad at whistling.

notes: "A woman's rights consist of women's rights." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 西洋と違い、日本では歴史上、大きな女権拡張運動は起きていない。
example_sentences.english: Unlike the West, Japan does not have a history of strong women’s rights movements.

notes: "Penalty gold is the money you pay when you get a penalty. It's for a fine." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The ばつ gets changed to ばっ though, so don't get it wrong (or you'll get a 罰金!)."

example_sentences.japanese: 罰金については、追ってご連絡を差し上げます。
example_sentences.english: We’ll contact you shortly about the fine.

notes: "The guests who are viewing are the audience and spectators. That's all that viewers who are guests at a location do, right? Makes total sense." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: サーモンとコンサートに行ったんだけど、なんと他の観客は全員お相撲さんだったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I went to a concert with Salmon and surprisingly, everyone else in the audience was a Sumo wrestler.

notes: "Here's a weird one for you. You have a red monk. What is this? It's a baby. Think about it. Babies, when they come out, are all red. Also, they have a shaved head, just like a monk would. So, a ""red monk"" is really just a baby. I wonder who's getting the shorter end of the stick here, the monk or the baby? Probably the monk." "The reading is the kun'yomi vocab reading of 赤 (you learned this with the kanji) and the reading you learned for 坊 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: あーどうしたら赤ん坊を泣き止ませることができるんだろう。ミルクもあげてみたし、オムツもかえてみたでしょ。それに、げっぷもさせてみた。あ、これはどうかな？赤ちゃんを体に引き寄せて抱っこして、左右に素早く揺らしてみるって書いてあるわ。
example_sentences.english: Well, how can we get this baby to stop crying? We already tried feeding him, changing him, and burping him. Oh, here is something! It says to try holding the baby close to your body and then rocking it quickly from side to side.

hiragana: ばつげーむ, ばつゲーム
notes: "A penalty game (ゲーム) is a fun kind of game you see on Japanese television a lot. When you mess up, you are punished. Usually it hurts. You can call this a batsu game or a penalty game. Don't call it anything else, though, or you know what happens..." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この罰ゲームについて、がっかりもしてるんだけど、ワクワクしてもいるんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I’m kind of disappointed about this penalty game, but I’m also a little excited.

notes: "The appearance of fault is a huge blunder on our family. At least do not have the appearance of fault." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The しつ gets shortened to しっ, though, so make that blunder."

example_sentences.japanese: 社長は大失態を犯し、それを隠蔽しようとしたが、さらにその隠蔽工作が裏目に出てしまった。
example_sentences.english: The president made a huge blunder and he tried to cover it up, but it backfired.

notes: "What shows the district and region and where they exist? That would be the boundary. It is what surrounds every district and region, showing where it exists." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本政府は、その区域の正確な大気中の放射能濃度を公表しているのですか？
example_sentences.english: Will the Japanese government announce the exact zone in the atmosphere where the radioactivity is concentrated?

notes: "A monk who is at master status is probably a priest by now... though not just any priest, this refers to a Buddhist priest." "The 坊 reads like you'd expect. Unfortunately 主 is an exception and read ず. Just think of a zoo that holds Buddhist priests in captivity. How sad, these Buddhist priests."

example_sentences.japanese: 息子よ。現実的になれ。いい加減俺の後を継いで坊主になったらどうなんだ？
example_sentences.english: Hey, son. You have to be realistic. Isn’t it about time you followed in my footsteps and became a Buddhist priest?

notes: "A company expense is a company expense. These are nice, by the way, if you can get them." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は社費で日本語を勉強させてもらっています。
example_sentences.english: I’m studying Japanese at my company’s expense.

notes: "The condition that something is in and the appearance of it is the condition / state of that object." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は、精神状態が不安定であるということを私に打ち明けた。
example_sentences.english: My little sister told me about her unstable state of mind.

notes: "You have each each which is each (or every, or ""respectively""). Kind of goes along the lines of ""each and every"" in English." "The reading is weird. So sorry. Just imagine you look at each item. Every single one is messed up in some way. Possibly they are robots all accidentally programmed to need to kill humans. You say ""oh no oh no"" in quick succession because this is a bad situation."

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら各々独自のポテトチップスの食べ方をもっているようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems that each person has their own way of eating potato chips.

notes: "Each self refers to each person or individual." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 遠足には、各自お弁当とお菓子、水筒を持参してください。
example_sentences.english: You need to bring your own bento box, snacks, and water bottle for the school trip.

notes: "The use of expenses are the expenses and costs we have to pay, I'm afraid." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では引っ越し費用の平均って大体どれくらいなの？
example_sentences.english: Roughly how much is the average cost of moving in Japan?

notes: "Someone who has experience (経験) is an experienced person." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはTofuguに犯罪経験者を雇うと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you think Koichi would hire an experienced criminal at Tofugu?

english: Government Management, Government Operation, Run By The Government, Government Run
notes: "Managed by the government? Then it is run by government management or it is a  government operation." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本郵政をどうして官営から民営に変える必要があったのか、未だに分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I still don’t understand why Japan Post needed to change from government management to private management.

notes: "Remember blood pressure (血圧)? Well, now the blood pressure is tall... so you have ""tall blood pressure."" Well that's dumb. Let's call it high blood pressure instead." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは高血圧で、塩分の少ない食事を取る必要があるとお医者さんから言われたのに、まだ毎日ハンバーガーを食べているの。
example_sentences.english: Fugu has high blood pressure and was told that he must stick to a low-salt diet by a doctor, but he still eats hamburgers every day.

notes: "Your force and power combine together to create an influence (or a force)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その武装勢力は、急速に勢力を増大している。
example_sentences.english: The armed insurgents are rapidly increasing their influence.

notes: "Someone who has territory under their sleeve is the leader. They're the boss of all this territory because they say so, and because they shoved it all into their big sleeves." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them already, so you should be able to read this on your own!

example_sentences.japanese: 領袖の言うことは絶対だ。
example_sentences.english: What a boss says is absolute.

example_sentences.japanese: その政治家こそが、党の領袖だ。
example_sentences.english: That politician is the leader of the party.

example_sentences.japanese: 「領袖」と言う言葉は、現代では、政治的な使われることが多い。
example_sentences.english: "These days, the word ""leader"" tends to be used in the political sense."

english: "New Year's Card, New Year's Greeting Card"
notes: "A year congratulations condition is when you tell the world about your condition for the new year. What's a better way to tell them than by using a New Year's Card?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 年賀状以外の挨拶状は出さない。
example_sentences.english: I don’t send any greeting cards save for New Year’s cards.

notes: "An undressed letter is one that's missing. It's an omitted character or omitted word." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 誤字脱字を見つけたら、遠慮せずに教えてくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Don’t be afraid to let me know if you find misspelled or missing words, please.

notes: "This shinto shrine you're staying at? Turns out you go inside and it is magically turned into this amazing palace. Wow! I'm totally becoming a Shinto monk." The reading is the same as the kanji reading you learned.

example_sentences.english: You remember these long speeches well.

notes: "One division is ten percent. You'll just have to imagine this in terms of tens going by. Must be some old Japanese percentage system that carried over or something. Just remember that one wari is ten percent, two waris are twenty percent, and so on." The readings are the same as what you learned with the kanji. You know much more than ten percent of this word's reading already.

example_sentences.japanese: 「この河豚、ちょっと高すぎますよ。まけてもらえませんか？」「一割引きにしてあげましょう。」
example_sentences.english: """This blowfish is too expensive. Can you give me a discount?"" ""We’ll give you a 10% discount."""

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. I'm Mickey Mouse and I don't stand for this."

example_sentences.japanese: 木の幹に絡まっているツタを取り除いた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You should remove the ivy winding around the tree trunk.

english: Unwritten Law, Unwritten Rule, Common Law
notes: "This not writing law is a law that hasn't been written down. It's an unwritten law, like taking your shoes off and showering every day." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校では日本語でしか話してはいけないという不文律のようなものがあります。
example_sentences.english: There is some sort of unwritten rule that says people are only allowed to speak Japanese in this school.

notes: "A demon that sucks blood? What mythological creature can you think of that sucks blood? How about a vampire? Them Sparklzzzz!" "吸血 should be easy for you to read. The 鬼 part uses the reading you already learned with the kanji, き. Easy, no?"

example_sentences.japanese: あの吸血鬼の野郎、俺の事、血を吸いたくない程インチキ臭すぎるって言うんだ。
example_sentences.english: That vampire told me that he wouldn’t even suck my blood because I am too much of a phony.

notes: "The year amount is the yearly amount." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 前回のサービスも良かったとは思いますが、今回の新サービスはもっとよくなったと思うんです。それでいて、会員費は変わらず年額80ドルのままなんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I think the previous service was good, but we feel we outdid ourselves on this new service. Furthermore, the membership fees are still only eighty dollars a year.

notes: "The angle of the touch is important with an antenna. Think about antennas. An ant's antenna wiggle around and move in different angles, touching things, to understand the world around them. Imagine their tiny bug antennas touching your arm to figure out who you are." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. しょく goes to しょっ."

example_sentences.japanese: 触角の先端に目があるなんて知らなかったので、その蝸牛の触角を切り落としてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I cut off the snail’s antennae because I didn’t know its eyes are on the tips of them.

hiragana: りょううで, もろうで
notes: "Both arms are both arms!" "This is a combination of the on'yomi reading of 両 and the kun'yomi reading of 腕. You've learned them both, so you know this too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 両腕に注射の跡がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of track marks on both my arms.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: You walk up to the boundary. You're there to pick something up to take it across. This thing you're smuggling across the boundary is a sockeye (さかい) salmon. You take it across the boundary and sell it for a big profit."

example_sentences.japanese: この川がちょうど両州の境となっているんですよ。
example_sentences.english: This river forms the boundary between the two states.

hiragana: かねんごみ, かねんゴミ
english: Burnable Garbage, Burnable Trash, Burnable Rubbish
notes: "Possible to burn ゴミ (garbage). This is burnable garbage." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが私から貰うクリスマスプレゼントは、可燃ごみだけだよ。
example_sentences.english: The only thing you’re getting for Christmas from me is burnable garbage.

notes: "Your special quality is your characteristics or your traits." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 笑いは人間だけの特質なのかな？それとも動物も笑うのかな？
example_sentences.english: Is laughter a characteristic that only humans have, or can animals laugh as well?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is the ぞう reading of the kanji. You're at the ぞう show. How exciting."

example_sentences.japanese: あの象、別の動物園から来た雌の象と昨夜交尾をしたよ。
example_sentences.english: That male elephant hooked up with the female from the other zoo last night.

notes: "A material you can burn is called fuel!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 単なる燃料切れだったよ。
example_sentences.english: I was simply running out of fuel.

english: Government Office, Government Authorities, Government Agency
notes: "A government government office is a government office. Did I mention government?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 主に官庁内で使われる特別な用語ってありますか？
example_sentences.english: Are there specific words that are used mainly within government offices?

notes: "A half amount sale is when things are half price. Cheap!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ、そろそろ起きる時間よ！ウォールマートの半額セールに行かなきゃいけないんだから。
example_sentences.english: Koichi, time to get up! We have to go to Walmart’s half price sale today.

notes: "You mix, but there's a distinction as to where you mix at this point. Where is this point? It can be found when two streets cross, at an intersection." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 次の交差点を左に曲がって下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please turn left at the next intersection.

notes: "Laws are standard in society. You must have laws and regulations in society." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 海戦に関する国際法規について書かれた本は、この図書館にありますか。
example_sentences.english: Is there a book about the international laws concerning naval hostility in this library?

hiragana: ひだりうで, さわん
notes: "Your left arm is your left arm." "The reading can either be a combination of the kun'yomi readings (more common) or the on'yomi readings (a little less common). That being said, you've seen all of these readings except わん. If you want to remember さわん just think: I have just one (わん) left arm!"

example_sentences.japanese: 左腕を骨折しました。
example_sentences.english: My left arm is broken.

hiragana: あめりかせい, アメリカせい
notes: "America manufactured is something that is made in America." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ製の寿司は食べられないだって？好き嫌いするんじゃないよ！
example_sentences.english: You really won’t eat sushi that was made in America? You’re too picky.

notes: "China (中国) manufactured items are made in China." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help if you know the word 中国 already."

example_sentences.japanese: インターネット上で、中国製の日本語学習サイトがどれだけあるのかについては、正確な数字は今は分かりません。調べてのちほどお答えします。
example_sentences.english: I’m afraid I’m not sure of the exact number of Japanese learning sites on the internet right now that were made in China. I’ll check on it and get back to you later.

notes: "Things that are manufactured in Japan (日本) are made in Japan. Good quality stuff, that is." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help if you know how to read 日本 already."

example_sentences.japanese: その日本製の刀の柄には、美しい宝石が散りばめられている。
example_sentences.english: The sword hilt was made in Japan and is studded with beautiful jewels.

notes: "If you take the road of the military you're going to have to fight a lot. Back in the day, this involved learning martial arts to fight with. Remember, just wax off." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 武道の経験が無い日本人はたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: There are many Japanese people who don’t have any experience in martial arts.

english: Material Quality, Item Quality, Product Quality, Quality
notes: "A product's quality is in its material quality. If the materials aren't any good then the product isn't either." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は品質管理マネージャーとして入社した。
example_sentences.english: She’s been brought on board as the quality control manager.

notes: "The metropolis agency is the government that controls the metropolitan area. This is the metropolitan government." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京都庁の展望台に行った事はありますか。
example_sentences.english: Have you been to the observation deck of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building?

english: Metropolitan Police Department, Metro Police Department
notes: "They warn, they look at crime, and they're an agency of the government. They are the metropolitan police department." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の兄は、東京都警視庁公安部に勤めています。
example_sentences.english: My brother works for the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department Public Security Bureau.
