example_sentences.japanese: 月額たったの5ドルでできる新しい日本語学習体験を促進するための広告キャンペーンを打ち始めます。
example_sentences.english: We are starting an advertising campaign to encourage a new Japanese learning experience that costs only five dollars a month.

notes: "Unlike the 警視庁, who look at things, this is just the police officer (警察) agency. Just the general police agency of the whole country, making them part of the National Police Agency." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 警視庁と警察庁の違いは何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What’s the difference between the Metropolitan Police Department and the National Police Agency?

hiragana: ふねんごみ, ふねんゴミ
english: Nonburnable Garbage, Unburnable Garbage, Nonburnable Trash, Unburnable Trash, Nonburnable Rubbish, Unburnable Rubbish
notes: "These are not burnable garbages (ごみ). Pay attention to this on signs when you throw things away. You want to put the right things into nonburnable garbage." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 不燃ゴミは火曜日に出してください。
example_sentences.english: Please take out the nonburnable garbage on Tuesday.

notes: "営業 means running a business. You're in the middle of running a business, which means you're open for business (otherwise you wouldn't be in the middle of running it, you'd be at the beginning or something)." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help to know 営業 first."

example_sentences.japanese: 営業中に電話しないでって言ったじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I asked you not to call me when the shop is open.

notes: "The past shape is how things were in the past. To describe those things (like you would with an adjective, aka 形容詞), you'd use past tense." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この場合は過去形は使わないんですか？
example_sentences.english: Don’t you use the past tense in this case?

notes: "A present time phenomenon is a phenomenon whether it's in the present or in the future or in the past." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本にUFO現象を調査しているUFO団体はありますか？
example_sentences.english: Are there any UFO groups investigating the UFO phenomena in Japan?

notes:
"The item is in a place in its existence where it is published. If something is in this place, it is printed and published." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"I write for purification. I do this purification writing in my study and den." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 『古事記』所載の日本最古の和歌について何か知っていますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know anything about the Japanese first waka published in the Kojiki?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は一日中書斎で重要書類を探していたんですが、まだ見つからないんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I was searching for an important document in my study all day today, but haven’t found it yet.

notes: "Manufactured goods are manufactured goods. What does that end up being? A product." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社の新製品に関する会議を火曜日の午後に延期することは可能かな？
example_sentences.english: Would it be possible to postpone the launch of our new product until Tuesday afternoon?

notes: "The remainder amount is the remaining amount." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 残額は五百円あるので、次の旅行に繰り越すこともできるし、半日市内バス観光をすることもできます。
example_sentences.english: The balance is 500 yen, so we could carry it over to the next trip or we could also go on a half-day bus tour of the city.

notes: "A group that roots for you is your rooting section or  cheerleaders. Go go go you!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. example_sentences.japanese: ああ、君が応援団長だね？噂はかねがね伺っておるよ。
example_sentences.english: Hey, you are the leader of the cheerleaders, right? I’ve heard a lot about you.

notes: "A military samurai is a samurai. This is how most people say ""samurai"" in Japanese." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは武士のようにストイックに走り続け、フルマラソンを完走した。
example_sentences.english: Koichi kept running as stoically as a samurai and finished the full marathon.

notes: "A stocks ritual is the dance we do in the modern world around stocks and shares of different companies. Buy! Sell! Buy! Sell!" The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 株式市場が底なしの下落に陥ったようだというニュースは、彼に大きな精神的ダメージを与えた。
example_sentences.english: The news that the stock market seemed to go into a bottomless decline was a great blow to him.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは株でガッポリ儲けたので、車のタイヤをどでかいホイール・タイヤに変えて、シートも革張りにしてカッチョ良くしちゃおうと決めた。
example_sentences.english: Koichi made tons of money on the stock market and decided to swag out his car with big wheels and leather seats.

notes: "The time distinction is how you tell apart time zones. It is the time difference." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ時差ボケに苦しんでいるんです。
example_sentences.english: I’m still suffering from jet lag.

example_sentences.english: Please pay the total amount for the candy yourself.

notes: "Sightseeing (観光) guests are tourists and sightseers." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help to know 観光 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: その観光客は、アメリカで医者の診断書をもらうために50ドルを支払わなければならなかった。

notes: "I want to expand my business. I want to show my goods. I want to do this in a place where everyone meets up to do these things. You can do this in a trade show." example_sentences.japanese: 私の兄は、カフェで初めての美術展示会を開催した。

english: Values, Sense Of Values, Moral Values
notes: "These views that have merit (価値) are your values." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚相手と価値観が近いことって結構大切だと思うんだよねー。
example_sentences.english: I think it’s quite important to share similar values with your spouse.

notes: "Automatic (自動) sell sell machine. The machine sells things by itself, basically. This is a vending machine. example_sentences.japanese: 10月23日の自動販売機に関する会議は、コウイチの誕生日会のため、10月24日に変更されました。
example_sentences.english: The October twenty-third meeting about the vending machines has been rescheduled for October twenty-fourth due to Koichi’s birthday party.

notes: "Remember how 時計 is watch? An arm is now there too, making this a wristwatch." "The readings are the words 腕 (same reading as what you learned with the kanji) as well as the reading for 時計. Just don't forget that rendaku!"

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の無くなった腕時計についてちょっと話がしたいんだけど、いいか？あまり時間は取らせないよ。
example_sentences.english: Can we talk about my missing wristwatch for a second? I won’t take up too much of your time.

notes: "It's a prize where you are given gold. In business, this is called a bonus. You didn't expect it (not your salary) and it is given to you (and is gold, if you're lucky)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 給料日は毎月5日と20日で、会社の業績次第で賞与金が年末に支払われます。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の景況感が大きく上向くのは、まだまだ先のことだろう。

notes: "The candidate is someone who's a supplement to the entire political system. Despite being a supplement, (s)he's still a candidate nonetheless, unless she can win!" example_sentences.japanese: 学歴的には、候補者として十分通用するはずが、彼は性格に難があるからね。
example_sentences.english: Academically speaking, the candidate would be very useful, but he has such a bad personality.

notes: "The energy of the climate is the climate. High energy? Climate. Low energy. Climate." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 気候は荒れ模様だが、新しい仕事ではいいスタートが切れた。
example_sentences.english: I got off to a good start with my new job, considering the threatening climate.

english: Complete View, Full View, Panoramic View, Panorama

"The front scene is the foreground." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は息を飲むような富士の全景を期待していたが、実際はかなりお粗末なものだった。

example_sentences.japanese: 効率が第一だということを、しっかり心に刻んで置いてください。
example_sentences.english: Keep in mind that efficiency is our top priority.

notes: "The above scroll is the top scroll, the one you read first. It's the first volume. Many Japanese books come in parts, so look for this if you want to get the first one." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 上巻の終わりは、すごく続きが気になる感じで終わった。
example_sentences.english: The ending of the first volume was a real cliff-hanger.

notes: "Fresh fish is fresh fish (and the best fish, nom nom nom)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の魚屋で働いている限り、従業員は福利厚生として鮮魚をもらう権利を、放棄することはできないぜ。
example_sentences.english: Employees cannot waive their right to receiving fresh fish as a benefit as long as they work for my fish shop.

notes: "In the shadows you still echo. Your echo leaves the shadows and hits people, creating an influence on them. You're like the shadow person pulling the strings, making things do what you want... influencing them." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 残業は健康に悪影響を及ぼす可能性があるということを考えた方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You should consider that working extra hours may have a negative influence on your health.

notes: "The comrade who's behind you is your junior." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The reading for 後 is the long こう reading, though. Just think of your junior being こういち."

example_sentences.japanese: お前は俺のお気に入りの後輩だから、どんなことがあってもちゃんと面倒みてやるよ。
example_sentences.english: I’ll take care of you, no matter what happens because you’re my favorite underclassmen.

notes: "The scroll that's below is the last scroll you read, making it the last volume." "The 下 uses the alternative reading of げ but 巻 is all good and normal."

example_sentences.japanese: 上巻を買ったつもりが下巻を買ってしまっていた。
example_sentences.english: I thought I bought the first volume, but it was actually the last volume.

hiragana: かわじゃん, かわジャン
notes: "革 is leather and ジャン is short for ジャンパー (Jumper, like a jacket). So, put those together and you have a leather jacket." "The reading is the same as the vocab word 革, because this word is like two separate words put together (so it's treated as single words too, giving it that reading)."

example_sentences.japanese: お洒落大好き人間にアドバイスされたってだけで、あんな高い革ジャンは買うわけないじゃん。
example_sentences.english: I’m not buying such an expensive leather jacket just because a fashionista told me to.

notes: "The limit degree is how far you can go. It's your limit. Turn things up one more degree and it's too much. Keep it right where it is and it's perfect. It's your limit." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このクレジットカードの限度額がいくらだったか忘れちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I forget what my limit is on this credit card.

notes: "Your fee for being obese is lots of manure coming out of your butt. If you eat a lot you'll poop a lot of manure." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 肥料工場での社員間のいざこざについて、どう対処していいか全くわかりませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I had no idea how to handle the conflict among the workers at the fertilizer factory.

notes: "Gold belongs to this family... ""What is metal?""" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 厳しい景況にもかかわらず、あの金属メッキ工場は成長を続けている。
example_sentences.english: The metal-plating factory is thriving despite the challenging business climate.

notes: "Long Cape Prefecture. This will make more sense when you look at the reading. Hint: It's Nagasaki Prefecture." "The readings are 長 from 長い, normal 崎 and normal 県."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は長崎県の出身で、家族の墓も全部そこにあります。
example_sentences.english: I am from Nagasaki prefecture and my family graves are all located there, too.

notes: "One scroll is one scroll back in the day, but now it refers to books and means one volume." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. いち goes to いっ."

example_sentences.japanese: 一巻では、全ての引用に脚注がつけられ出典が記されています。
example_sentences.english: In the first volume, all sources are cited in the footnotes.

notes: "An imitation manner is something that does something in the manner of something else. Imitation over and over and over. Make it into a pattern." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Since you didn't learn the on'yomi for 様 with the kanji, here's a mnemonic to help you out. You see a pattern in your yogurt (よう). The yogurt is an imitation of life. So deep, man. So deep."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妻は、小さな花の模様が好きです。
example_sentences.english: My wife likes patterns with small flowers.

notes: "A person who lives in a revolution (革命) house is a revolutionary. They want government change! They want to take down the people in power!" "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Of course it will help to know 革命 already as well."

example_sentences.japanese: あの革命家は、ネット弁けいだ。
example_sentences.english: That revolutionary is only hot-tempered on the Internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 革命家になりたければ、まずは効果的な話し方を身につけないといけないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you want to be a revolutionary, first you need to be able to speak effectively.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は情熱的なフランス人革命家と恋に落ちた。
example_sentences.english: She fell in love with a passionate French revolutionary.

notes: "Quite the scene, this view is. What you're looking at is called scenery. And, in fact, it's a spectacular view!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は京都の景観がとても好きです。
example_sentences.english: I really like Kyoto’s scenery.

notes:
"The time's climate is the current season. Each season has a different climate and exists in a different time of year." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"An action paragraph is a paragraph that shows the matter or the items or the facts. Sort of the action items, you know?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では、通常手紙は時候の挨拶から書き始められる。
example_sentences.english: People usually begin letters with a seasonal greeting in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 用紙に必要事項を記載のうえ、郵送をお願い致します。
example_sentences.english: Could you fill out the form and mail it to us, please?

notes: "The number two scroll is the second volume. With Japanese books, they often come in pieces with groups of three being common. This represents the second volume." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 二巻では、引用の出典に関する別表が作成されました。
example_sentences.english: They made an appendix for all sources cited in the second volume.

notes: "My comrade who came before me is my senior, my senpai (せんぱい)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の先輩、悪い人では無いんだけどさ、ただちょっと俺とは反りが合わないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: My superior isn’t a bad guy, but he and I just haven’t been able to hit it off.

notes: "A scene that's as awesome and bright as sunlight is quite the spectacle." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: このような絵のように美しい光景は今までみたことがありません。
example_sentences.english: I’ve never seen such a beautiful sight before.

notes: "Heaven's climate is the weather." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 繁忙期に旅行をすれば費用が嵩むのは分かっているけど、そうはいっても天候もその時期が一番いいからね。
example_sentences.english: I know there will be extra costs if we travel during peak season, but the weather will be the best around that time.

notes: "This is a combination of the words 家庭 and 教師. A ""teacher"" who only teaches when you're with your ""family"" is known as a tutor. They don't teach you at school, they're a private teacher that comes to your home to help you learn." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 家庭教師のアルバイトをしています。
example_sentences.english: I work part time as a tutor.

notes: "Needle medicine is when you stick needles into people to cure them. This is done via an acupuncturist." "This word uses the kun'yomi reading for 針 and the on'yomi reading for 医. You haven't learned this reading for 針 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:If you do acupuncture and stick a bunch of needles in your back it's going to look really hairy (はり). Needles look just like metal hairs when they're coming out of someone. Just picture hairy little needles all over your body and you'll never forget this reading!"

example_sentences.japanese: 針医の技術の進歩には驚くばかりです。
example_sentences.english: It’s amazing to think that acupuncturist techniques have come this far.

notes: "Again with that occurrence? That occurrence has now happened again." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just remember that there's a い hiding in there!"

example_sentences.japanese: 相手は、埋め立て計画に反対する請願書を再度持ってくるかもしれませんよ。
example_sentences.english: They may bring forward a petition against our landfill project again.

notes: "We waited an interval of time, and at each interval it was different. They're all supposed to be the same. Is there some kind of mistake?" "Take the reading of 間 (ま from 間に合う) and 違う and you'll have the reading for this word too."

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい市場に参入したことは間違いじゃなかった。
example_sentences.english: Expanding into new markets was not a mistake.

notes: "違い is difference, so a big one of those is a big difference." "The reading is 違う plus 大 of 大きい (おお) put together. You can remember this because when you see the difference (the BIG difference), you say ""oohhhhh"" (お), because you were surprised you didn't see it before."

example_sentences.japanese: 堅い木の椅子と柔らかい快適な椅子じゃあ大違いだよ。
example_sentences.english: There is a big difference between a hard wooden chair and a soft cushy chair.

notes: "The act of alcohol creation is done via brewing and distilling." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ジムの会員権や食事だけではなく酒まで無料の特典として提供されるので、私はこの酒造での仕事が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like working for this brewing company because they offer all these perks like free gym membership, free food, and even free sake.

notes: "It can carry a river. It's a canal." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The か goes to が, probably while floating down said canal."

example_sentences.japanese: 冬には運河の上でスケートができますよ。
example_sentences.english: You can skate on the canal during the winter.

notes: "A special indication on something or yourself is a special characteristic. It's a distinctive feature that exists." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 優柔不断と事なかれ主義が彼の特徴だ。
example_sentences.english: His personality is characterized by indecision and immobilism.

hiragana: かぶしきがいしゃ, かぶしきかいしゃ
notes: "This company (会社) has done the ritual required to create stocks for their company. When a company has stocks, they become a corporation." The readings for everything here are the readings you learned with the individual kanji, though not all are on'yomi. This word is usually rendaku'd too, but sometimes you'll see the non-rendaku version when it comes to English language legal stuff, so keep that in mind.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofugu株式会社に電話を入れて、ファックスの送信がきちんと完了しているかどうか確認してくれる？
example_sentences.english: Can you call Tofugu Corporation to make sure the fax went through alright?

notes: "The first (第一) phenomenon is what's sealed into your head. This is your first impression of something." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: オペレーターは、電話をかけてくださったお客様にとって、会社の 第一印象になるということを教えられました。
example_sentences.english: We were all taught that an operator is the first impression that a caller has of our company.

notes: "Although this has a い on the end it's tricky and not an adjective. The kanji is fortune, and the vocab word is fortune telling." "I'm going to do some fortune telling on you... hmmm... I see... ohhhh... Looks like you'll be living on Uranus (うらな) in your near future, that will be $50. What a dumb fortune telling for $50, you definitely won't be living there, unless he meant your butt, then maybe."

example_sentences.japanese: 星占いによると、フグと私ってあまり相性が良くないみたいなんだよね。
example_sentences.english: According to the stars, Fugu and I aren’t supposed to have so much chemistry between us.

notes: "The only kind of writing brush you can use for ten thousand years is a fountain pen! All other pens run out of ink and then you're out of luck. But fountain pens can be refilled, making them work for pretty much exactly ten thousand years.  " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 万年筆を落とされましたよ。
example_sentences.english: You dropped your fountain pen.

notes: "The river pig is what's known as fugu or blowfish. That's the mascot for our best friend, the Tofugu!" "The reading makes no sense, really. Neither kanji readings work. But, if you remember that a river pig is a fugu, you can know the reading is ふぐ as well! YOU ARE A BLOWFISH, JESSE!"

example_sentences.japanese: 「豆腐と河豚のサンドイッチをお願いします。」 「同じく。」
example_sentences.english: """I’ll have a blowfish and tofu sandwich."" ""I’ll have the same."""

notes: "Look at that suspicious beast... it's Godzilla, walking around looking suspicious. What is Godzilla? He is a giant monster." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーマンは、怪獣に数分遅れて現れた。
example_sentences.english: Superman turned up a few minutes later than the giant monster.

notes: "An ice river is some ice that moves (very slowly) like a river. That is a glacier. In fact, many inlets and sounds were created with glaciers, because glaciers moved through them like rivers... not very quickly, though." "The reading for 氷 is the one you didn't learn. Think of the glacier coming slowly to your door. It rings your doorbell and says heyo (ひょう)."

example_sentences.japanese: 地球温暖化のために、毎年溶けている氷河が増えている。
example_sentences.english: The number of melting glaciers has been increasing every year due to global warming.

notes: "It can hinder a child, but that's about it. This is a Japanese Sliding Door. They're often made of rice paper after all, so, you know, an adult can go through it but a child would be hindered by it." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The 子 is changed from し to じ, though, so be careful."

example_sentences.japanese: 障子から差し込む光で、朝目を覚ますのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like being woken up by the sunlight filtering gently through shoji screen.

notes: "A river juvenile... not what you think. It's a kappa, a mythological Japanese creature. That being said, it lives in / around rivers and is about the size of a juvenile, so maybe this makes sense." "The reading for 河 makes sense. The reading for 童 however is weird. Since the meaning is ""kappa"" though you can use that to remember the reading as well. If you don't know what a kappa is do some research on the internets and figure out about them. It's interesting, and it will help you to remember this word."

example_sentences.japanese: まるで河童が存在していることを信じているかのようにリアクションしてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Can you react as if you believe Kappa really exist?

notes: "Create a garden? You'll have to know a lot about landscape gardening." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業した時、造園会社から内定をもらっていました。
example_sentences.english: When I graduated from the college, I had a job offer from a landscape gardening company.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Lots of lead, all in bullet form. That's what it was like in nam, 'arry"" (なまり)."

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はすごくやる気が無くて、体が鉛のように重く感じる。
example_sentences.english: I’m so unmotivated today, my body feels as heavy as lead.

notes: "A lead pipe is a lead pipe. Don't hit people with this in the knees." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 水道の配管には、かつては鉛管がよく使われていました。
example_sentences.english: Lead piping was once often used in plumbing systems.

notes: "Mail has convenience because it is sent for you in the mail." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The reading of 便 (びん) in this vocabulary is an exceptional reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you out. You get a lot of junk mail so you throw it in the waste bin (びん). The waste bin is where junk mail goes."

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便業においては、効率とスピードが全てだ。
example_sentences.english: Efficiency and speed are everything in mail service.

notes: "管理 is ""management."" A management person is a manager." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 忙しい一日を終えて、管理人に「早く仕事を切り上げて帰りたい」という魔がさした。
example_sentences.english: After such a busy day, the manager was tempted to close up and go home early.

notes: "The kanji and the word are almost exactly the same. This word means mark." "You see a beautiful woman in front of you. She shows you a mark on a piece of paper. It's a mark that tells you she's Russian (しるし)!"

example_sentences.japanese: 私は手紙の最後にハートの印を付けるのが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like putting a heart mark at the end of letters.

notes: "If you come across a suspicious thing it's probably a monster! Run away!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この山には、心の優しい怪物が住んでいるという言い伝えがある。
example_sentences.english: Legends say there is a kind hearted monster living in this mountain.

english: Month After Next, The Month After Next
notes: "The next month (来月) isn't enough... one more next month, please. Let's do it again. That month is the month after next." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 再来月に一週間の休暇が取れるんだけど、どこか一緒にいかない？
example_sentences.english: I have the vacation time to take a weeklong getaway a month after next so do you want to go somewhere with me?

notes: "Your lead writing brush has lead in it. What kind of writing instrument has lead in it? How about a pencil?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: そのパグは、このHBの鉛筆で描いたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I drew the pug with this HB pencil.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に豚呼ばわりされて腹が立ったので、速攻で人事課に退職届けを叩きつけてやった。
example_sentences.english: My boss called me a pig and I was so upset that I immediately turned in my letter of resignation to the Human Resources department.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you:When thinking about the circumstances of your current situation and the reason you're there (which is studying kanji and vocab). Who's fault is it? It's WaniKani's fault! But, your brain has been beaten to a mush from all the studying, so when you say ""it's your fault"" it comes out as ""it's yue fault!"" Go ahead and say it out loud that way."

example_sentences.japanese: それ故、兄は両親から勘当されてしまったのです。
example_sentences.english: For that reason, my older brother was disinherited by our parents.

notes: "Your right arm is your right arm." The reading can either be a combination of the kun'yomi readings (more common) or the on'yomi readings (a little less common). That being said, you've seen all of these readings one way or another by now. Yay!

example_sentences.japanese: 奴の右腕には、龍のタトゥーがあるハズだ。
example_sentences.english: I think that’s supposed to be a dragon tattoo on that guy’s right arm.

notes: "The second needle is the thin hand that indicates seconds on your clock. That's the second hand of a clock." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 腕時計の秒針が折れちゃってるの。
example_sentences.english: My wrist watch’s second hand has been broken.

notes: "There is not any of I. It is all about everyone else. It is all about selflessness." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は鮫に追いかけられて、無我夢中で泳ぎました。
example_sentences.english: I was being followed by a shark so I lost myself swimming for my life.

notes: "The location in the city where the stocks ritual takes place is the stock market. Just think of what happens in a stock market... the stock ritual, where people buy and sell stocks. And, of course, this is located in the city." "The readings are all readings you've seen before - either from other words or from the kanji. Go through each kanji here and figure out which is which and try to remember. Just think of Joe (場) the stock broker for the last kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: 世界的な景気の減速は、私たちの株式市場にも影響を及ぼした。
example_sentences.english: The global slowdown has significantly affected our stock market, as well.

notes: "A suspicious incident (事件) always has a strange mystery behind it. It also always turns into a mystery case." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ホームズでさえもその怪事件の糸口を見つけることはできないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even Holmes wouldn’t be able to find a clue to that mystery.

notes: "First you have to set up the structure of something to create it. This structure is important for the creation of everything, otherwise it would just fall apart." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はエッセイの構造とルールについて授業をします。
example_sentences.english: I’ll teach you guys essay structure and rules today.

notes: "Remember the super long vending machine that is 自動販売機? This is a shorter easier to remember and say version. Basically every other kanji is removed, making it 自販機." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will also help if you know 自動販売機 already."

example_sentences.japanese: 父親が誕生日に自販機をプレゼントしてくれた。
example_sentences.english: My father gave me a vending machine as a birthday present.

notes: "The energy phenomenon agency sounds like something that could be really cool but it's really just the weather agency / meteorological agency. Nothing shady going on here." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: やっと気象庁に電話が繋がったと思ったら、切られたんだよ。ありえなくね？
example_sentences.english: I thought I finally got my call through to the weather agency, but they hung up on me. Unbelievable.

notes: "You know how 来週 is next week? Well, if you do next week again, you have the week after next." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーメーカー とか、キッチン向けの小型電気器具を売ってるいい感じのお店を見つけたんだけど、再来週一緒にいってみない？
example_sentences.english: I found a really nice shop selling small kitchen appliances, like coffee makers, so do you want to go there with me week after next?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: For as long as you can remember, your family and another family has had a bloody feud (ふで) over this one writing brush. Just think of all the people killed over this brush. This feud has to end."

example_sentences.japanese: 筆マークのアイコンの上にカーソルを合わせて、マウスの左のボタンをカチカチッと２回クリックしてください。
example_sentences.english: Put the cursor over the brush icon and click the left mouse button twice.

notes: "You have next year (来年), but then you do a year again. That's the year after next." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 再来年まで継続する二年契約を提案するべきではないでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: We should propose a two year contract that lasts until the year after next.

english: Allowance, Wages, Pay, Salary, Gross Pay
notes: "The salary I give you is your allowance. It is the wages you earn." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎月の給与は、指定の銀行口座にお振り込み致します。
example_sentences.english: We transfer your monthly allowance to your appointed bank account.

notes: "A healthy bit of forgetting symptoms means you might have amnesia." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 健忘症に苦しんでいる親戚がいます。
example_sentences.english: I have a relative who is suffering from amnesia.

notes: "影響 is influence, so an evil influence is a bad influence." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪影響が自分の子どもにまで及んでいたことに気が付き、彼女は泣き出した。
example_sentences.english: She cried as she realized that her bad influence filtered down to her children.

notes: "Ugh, that field guy. He's the worst. Always in the fields, making us look bad, quite the bastard. Really though, he's just this guy, but for some reason I sometimes don't like him." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あのクソ野郎がセールス・マネージャーに昇進するなんて本当に気に食わねぇ。
example_sentences.english: That bastard got promoted to sales manager. I’m sick to my stomach.

notes: "Long shoes aren't long in that the feet part are long (that wouldn't make sense). Instead, the top part is long, making them into boots." "The reading is a bit weird. Double kun'yomi, so think along the lines of 長い and 靴 getting added together. 靴 is the reading you learned with the kanji, however. It also gets rendaku'd."

example_sentences.japanese: 病院のベッドに横になりながら、彼は明日妻にいい長靴を買ってやろうと思った。
example_sentences.english: While laying in his hospital bed that night, he decided he would get a nice pair of rain boots for his wife next day.

notes: "The degree of human thickness in the area will show the amount of people. Higher degrees of human thickness = more people. Lower degrees of human thickness = less people. That is the population density of the area, or the concentration of people." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの血中アルコール濃度については追って連絡致します。
example_sentences.english: I’ll get back to you on your blood-alcohol concentration.

notes: "Head pain is when you have a headache." "The reading for 痛 should be okay. The reading for 頭 isn't one you've learned before, however. Just think, every time you go to the zoo (ず) you get a terrible headache. Must be the animal feces floating around in the air."

example_sentences.japanese: 頭痛が頻発することを母親に相談しました。
example_sentences.english: I discussed my frequent headaches with my mother.

notes: "The rest you do in your spare time is your time off. It is your holiday." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもどのくらい前から休暇の予定を立てますか？
example_sentences.english: How far in advance do you usually make vacation plans?

notes: "The not sleep symptom shows you have a disorder that involves not sleeping. That is insomnia." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼と仕事をするのがストレスで、不眠症になってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Working with him is so stressful that I got insomnia.

notes: "An alive alcohol shop is a place that does a lot of alcohol. In Japan, these places are often izakaya, or, if you don't know Izakaya already from English, you can consider it to be a Japanese Style Bar." The readings here are a bit weird. If you know what an izakaya is already from English, you can use that to remember the reading quite easily.

example_sentences.japanese: 扉が開き、居酒屋の中に老婆が一人ぼっちで入ってきた。
example_sentences.english: The door opened and an old woman walked into to the Izakaya restaurant by herself.

notes: "The selling (販売) of something has a limit (限定). This kind of item is one of limited edition." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では三台のみの限定販売になるそうなんだが、寝台車付き特急の実物大型模型を買おうか迷っているんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m thinking of getting a life‐size model of bullet train with sleepers but they’re limited edition and only three will be sold in Japan.

english: Lost Child, Lost Kid, Lost Person
notes: "A child that's astray is a lost child. Help them home, don't invite them into your windowless van, please." "The reading for 迷 is an exceptional reading. The ご comes from こ. Think of the まい as the child asking: ""Where is my (まい) mommy???"""

example_sentences.japanese: 迷子の子どもの両親を探してあげようとしていただけなのに、誘拐未遂で起訴されてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I was just trying to find the parents of a lost child, but I was accused of attempted kidnapping.

notes: "If you're in the middle of the planned route you're on the way / en route." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今すぐに来られますか？」「ええ。今向かっている途中です。」「え？ということは、場所をご存知なんですね？」「いいえ、分かりません。」
example_sentences.english: """Can you come over right now?"" ""Sure, I’m actually on my way now."" ""Huh? Do you know where you’re going?"" ""Nope, I don’t."""

notes: "This place has extreme comfort. It is paradise." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 間違いで極楽に行った男についての小説が、映画化されました。
example_sentences.english: The novel about a man who went to paradise by mistake was made into a movie.

notes: "The value is in various steps. Each step is a different amount, and each amount is a price or cost." "The reading is the kun'yomi reading for 値 plus the on'yomi reading for 段. Combine them together to get the reading here. You've learned both of these readings already, so just remember 値 is ね because you neigh (ね) when you see a good price."

example_sentences.japanese: テレビとタイアップした書籍を手がけているのは本当だが、まだ値段は決まっていない。
example_sentences.english: It’s true that we are working on our TV tie-in book, but the price hasn’t been decided yet.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji. Huzzah!

example_sentences.japanese: 「ああ、足が棒だよ。痛くて死にそう。」「言わんこっちゃない。だから、もっと歩きやすい靴を履けって最初に言ったじゃないか。」
example_sentences.english: """Ah, my feet are killing me."" ""Told you so! That’s why I told you to wear more comfortable shoes."""

notes: "A shoes shop is one that sells shoes. It's a shoe store or shoe shop." The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 靴屋での仕事に内定が出たが、丁重にお断りさせてもらったよ。
example_sentences.english: I was offered a job at the shoe store, but I politely declined.

notes: "What's below your shoes? Your socks." This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji. You've learned them already, so you should be able to read this word too!

example_sentences.japanese: ピンクの靴下を取ろうと一番上の棚に手を伸ばしたが、背丈が足りずに届かなかった。
example_sentences.english: I tried to reach the top shelf to get a pair of pink socks, but I wasn’t tall enough.

notes: "The current step of the floor is at the second stage. Now it's at the third stage. Now it's in the final phase! Nice!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏は、私が妊娠からかなり経った段階まで妊娠の事実を伝えなかったことについて私を責めました。
example_sentences.english: My boyfriend accused me of not telling him I was pregnant until I was in the advanced stages of pregnancy.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: ストレスで、胃がキリキリします。
example_sentences.english: My stomach aches from stress.

notes: "When your stomach hurts you have yourself a little stomachache. Try keeping your stomach warmer next time." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 禁煙してから、激しい胃痛も治まっている。
example_sentences.english: Since I quit smoking my intense stomach aches have also stopped.

notes: "第一 is the first thing. 段 is a step. So, this is the first step." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 第一段階として、まずは基本の復習をしなくちゃいけないかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: I may need to review the basics for the first step.

notes: "Reason yields to theory and more reason." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 理屈ばっかりこねて、本当に嫌味な人ね。
example_sentences.english: The only reason you argue is because you’re really a disagreeable person.

english: Wages, Pay, Salary, Net Pay, Base Wages, Base Salary
notes:
"Your salary fee are the moneys you get for your salary. These are your wages and pay." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

"Just because there's a mausoleum on this hill doesn't mean it isn't still a hill. (It is. It's still a hill.)" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「君の上司が、君の給料を上げるつもりだって聞いたよ。」「まさか！そんなことあり得ないよ。」
example_sentences.english: """I heard your boss is going to give you a raise."" ""Really? That’ll be the day."""

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は天気が良かったので、矢田丘陵を歩きました。
example_sentences.english: The weather was nice today so I walked the Yata hills.

english: Advance Ticket, Ticket Sold In Advance
notes: "A ticket you sell beforehand are advance tickets. This is a ticket sold in advance. Buy your tickets early, or how else will you get in on a Conan audience?" "The readings are 前 売る and 券 combined into one awkward word."

example_sentences.japanese: 前売り券は他の割引とは併用できませんって書いてあるよ。
example_sentences.english: It says that tickets sold in advance can’t be used with other discounts.

notes: "A giant person is a giant." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「何してるの？」「俺達、進撃の巨人を見てるんだよ。って、あぁ、しまった。最後の字幕見逃しちゃった。ちょっと巻き戻してくれない？」「了解。ストップって言ってね。」「ストップ！」
example_sentences.english: """What are you guys doing?"" ""We are watching Attack on Titan. Oops. I totally missed the last subtitle. Can you rewind it a bit?"" ""OK. Just tell me when to stop."" ""Stop!"""

notes: "The army squad is an army. It's also just the army. It refers more to ""an"" army rather than ""the"" army. Just a group of people who do army things." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この鰐蟹軍隊の成功のためには、あなたが必要なんです。どうか入隊してください。
example_sentences.english: I need you. You are crucial to the success of this crabigator army. Please join us.

notes: "An arrow seal is an arrow you stick down on a sign or piece of paper or document or whatever. We can just call it an arrow, though." "The reading is 矢 and 印 put together into one. The 印 is like the actual vocab word 印, so think back on that."

example_sentences.japanese: あの矢印の道路標識は何という意味ですか。
example_sentences.english: What does the arrow road sign mean?

notes: "Gold storage is where you put your gold. You want it to be safe, so you put it in a safe." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が私の金庫を盗んでいた時、私はその物音が聞こえないふりをしていました。
example_sentences.english: I pretended not to hear him when he stole from my safe.

notes: "A beach area is just a beach!" "The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You haven't learned this reading for 辺 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Beach starts with be. Be is べ! (I mean, it's pronounced differently, but they're spelled the same!) When you think of the beach, think of べ!"

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒に浜辺を散歩しないか。
example_sentences.english: Shall we take a walk on the beach together?

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. A better way to say beach is 海." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: エンジンの調子がおかしくなったので、浜に着くほんの手前で車を止めなきゃいけなくなっちゃったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Our car’s engine was making strange sounds so we had to stop right before we were going to arrive at the beach.

english: Book Of Tickets, Train Tickets, Train Coupons
notes: "Many times is how many times you can use this number of tickets. That means there are many tickets, making this a book of tickets." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車の回数券は金券ショップでも買えますよ。
example_sentences.english: You can also buy a book of train tickets from a ticket outlet.

english: Candy Store, Candy Shop, Sweet Store, Sweet Shop
notes: "お菓子 is ""candy,"" right? Add store onto that and you have a candy store." "This word uses the readings you learned with the kanji. It will help to know the word お菓子 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん、心配しなくていいよ。あのお菓子屋さんなら僕、一人でも行けるよ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t worry mom. I can go to the candy store by myself.

notes: "You have 時代 as a ""period"" of time you're talking about. What period? The infancy years. Those years are not just when you're a baby, but when you were growing up, too. That was your childhood." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「昨日、幼年時代の友人に偶然会ったの。彼には何年も会っていなかったんだけど。」「そう言えば、サーモンって、幼年時代の友人のフグと結婚したのよね。」
example_sentences.english: """I ran into a childhood friend yesterday. I hadn’t seen him in years."" ""Speaking of which, Salmon married her childhood friend, Fugu."""

notes: "The child who is a juvenile is just a child. A group of them is children." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 児童の九割が欠席しました。
example_sentences.english: Ninety percent of the children were absent.

notes: "A constitution government is a constitutional government." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 憲政の危機って何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What is a constitutional crisis?

notes: "Remember how 兄弟 means ""siblings?"" Well when they're siblings you have to obey they're not your brother or sister, they're your cousin." "The entire reading for this is an exception. Sorry about that. Here's a mnemonic to help you:What are the two defining traits your cousin has? They're good and a child. いいと子, or いとこ for short. Just remember your good, kid cousin. Your いとこ cousin."

example_sentences.japanese: 従兄弟同士は結婚できるんだぜ。
example_sentences.english: Cousins can get married?!

notes: "If 創造 is creation and you add power to it, you have creative power." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well!

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのような創造力のある人と仕事ができることを、とても楽しみにしています。
example_sentences.english: I’m so excited to work with a creative person like you.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "You'll remember this kanji to the extent that you study it. If you study it like Hodor (ほど) would study it, you won't learn it at all. You would only be able to say ""hodor, hodor,"" over and over again, which isn't helpful at all."

example_sentences.japanese: まだ夜明けまでは一時間程あったが、驚く程青い目をした男は既に起床し、珈琲を作り始めていた。
example_sentences.english: It was still an hour before dawn, but a guy with startling blue eyes already had gotten up and was making coffee.

notes: "A cool frozen storage is one which is really cold on the inside, so cold it can freeze things. This is called a freezer, not to be confused with 冷蔵庫, which is refrigerator, and doesn't have the kanji for ""freeze"" in it." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 良い冷凍庫が見つかるといいですね。
example_sentences.english: I hope you find a good freezer.

english: Furigana, Small Kana Next To Kanji
notes: "振る is ""to shake."" 仮名 is kana. This word refers to furigana, which is the little kana that's put next to kanji for the people who don't use WaniKani and can't read anything. As to why it's called ""shake kana""? I have no clue. Just imagine putting little kana next to kanji and watching them shake around, though, and you should be good to go." "The readings are 振る and 仮名 put together into one. If you know those words, you won't need no furigana to help you with this word."

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字に振り仮名を振る仕事を見つけました。
example_sentences.english: I found a job where I write furigana above kanji.

notes: "A gambling hit can be multiple things. One type of gambling in Japan that was popular in the day involved betting these awesome wooden block things. You'd gamble by hitting them down on the ground, making a nice thunk sound. Another way to think about it is like blackjack. You want a card? You hit! Either way, it's gambling." "The reading is weird on this one, but gambling is weird, I guess. はく goes to ばく, maybe because you're playing some gambling backgammon. The ち can be cheating, where you cheat at this gambling backgammon. So, you're backgammon cheating (ばくち), you big cheater."

example_sentences.japanese: 博打を打つことは日本では違法です。
example_sentences.english: Gambling is illegal in Japan.

notes: "Car storage is where you store your car. It's your garage." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 両親の車を車庫に入れる時に、柱にぶつけてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: When I was backing my parents’ car into the garage I ran it into a pole.

notes: "Somebody shakes something at you. It was a finger, it seems. What a weird little gesture." "The reading is 身 and 振る put together, where the 振り gets rendaku'd to ぶり."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人の人たちと、身振り手振りで何とかコミュニケーションをとることができた。
example_sentences.english: I managed to communicate to Japanese people with gestures.

notes: "The person who governs your house like a wife is your housekeeper." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 家政婦を雇おうかと思っているんです。
example_sentences.english: I think we should hire a housekeeper.

notes: "It's the institution that does deliberation on behalf of the populace. They represent the people. They are the house of representatives." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ある衆議院議員が公費でボートを借りたことが明らかになりました。
example_sentences.english: It was revealed that a member of the House of Representatives chartered a boat at government expense.

notes: "The master wife is the one that takes care of all your stuff for you. She is the housewife, a very common profession for married ladies in Japan, though things have been changing little by little. Still, being a housewife means you control the money, which is pretty neat if you ask me." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: あの主婦の肌はものすごくスベスベしている。
example_sentences.english: That housewife has really smooth skin.
