example_sentences.english: My brother is a complete moron. Yesterday, he went out to get some milk in the shopping district so he could try and drink milk with his nose, but he got lost there and ended up not buying it.

english: Sleeping Pills, Sleeping Drugs, Sleeping Medicine
notes: "Some kind of sleep medicine? That's sleeping pills." "The reading is 眠い plus 薬 put together in one ... zz zzzzzZZZzz"

example_sentences.japanese: おい、お前、今の見てたか？俺、今ドリブルで三人のバックを抜いたんだぜ！俺ってば、ほんと、最高！相手チームにあげた眠り薬入りのオレンジジュースがうまく効いてたみたいだな。
example_sentences.english: Did you see that? I just dribbled around three defenders! I am the man! The orange juice with sleeping pills that I gave the other team worked perfectly!

english: Sleeping Pills, Sleeping Drugs, Sleeping Medicine
notes: "Sleepy sleep medicine is sleeping pills. Don't take too many or you might get addicted." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: さっき飲んだ睡眠薬のせいで、手足が思うように動かないんだけど。
example_sentences.english: I’m so uncoordinated right now because of the sleeping pill I took.

notes: "The Korea Country is Korea, of course... well, South Korea that is." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この韓国ドラマ、再放送されるのかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if this Korean drama series will be rebroadcasted.

hiragana: めいわくめーる, めいわくメール
notes: "When you have troublesome (迷惑) mail, you have mail you don't want. This is known as spam or junk mail. On a more technical level it's unsolicited mail." "The reading comes from 迷惑, so if you know that you know this (and then this vocab word won't be unsolicited as well!)"

example_sentences.japanese: 迷惑メールが次から次へと送られてくる。
example_sentences.english: The spam mail was sent out one after the other.

notes: "A watch over board is a board that goes over your store and watches over everything. What board on a store watches everything? It's the one that gets the most visibility, so it's probably the store sign." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 酔っぱらいの男が殴ったせいで、お店の看板がへこんでいるんです。
example_sentences.english: There is a dent in the store sign because some drunk guy punched it.

notes: "The big abbreviation is where you take everything and abbreviate it down to show the big picture. This abbreviation is the summary or outline of something bigger." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: まずは事件の大略を説明してくれないか？
example_sentences.english: Can you explain the outline of the incident first?

english: Three Cups, Three Cups Of Liquid
notes: "Three cups of liquid is three cups of liquid, or more simply, three cups." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その時ちょっとへこみ気味だったもんで、ビールを三杯一気飲みしちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I was depressed at the time, so I chugged three glasses of beer.

english: Two Cups, Two Cups Of Liquid
notes: "Two cups of liquid equals two cups of liquid, aka two cups, not to be confused with 二女一杯, however." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車が運行を見合わせている間に、珈琲を二杯飲みました。
example_sentences.english: I had two cups of coffee while railroad operation was suspended.

notes: "In the body, liquids accumulate. It can be the body of a cup, a body of a bucket, or the body of your body. Whatever it is, this body accumulation represents the volume of liquid in your body." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 父さんにガレージの体積を測るように言われたんだけど、理由は知らないよ。何か変だよね。
example_sentences.english: My dad told me to measure the volume of our garage, but I don’t know why. It seems kind of weird to me.

notes: "The zen religion is a part of Buddhism. It is the Zen Sect of Buddhism." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: その禅宗に関する映画は、この映画館で上映中です。
example_sentences.english: The movie about the Zen sect of Japanese Buddhism is playing at this theater.

notes: "The alluring power is the power of allure." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はゴルフの魅力に取り憑かれてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I became obsessed with the charm of golf.

notes: "The play park ground is where you go play. It's fun. It's an amusement park!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「スカイダイビングをして、その後遊園地に行くんだけど、一緒に行かない？」「えーっ、絶対に嫌！」
example_sentences.english: """I am going to go skydiving then afterwards go to a theme park. You want to join me?"" ""What? Absolutely not!"""

notes: "The previous extent of time was a while ago. Just think to a previous extent of time that was indeed a while ago, now, associate!" "The reading is the words 先 and 程, put together."

example_sentences.japanese: 先程あなたからの手紙を読ませて頂きました。
example_sentences.english: I read the letter from you some time ago.

notes: "The back scene is the scene going on in the back. You don't really notice it, because it's the background." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: Tofuguの本社を背景にして写真を撮ってもらえませんか。
example_sentences.english: Could you take my picture with the Tofugu headquarters in the background?

notes: "You are strong so you break into someone's home, hold them up, then steal from them. Ha ha! Take that, next door neighbor! This is a burglary / robbery, depending on how crazy you get after you use that strength to break down that door." "The reading for 強 is all messed up. Think about how when you commit a robbery, you go (ごう) into someone's house, then you go to jail as well, if you're caught."

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行強盗をやってみないか？今を逃がすと一生ないよ。
example_sentences.english: Do you want to rob a bank? It’s now or never.

notes: "You have edition rights over this. This edition is yours, and if anyone copies this edition, they get in trouble. You have copyright." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この手紙には、版権に関する契約更新予定日が記載されています。
example_sentences.english: This letter states the possible contract renewal date for the copyright.

notes: "The 電 is what powers electric things. Many times, these electric things light up (especially back in the day, when electricity did this a lot more than other things). So, you have ""lighting."" Then, you have decorate. So, if you decorate with lighting, you have decorative lighting." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 省エネのために電飾にOAタップを使ってるって聞いたんだけど、タコ足配線にするのは危ないわよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that you use power strips for decorative lighting to eliminate wasted energy, but you might overload the circuits so it’s dangerous.

notes: "Someone who has to shift their dwelling is someone who moves their home (and in this case) to another country. They are an emigrant / immigrant. Welcome to this country, friend!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 国外移住者になるのは容易なことではない。
example_sentences.english: It’s not easy to be an international immigrant.

notes: "An exhibition that you look at and all the people come meet together. Well, that just sounds like the description of an exposition." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この博覧会は無料で入場できます。
example_sentences.english: You can enter this exhibition free of charge.

notes: "The first edition is the first edition." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の小説の初版は半年で売り切れた。
example_sentences.english: The first edition of his novel sold out in six months.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The one with the flag is the Mad Hatter (はた). Just imagine looking through a group of people. You have to find the Mad Hatter, and he has to find you. That's why he offered to wear a flag on his hat."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は可愛い爪楊枝の旗を衝動買いしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I bought the cute toothpick flags on impulse.

notes: "If 幼稚 is childish, then a garden for childish people would be a place full of lots of children, probably growing in some way. When you're growing little children in a garden, you're putting them into some kind of school. In this case, it's a kindergarten." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help to know 幼稚 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 幼稚園のクリスマス会のスケジュールをまた微調整しなくちゃいけないかもしれないの。
example_sentences.english: We might have to make another small adjustment to the kindergarten Christmas party schedule.

notes: "This has a similar meaning to 主人 (head of household), but we're mainly learning it so you can learn some other vocab later on. You can remember it also as the meaning you learned with the kanji 主, which is master." "The reading is of course different from what you learned with the kanji. Think of this: The person who was your head of household was very strict. Anytime you did anything that was incorrect or bad, he/she would pull out the noose (ぬし), but would call it a ""noosey"" to be cute, since you were just a kid."

example_sentences.japanese: この池には、古池の主と呼ばれる大きな殿様蛙がいると言われています。
example_sentences.english: It’s said that in this pond there is a huge leopard frog called the master of the old pond.

notes: "精神 is your spirit, both religiously and spiritually. When those are sick, you have a problem. Back in the day, a mental illness was thought to be a sickness with your spirit. Nowadays you can just call it a mental illness or mental disorder." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help if you know 精神 already, though."

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の友達は精神病で頭が少しイッっちゃてるけど、良い人だよ。
example_sentences.english: My friend is kind of messed up in the head from some type of mental illness, but he’s a nice guy.

notes: "A country's flag is the flag they use for their nation. It's the national flag." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The こく gets shortened to こっ, though, so look out for that."

example_sentences.japanese: やっべーな。お前この巨大国旗を買ったのかよ？いったいどこに掲げるつもりなの？
example_sentences.english: No way! You bought this huge national flag? Where the heck are you thinking of putting it up?

notes: "Boisterous sound is when there's a lot of noise around you. It's the din of the crowd or environment." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 騒音問題について、お隣さんにどうやって切り出したらいいんだろう。
example_sentences.english: How should I approach my neighbor about a noise problem?

notes: "When you have the feeling of pleasantness, you are experiencing pleasure." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 人に恥をかかせることで快感を味合うような人にはなってもらいたくないわ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t want you to be a person who derives pleasure from humiliating people.

notes: "The lineage of the sun (太陽) is that of everything surrounding it. This is the solar system." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help to know 太陽."

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽系には惑星はいくつあるんだっけ？
example_sentences.english: How many planets does the solar system have?

english: The Next Day, Next Day, The Following Day
notes: "The following day is the day coming the day you're talking about. It's the next day." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 列車は翌日平常運転に戻りました。
example_sentences.english: The railroad service went back to normal the next day.

english: The Next Month, Next Month, The Following Month
notes: "The next moon refers to the next month." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は翌月黄色いドアがある小さな家に引っ越しています。
example_sentences.english: He is moving to the small house with the yellow door next month.

hiragana: よくあさ, よくちょう
english: The Next Morning, Next Morning, The Following Morning
notes: "The next morning is the next morning." "The reading can be what you've learned with the kanji, よくあさ, or it can be the on'yomi reading across the board, よくちょう. Both are good to remember because よくちょう is more formal (you'll use that reading in writing more often) and よくあさ is more informal - you'll use that in speaking more often."

example_sentences.japanese: 申し訳ありませんが、お客様の足つぼマッサージのご予約は、本日の夜9時から翌朝9時30分にご変更されております。
example_sentences.english: I’m afraid that your 9:00 p.m. foot-pressure massage has been pushed back to 9:30 tomorrow morning.

hiragana: よくねん, よくとし
english: The Next Year, Next Year, The Following Year
notes: "The next year is the next year." "The reading can be the on'yomi for 年 or the kun'yomi. So, you can do either よくねん or よくとし, or preferably both."

example_sentences.japanese: 翌年彼は起業しました。
example_sentences.english: He started his business the next year.

notes: "A cut token is a token you cut out from a sheet of paper into smaller sheets, and each of these pieces is a ticket." "The reading is 切る cut short to きっ, then ふ rendaku'd to ぷ. It's a bit of a troublesome word, so concentrate on this now a bit so you can get it in the reviews."

example_sentences.japanese: そのツアーの切符は、現地で購入することもできます。
example_sentences.english: You can buy tickets for that tour on site.

notes: "研修 is a training or study of some kind. If it's your current life to do training, then you are a trainee. This is a lot like how a student is in the status of ""study life.""" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The reading from 研修 should also help you too."

example_sentences.japanese: こちらが、新しい研修生の三浦くんです。
example_sentences.english: This is the new trainee, Miura.

english: Ukiyo-e, Ukiyo-e Woodblock Print, Ukiyo-e Painting
notes: "A floating world painting is what you call an ukiyo-e woodblock print in Japan. The ""floating world"" refers to an evanescent world that is impermanent (floating), just as beauty and entertainment is. Back in the day, this type of art was made into woodblock prints and paintings. Unfortunately, we don't have a name for these in English because they're so unique and special, but they come up more than you'd think, so get used to ukiyo-e!" "The readings don't really line up perfectly, but they're close (although mixed in terms of what has what reading). Take a look at the word and break everything down. 浮 takes the kun'yomi うき (from 浮く), 世 also takes the kun'yomi よ, and then 絵 takes the on'yomi え. Put that all together and you have うきよえ! Or if you already know the word ukiyo-e, that works too!"

example_sentences.japanese: その浮世絵についてお話をしませんか？
example_sentences.english: Why don’t we talk about the ukiyo-e?

english: "With All One's Might, With All Your Might"
notes: "You put one cup of liquid... no, one full cup of liquid spirit into what you're doing. None of this half-cup garbage. A full one. That means you're going at it with all one's might." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help if you've seen 一杯 before."

example_sentences.japanese: 今は古い写真を捨てることが私にできる精一杯です。
example_sentences.english: Getting rid of old pictures is the best I can do for now.

notes: "An aviation (航空) ticket is the kind of ticket you need to fly on an airplane. That's an airplane ticket." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 博多までの航空券を手配してもらえますか。
example_sentences.english: Could you arrange a flight for me to Hakata?

notes: "Rescue in a hurry using this car. What kinds of cars can do this? How about an ambulance." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 救急車が急発進して男性にぶつかったため、もう一台別の救急車も必要になった。
example_sentences.english: The ambulance suddenly took off and hit a guy, so we needed another ambulance.

hiragana: はちのす, ハチのす
notes: "ハチ is a bee. Buzz buzz. Just imagine ""eight bees"" combining into one bee, making it a ""hachi."" Then, there's a nest. What is a nest for bees? A beehive." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ハチの巣の周りで沢山のハチがブンブン飛び回っている。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of bees buzzing around the beehive.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Just keep in mind that this is the type of belt you use for kimono and yukata (traditional Japanese clothes) and not the kind you use to hold up your blue jeans." "What is the first letter in belt? Hmm, I can't remember. OH! ""B"" (おび)! I remember now."

example_sentences.japanese: 白い帯はお手入れが大変です。
example_sentences.english: It’s difficult to care for a white obi.

notes: "A blood's vein is a blood vessel." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々の血脈を絶やさせるべきではない。
example_sentences.english: We shouldn’t allow our bloodline to die out.

notes: "Who do you know that will use a pole to stop someone from breaking your heart? Your bodyguard! He's there to make sure no one hurts you, and for some reason he really likes using a pole to do it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の用心棒をしてくれない？
example_sentences.english: Will you work as my bodyguard?

notes: "A child who is the grandchild of someone else is a descendant of that person." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は宮家の子孫です。
example_sentences.english: He is a descendant of the imperial family.

notes: "Fix the diameter. It is the wrong diameter and must be a new diameter. Test it now, what's the diameter?" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 直径100フィートもある巨大な新種のクラゲが、ビーチをドロドロにしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: A new, giant 100 foot in diameter species of jellyfish oozed on the beach.

notes: "A knit someone is one who knits words together and makes them better. This someone is an editor." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの雑誌の編者を務めてくれた丸山君です。
example_sentences.english: This is Mr. Maruyama, who worked as the editor for this magazine.

notes: "A feeling where you sigh is one in which you're surprised by something, and can't believe it, so you sigh. Ugh, *sigh*. What token represents this in writing? An exclamation mark!!!!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: メールで語尾に必ず感嘆符を付ける友達がいます。
example_sentences.english: I have a friend who puts an exclamation mark at the end of every single sentence in her emails.

english: Fear, Horror, Anxiety, Concern, Uneasiness, Dread
notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji fear, so it means fear too." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading already so you should be able to read it!

example_sentences.japanese: 土砂崩れの恐れがあります。
example_sentences.english: I’m afraid there will be a landslide.

notes: "The way of the flower is flower arrangement." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さい頃からずっと華道を習っています。
example_sentences.english: I’ve been learning flower arrangement since I was little.

notes: "A thing that could break easily, is a fragile thing. Be careful with things like this." "The reading is 壊れる and 物 put together."

example_sentences.japanese: 小包に、「壊れ物、取扱注意」って書いておいた方がいいかな。
example_sentences.english: "Should I write down ""Fragile - Handle with Care"" on the package?"

notes: "Freight things is freight or cargo." "The reading is the 物 reading that's もつ. You can know this because you have to carry the freight and cargo (持つ it!)."

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日札幌貨物ターミナルと福岡貨物ターミナル間を走行する貨物列車があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a freight train that runs between Sapporo cargo terminal and Fukuoka cargo terminal every day.

notes: "How many? What? In this area of study, you ask these questions a lot. This area of study is geometry, because you have to ask how many sides and how much the area is or something (can you tell I don't remember any maths?)." "The 学 is read correctly, in terms of what you learned. The 幾 and 何 is weird, though. Just think how when you're asking a question in Japanese, you end the sentence with か. So, it's like, ""何か????"" and that's why it becomes か. Then, for 幾 think about how the key (き) to answering geometry questions correctly is figuring out ""how many"" sides something has. So, ""do you have the keyか?"""

example_sentences.japanese: 幾何学のテストでAプラス取ったの？すごいじゃん、よくやったね！

example_sentences.japanese: これは普通の醤油じゃなくて、最高の醤油だよ！
example_sentences.english: This isn’t normal soy sauce. This is supreme soy sauce!

english: Single Mindedly, Intently, Earnestly, A Line
notes: "You have one muscle, therefore it only does one thing. That's it. It is single mindedly doing that one thing. It is intently and earnestly doing that one thing." "The reading is a bit weird. It's the kun'yomi readings, where 一 is ひと and 筋 is すじ. Look back on the vocab words that use these readings to remember this one."

example_sentences.japanese: うちの長男は野球一筋なのよ。女っ気も無くてさ。
example_sentences.english: Our oldest son does nothing but play baseball. He doesn’t have a girlfriend either.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You are given some soup. You take a bite and your mouth is cut clean off. That is because you're eating sheer (しる) soup."

example_sentences.japanese: 熱々の豚汁をもらえますか。
example_sentences.english: Can I have the boiled pork miso soup, please?

notes: This is ateji, meaning the meanings of the kanji don't mean anything, only the sounds are being borrowed to make the word in Japanese. So, skip to the reading and use that to remember the meaning. It's an English word too now, after all. This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 近所にお寿司屋さんがあるんだけど、すごく旨いちらし寿司をたったの10ドルで出しているんだよ。これ以上のものはないね。
example_sentences.english: There is a sushi restaurant in my neighborhood that has great Chirashi-zushi for just $10. It’s tough to beat.

english: Sword, Sabre, Blade, Double Edged Sword
notes: The kanji and the word are the same. That means they share meanings as well. Just remember that this is the kind of sword that usually has two sharp sides, not one. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は午前二時に剣で戦うことにした。
example_sentences.english: We decided to fight with swords at two in the morning.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. BURN BURN BURN. The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: なんかその亀に親近感を感じるんだよな。
example_sentences.english: I feel an affinity with the turtle for some reason.

notes: "You have various various things. They are various. You have all kinds of them. " "The reading is a bit weird. Just think about how when you have various things, you probably have a lot of things. What do you want? You want more (もろ) of those things. More more more!"

example_sentences.japanese: 諸々の理由がありまして、しばらく一時的に店を閉めることにしました。
example_sentences.english: We decided to temporarily close our shop for a bunch of reasons.

notes: "A vinegar thing is a thing that has been vinegared. This is a vinegared food or a pickled food." "The readings are the readings for 酢 and the kun'yomi reading for 物 which you've seen quite a bit by now."

example_sentences.japanese: 大人になったら酢の物が好きになりました。
example_sentences.english: She came to like pickled food as she grew up.

notes:
"I have debt for the ticket you gave me. Forever we shall have this bond of me owing you for all the great things (like giving me a concert ticket to see Flight Of The Conchords in concert)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"Your debt rights state that you have a certain amount of credit with your bank. And if they try to say you don't have that credit you can file a claim against them!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 債券市場は何時まで開いてますか。
example_sentences.english: What time is the bond market open until?

example_sentences.japanese: 債権者は破産手続きによっていくらかお金を受け取れることが多いが、株主は滅多に受け取ることがない。
example_sentences.english: Creditors often receive some money from bankruptcy proceedings, but stockholders barely do.

english: Commander, Commander In Chief, Team Captain
notes: "The master commander is the commander of all commanders, the commander in chief if you will... or, even the team captain." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どちらの主将もそんなに強くはなかった。
example_sentences.english: Both of the team captains weren’t very strong.

notes: "If 指揮 is ""command"" or ""lead"" then someone who does those things is a commander, or conductor. Usually the kind that conducts an orchestra!" "The reading for this is the reading of 指揮 plus the on'yomi reading of 者."

example_sentences.japanese: どちらの指揮者もまだ来てないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Neither commander has come yet.

english: Consent Or Refusal, Yes Or No
notes: "Do we have agreement or no? Which is it? consent or refusal? Yes or no? Choose!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 「諾否を御一報ください」という言葉は、仕事の手紙やEmailなどでよく使われるフレーズです。
example_sentences.english: """Please let us know whether this is acceptable or not"" is a common phrase used in business letters and emails."

notes: "You leave behind your body to join the spirit realm. This body remainder is your corpse or remains." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして犯人が遺体の唇を舐めたのかは不明です。
example_sentences.english: We have no idea why the murderer licked the corpse’s lips.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: You're staring really closely at this deer, but something looks off. You get closer, slowly, and you realize it's a sheep in a car (しか) shaped like a deer. The sheep car deer suddenly turns toward you rushing forward, legs raised. Ahh, get outta there! (The lesson here is to never get too close to a deer. You never know its true form until it's too late.)"

example_sentences.japanese: 牡鹿と牝鹿の区別がつきません。
example_sentences.english: I can’t distinguish between male and female deer.

notes: "A branch bean doesn't mean a whole lot this way, but you probably know the food that this describes anyways. This is edamame, a food made from steamed soybeans, usually with a bit of salt added for flavor." "The readings are the kun'yomi readings of the two kanji, unfortunately. That's the vocab words 枝 and 豆 combined into one."

example_sentences.japanese: 「お早うございます。何にいたしましょうか？」「いつものやつ頼むよ。」「かしこまりました。ビールと枝豆でございますね。」「そうだよ。」
example_sentences.english: """Good morning. What can I get you?"" ""I’ll have the usual."" ""Alright. Beer and Edamame, right?"" ""That’s it."""

notes: "A 磁場 is a ""magnetic field."" An electricity version of this is an electromagnetic field." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Will of course help to know 磁場 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の父は、電磁場発生装置の特許を持っているんですが、私はそれが何のためのものなのかよく分かりません。
example_sentences.english: My father has a patent for an electromagnetic field generator, but I’m not sure what it’s for.

notes:
The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Using your animal fang you are able to eat kibble (きば)."

"Horse horse, look at all these horses. What do you do with horses? You do horse riding." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ハロウィン用の偽物の牙の在庫が切れそうです。
example_sentences.english: Our stock of fake fangs for Halloween is running out.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動会の騎馬戦の練習があるので、明日は早起きしなくてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: I have to wake up early tomorrow morning to practice for the athletic meet’s mock cavalry battle.

notes: "Your surname and your name put together create your full name." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の姓名を使用しないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don’t use my full name.

notes: "The commander will come in the future. Not anytime soon, but in the future." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 将来いつか、もっといい飼い犬の名前を思いつくかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: I may come up with a better name for my dog someday in the future.

notes: "What you leave behind to those you give birth to is known as an inheritance." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 父の遺産を巡る家族間の争いが起きてるんです。
example_sentences.english: We’re going through a family conflict over my father’s inheritance.

notes: "An elephant tusk is the material known as ivory (or just an elephant tusk)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 印鑑を高級な象牙の物に変えました。
example_sentences.english: I switched out my name stamp for an expensive ivory one.

english: Jomon People, Joumon People, Joumon, Jomon, Ancient Japanese
notes: "The rope writing people are known as the Jomon People, which are the ancient Japanese." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 縄文時代にもおしゃぶりみたいなものはあったのかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if there was the equivalent of teething rings in the Jomon era.

notes: "A song dance deed is a deed you do that involves singing and dancing. This is the traditional form of stage deeds, known as kabuki. Watch it on YouTube if you want a taste." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌舞伎のチケットが見当たらないんだけど。
example_sentences.english: My kabuki ticket is missing.

notes: "The deer child island prefecture is Kagoshima Prefecture. " "The readings are part on'yomi, part kun'yomi, but you should know them all if you look at them one by one. Just remember that 児 is read as ご here. Go, Kagoshima Prefecture! Go!"

example_sentences.japanese: 鹿児島県で、今までで運転した中で一番デッコボコの道路をドライブしました。
example_sentences.english: I drove on the most bumpy road I’ve ever driven on in Kagoshima prefecture.

notes: "The god Nara river Prefecture is Kanagawa Prefecture." "The か of 神 is used here (losing the み). Then, everything else should be self explanatory."

example_sentences.japanese: 神奈川県では漫画がブームです。
example_sentences.english: There is a boom in manga in Kanagawa Prefecture.

notes: "Your former surname is your maiden name, the name you had before you got married." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもパスワードに母親の旧姓を使うんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I always use my mother’s maiden name as my password.

notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji mistake, so it means a mistake or if it's on a computer, an error." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: When you make a mistake, you need to admit to it. When someone asks, ""Who's responsible for this mistake?"" You say, ""I am (あやま)."""

example_sentences.japanese: ようやく誤りに気がついた。
example_sentences.english: I finally noticed my mistakes.

notes: "Nara is good and it is Nara (the place, we're talking about)." "The reading for 奈 is good, the reading for 良 is pretty off in terms of what you've learned. But, if you know that the meaning is Nara, you know the reading is なら as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は歯のしつこい着色汚れを奈良の歯医者さんで落としました。
example_sentences.english: I removed stubborn color stains on my teeth at the dental clinic in Nara.

notes: "A country's debt is the national debt. It can also be bonds, like the ones you buy from your country." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうど国債を売ろうとしたところで、値が急激に下がって、売り損ねちゃったんだ。
example_sentences.english: We were on the verge of selling the government bonds, but the price rolled down too quickly and we couldn’t sell.

english: Nuclear Test, Nuclear Bomb Test, Nuclear Testing
notes: "A nucleus experiment (実験) is a nuclear test." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 予算の都合上、核実験への臨時スタッフの採用は増やせない。
example_sentences.english: Budget-wise, we are unable to increase our temporary staff for nuclear testing.

notes: "Nucleus arms (へいき), aka weapons, are nuclear weapons." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 核兵器を使用する前に、説明書に書かれている操作方法を必ずお読みください。
example_sentences.english: Before using the nuclear weapon, please carefully review the instruction booklet.

notes: "The open sea is where the sea joins together to be the open sea." "The readings are the kun'yomi readings that you learned when you learned the kanji. Just remember that this time 合 takes the あい reading."

example_sentences.japanese: ピンク色の怪獣は海岸から約8km沖合いにいるとの報告を受けました。
example_sentences.english: They reported that the pink monster is about eight kilometers offshore.

hiragana: おやこどんぶり, おやこどん
english: Parent And Child Bowl, Parent And Child Rice Bowl, Chicken And Egg Rice Bowl, Chicken And Egg On Rice
notes: "A very common food item, though the name for it is a little weird. 親子丼 is Parent and child rice bowl, aka a parent and child bowl. The parent is a chicken. The child is an egg. So, this is a chicken and egg donburi, basically." "The reading is 親 and 子 and 丼 combined together into one sick parent and child meal. Just think, that egg could be that chicken's child. At least they're together."

example_sentences.japanese: てか、あの親子丼超まずかったよね！トイレで吐いちゃったよ！
example_sentences.english: God! That parent and child bowl was so disgusting! I threw up in the bathroom.

notes: "放射 is ""radiation."" Add the ability of radiation and you have radioactivity, for some reason. I guess things don't have radioactivity until you have given them the ability of radiation, right?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 放射能に関する会議を招集する前に、出席者を決める方がいいだろう。
example_sentences.english: Before calling the meeting about the radioactivity, we should decide who should attend.

notes: "We must maintain the new and get rid of the old. It's time for a restoration of policy! This also refers to the Meiji Restoration too. In fact, it probably mostly refers to this, though you'll learn a more full version of this later." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校で明治維新について勉強はしたんですが、名前以外は何にも覚えていません。
example_sentences.english: I studied the Meiji restoration in school, but I can’t remember anything about it other than it’s name.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: Please hand me the rope, right now (なわ), otherwise I will fall to my death!"

example_sentences.japanese: 私にはどっちの縄も同じに見えますね。違いは全く分かりません。
example_sentences.english: Both ropes look the same to me. I can’t tell the difference at all.

notes: "The commander of the army is the shogun. Do you know the shogun? He ran Japan, and was like the ruling general over the states. You can also call him the general or commander, if you like." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: つまり、敵の将軍と付き合っているってこと。
example_sentences.english: That is to say, I’m dating the enemy shogun.

notes: "A dance machine isn't really a machine... a 台 is a large machine thing counter, so in this case it's talking about a stage. A dancing stage is a stage." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just remember that 台 is read as たい here, not だい."

example_sentences.japanese: すごくいい声持ってるね。舞台で歌を歌ってみようと思った事はないの？
example_sentences.english: You have such a great voice. Have you ever thought about singing on stage?

notes:
"A father you've inherited isn't your original father, he's your stepfather." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"Your lineage and genealogy make up your genealogy, also known as your family history." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さい頃、継父にいつもおんぶをしてもらっていました。
example_sentences.english: My stepfather used to give me piggyback rides all the time when I was little.

example_sentences.japanese: この巻紙に一族の系譜が描かれています。
example_sentences.english: I’m sketching my family’s genealogy on this roll of paper.

notes: "A super sound that's fast is supersonic speed." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のパンダロボットは、超音速で空を飛べるんだぜ。
example_sentences.english: My panda robot can fly at supersonic speeds.

notes: "The sweet group is a group of people who love sweet things. They really have quite the sweet tooth." This is a jukugo word that uses the readings you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は甘党で、ケーキには目がないの。
example_sentences.english: I have a sweet tooth and I’m extremely fond of cake.

english: Tale Of Genji, The Tale Of Genji
notes: "Remember 源氏? He has his own 物語. This is the very first novel ever written (that we know about). This is the Tale of Genji." "The reading is the combination of 源氏 and 物語 which you have learned before so you should have no problems with this one."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は源氏物語を漫画でしか読んだことがありません。
example_sentences.english: I’ve only read the manga version of the Tale of Genji.

notes: "If a 奴 is just some dude or some guy, adding a ら on there makes it plural. Now it's those dudes or those guys." "The reading comes from 奴."

example_sentences.japanese: 奴ら、俺たちは働いてるってのに、呑気に日光浴なんかしてやがるぜ。
example_sentences.english: Those guys are bathing and relaxing in the sun while we are working.

notes: "Bean rot is when you take soy beans, let them ferment, and then you make tofu out of them! Yep, that's what tofu is. Rotten beans." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: うーん。どっちの豆腐もいまいちかな。実は豆腐はあんまり好きじゃないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Well, neither tofu tastes very good to me. I’m actually not a fan of tofu.

notes: "A haven for waves would be inside the greatest most deadly wave of them all... the tsunami or tidal wave. Dun dun dunnnn!" "The reading is the 津 and 波 kun'yomi readings, combined together."

example_sentences.japanese: たくさんの人達が津波に流されてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Many people were swept away by the tsunami.

notes: "An ultra sound wave is an ultrasonic wave." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just remember that the は changes to ぱ for 波."

example_sentences.japanese: 超音波なら脂肪細胞を永久に破壊することができると言われたので、この3000ドルもする機械を買ったんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I was told that ultrasonic waves destroy fat cells permanently, so I bought this machine for $3,000.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 貴重 means ""valuable?"" Well valuable products are your valuables!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 貴重品はご自身で管理して下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please manage your own valuables yourself.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: うちのお母さん、肩幅が広いから、私はそれが遺伝したの。
example_sentences.english: My mom has wide shoulders and I inherited them.

notes: "Confront your body? Sounds like it's something that's against bodies... perhaps, something that's antibody?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてボスに逆らって、そのウィルスへの抗体を作り出そうとするのですか？予防接種を受ける！
example_sentences.english: Why do you defy your boss and try to build up antibodies to the virus? Get a vaccination!

notes: "An afflicted someone is someone who is a patient / medical patient. They are afflicted with some disease which is why they need medical attention." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その患者は、左足が麻痺してもなお、サッカー選手になれるという希望に固執していた。
example_sentences.english: That patient clung to his dream of being a soccer player even though his left leg was paralyzed.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が塁を踏んだのかどうか、よく見えなかった。
example_sentences.english: I couldn’t really see if he stepped on the base or not.

notes: "A baseball base judge is one who judges things on a baseball field. This is a baseball umpire, or more simply, an umpire." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの一塁の塁審、試合中に屁をこきまくってたぜ。
example_sentences.english: The umpire at first base kept farting during the game.

notes: "A baseball base hit is a base hit or single in baseball terms. A 二塁打 is a double, a 三塁打 is a triple, and a homerun is something you'll learn here on WaniKani at some point if you haven't already." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned the readings for both of these kanji, so you should be able to read this word already!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が塁打を打つのは久しぶりだね。いつもはホームランだからな。
example_sentences.english: It’s been a long time since he made a base hit. He always hits homeruns.

notes: "An explode bullet is when an explode shoots out of something like a bullet, but much bigger, like from a bomb." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 爆弾を分解することは危険だってことは分かってたんだけど、すごく興味があったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I knew taking apart the bomb could be very dangerous, but I was really interested.

notes: "Back in the day, a bullet was a circle shape. So, this word is bullet." "The 弾 part is okay, but you never learned the on'yomi reading of 丸, which is がん. When you shoot a bullet, you are using a gun (がん). Bang!"

example_sentences.japanese: 俺は弾丸の雨をとても上手くかわした。
example_sentences.english: I expertly dodged a spray of bullets.

notes: "An army base is managed from the camp. This is where all the bigwigs get together, talk, and manage things, right over the open fire." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 敵の陣営が見えてくると、恐怖を感じ始めました。

example_sentences.english: This is such a boring memoir.

notes: "A neighbor country is a neighboring country. For us, our 隣国 in America are those sneaky Canadians... always waiting to strike, I can tell..." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして隣国の肩を持つのさ？日本人じゃないの？
example_sentences.english: Why are you taking sides with the neighboring country? Aren’t you Japanese?

notes: "Remember how 沖縄 is ""Okinawa""? This is the prefecture, Okinawa Prefecture." "The reading comes from 沖縄 and 県 put together."

example_sentences.japanese: 我々は、人々が沖縄県から去るのを食い止めた。
example_sentences.english: We stopped everyone from leaving Okinawa Prefecture.

notes: "The outside ditch is the ditch around our town that's on the outside (not the inside ditch, which is the inner moat). This is the outer moat." "This word uses the same readings from the previous vocabulary except that 堀 gets rendakued - don't forget!"

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと気が変わって、外堀は必要がないようと思うようになりました。
example_sentences.english: I’ve changed my mind, I don’t think we need an outer moat.

notes: "Milord's hall is a nice place. It's where a lord would live. A palace." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お前にとって、殿堂入りを果たした選手といえば、誰になる？
example_sentences.english: Who would you say are the players that should be inducted into the hall of fame?

notes: "A location where cars can be a resident is a parking lot." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned these readings already, so you should be able to read this on your own!

example_sentences.japanese: ショッピングモールの駐車場で渋滞に巻き込まれちゃってるよ。クリスマス前の日曜日なんかに、こんなところに来るんじゃなかったよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m stuck in a traffic jam in a parking lot at the mall. I shouldn’t have come here on the Sunday before Christmas.

notes: "A medicine dose expert is someone who knows exactly how much dose of each medicine you should be getting. The person who specializes in this is a pharmacist." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 薬剤師は別に白衣を着る必要はないと思うんだよな。
example_sentences.english: I don’t think pharmacists really need to wear white coats.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "You'll have to imagine a pillar standing tall, and made entirely of the Egyptian god Ra and hashbrowns. It is a hash-ra (はしら) pillar, made by the Egyptians who love breakfast."

example_sentences.japanese: そのスーパーで買い物をしてる間、私は犬を柱に繋ぐんですが、いつもちゃんと大人しく待ってますよ。
example_sentences.english: While shopping in the grocery store, I tether my dog to a pole and he always waits for me obediently.

notes: "Those who patrol and inspect on their patrols are the police or policeman." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その巡査は、スコッチを一気にゴクリと半分飲み干した。
example_sentences.english: The policeman drank half the scotch in one gulp.

notes: "A prevent rot dose is a dose of something you put on your cut or wound that prevents it from rotting (or you put it on something else to prevent it from rotting). This is an antiseptic or preservative." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い防腐剤はどこに捨てればいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Where should I throw away old antiseptics?

notes: "Your roofs are spread out around your property. Put these roofs and areas all together and you have your residence or estate." This word uses the readings you learned with the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 男の妻は毎日お屋敷で何もせずただブラブラしている。
example_sentences.english: His wife does nothing but aimlessly wander around the estate everyday.

english: Resident Of Japan, Stationed In Japan
notes: "A resident of 日本 (Japan) is a resident of Japan. Alternatively you could be stationed in Japan." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜は駐日アメリカ大使主催のパーティーに行かなくちゃいけないんです。
example_sentences.english: I have to go to a party tonight that is hosted by the U.S. Ambassador to Japan.

notes: "I praise you for your beauty. I'm so into your beauty, I hand you a reward... a prize, basically." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 頑張ったご褒美がもらえることを期待しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m hoping to get a reward for my hard work.

notes: "A sacrifice hit is one you do in baseball, when you hit the ball in the air, and then the person on third tags up and scores. In baseball, this can either be a sacrifice bunt or sacrifice fly." "You didn't learn this reading for 打 with the kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you out. Who catches your sacrifice fly/bunt? It's your da だ. Your da is playing for the other team and he gets you out when he catches the ball :("

example_sentences.japanese: 犠打にならないか心配です。
example_sentences.english: I can’t help but worry about the sacrifice fly.

notes: "Spread the gold around. First part, I want you to put in a security deposit." This word uses the readings you learned with the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 敷金を全額返金してもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got a full refund on my security deposit.

notes: "A seized thing is something you've seized from your victory. It's your spoils. It's your trophy!" "Since you didn't learn the kun'yomi for 獲 with the kanji, here's a mnemonic to help you out. Eh (え)? We won the game? Ehhhh?! No way! To the victor belong the spoils! Yay!"

example_sentences.japanese: 都会には、我々の詐欺の獲物がたくさんいるんだよ。
example_sentences.english: There is a lot of easy prey for us to swindle in this city.

notes: "A resident detained in a location who is in the army is a member of the stationed troops at this location. They could also be the occupying troops as well." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 駐留軍向けの洗濯サービスとかはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Is there a laundry service for the stationed troops?

notes: "A sitting spread is a spread of tatami mats, making up the tatami room in a Japanese house." This word uses the readings you learned with the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お座敷のどこかでコオロギが鳴いている。
example_sentences.english: There’s a cricket chirping somewhere in the tatami room.

notes: "An electricity pillar is a telephone pole. All those wires and telephone wires going to and from those telephone poles." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日車を電柱にぶつけちゃったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I ran my car into a telephone pole today.

notes: "An aviation (航空) mother warship is a warship that is like mother to all the aviation things (the airplanes). They come home to their mother warship, which is an aircraft carrier." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その航空母艦は突然視界から消えたんです。
example_sentences.english: The aircraft carrier suddenly disappeared out my field of vision.

notes: "A mineral mountain is one that you should build a mine in, to get all those minerals." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 鉱山で働いてる時は、いつも背中に痛みがありました。
example_sentences.english: When I worked in a mine, I always had back pain.

notes: "原 is often tied to atomic things, as atoms are the origin of all things. If an atom explodes, you have yourself an atomic bomb." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 原爆のことを言ってるんじゃないよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m not talking about atomic bombs.

notes: "Your hand's turtle shell is the back of it (see you can make it shaped like a turtle shell if you try hard!). That's why this is the back of one's hand." "The readings are the respective vocab readings of 手 and 甲."

example_sentences.japanese: とても綺麗な手の甲を持っていることが彼女の自慢です。
example_sentences.english: She is proud that the backs of her hands are so beautiful.

notes: "An army warship is a battleship. Did you sink it? Oh oh! You sunk my 軍艦!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 軍艦プラモの専門店を開く予定なんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to open a specialty shop for plastic battleship models.

notes: "A celebrate ceremony is a celebration." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You just need to remember that 祝 is read as しゅう for this one and you'll be fine."

example_sentences.japanese: 封筒の表には「御祝儀」と自分の名前を、裏には金額を書いたよ。
example_sentences.english: "I wrote ""congratulations"" and my name on the front of the envelope and the amount of money on the back."

english: Changing Room, Locker Room, Dressing Room
notes: "An again clothes room is a changing room. You get to change again, even after changing in the morning for the first time to leave your house. This can also be a locker room or a dressing room, so really anywhere you can change that's not your home, usually." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今更衣室であの女のロッカーを探しているところよ。
example_sentences.english: I’m in the dressing room looking for her locker now.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "You pick up some clothes. Hmm, I'd like to wear these, you think. But, the shopkeeper comes up and says, in a really weird accent, ""No, I'm afraid those are ころも clothes."" ころも clothes? What is that? Oh... you find out this guy has a speech impediment and is trying to say ""こども (子供) clothes."" Try to say the word with him, but he keeps saying it wrong. You get frustrated and blurt out, ""It's the key to not being nude (きぬ)!"" This does the trick, he lets you have your ころも clothes and goes into the back room to cry."

example_sentences.japanese: 衣替えをするのって、とても面倒くさいと思うんだけど、どう思う？
example_sentences.english: I think dressing for the season is so tiresome, what do you think?

notes: "Clothes clothes are still clothes!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが彼女の衣服を盗んだんですね。
example_sentences.english: You stole your girlfriend’s clothes, didn’t you?

notes: "A stone charcoal is charcoal shaped like a little stone. Or, maybe it's often found in stone. That's coal." "The reading for 石 isn't the one you learned for the kanji, but you've seen this reading before with 宝石. Coal is like a little black ""jewel,"" right?"

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、石炭ビジネスでの成功を自慢しました。
example_sentences.english: He boasted about his success in the coal business.

notes: "Charcoal mineral has been found! Time to dig a coal mine or coal pit to retrieve it!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: うーん。この炭鉱が閉山するってのは、本当に残念ですね。
example_sentences.english: Well, it is really disappointing that this coal mine is going to be closed.

notes: "An employment (雇用) someone is someone who gives you employment, aka an employer." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 雇用者に新しい電話番号を何度も教えてるのに、いっつも古い方の番号に掛けてくるんだよな。
example_sentences.english: I’ve told my new phone number to my employer over and over again, but he always calls me at the old number.

english: Field, Field Of Rice, Field Of Crops
notes: "A rice paddy field. You'd think this would refer only to a rice field, but it actually refers to other types of fields too, making this word simply field. I guess that shows how important rice is, because if a field isn't growing rice, it ain't no field o' mine." "The readings come from what you learned with the kanji. 畑 uses the shorter はた reading that you learned."

example_sentences.japanese: 今時田畑を機械を使わずに耕すなんて、時間の無駄だよ。
example_sentences.english: Nowadays ploughing fields without any machinery is a waste of time.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 蛍の光は、誰にとっても見ていて心地の良いものです。
example_sentences.english: The glow of fireflies is pleasant for anyone who watches.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: You make a fist. Why? Because she stole your corn on the cob. ""Cob! She (こぶし) stole my cob!"""

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は拳についた血をハンカチで拭いました。
example_sentences.english: He cleaned the blood off his fist with his handkerchief.

notes: "A fruit wood is what a fruit grows on (the wood of a fruit is a tree, dummy). That makes this word a fruit tree." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 果樹園での仕事は結構退屈です。
example_sentences.english: The job at the orchard is pretty boring.

notes: "A burial ceremony is known as a funeral." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 中村は、葬儀に一人で行くと言って聞かなかった。
example_sentences.english: Nakamura insisted on going to the funeral by himself.

notes: "You've seen how 岐阜 is ""Gifu."" Now make it a prefecture to make Gifu prefecture." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 岐阜県に行くには、電車の乗り換えが必要ですか？
example_sentences.english: Do I have to change trains to get to Gifu prefecture?

notes: "Your hometown home village is the one that's your hometown. It's also your birthplace, where you were born." "The reading for 郷 is the one you learned, but the reading for 里 isn't the one you learned. To remember this reading, just think about how your birthplace is the place you were reared (り), and you really (り) miss the place."

example_sentences.japanese: 郷里を訪れるのはお金と時間の無駄です。
example_sentences.english: Visiting my hometown is a waste of time and money.

hiragana: こきょう, ふるさと
notes: "By circumstance this is your hometown. Not much to say other than it's your hometown and birthplace." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 聞いたところによると、彼女、離婚後故郷に戻ったらしいぜ。
example_sentences.english: From what I’ve heard, she moved back to her hometown after the divorce.

notes: "A bee's honey is its honey, honey." The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は私の蜂蜜プリンを一口味見しました。
example_sentences.english: She took a bite of my honey pudding.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. That's honey, baby!

example_sentences.japanese: その熊は、蜜の入った瓶を五本、次々飲み干しました。
example_sentences.english: The bear swallowed five jars of the honey, one after the other.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji!

example_sentences.japanese: 私の一番好きな日本の諺は、「身を殺して仁を成す」です。
example_sentences.english: "My favorite Japanese proverb is ""sacrifice one’s life to do good."""

notes: "Humanity and righteousness. This is your duty. This is humanity and justice." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 盗人には仁義はない。
example_sentences.english: There is no honor among thieves.

notes: "The iron mineral is iron ore." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: マイクラでたくさん鉄鉱石を採掘した。
example_sentences.english: I mined a bunch of iron ore in Minecraft.

notes:
"If 躍る is ""to leap"" or ""to jump,"" then this noun version will be jumping or leaping." "The reading comes from 躍る."

"A dance is a dance." The reading is the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は小躍りして喜びました。
example_sentences.english: I jumped for joy.

example_sentences.japanese: 盆踊りの練習をして時間を潰しました。
example_sentences.english: I killed time by practicing the Bon Festival Dance.

notes: "Wrap up the street and take it away. I cut it apart with my kitchen knife (don't ask why this word comes from these kanji). Just imagine yourself using a kitchen knife to cut up the street so you can wrap it up and take it away." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 包丁を研いで二、三時間潰しました。
example_sentences.english: I killed a couple hours by sharpening my kitchen knife.

notes: "The thanks ceremony is the dance you do in life when it comes to your manners and courtesy to others. Also means etiquette." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の礼儀作法について学んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I’m studying Japanese etiquette.

notes: "A mineral thing is a mineral." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: これは今までで最高の鉱物さ。これに敵うものはないね。
example_sentences.english: This is the best mineral I’ve ever seen. Nothing can match it.

notes: "A warship squad is a naval fleet or an armada." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 敵の艦隊からもっと激しい抵抗があると思っていたので、なんだか拍子抜けです。
example_sentences.english: I expected stronger resistance from the enemy’s naval fleet, so I’m kind of disappointed.

notes: "The original (often associated with atoms and nuclear tech) concealing machine is the nuclear submarine. It is nuclear, and it conceals itself." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 原子力潜水艦は、略して原潜と呼ばれることもある。
example_sentences.english: Nuclear submarines are sometimes called Gensen, for short.

notes: "Something based on points has a ranking, meaning you'll know where your position or location is, compared to everyone else." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々は生産拠点を海外に移します。
example_sentences.english: We are going to move our production bases overseas.

notes: "The result (甲斐) of being your own gender shows your resourcefulness. Depending on your gender, certain things are harder than others, so your resourcefulness and competence will help you to overcome those hurdles." "This word combines the word 甲斐 (that you already learned) with the on'yomi reading for 性. You know them both, just put them together!"

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてあの甲斐性無しが彼女の愛を復活させることができたのか、全く理解できないね。
example_sentences.english: I really can’t understand how such an incompetent man like that was able to rekindle her love.

notes: "You know 手洗い, right? This is like that, but way more polite sounding. The meaning is still the same though: restroom, bathroom, toilet." "The reading for the 御 is お, the rest is てあらい, even though the い isn't showing on the end. It gets pushed into the 洗い."

example_sentences.japanese: 何時までに御手洗からバスに戻らなくてはいけませんか？行列ができているので、遅れないか心配してるんですが。
example_sentences.english: How long before we have to be back to the bus from the bathroom? There is a long line, so I’m worried I’ll be late.

notes: "A fist gun is a small fistish sized gun that has some punch (because, you know, fist!). The gun I'm describing is a revolver, or a handgun." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は拳銃を派手なスパンコールで飾り付けしてみました。
example_sentences.english: I decorated my revolver with flashy sequins.

notes: "Obsolete ruins are places that are abandoned because nobody can run them anymore (due to being obsolete, or due to not having money, or due to whatever else). These things are ruins or abandoned buildings. People like to explore these, a lot." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日廃墟で鬼ごっこをしたので、筋肉痛になりました。
example_sentences.english: I have muscle pain because I played tag in the abandoned building yesterday.

notes: "The rapids door is like a door of water coming in to somewhere. This is a strait or channel. Also, this is the Seto area." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日市場ですごくいい瀬戸物を見つけたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I found really nice chinaware at the market today.

notes: "The tall rapids are the shallows. I have no idea how this makes sense, but I suppose if the water is taller, it's not going to have as much rapids going on, meaning it's just shallows (but not too tall to become something else, like a lake, or whatever)." "The reading comes from 高い and the reading you learned for 瀬."

example_sentences.japanese: この川はこの辺りは高瀬になってるから、きっと足が底に着くと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: The river is pretty shallow around here, so I’m sure you’ll reach the bottom.

notes: "The bitter valley is a place known as Shibuya. This is a very famous area in Tokyo. Very busy too." "The reading of 渋 comes from 渋い. The reading for 谷 is an exception. Just think about someone asking you if  Shibuya is cool. Your answer of course is ""yah."" (や)"

example_sentences.japanese: 私はよく渋谷駅で外国人を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I usually see foreigners at Shibuya Station.

notes: "Cooked sake is slightly higher in alcohol content. This is shochu, which I'm guessing gets cooked in some way during its production." "The reading for 焼 and 酎 are the on'yomi readings, but you didn't learn the reading for 焼 yet. That's okay, because if you know the (also English) word Shochu, you'll be able to remember the reading for this one as well too."

example_sentences.japanese: この焼酎のもっと大きい瓶ってありますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you have a bigger bottle of this shochu?

notes: "The idea of sincerity is sincerity. It's also to have good faith in others." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 誠意のこもった説明が聞けたので、今回は彼女の言い分を聞いて上げることにしました。
example_sentences.english: After hearing her sincere explanation, I decided to give her the benefit of the doubt this time around.

notes: "福祉 is welfare, 社会 is society. So, a society's welfare is social welfare." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日なら、家族の墓参りをした後に、その社会福祉施設に寄れなくもないよ。
example_sentences.english: I could stop by the social welfare facility after visiting my family’s graves tomorrow.

notes: "A conceal in the water warship is a submarine." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.
