This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その会社の株主総会の後には、懇親会があります。
example_sentences.english: There will be a friendly reunion after the company’s stockholders’ meeting.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Oh my goodness. The reading of this word! Try to think of it as your thought (思) cow (む) key (き). In your thoughts, you think of the cow key, which will unlock the door in front of you... at least that's what you think it is... you're not sure. But, you're pretty sure it's the gist of how you get inside the door. Is it?"

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに趣のあるお持ち帰り用の容器を見たのは初めてです。
example_sentences.english: I’ve never seen such a tasteful doggie bag before.

notes: "A bright news report is going to be one full of good news. A dark news report is probably bad news, but we only care about good news right now, don't we?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 朗報を伝えるためにここに来ました。
example_sentences.english: I’m here to tell you some good news.

notes: "A hedge (or fence) root is where the hedge and fence grow from. What grows from this? Well, it's simply a hedge or a fence." "The readings are the kun'yomi readings of the kanji. With 垣 that's the one you learned and with 根 that's the vocab version of the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: 男は垣根の上にそっと義手を置きました。
example_sentences.english: The man placed his prosthetic hand gently on the hedge.

hiragana: まんちょう, みちしお
notes: "A full tide is a high tide or full tide. That's when the water comes up." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 一番釣りに適しているのは満潮時でしょうか？
example_sentences.english: Is high tide the best time to go fishing?

notes: "It's instantly effective! Sounds like something out of Pokemon. This word means immediate effect or instant effect." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the shortening.

example_sentences.japanese: 即効で目の疲れを取る方法をお教えしましょう。
example_sentences.english: I’ll show you a way to instantly remove eye strain.

notes: "The gentle path is, surprisingly, judo. Yep, the sport / art based on throwing people around." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: もし柔道が何かを知らないって言うなら、ここに超簡単な入門書があるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don’t know what Judo is, here is a book with a very brief introduction of it.

hiragana: ぼくじょう, まきば
notes: "A pasture place is a livestock farm. It's also a ranch. The place where things pasture is this place." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この牧場には、絞り立ての牛乳を使った自慢のアイスクリーム屋さんがあるんだ。
example_sentences.english: This farm boasts a good ice cream shop that uses fresh milk.

english: Marshy Rice Field, Marshy Rice Paddy
notes: "A bog rice paddy is a marshy rice field. This is just a rice paddy in marshy form." The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 沼田を裸足で歩いたことはありますか。
example_sentences.english: Have you ever walked barefoot through a marshy rice paddy?

notes: "The furnace heart is the heart of the furnace. The heart of this particular furnace, the one we're talking about here, is the nuclear reactor core." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして奴らは原子炉の炉心が溶解してしまったことを隠そうとしたんだ？
example_sentences.english: Why did they try to hide that the core of the nuclear reactor had melted?

notes: "The pasture grass is the pasture and grass." "With 草 you learned a different reading from the one here. Just think about how with this pasture you have to constantly sew (そう) it together to make it come together, otherwise it comes apart and moves all around, and that's no good for any pasture."

example_sentences.japanese: 氷点下の日々が続いているせいで、牧草が全てやられてしまった。
example_sentences.english: It has been below freezing for days, so all my grass is dead.

notes: "A pasture field is pasture land. It's also a ranch." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.The secondary reading is a bit different. That's a family name, and uses the kun'yomi readings of both kanji. We'll consider this secondary for now, but you may have to come back to this when you see this as a name and are all like ""what's going on here??"""

example_sentences.japanese: 二、三年くらいしたら、父親が死んで、俺は父さんの牧野を相続する事になると思うよ。
example_sentences.english: In a few years my father will die and I’ll inherit his ranch.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Additionally, a cylinder is a pipe as well." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: When it comes to pipes, you always want to have two sets of two of them, just in case. So, that's a two two (つつ) set of pipes, lined up next to each other for backup."

example_sentences.japanese: 使い終わったら、体温計を筒の中に戻しておいてね。
example_sentences.english: Can you put the thermometer back in its tube when you’re done using it?

notes: "The point to my theory is the point of an argument. That's what I'm trying to say in my theory / argument, man!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の話の論旨があまりに不明瞭だったので、苛々しました。
example_sentences.english: I got frustrated because the point of his story was very vague.

notes: "The instant day is the day that's going on this instant. It's the same day as now." "The reading for 即 is the normal one. For 日 you're going to want to use the じつ reading, because, the truth (じつ) is that it's the same day today."

example_sentences.japanese: この回転肉焼き器は、注文日の即日に発送致します。
example_sentences.english: We sent out this rotisserie on the same day as you order.

notes: "The kanji is seal in, but the vocab noun version is seal. This is simply a seal (not the water kind, the kind you use to seal something with)." "The reading is the same as one of the readings you learned: ふう. Don't be a fool, make sure you seal your envelopes."

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が六歳の子どもだってことは分かってたけど、父さんが勝手に封を開けて友達からの手紙を読んだことにはすごく腹が立ったわ。
example_sentences.english: I know I was just a 6-year-old kid, but I got so mad when my dad opened the envelope and read the letter from my friend without asking me first.

notes: "A seal in writing is writing that has been sealed into an envelope. This is a sealed letter." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 契約書にサインをして封筒に入れてありますが、まだその封書を郵送していません。
example_sentences.english: I signed the contract and put it in an envelope, but I haven’t mailed the sealed letter to them yet.

notes: "At one moment it happened simultaneously. It was simultaneous. It was all at once." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the shortening of 一."

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒達は一斉に温度計に目をやりました。
example_sentences.english: The students looked at the thermometer simultaneously.

notes: "A stone hedge is a wall (hedges are nice walls), but it's made of stone. It's a stone wall." "The reading is the readings for 石 and 垣 combined into one word. Be careful of the rendakus."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は義足を付けていたので、石垣を乗り越えられませんでした。
example_sentences.english: He couldn’t climb over the stone wall because he has artificial legs.

notes: "An exposed shop is one that's not inside. It's outside, and exposed. It's a street stall." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの露店で買ったアクセは全部すぐ壊れちゃったよ。
example_sentences.english: Every accessory I bought from the street stall broke immediately.

notes: "A mutual slap is when two big guys run at each other and slap each other. This is sumo wrestling." "The reading is pretty weird, and not one you've learned. But, you know what sumo is, right? It's just the same as that. It's すもう."

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜ビールを飲みながら相撲を見るってのはどうだい？
example_sentences.english: Do you want to drink some beer and watch sumo wrestling tonight?

notes: "A bog swamp is a swamp or marsh." "Oddly, this is the one word that uses the on'yomi reading, which you didn't learn with the kanji. To remember this particular swamp, note how there are two kanji in here that make this area particularly swampy. Because it's the swampiest, boggiest place in all of Japan, of course the Shogun (しょう) wants it for himself. Even though it's useless land, he wants the best of everything, being the Shogun and all."

example_sentences.japanese: この黄色い花を咲かせる植物は、沼沢地に生息します。
example_sentences.english: This plant with yellow flowers lives in swamps.

notes: "The wind tide is the direction in which the tide is blowing. Is it blowing in? Is it blowing out? It is the tide and current. These days, we usually use this word for the current trends that come in like the tide." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは、富裕層に反対する社会的風潮を生み出した。
example_sentences.english: They brought about a social trend against the rich.

notes: "A tides stream is the stream going through the tide. It's the tide or the tidal current." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 荒い潮流に逆らってボートを漕ぐのは簡単ではないが、コテージに戻るにはそれしか方法がない。
example_sentences.english: It’s not easy to row against the rough tide, but that’s the only way for us to get back to our cottage.

notes: "The bathe clothes are the clothes you take with you to bathe with. This is Yukata." "The reading is totally an exception. The reading comes from the meaning, though. Yukata = ゆかた."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は自分の古い考え方にしがみついて、毎晩パジャマの代わりに浴衣を着て過ごした。
example_sentences.english: She clung to her old ways of thinking and wore a yukata instead of pajamas every night.

notes: "A challenge (挑戦) someone is someone who is going to challenge you. They are a challenger." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 腕相撲の挑戦者は、握力を見せつけるために、右手で林檎を潰してみせました。
example_sentences.english: The arm‐wrestling challenger crushed an apple in his right hand, showing off the strength of his right hand.

notes: "A sleep bed is where you sleep. Where do you sleep? In a bed or a crib, if you're a baby you really wants to learn kanji." "This word uses the kun'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn the second kun'yomi reading for 床. You take とこ and rendaku it into どこ. How do you remember this? Just think about your bed. Then wonder, ""where (どこ) is it?"""

example_sentences.japanese: 「さぁ、そろそろ寝床に着く時間じゃぞ。」子供の頃、毎晩祖父にこう言われました。
example_sentences.english: """Come now, isn’t it about time for bed?"" My grandfather used to say that to me every night."

notes: "A book shelf is a bookcase or bookshelf." The readings are the ones you learned with the individual kanji. Be careful of the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の本棚に、食い逃げの仕方について書かれた本を見つけたんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I found a book in this bookcase about how to eat and run.

notes: "Both wings are both wings! There are two and you have them all!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 二遊間、外野の両翼のポジションはまだ空いています。
example_sentences.english: A ball was hit between the second baseman and the shortstop, and both outfield positions are still vacant.

hiragana: かんびーる, かんビール
notes: "A can of beer (ビール) is a can beer or canned beer. Not a bottled one." The reading is the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: ああ、この缶ビールはマジでうますぎる。
example_sentences.english: Oh, this canned beer is way too good for me.

hiragana: かんこーひー, かんコーヒー
notes: "A can coffee (コーヒー) is coffee that's in a can. That's canned coffee or can coffee." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは、とても美味い缶コーヒーを販売して、大儲けしている。
example_sentences.english: They’re making a killing selling delicious canned coffee.

notes: "A big cannon is... wait for it... just a cannon. I guess all cannons are big, right? At least when you compare them to guns." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大砲がズドーンと鳴り響き、男は三人の子どもたちを残したまま逝ってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The cannon went off with a bang and the man passed away leaving three children behind.

hiragana: けいたいすとらっぷ, けいたいストラップ
english: Cell Phone Strap, Mobile Phone Strap
notes: "You know how 携帯 refers to a mobile phone? This is a strap (ストラップ) for a mobile phone, making this a cell phone strap or mobile phone strap." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Will help to know the reading of 携帯."

example_sentences.japanese: あの携帯ストラップが気色悪すぎて、考えるだけでも吐きそうだわ。
example_sentences.english: The cell phone strap is so gross just thinking about it makes me puke.

notes: "The pipe control tower is the tower that controls all the pipes... think of the pipes not as pipes, but as directions things are moving in. This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: もし巨大な竜巻がこの地域を襲ったら、管制塔はどうなるんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: If a huge tornado hit this area, how do you think the control tower would fare?

notes: "A door shelf is a shelf with a door on it. What kinds of shelves do you know of that have doors on them? How about cupboards?" These readings are the ones you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日買った単三電池は戸棚の上に置いておいたよ。
example_sentences.english: I put the double A batteries that we bought today in the cupboard.

notes: "The fear dragon is a dinosaur. Not sure why dinosaurs > dragons on the fear scale, but I'm sure they'll take what they can get." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 恐竜の化石を見つけるのに一番いい方法はなんでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: What’s the best way to find dinosaur fossils?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: その小説家は、55冊目の竜を題材にした小説でようやく大儲けすることができた。
example_sentences.english: The novelist finally hit pay dirt with his fifty-fifth novel about dragons.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Things left near the edge tend to fall off. Remember the old Koichidamus proverb, ""Only a fool (ふ) leaves his cheese (ち) on the edge of a table."""

example_sentences.japanese: 縁が無い眼鏡はありますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you have any rimless glasses?

english: Edged Tool, Cutlery, Kitchen Cutlery, Knife
notes: "A blade thing is an edged tool or cutlery." "The reading is the kun'yomi readings of the kanji. You learned 刃's reading with the kanji, and you probably remember 物 from so many other words."

example_sentences.japanese: 刃物をちらつかせながら、男は低い声で私に「こっちへ来い」と言いました。
example_sentences.english: "While brandishing his knife, he said to me in a low voice, ""Get over here."""

notes: "The blade's ahead is the farthest part of the blade away from you (since it's ahead of you). This is the edge of the blade or blade edge." "The reading is the kun'yomi readings of the kanji. For 刃 you learned that with the kanji. For 先 that's the vocab version of the kanji."

example_sentences.japanese: 刃先を俺の首に当てながら、奴は、皆にいつもご機嫌をとられてるってのはどんな気分なのかと聞いてきたんだ。
example_sentences.english: While putting the edge of the blade in my neck, the guys asked me what it’s like to have people fawning over me all the time.

hiragana: えっふぇるとう, エッフェルとう
notes: "The Eiffel (エッフェル) tower is the Eiffel Tower." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: エッフェル塔のどんなところが好きでしたか？
example_sentences.english: What did you like about the Eiffel Tower?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji!

example_sentences.japanese: 父親同様、魚釣りは彼のお気に入りの気晴らしだ。蛙の子は蛙ってことだね。
example_sentences.english: Fishing is his favorite pastime, just like his father. They say like father, like son.

notes: "Four small animals is four small animals. Use this to count four dogs, or cats, or whatever else." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの四匹のマルチーズは、昨日、誕生日だったので、とても美味しい晩ご飯を食べました。
example_sentences.english: My four Maltese dogs had a scrumptious supper because yesterday was their birthday.

notes: "A hand sack is a sack for your hands... better put, these are gloves." "The readings are both the kun'yomi vocab readings, so think of 手 and 袋 as individual words, put together to make hand sacks. Watch out for the rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: どうして裸んぼで手袋だけはめて走り回ってるの？あんたは本当に馬鹿ね。
example_sentences.english: Why are you running around naked with only gloves on? You’re such an idiot!

notes: "Remember how 握る is ""to grasp""? This is the noun version, making it a grip." "The reading comes from 握る, so get a grip on that!"

example_sentences.japanese: 怒ったコウイチは、握りこぶしで机をバンバン叩いた。
example_sentences.english: Angry Koichi banged on the desk with his clenched fists.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading for the vocab version of this word is the same as 岡 which has the same meaning and the same reading. Lucky! "

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてマニュアルで運転した時、丘のてっぺんでエンストしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: On my first day of driving a stick, my car stalled at the top of a hill.

notes: "Let's take the edge and discuss it. That edge is the edge of getting married. But, when you reach that edge, before you jump over, you have to do a marriage proposal." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 高卒以下の学歴の男との縁談を私に持って寄越すなんて、一体どういう神経してる訳？
example_sentences.english: How dare you to bring me a marriage proposal from a guy who has less than a high school education?!

notes: "One of the easiest methods of measurement is to just check the size and dimensions, and there you go, you've got the measurement." "This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just remember that the ほう changes to ぽう."

example_sentences.japanese: この寸法は正しいですか？
example_sentences.english: Is this measurement correct?

notes: "Your mourning clothes is your mourning dress or mourning clothes." "The reading comes from the on'yomi for 服 and the kun'yomi for 喪, which you learned with the word 喪. You should know how to read this word!"

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妹は拒食症なのですが、喪服を着ているとより一層痩せ細ってみえました。
example_sentences.english: My sister is anorexic and when wearing her mourning dress, she looked even skinnier.

notes: "An endure someone is someone who can endure. Who endures everything better than anyone? A ninja." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは忍者に、正々堂々と勝負で勝った。
example_sentences.english: Koichi beat the ninja fair and square!

notes: "The edge of wake up is right before you wake up. And, by wake up I mean you're about the wake up to the truth. But, you're only at the edge, so for now what you see is an omen... an omen that will show the truth." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just remember that 起 is rendaku'd and becomes ぎ here. "

example_sentences.japanese: カラスは、日本だけでなくヨーロッパでも、縁起の悪い鳥とみなされます。
example_sentences.english: The crow is seen as an ominous bird not only in Japan but also in Europe.

notes: "One small animal is one small animal. Use this to count small animals like cats and dogs." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Be careful of the shortening and the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 「なあ、今夜俺たちと遊ばないか？金曜日の東京の繁華街はめちゃくちゃ楽しいぜ。」「俺は一匹狼なんだよ。放っておいてくれ。」
example_sentences.english: """Do you want to hang out with us tonight? Downtown Tokyo is crazy on Fridays."" ""I’m a lone wolf. Leave me alone."""

notes: "You know that 泊まる is ""to stay the night."" The noun version is a overnight stay or sleepover." "The reading comes from 泊まる, so pull from that and you shall know this."

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子、幼稚園のお泊まり会をすごく楽しみにしてたんだけど、風邪を引いちゃって、今抗生物質を飲ませたところなんです。だから、残念ながら今夜は欠席させて頂きます。
example_sentences.english: My kid was really looking forward to the kindergarten sleepover, but he got a cold and I just made him take antibiotics. So, sadly, he’ll be absent tonight.

notes: "If you only have one wing you only have part of a bird. Or a plane. Either way, you only have a part of it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大きなプロジェクトの一翼を担えることになりました。
example_sentences.english: I’ll handle part of the big project.

notes: "A grain's child is even smaller than a grain. It's a particle, sometimes even an atomic particle." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 光が粒子なのか波なのかを考えていて、昨日は眠れませんでした。

english: Edge Of A Sumo Ring, Sumo Ring Edge, Edge, Sumo Ring
notes: "A soil sack on the edge. Pretend the sacks are lined up around in a circle. It's the edge of a sumo ring. Can also be a sumo ring." "The first two kanji (土俵) use the on'yomi reading you learned. The last kanji 際 uses the kun'yomi reading, which you should know via the vocabulary. Just think of these two parts as somewhat separate bits of the word, which is why one part is on'yomi and another (the addition) is kun'yomi."

example_sentences.japanese: その力士は土俵際で踏ん張り、相手力士に打っ棄りを食らわせた。
example_sentences.english: The sumo wrestler braced himself at the edge of the ring and was able to throw his opponent out.

notes: "An electricity lamp is an electric lamp. Nowadays they're all electricity, though, which means it's a lamp." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの嫁さんは全然電灯を消さないんだよね。きっとスイッチがあることを知らないんだと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: My wife never turns off the light. She probably doesn’t even know there is a switch.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんなら今うちの冷蔵庫の霜取りをしてるよ。
example_sentences.english: My dad is removing the frost from our fridge right now.

notes: "The neck of the squad is the most important part of the squad, for if you lose the neck you lose the head (they're all one thing). This person is the head or leader of a group." This is a jukugo word so it uses the on'yomi readings, which you've learned already. Go you!

example_sentences.japanese: どいつが新入生の首班を占めることになると思う？
example_sentences.english: Who do you think will be the leader of the first-year students?

notes: "A horse hand is the hands that ride the horse. These hands belong to a horse rider." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その騎手は、自分の初めてのG1レースの日に朝寝坊をしました。
example_sentences.english: The rider overslept on the day of his first G1 race.

notes: "It can melt a boulder? What is this stuff that's so hot? It's lava. It's also probably made from melted boulders too, come to think of it." "This word uses the on'yomi reading for the kanji, but you haven't learned the on'yomi reading for 岩, which is がん. When you think of lava, think about Gandhi, coming out of the lava. He's immune, because he's a robot."

example_sentences.japanese: 火山が溶岩を吹き出していて危険なので、これ以上近づくことはできません。
example_sentences.english: We can’t go any closer because the volcano is spewing out lava and it’s dangerous.

notes: "The degrees of radiance show the luminance and brightness of something, so long as the degree is the right degree." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 例えば、太陽の輝度値はとても高いです。
example_sentences.english: For example, the sun’s luminosity value is very high.

hiragana: めもちょう, メモちょう
english: Memo Book, Memo Pad, Notebook, Notepad, Scratchpad
notes: "A memo (メモ) notebook is a memo book or memo pad that you use to write notes in." "The reading is the one you learned with the kanji, plus メモ."

example_sentences.japanese: 話の途中で申し訳ありませんが、あなたのメモ帳のことでどうしても質問したいんです。
example_sentences.english: Forgive me for interrupting, but I must ask you a question about your memo pad.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 根っからの蚊取り線香派なんで、電気のやつを使うのは好きじゃないんですよね。
example_sentences.english: I’m a die hard mosquito coil user, I don’t like using the electric ones.

notes: "A mosquito notebook, for some reason, is a mosquito net. Think of a notebook with graph paper lines on it, perhaps. These lines are shaped like a net. Surround yourself with it to make your own mosquito net." "The first kanji, 蚊, uses the reading you learned. The second kanji has an exceptional reading, や. To remember や, think about how you had to take a giant mosquito net and cover all of Yankee (や) Stadium. They have a rough mosquito problem."

example_sentences.japanese: 十人用の大きな蚊帳はありますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you have a mosquito net big enough for ten people?

notes: "A hand notebook is a notebook you can hold in your hand. This could simply be a notebook, but it could also be a planner." The readings are the readings you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 手帳を盗み見すると、彼女は物凄く怒りました。
example_sentences.english: She got unbelievably angry at me when I peeped at her notebook.

notes: "Oil coloring is better known as oil painting. What fine strokes! What fine lines!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 油彩画のコツを掴んできました。
example_sentences.english: I’m getting the hang of oil painting.

notes: "The painting fee isn't one of money. If you want to paint, you will have to pay the fee for paints and painting materials." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 刷毛に蛍光塗料を付けました。
example_sentences.english: I dipped the paint brush in the fluorescent paint.

notes: "A diagonal surface is a slant. A slope." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの私道は急斜面になってるので、上まで上がってくるにはスノータイヤがいります。
example_sentences.english: Our driveway has become a steep slope, so you need snow tires to get up it.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: この町で蛇がペットとして普及した時には、身震いしましたよ。
example_sentences.english: When keeping snakes as pets spread throughout the city, I trembled.

english: Squad Leader, Honcho, Team Leader, Group Leader
notes: "The squad leader is the squad leader. Can also be the honcho (ever wonder where this word came from?)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は社交的でみんなから好かれているので、班長に選ばれました。
example_sentences.english: He is sociable and everyone likes him, so he was elected to be the team leader.

notes: "One person starves and another person starves. Then more people. So much starve that there's starvation going on. It's famine and hunger, everywhere." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてそんな風にクッキーを踏みつけたりしたんだ？毎日何千何百人という人が飢餓で亡くなるのを知らないのか。
example_sentences.english: Why would you step on a cookie like that? Don’t you know that thousands of people die from starvation every day?

notes: "A street lamp is a streetlight. Brightening up my street!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大量の蛾が、各街灯の周りを飛び交っています。
example_sentences.english: There are a ton of moths flying around each street lamp.

notes: "A telephone (電話) notebook is a book you use with your telephone. It's a telephone book or telephone directory." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この電話帳を整理してしまう方がいいと思います。
example_sentences.english: We should finish arranging these telephone books.

notes: "A water coloring painting is a watercolor painting." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は素晴らしい水彩画家だそうですよ。
example_sentences.english: She is supposed to be an amazing watercolor painter.

notes: "With water it will melt. It is naturally like this. It is water soluble." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 水溶性のビタミンCはすぐに体内から排出されるので、私達の体に蓄えることはできないと読みましたよ。
example_sentences.english: I read that water-soluble vitamin C generally leaves the body quickly, so our bodies can’t store it.

notes: "You know that 椅子 is a ""chair."" What about a car chair? It's a chair with wheels. A wheelchair." "The reading for 車 is the vocab reading, くるま. Then, 椅子 is いす."

example_sentences.japanese: あの車椅子に座ってる女の子、めちゃくちゃセクシーじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Isn’t the girl in the wheelchair ridiculously sexy?

notes: "A clever person is a wise man. I could use a wise man around me. Seems like a good kind of friend to have." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの教授、外では賢人って言われてるけど、実は内弁慶らしいぜ。
example_sentences.english: That professor is called a wise man outside, but I heard he’s actually a braggart at home.

notes: "Pluck an elephant out at random. It doesn't make sense. What is that doing here? The reason is abstract." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のレビューは何だか抽象的だったので、あまりよく分かりませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Her review was kind of abstract, so I didn’t really understand it.

notes: "Boiled things turn into boiled foods or stewed foods. You can eat anything, if it's boiled long enough." The reading is the readings you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は小食ですが、煮物ならモリモリ食べます。
example_sentences.english: She is a light eater but when it comes to stewed foods she eats with gusto.

notes: "A buddha podium is the podium on which you put Buddha. This is a Buddhist altar." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 仏壇の前でうつ伏せになって寝転がっていると、母がやって来てそれは失礼なことだと怒られました。
example_sentences.english: When I was laying on my stomach in front of the buddhist altar, my mom came over and told me doing that was rude.

notes: "A pearl calculation is calculations you do with pearls. If you think about using pearls to calculate something, it's going to look a lot like using an abacus. That's why this calculation is calculation with abacus." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は珠算を勉強するって気分じゃないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I don’t feel like studying calculations on an abacus today.

notes: "The Pottery art is making pottery. That is the ceramic arts or simply ceramics." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の陶芸作品のルーツは、日本文化にあります。
example_sentences.english: Her ceramic works have roots in Japanese culture.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Can also refer to a shogi piece too, since that's Japanese chess, after all." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 父さんが日曜日にチェスの駒の動かし方を教えてくれるって約束してくれたんだ。
example_sentences.english: My dad promised me that he would teach me how to move chess pieces this Sunday.

notes: "Under the shade people conspire. When people do this, conspiracy appears." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は秘密結社が世界を支配しているという陰謀論を信じています。
example_sentences.english: He believes in a conspiracy theory that a secret society is controlling the world.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading for this word is the same as the one you learned with the vocab.

example_sentences.japanese: たくさんの折り紙の鶴を醤油につけて、日本人の女の子の部屋に置いてみるってのはどうかな。
example_sentences.english: What about dipping a bunch of origami cranes in the soy sauce and putting them in the Japanese girl’s room?

notes: "貨幣 is ""currency"" and 価値 is ""value."" This shows the currency value. Hopefully it's good for you when you visit Japan!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その時からどれぐらい貨幣価値が変わったか、知っているかい？
example_sentences.english: Do you know how much the value of money has changed since then?

notes: "Isolate this week from next week, and do that over and over. That way we have every other week." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: このアニメは隔週で放送されていて、私はそのオープニング曲とエンディング曲が好きです。
example_sentences.english: This anime is airs every other week and I like its opening and ending songs.

notes: "A group of folding fans, no matter how big it gets, is still a fan." "The reading for 団 is an exceptional reading. It's the same as 内's reading so you can think about how a group of folding fans to make a big fan is just a bunch of fans inside of fans.The reading for 扇 is also an exceptional reading. Imagine a walrus (わ) using the 内 fan."

example_sentences.japanese: 同じ模様の団扇だけど、私の物の方があなたのより少し小さくて軽いみたいね。
example_sentences.english: Our fans have the same design, but mine seems to be a little smaller and lighter than yours.

notes: "A flower podium is a podium of flowers, put up higher than the ground. This is a flower bed." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その花壇を見ると、いつも母を思い出します。
example_sentences.english: I always think of my mother when I see a flower bed.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is different from the one you learned with the kanji. Someone waves a folding fan at you, but it just blows hot air at you. ""ohh gee"" (おうぎ), you say. ""Thanks for nothing."""

example_sentences.japanese: あの、紫色の扇をもったご婦人は一体どなたですか。
example_sentences.english: Who on earth is the lady holding the violet folding fan?

notes: "The peoples who are vulgar aren't refined city folk. They're people with folk customs and ethnic customs." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、歴史民俗資料館の館長です。
example_sentences.english: He is the director of the Museum of History and Folklore.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "A foundation is made of stone (いし). And it holds up an entire zoo A (ずえ) but none of Zoo B. Zoo B will fall apart when an earthquake hits."

example_sentences.japanese: ここにいる人は皆、総合格闘技の礎を築いた故人の死を悼んでいると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think everyone here is mourning over the deceased who laid the foundation of mixed martial art.

notes: "An approximation of thought is just thinking up the general idea. The concept or notion." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんどの無神論者は、神や神々の概念に対して否定的です。
example_sentences.english: Most of the atheists have negative feelings regarding the concept of God or gods.

notes: "Inferiority is how I feel because I don't have an ""equal"" feeling with you. This is due to my inferiority complex." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が私に対して劣等感を抱いていると誤解していました。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that she had an inferiority complex towards me.

notes: "The solely things theory is the theory that only things are important. This is also known as materialism." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 母国語でも唯物論について説明できないのに、どうして外国語で説明できるというのか。
example_sentences.english: I can’t even explain materialism in my native language, so how can I explain it in a foreign language?

notes: "Let's take the grass and prune it. This is called mowing." "The reading is 草 and 刈 put together into one. The か reading for 刈り comes from the kanji's reading."

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は俺が悪かったよ。本当にごめん。お詫びの印に、今日は草刈りをするよ。
example_sentences.english: I am really sorry for being a jerk yesterday. I’ll mow the grass today to apologize.

notes: "A mulberry field is a mulberry field or mulberry plantation. This is more like a commercial / organized mulberry growing operation, so not some random field of mulberries." "The reading comes from 桑 (kanji reading) and the vocab word 畑. Watch out for the rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: 私の地元には、桑畑があちこちにあります。
example_sentences.english: Mulberry fields are everywhere in my hometown.

notes: "A mulberry field is a mulberry field." "These are both the kun'yomi readings, but you haven't learned this for 原 yet. It's actually the rendaku'd version, so let's just use mnemonic to remember it instead:You know you're in a mulberry field when you see a bunch of capybaras (ばら) rolling around in there with you. Capybaras love mulberries! Picture a whole family of capybaras munching on mulberries. Mm Mmm!"

example_sentences.japanese: かつては桑畑がたくさんあったため、この場所は「桑原」と呼ばれるようになりました。
example_sentences.english: "People started calling this place ""Kuwabara"" because there used to be a lot of mulberry fields here."

notes: "The kanji means mulberry, but this refers to a mulberry tree. " The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 桑の実と林檎と胡桃の組み合わせが最強に美味しいんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Mulberries, apples, and walnuts taste best when they’re combined.

notes: "A random boil isn't all that random. It's specifically the new year's dish or mochi soup, eaten on new years. Old people and children tend to die every year from this (choking on the mochi), so be  careful if you eat it! Maybe the reason it's called ""random boil"" is because someone decided to boil a bunch of random things (like mochi) and then it became a new years dish later on. Who knows. That information isn't even known by the ancients." "You learned the reading for 煮 on the kanji page, but the reading for 雑 is an exceptional one. You did learn this reading with 雑巾, though. Just imagine yourself with a dust cloth in your new year's dish."

example_sentences.japanese: お雑煮そろそろ煮えたんじゃないかな。
example_sentences.english: The New Year’s mochi soup should be ready by now.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Are you a nun? I am a (あま) nun."

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は尼さんなのにお酒をたくさん飲みます。
example_sentences.english: Even though she’s a nun, she’s a heavy drinker.

notes: "A nun priest is a nun or priestess." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その尼僧は、寝起きはいつも顔がむくんでいます。
example_sentences.english: That nun’s face is always swollen when she wakes up.

notes: "An approximation of what we need is my outline / summary." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 青年海外協力隊についての概要は、こちらのページでお読み頂けます。
example_sentences.english: You can read an outline of the Japanese Peace Corps on this page.

notes: "A reality pearl is a real pearl! That's just a pearl." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 真珠を身につける人は減ってきています。
example_sentences.english: Less and less people are wearing pearls.

notes: "The profits that I'm watered with are pouring all over me. That's my profit and returns." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本には資源超過利潤税は無かったと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t think there is a Resources Super Profits Tax in Japan.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is different from the one you learned with the kanji. To remember this reading, think about how the previous village you went to was all purple. It was the ""村先"" (むらさき) that you went to. Everything. Absolutely everything was purple."

example_sentences.japanese: 暗闇の中でキラキラ光る紫色の光を見た瞬間、「母だ」と思ったんです。
example_sentences.english: "The instant I saw purple light shining through the darkness, I thought, ""Mom."""

notes: "The king of princesses is the greatest and highest ranking princess of them all." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は王妃と友情を育んだ。
example_sentences.english: I cultivated my friendship with the queen.

english: Red Light District, Pleasure Quarters, World Of The Geisha
notes: "The red light district (花柳) world of the red light district is the red light district, though this can refer especially to the ""pleasure quarters"" or ""world of the geisha"" as well." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 花柳界を経験してみるのが夢だったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I’ve always dreamed of experiencing the red-light district.

notes: "A rest (休憩) place is a rest area or rest stop." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 逮捕された男は、休憩所に不法侵入した疑いがかけられていた。
example_sentences.english: The man they arrested is suspected of breaking into the rest area.

notes: "A number of pearls, put together on a string. This refers to a rosary or prayer beads. You'll see these a lot in Japan, for sale or with monks wearing them." "The reading for this word is different from both of the kanji readings you learned. This word sounds a lot like Jews (じゅず), so we'll have to go with that. Just imagine a Jewish rosary or prayer beads, with a Jewish person using it."

example_sentences.japanese: 高額な数珠を私に売りつけようとした男の名前が思い出せません。
example_sentences.english: I can’t remember the name of the guy who tried to force me to buy an expensive rosary.

notes: "Encourage study money is money that you give to a kid to encourage him to study. That comes in the form of a scholarship or stipend." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その占い師に、私は奨学金をもらえるだろうって予言されたんだけど、当たったよ。
example_sentences.english: The fortuneteller predicted that I would receive the scholarship and she was right.

notes: "I'd like to isolate this interval of time. Take it, make it separate, and then look at it. Now there is a space there. An interval, if you will." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 生理痛程度の陣痛が15分から20分ぐらいの間隔で始まって、今行った方がいいのか病院に電話をしました。
example_sentences.english: Mild contractions are starting in 15 to 20 minutes intervals and I called the hospital to see if we should go now.

english: Splitting The Cost, Splitting The Bill
notes: "I will divide the intuition up. For some reason when I say ""intuition"" I mean ""money"" because this is referring to splitting the cost, like when you're at a restaurant." "The reading is 割る and 勘, put together."

example_sentences.japanese: 私は下戸でお酒を飲まないので、お酒のお勘定は割り勘じゃない方が嬉しいんですが。
example_sentences.english: I can’t drink because I get drunk easily, so it would be nice if we didn’t split the alcohol bill.

notes: "If 粘る is ""to be sticky"" then the noun version is stickiness." "The reading comes from 粘る."

example_sentences.japanese: 一生懸命粘り強く努力すればいつかは報われると思っていましたが、それは間違いでした。
example_sentences.english: I believed hard work and persistent efforts would pay off some day, but it was wrong.

notes: "A spirit of approximation is the approximation of spirit. My approximation of your spirit? I think you have a strong spirit. I think you have backbone." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その教師は、教室で見て見ぬふりをされている問題に取り組む気概がなかった。
example_sentences.english: The teacher didn’t have the guts to deal with the problems in the classroom.

notes: "You know that 詐欺 is ""fraud."" An expert at fraud (詐欺) is someone who does this a lot and possibly for a living. A swindler, some would say." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Will help to know the reading of 詐欺 as well."

example_sentences.japanese: 「ねぇ、今俺のこと、嘘つきって言った？」「そうは言ってないけど、詐欺師とは言ったよ。」「はぁ？何言ってんだよ。マジ、信じらんねぇ。」
example_sentences.english: """Hey, did you just call me a liar?"" ""No, but I called you a crook."" ""Huh? What are you talking about!? I seriously can’t believe you."""

notes: "The purple outside line is the color spectrum that's outside purple. Those are ultraviolet rays (the lines are the rays)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あんたはまずその紫外線恐怖症を克服しなきゃいけないね。
example_sentences.english: You must first conquer your fear of the ultraviolet rays.

notes: "A notebook that is also a record book is an account book or register, showing the records of all the transactions that have gone through." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 帳簿を燃やしてしまうという考えは思いつきませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I didn’t think of the idea to burn the account book.

notes: "An old tomb is an ancient tomb though it can refer to the ancient mounds (of the Jomon, I'm assuming)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 近年その古墳を訪れる人が増えています。
example_sentences.english: The number of people visiting the ancient tomb has been increasing in recent years.

notes: "The inscription's pattern shows what brand or make this item is. If the pattern of the inscription is an apple, you'll know the brand is Apple. If it's a Window, you know it's Microsoft. Etc." This word uses the on'yomi reading for the first kanji and the kun'yomi reading for the second. Luckily, you've learned them both already so you should be able to slap them together and know the reading of this word!

example_sentences.japanese: 後どれくらいでお客さんに推奨する銘柄が決まりそうですか。
example_sentences.english: How much longer will it take you to decide which brand to recommend to your customer?

hiragana: どうけつ, ほらあな
notes: "A cave hole is a cave or den." "The reading of 洞 is one you've learned. The reading of 穴 isn't one you've learned, though. So, think about how you go inside this cave, only to find yourself covered by some red goopy liquid. You think it's blood, but luckily it just turns out to be ketsup (けつ). If you want to be less formal, you can also use the kun'yomi and say ほらあな, but then you'd never learn that reading for 穴, and where's the fun in that?"

example_sentences.japanese: その洞穴で躓いて、足首を捻挫しました。
example_sentences.english: I stumbled into the cave and sprained my ankle.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Hoe Ra (ほら), the version of Ra who carries a hoe around, is using said hoe to dig out a cave for himself, to provide shade from the sun (despite being the god of sun). He digs digs digs and then sits in his nice cave, hoe in hand."

example_sentences.japanese: その薄気味悪い洞は、村の北外れにひっそりと佇んでいました。
example_sentences.english: The eerie cave stood silently in the outskirts north of the village.

notes:
"The chief of this district is that guy, the count. He's also the earl of another district, and the chief of yet another." "The reading is the はく reading you learned with the kanji."

"This counter is used to count musical beats when you're listening to or playing music." This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: フグの爵位を伯爵にして、フグ伯って呼ぶことにするのはどうかな。
example_sentences.english: How about giving Fugu the title of an earl, and calling him Count Fugu?

example_sentences.japanese: 4分の4拍子の曲では、通常、1拍目と3拍目の頭に強拍が来ます。
example_sentences.english: For music in four-four time, the stress usually comes to a head at the first and third beats.

english: Comic Dialogue, Two Man Comedy Act
notes: "A manga genius! For some reason, this is a comic dialogue or two man comedy. Look up ""manzai"" on YouTube for some good times if you don't know what this is. It's not exactly the same, but 漫 DOES refer to manga, which is a type of comic book. Take the ""comic"" part from ""comic"" book, then change it to the ""haha funny!"" meaning of ""comic,"" and then imagine people doing a dialogue. Then, you have a comic dialogue. Lots of steps, but hopefully it'll get you there." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 漫才を見て大声で笑うことはストレス解消になる。
example_sentences.english: Watching two man comedy acts and laughing loudly relieves my stress.

notes: "The meaning is the same as the kanji's meaning, crab. If you know this word, and you know the word 鰐 as well... then, well, you know something, though I'm not sure what that something is." The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. But you knew that already, didn't you?

example_sentences.japanese: お腹がすいてきた。晩ご飯の蟹が楽しみだ。
example_sentences.english: I’m getting hungry. I’m looking forward to having crab for dinner.

notes: "A water crystal is just a crystal. I guess crystals are clear and look kind of like water, yeah? That's why it's being referred to as a water crystal, making it really just a crystal." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この水晶は大中小の三つの大きさがあります。
example_sentences.english: This crystal comes in three sizes; small, medium, and large.

notes: "You look at this inscription then you look at that inscription and you notice that each one is an individual inscription." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの家族の銘々がその写真を持っています。
example_sentences.english: Each member of my family has this photo.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is like the reading of 包み, which means ""bundle"" or ""package."" Try to think of an embankment that's made purely from bundles and packages. These 包み (つつみ) are the only thing holding the water in!"

example_sentences.japanese: 村長は、堤が切れるのを防ぐため、堤に人柱を埋めることを決意しました。
example_sentences.english: The village head decided to bury a human sacrifice in the embankment to prevent it from collapsing.

notes: "Look below you. These things carry your burdensome weight. All of it. These are the shoes you wear, though in this case they are specifically geta, or Japanese wooden clogs. The clogs themselves are kind of burdensome and hard to wear too, actually, so you can think of it that way as well." "The reading for 駄 is the secondary kanji reading. Instead of だ it's た. Hopefully you've heard of ""geta"" before. This will make it really easy for you to remember the reading of this vocab word."

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの下駄は二色のお色をご用意しております。
example_sentences.english: These wooden clogs come in two colors.

notes: "A gloomy energy has filled the room. This makes for a gloomy feeling. One of melancholy." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Careful of the shortening of 鬱 or you'll feel gloomy."

example_sentences.japanese: 伯父は、鬱気で家でふさぎ込んでいる。
example_sentences.english: My uncle's been home feeling melancholy.

example_sentences.japanese: 鬱気を吹き飛ばしてくれるような歌ですね。
example_sentences.english: This song can really blow the gloom away.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は鬱気が邪魔をして、日本語を勉強する気になれません。
example_sentences.english: My depression's bothering me today and I can't get myself to study Japanese.

notes: "A tomb grave is a grave... or it could be a tomb. Or maybe both." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ツタンカーメンの墳墓は絶対に訪れた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You should definitely visit the tomb of Tutankhamen.

notes: "A hemp cloth is a hemp cloth." "The reading is the individual vocab readings of 麻 and 布 combined together."

example_sentences.japanese: 麻布の服が好きなんだけど、結構お値段が高いんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I like clothes made of hemp cloth, but they’re rather expensive.

notes: "A sky cave is a cave with sky (open space) in it. This is a hollow, but can also refer to a cavity." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 白熊が木の空洞の中でうたた寝をしていると、近くに木こりがやって来ました。
example_sentences.english: A polar bear was snoozing in the hollow of a tree and a lumberjack soon came along.

notes: "To excuse yourself from the epidemic, you'll have to have immunity or immunization from the disease." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも微熱とひどい頭痛があるのでお医者さんに行ったら、免疫機能が弱ってきていると言われました。
example_sentences.english: I went to the doctor because I always have a slight fever and terrible headache, and I was told that my immune system is weakening.

notes: "A fluid crystal is a liquid crystal." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の投げたライターがテレビに当たって、液晶画面にヒビが入りました。
example_sentences.english: The lighter I threw hit the TV and cracked the LCD screen.

notes: "Take along this summit and move it across a range, visiting more summits. One summit after another you take the summit along to. By covering this many summits, you notice there's a string of mountains. This is a mountain range!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の連峰はよく晴れていて見晴らしがいいです。
example_sentences.english: Today’s mountain range cleared up nicely and the view is great.

notes: "A life horizon is your life, which you're looking out over, all the way to the very end. This is one's lifetime, though it could also refer to one's career. Basically, at the end of it something dies." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 生涯ずっと独身なんて嫌だよう。
example_sentences.english: I don’t want to stay single my whole life.

notes: "A rut in the road is for some reason an orbit or trajectory. Maybe imagine a big ol' rut in the road. You drive at it at very high speeds, hit it, and fly into the sky at a trajectory that will send you into orbit. Now you're up in space, circling the earth, wishing you didn't drive so fast." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ロケットが軌道に入ったというニュースを聞いて、誰もが喜びました。
example_sentences.english: Everyone was delighted to hear the news that the rocket entered orbit.

notes: "Your robust years are the best years of your life! This is the prime of life." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のお兄さんは壮年期に心臓発作を起こして亡くなりました。
example_sentences.english: His older brother had a heart attack and passed away in the prime of life.

english: Register Of Names, List Of Names, Roll
notes: "A name record book is a book that contains names. That is a register of names or a list of names. Is your name on the list?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は仰向けに寝転がって、名簿の全ての名前に目を通した。
example_sentences.english: He laid face up and looked through all the names in the register.

notes: "The renewed and revised edition of something is the revised edition." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out for the rendaku.

example_sentences.japanese: バスの時刻が改訂されたなら、改訂版の時刻表をもらわなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: If the bus schedule was revised, I need the revised edition.

notes: "Distribute yourself accidentally to someone. That person ended up becoming your spouse. You distributed yourself to one person a little too much, it seems." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい配偶者を探そうかとずっと考えているんです。
example_sentences.english: I’ve been thinking about looking for a new spouse.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Can also be peak or ridge." "Look up at the summit. It's such a mean (みね) summit. So big, so stormy, so mean."

example_sentences.japanese: 妹と私は、雲の上にそびえる富士山の峰に登頂しました。
example_sentences.english: My sister and I climbed up to the peak of Mt. Fuji, rising up above the clouds.

notes: "The eddy river isn't so much a thing as it is a famous place. We're talking about Yodogawa. It might be better to look at the reading to learn the meaning. Look up this Osaka Prefecture river if you'd like more info." "The reading is 淀 plus 川. Be careful of the rendaku."

example_sentences.japanese: 汚い水にも怯まず、彼女は淀川で泳いだ。
example_sentences.english: The dirty water didn’t stop her swimming in the Yodogawa.

notes: "When you have mercy upon those you love it's called affection. You end up doing things out of the kindness of your heart because they mean a lot to you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は慈愛に満ちた微笑を僕に向けた。
example_sentences.english: She turned her affectionate smile toward me.

notes: "Plowed land is called arable land. This is the kind of land you use for growing crops or for pastures." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺りには耕地が広がっています。
example_sentences.english: The arable land is spread out in this area.

notes: "The point at which something starts to boil is the boiling point." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 沸点は何度ですか。
example_sentences.english: How many degrees is the boiling point?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 瓶ビールを一本ください。
example_sentences.english: One bottled beer, please.

notes: "You are a strong, independent person and you are the only one who can manipulate your chastity. Nobody else can. So if you want to keep your chastity that's completely up to you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男が彼女の貞操を奪ったのよ。
example_sentences.english: That man robbed her of her virtue.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 襟が曲がっていますよ。
example_sentences.english: Your collar is twisted.

notes: "If you have mercy for people who are sad you have a lot of compassion. You just can't help but go easy on sad people." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は本当に慈悲深い人だった。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother was a really compassionate person.

notes: "A one sided corner is still a corner, just a really small one." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: そのことが心の片隅にずっと引っかかっていたんです。
example_sentences.english: That had always been stuck in the corner of my mind.

notes: "Wash wash powder is the detergent you put in the wash you make sure your clothes are washed well. Detergent used to only be available in powder form back in the old days, and it still can be, so this is for that good powdery stuff." "This is a mix of the on'yomi readings for 洗濯 and the kun'yomi reading for 粉. You already learned this reading for 粉 when you learned the word 麦粉. If you can remember that, you should know the readings for this one too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 洗濯粉がきれちゃった。
example_sentences.english: We ran out of detergent.

notes: "The wash wash shop is where you go to get your clothes washed extra well. It's the dry cleaners! They wash your clothes way better than you can because they wash them twice." "This is a mix of the on'yomi readings for 洗濯 and the kun'yomi reading for 屋. You've learned all of these readings by now, so you should be able to read this word too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 洗濯屋にワイシャツを取りに行ってきます。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to pick up my dress shirt from the dry cleaners.

english: Eaves, Stand In A Row, Stand Side By Side
notes: "In order to use a house counter in the first place, you need to have something to count. That's why you have to find eaves. And all those eaves together stand in a row." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: These houses that stand in a row are neat and fun to count, but you can't go in because you have no key (のき). With no key, those eaves are just there for you to look at."

example_sentences.japanese: ここには多くのラーメン屋台が軒を連ねています。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of ramen carts standing in a row here.

notes: "The prefecture in Japan where they love princesses is Ehime Prefecture." "This reading is a little messy. This reading for 愛 is an exception, 媛 uses the kun'yomi reading ひめ, and 県 uses the on'yomi reading けん. Here's a mnemonic to help you remember this reading for 愛:If you ask anyone outside of Ehime Prefecture what they think of princesses they'll respond with, ""Eh"" (え). They don't really care either way. If someone from Ehime heard that they'd says, ""EH? EH?! Princesses are the BEST!"""

example_sentences.japanese: 私は愛媛県の出身です。
example_sentences.english: I am from Ehime Prefecture.

notes: "Farming with a plow is still farming." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のおじいさんは農耕をしています。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather farms.

notes: "Something that's both fat and obese has even more fat on it than you first thought. Like the blubber on a really big whale." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 太ももの脂肪を落としたいんです。
example_sentences.english: I want to lose the fat from my thighs.

notes: "Four corners are four corners!" The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned them both by now, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 写真の四隅を暗く加工するにはどうすればいいのか教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Can you teach me the best process to make the four corners of a picture dark?

notes: "A person with a lot of greatness is a great person." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界の偉人たちの名言を集めました。
example_sentences.english: I’ve collected wise sayings from great men of the world.

notes: "The land inside of a residence is called the grounds or the premises. Only really big residences have land inside them big enough to be called the ""grounds"" though." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、邸内の写真です。
example_sentences.english: This is a picture of the grounds.

notes: "A lotus flower is a lotus flower!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 花 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Something is on the lotus flower... something little and kinda shiny. It's a little gecko (げ). It's hiding in the lotus and trying to catch flies. How cute!"

example_sentences.japanese: この池にはいつから蓮花があるのですか。
example_sentences.english: How long have lotus flowers been in this pond?

notes: "If you have a residence that's also your house, it's still your residence. But you probably have a lot of money if you can own your own house, so it's probably a nice, big mansion too." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この邸宅は、幽霊が出ることで有名です。
example_sentences.english: This mansion is famous for ghosts appearing in it.

notes: "A fire in a bottle that makes a big fire when thrown is called a Molotov Cocktail. Don't throw them in the house please." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 男は火炎瓶を投げつけた。
example_sentences.english: The man threw a Molotov cocktail.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Usually these types of mounds are burial mounds. (There's bodies under there!)" This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 塚を見下ろすことのは失礼です。
example_sentences.english: It’s rude to look down at a burial mound.

notes: "Corner corners are still corners. Sometimes they're the corners TO corners, so they're the little nooks and crannies that are hard to get at." This word uses the kun'yomi readings of the kanji you learned, twice, with the second one rendaku'd. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は部屋を隅々まで掃除しました。
example_sentences.english: Today I cleaned every nook and cranny of my room.

notes:
"A government residence is one that is assigned to government officials. That means it's their official residence, and it goes on all their official paperwork." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

"What does a warship and a rowboat have in common? At wartime they're both considered military vessels." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 首相官邸ツアーに参加しました。
example_sentences.english: I participated in a tour of the Prime Minister’s official residence.

example_sentences.japanese: 海軍の艦艇の乗組員が不足しています。
example_sentences.english: The crew of the navy’s war fleet is lacking.

notes: "A private residence is a private residence!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この豪華な建物は、大統領の私邸です。
example_sentences.english: This gorgeous building is the president’s private residence.

notes: "This isn't just any lotus. It's THE lotus. The Sacred Lotus. When you see it blooming all alone in a murky pond, you'll know." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The sacred lotus has (はす) a strong significance (and probably some powers). It has something at least, just remember it has something special going on, and you'll be fine."

notes: "If you have the leadership spirit it means you have a lot of ambition to go after the things you want. And you'll be able to lead others because of it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: Despite his youth, my son lacks ambition.

notes: "The constant normal things in your life are also constant. If you normally always do them, then they're also probably a part of your everyday routine." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: You can’t blame your environment for your own unhappiness.

notes: "Constant examples that you use all the time end up becoming part of an established practice. You constantly use them so it just stays that way after a while." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

notes: "If you have the nature of being lazy it will become a habit. The momentum created by your natural laziness will make it so you can't break out of your lazy cycle." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: I had no will to study, I simply attended university out of habit.

example_sentences.english: She seems to be prejudiced against Asian people.

example_sentences.english: They’re the tournament champions from last year.

example_sentences.english: How dare you say you’ve dealt with walking down the thorny path in life just to keep up with their level of hardship.

notes: "Silver apricots are called ginkgo nuts. Okay, they aren't really apricots, but they are silver and they sure look the same." "This word is an exception. You'd think it would be the same in Japanese as it is in English, but it's not. And it has two different readings and meanings. Yikes, sorry. Here's a mnemonic to help you out:Before you read this PLEASE PLEASE REMEMBER this is NOT a jukugo word. It's weird. You're gonna want to type ぎんこう but that's wrong. Stop that now.When you think of a ginkgo tree think about this: Ginkgos are a favorite nesting place for eagles but evil Mrs. Chou likes to eat eagles AND whole gingko trees. She prefers eating eagles WHILE THEY'RE IN THE GINKGO TREES AND ARE STILL ALIVE. So いちょう. Eagles and Mrs. Chou. And gingko trees. It's horrible to think about. Just like this reading not being jukugo.The other meaning is the ginkgo nuts themselves. They taste like 銀 (ぎん) naan (なん). Mm mm soft and metallic, but still not the jukugo word though. How sad for you and all Japanese learners everywhere."
