example_sentences.english: I know a delicious whale meat shop.

notes: "If you catch a whale you're whaling, and that's illegal now so you should probably put the whale back." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は捕鯨には反対です。
example_sentences.english: I’m against whaling.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: うちは雑貨の卸をしています。
example_sentences.english: We sell wholesale goods.

notes: "When you sell something at wholesale value it's being sold at a wholesale price." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: それは卸値で購入することができたんです。
example_sentences.english: I was able to buy it at wholesale price.

notes: "Erase one part of your feelings and you'll only feel a little bit of them. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 一抹の不安が胸をよぎった。
example_sentences.english: For a moment I felt a little anxious.

notes: "A soldier only lays down when she's about to ambush the enemy! If you see some soldiers laying around, it's not that they're lazy, it's because they're getting ready to pounce! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 伏兵に襲われたんだ。
example_sentences.english: They were attacked by an ambush.

english: Captive, Prisoner, Victim To Love, Slave To Lust
notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The worst thing to see as a captive is a 鳥子 (とりこ), a bird child. Imagine seeing a baby bird held captive in a cage. So sad!"

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は、毎日ブログで男を虜にするテクニックについて書いています。
example_sentences.english: She writes on her blog everyday about techniques to captivate men.

notes: "You already learned that the word 洗浄 means ""washing."" So when you're washing the laundry you have to use just the right dose of detergent to make sure they wash properly. If you use too little detergent they'll still smell, but if you use too much detergent the washer will explode with bubbles! Just be careful okay, don't end up like me." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 洗浄剤なら、洗い場の下の棚にあります。
example_sentences.english: There’s detergent under the shelf in the washing area.

english: Fine Work, Good Piece Of Work
notes: "Make something excellent and everyone will call it a fine work. Or make something that sucks and let everyone down. It's your call." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の描いた絵が佳作で入選しました。
example_sentences.english: The picture I drew was chosen as a good piece of work.

notes: "Connect a bunch of things laying in a line. Something's happening here. You can't put your finger on it, but you're pretty sure this is foreshadowing for something else." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 伏線の張り方がすごい。
example_sentences.english: This method of foreshadowing is amazing.

notes: "A VIP comes to your door. They're your guest! I hope you aren't going to make them sleep in the couch." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 来賓の方々をはじめ、皆様にはお忙しい中、ご臨席を賜り誠にありがとうございます。
example_sentences.english: We’d like to thank everyone, including the guests, for honoring us with your presence while you’re all busy.

hiragana: ひんきゃく, ひんかく
notes: "A VIP guest is a guest of honor. They're even more important than a normal guest." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外の賓客を一流の和食でもてなしました。
example_sentences.english: We welcomed the foreign guest of honor with first class Japanese cuisine.

notes: "If you tranquilize yourself heavy enough you'll be just like all the other world leaders today. They're all pretty sedated. Tranquilize yourself too and you'll be just like them!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の会社は、業界の重鎮達を次々と役員に迎え入れた。
example_sentences.english: That company ushered in leaders of industry one after another to their staff.

notes: "At dawn what's the first thing you're supposed to see? Your master. He wants you to wake him up and bring his slippers. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 旦那は出張で今週ずっと留守にしています。
example_sentences.english: The master will be away all week.

notes: "Erase your need for normal tea by drinking matcha. It is far superior to all others and you'll never turn back once you've had a taste." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝抹茶ラテを飲んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I drink a matcha latte every morning.

notes: "Something nearby is near to you. It's very close." "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: There is a restaurant near your house that only sells dishes with soba (そば) noodles in them. They're delicious, but it's so close to your home that you can smell them all the time. Sometimes it feels like that's all you'll ever smell anymore."

example_sentences.japanese: いつまでも君の傍にいるよ。
example_sentences.english: I am always with you.

notes: "The origin of dawn can be found on New Year's Day. That's when the new sun is born and rises above the earth for a whole year until it dies. And that's the origin of dawn, children. Don't let your teachers tell you otherwise." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You didn't learn this reading for 元 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Who's always there on the dawn of New Year's Day welcoming the new sun? Gandhi (がん). He sits on the edge of the earth and makes sure the sun feels welcome. What a nice guy."

example_sentences.japanese: 元旦には家族で初詣に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I’m going to visit a shrine with my family on New Year’s Day.

notes: "A valuable VIP is a noble visitor. They're probably a queen or a diplomat or something. So you better treat them really well." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長が外国の貴賓を接待する際に、通訳として同行しました。
example_sentences.english: When the company president went to welcome a distinguished foreign visitor, I attended as an interpreter.

english: Outline, Border, Silhouette, Summary, Features, Appearance
notes: "Trace the enclosure of a wheel on paper and you'll have drawn its outline." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 涙で輪郭が霞んで見えました。
example_sentences.english: The outline grew hazy from my tears.

notes: "If you ask me to tell the truth I'll say your face is shaped like a melon. No no, it's not a bad thing! You just have a really oval face!" "This word consists of the kun'yomi readings for 瓜 and 顔, but in the middle there, 実 has a bit of an exceptional reading. You certainly haven't learned this weirdness before, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You know who has an oval face? Zane (ざね) formerly from One Direction. When you think of handsome oval faces, picture Zane's."

example_sentences.japanese: 瓜実顔で雰囲気のある女優を探しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m looking for a woman who has an atmosphere with classic features.

english: Painkiller, Pain Reliever, Sedative, Tranquilizer, Tranquiliser
notes: "Tranquilize your pain with a strong dose of painkillers! Yum yum. Don't take too many though!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者に鎮痛剤を注射してもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I received a shot of the painkiller from the doctor.

notes: "Whenever something bad happens to your country to feel an exceptional amount of grief for your fellow country people. This is some serious patriotic concern you've got going on. Let's hope you use those concerns for something good and don't get too carried away." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 憂国の若きサムライたちよ、今こそ立ち上がれ！
example_sentences.english: Young warriors of patriotism, now is the time to stand up!

notes: "Melons from the south are lumpy and orange, sometimes orange and green because they try to look like the hot sun. Wait, those aren't melons, they're pumpkins and squash. Or... kind of a mix of the two, if you already know what kabocha tastes like. " "The reading for this is an exception, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember it:Japanese pumpkins don't taste like American pumpkins. They taste more like canned boiled chocolate (かぼちゃ). Oh, you don't know that either? Well then just taste the pumpkin and you'll know what that tastes like too."

example_sentences.japanese: 南瓜の煮物を炊きました。
example_sentences.english: I’m cooking boiled kabocha.

notes: "A VIP from another country is a state guest." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ大統領が国賓として来日しました。
example_sentences.english: The American President visited Japan as a state guest.

notes: "The prefecture with lots of horse chestnut trees is Tochigi prefecture." "This word consists of the kun'yomi readings for 栃 and 木 and the on'yomi for 県, like most with prefectures. As long as you remember that き is changed to ぎ here, you should be able to remember this reading easily!"

example_sentences.japanese: 栃木県の出身なんですか？
example_sentences.english: Are you from Tochigi Prefecture?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 病院で尿検査をして、妊娠していると言われました。
example_sentences.english: I took a urinalysis test at the hospital and it said I was pregnant.

notes: "If you dig up hollyhocks in the mountains, and grind up their roots, you'll have wasabi! Don't eat too much, or you'll burn your tongue off." This reading is an exception, but I'm sure (at least I hope) that you've heard the word wasabi before. It's the same in Japanese so just remember the meaning and you'll know the reading too!

example_sentences.japanese: やはり、すりたての山葵は美味しいね。
example_sentences.english: Of course, freshly shaven wasabi is delicious.

notes: "You already learned that 披露 means ""announcement"" or ""display,"" so add a banquet to that and you're at a wedding reception! Or if no one's getting married but they're showing off something at a big place with food and stuff it's a just a normal reception." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人の披露宴に出席する際のマナーを教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach me manners for when I attend my friend’s wedding reception.

notes: "Life in Japan was increasing at its fastest rate during the Yayoi Period. It's one of the earliest periods of history in Japan that we know about! You should look it up, if you don't already know about it." "The reading for this word is an exception but it's the same in Japanese as it is in English. So if you just remember it's Yayoi (やよい) in English, you'll remember the Japanese too!"

example_sentences.japanese: 弥生時代のはじまりは紀元前300年頃です。
example_sentences.english: The beginning of the Yayoi Period was approximately 300 BCE.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You meet an artisan and they're tacking pictures on a wall to sell. You want the artisan to make a picture of you too so you yell, ""TACK ME (たくみ)!"""

example_sentences.japanese: この商品のデザインは、匠の技をもって初めて実現することができました。
example_sentences.english: This product’s design was the first time I was able to implement that technique.

notes: "A day you hold in high esteem is an auspicious day. That's a fancy way of saying it's a really lucky day! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 本日は、皇太子殿下御生誕の嘉日なり。
example_sentences.english: It’s the auspicious day of the Crown Prince’s birth today.

english: Bitter Enemies In The Same Boat, Classic Rivals, Traditional Rivals
notes: "You give your rival information that will go beyond what you normally say and you realize the two of you are in the same boat on a lot of personal things. You are bitter enemies in the same boat! Or classic rivals, like you see in movies and read about. You never would have known if you hadn't gone beyond what you normally give people." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 舟 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:What are bitter enemies in the same boat supposed to do? They shoot (しゅう) each other!"

example_sentences.japanese: 利害が一致すれば、呉越同舟も厭わない。
example_sentences.english: If we can share mutual interests, I won’t mind being in the same boat as my rivals.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Snap all the bowstrings! Now none of the musicians can play their instruments. ""You're too rude (つる)!"" they yell, as they cry over the snapped bowstrings. They aren't wrong, that was just too rude of you."

example_sentences.japanese: ギターの弦が緩んでいます。
example_sentences.english: The guitar strings are loose.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 父は、毎日色の違う蝶ネクタイをしていた。
example_sentences.english: My father has a different colored bow tie every day.

notes: "The big military officer is in charge of everyone else. He's the captain. You can tell because he wears a really big captain hat." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大尉の死を決して無駄にはしません。
example_sentences.english: The captain’s death wasn’t useless by any means.

notes: "An artisan has an idea and makes a brand new design!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: これは、意匠が凝らされた素晴らしい作品です。
example_sentences.english: This is a work that had a splendid design applied to it.

notes: "Destitute lands will be faced with a dilemma. Do they leave? Or do they try to make the best of it?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 窮地に追い込まれ、ようやく尻尾を見せました。
example_sentences.english: It was driven into a corner and finally showed it’s tail.

notes: "Destitute conditions lead to distress." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 役所に窮状を訴えたのですが、聞き入れてもらえませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I appealed to the government about the wretched conditions, but I didn’t receive a response.

notes: "If you want to give clothes to other people, you have to buy draperies first and then sew them together. That's a fancy word for cloth. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は呉服屋の一人息子でした。
example_sentences.english: He’s the drapery store’s only son.

notes: "The evil damage you do has an evil effect on people. All that negativity can have a really harmful influence on them. You should think before you do things." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供にゲームをさせないことによる弊害も考えておくべきです。
example_sentences.english: You should also think about how evil it is to not let children play video games.

notes: "A military officer who's in the middle of their career has become a first lieutenant." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が軍の中尉が敵軍に拉致され、処刑されました。
example_sentences.english: Our army’s first lieutenant was captured by the enemy and executed.

notes: "A flood of water still makes a flood." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. But watch out because すい becomes ずい here."

example_sentences.japanese: 台風で川が氾濫し、洪水になりました。
example_sentences.english: The river overflowed from the typhoon and became a flood.

english: Free Of Charge, Gratuitous, Without Pay
notes: "You already learned that 報酬 means ""compensation,"" so adding not to it means you don't have to pay anything. It's free of charge. Nice!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 無報酬でもかまいませんよ。
example_sentences.english: There’s no pay, but I don’t mind.

notes: "Gentlemen who are also samurai are still gentlemen. They just carry swords." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、英国紳士の鏡のような人でした。
example_sentences.english: He looked like the spitting image of an English gentleman.

notes: "Combine a grave and a tombstone and you make a gravestone." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かが墓碑を倒したんです。
example_sentences.english: Someone knocked over the gravestone.

notes: "An artisan who is a giant in their field is a master! Everyone knows their name! Or, they're just really large... like tall, so everyone calls them a master cause they don't want to get crushed." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この女優は、多くの巨匠たちを唸らせた。
example_sentences.english: This actress made many great master’s grunt in admiration.

notes: "An artisan who's good enough to be a teacher has to be a master of her craft." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 師匠と呼ばせてもらえませんか。
example_sentences.english: "May I call you ""master?"""

notes: "If you're confused and you make a mistake, no matter how much you didn't mean it, it's still a mistake. You should ask for help next time you don't know what you're doing and you won't make these errors." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっとそれは時代錯誤じゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Don’t you think that’s a little anachronistic?

notes: "Some tombstones are used to write down the thoughts of dead people. They're monuments. They can be really big or really small, but they have to be dedicated to somebody (usually a dead somebody)." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: これは何の記念碑ですか。
example_sentences.english: What kind of monument is this?

english: No Sense Of Direction, Bad Sense Of Direction
notes: "This is a combination of the words 方向 and 音痴. When your sense of direction is tone-deaf, it means you have no sense of direction. You get lost no matter how hard you try." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は方向音痴で、すぐ道に迷います。
example_sentences.english: I have no sense of direction so I get lost immediately.

notes: "A mediocre person is an ordinary person. There isn't anything weird or interesting about them." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あんたみたいな凡人が書いた本、誰が読むのさ。
example_sentences.english: Who would read a book written by an ordinary person like you?

notes: "You already learned that 歌謡 means ""song,"" so when you add music to that it becomes a super popular song. It's not just a song anymore. It's in everything you hear!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 心に残る昭和の歌謡曲ベスト100のリストが公表されました。
example_sentences.english: A list of the 100 best, most unforgettable, popular songs from the Showa Era was announced.

notes: "The person everyone comes to a mutual agreement about to be the manager of the country is the Prime Minister." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 相 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:The first Prime Minister of Japan was actually the shogun (しょう). That was before everything got complicated."

example_sentences.japanese: 英国宰相から直々に手紙を頂きました。
example_sentences.english: I received a letter from the prime minister of the UK personally.

notes: "Rice grains make up the rice we eat everyday. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社は、米国で米穀を売っています。
example_sentences.english: My company sells rice to America.

notes: "Someone who's only been a military officer for a few years hasn't been able to get very far in the ranks. They're an ensign, or a second lieutenant. That's still not a bad position to be in!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の曽祖父は、旧日本陸軍少尉でした。
example_sentences.english: My great-grandfather was an ex-second lieutenant in the Japanese army.

hiragana: しばいぬ, しばけん
notes: "The brushwood dog is the Shiba Inu. They're the same pretty orange color as brushwood trees, so that's how they got their name." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ニッカは柴犬ではなく珍島犬です。
example_sentences.english: Nikka isn’t a Shiba, she’s a Jindo.

notes: "A tombstone made of a big stone is used as a stone monument. These stones are usually so big that they're used for multiple people who died together. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 津波が襲った高さの地点に石碑が建てられているのです。
example_sentences.english: A stone monument was built at the site where the height of the tsunami hit.

notes: "Remember how 楽 was used in 音楽 and meant ""music?"" Well this is that 楽 again. Music made with a bowstring is string music." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 学生時代に数年ほど弦楽をやっていました。
example_sentences.english: I played string music for several years during my school days.

notes: "You already know that 神社 means ""shinto shrine,"" so add peaceful and country to it and you get a shrine that calls for the peace of the entire country. It's Yasukuni Shrine. If you watch the news you know that this name and everything it stands for is always a topic of current debates." "This is a combination of two words. The first two kanji take the kun'yomi readings and the second two are the jukugo word 神社. You already learned all of these readings, so you should already be able to read this word!"

example_sentences.japanese: 靖国神社に参拝したことはありますか。
example_sentences.english: Have you ever visited Yasukuni Shrine?

english: A And B, First And Second
notes: "A and B make A and B!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どちらも甲乙つけがたい出来栄えだ。
example_sentences.english: It’s hard to say which result is better.

example_sentences.english: This player was offered an extraordinary annual salary, but he rejected it and stayed with his team.

example_sentences.english: If I make this sample I can easily draw up a company statute.

example_sentences.english: When I don’t clean it everyday, the bathtub accumulates grime.

notes: "A blind person is a blind person." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: A man lives in that house who was born blind.

example_sentences.english: The criminal hit a blind spot in the investigation.

example_sentences.english: We’ll cross the channel in this ferry.

notes: "You already know that 循環 means ""circulation,"" so adding container makes it what holds things that circulate. They're your circulatory organs. example_sentences.japanese: 当院には、循環器専門医が五人います。
example_sentences.english: There are five circulatory organ specialists in this hospital.

notes: "I want you to try to bear this truth and that's these kanji make up the word clownfish! Do you think a clownfish is this bear? I'm telling the truth! Maybe. " "This word consists of the kun'yomi readings for all the kanji. You haven't learned these readings for 之 or 実 yet though, so here's a mnemonic to help you:If you get too close to a clownfish, it will hide inside its stinging anemone and shout, ""YOU DON'T KNOW ME (のみ)! It's true, you don't know this clownfish, but you want to. I guess all of them are afraid of strangers though... how will you know me if you don't give me a chance, clownfish?!"

example_sentences.japanese: ニモやその家族は、隠熊之実という魚だよ。
example_sentences.english: Nemo and his family are fish called clownfish.

notes: "Spread out a needle in a tray of water after rubbing it with a magnet and you'll have made a compass! Try it at home kids! It really works!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私にとって、人生の羅針盤だったのです。
example_sentences.english: He was my life’s compass.

example_sentences.japanese: 黒と濃紺のスーツが一着ずつあると便利ですよ。
example_sentences.english: Having one black and one dark blue suit is convenient.

notes: "A tank of water can be used as a fish tank or a water tank for drinking. It really only depends on you and how many fish you have." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どのくらい頻繁に水槽の掃除をしますか。
example_sentences.english: How often do you clean the fish tank?

example_sentences.english: I introduced exercise to improve my bowel movements.

notes: "What do you hit to make a sick beat? A cool little hand drum. " "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You drum and tap it and it as they high five and it makes them super uncomfortable with makes you super happy. That's why you love your hand drum so much."

example_sentences.japanese: あの女性の鼓の打ち方は絶品だ。
example_sentences.english: The way that woman hit her hand drum was superb.

notes: "What's universal? How many times do you think that question's been asked throughout time? Probably a lot of times." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just watch out because へん becomes べん here."

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は何遍みても泣けます。
example_sentences.english: No matter how many times I see this movie, I always cry.

notes: "An article that proves that you're only borrowing money or stuffed animals is called a loan. You have to pay that person back for those fluffy critters." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本が多くの国に円借款を提供しているのはご存知ですか。
example_sentences.english: Did you know that Japan offers international yen loans to many countries?

example_sentences.japanese: 料理には砂糖の代わりに楓糖を使うことが多いです。
example_sentences.english: I often use maple sugar instead of sugar in my cooking.

notes: "When someone quits living you need to offer your condolences during their memorial address. Let it all out and tell everyone what you thought about that dead guy." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: Who will read the funeral address?

example_sentences.english: The navy blue dress suits that young lady’s fair skin.

notes: "One universal event can only happen once. It's too rare to happen more than that." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just watch out because へん becomes ぺん here."

example_sentences.japanese: 一遍だけでいいから、キャビアを食べてみたかったの。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to eat caviar but one time was enough.

hiragana: うーろんちゃ, ウーロンちゃ
notes: "Imperial tea the color of a crow's feathers can only be the famous, delicious Oolong tea. It came from the imperial people of China to Japan (probably) and there are lots of different variants. But the leaves are all that blackish/grey crow feather color." "This word takes the on'yomi readings except for 龍 which is an exception (sorry). You haven't learned the on'yomi for 烏 yet either, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Who loves Oolong tea more than anyone else? Oooo Ron (うーろん) Weasley from Harry Potter. He's British, so of course you'd think he loves tea, but Oolong is his jam. Just picture him and think, oooooh it's Ron, when you drink this kind of tea.And make sure you remember that, because this is also a written in katakana when the kanji isn't used, to type out the long mark ー when you enter your answer."

example_sentences.japanese: 烏龍茶を氷抜きでください。
example_sentences.english: Oolong tea without ice, please.

notes: "A ravine in a valley is still a ravine. It can also be a gorge or a canyon. They're usually really big. Like the Grand Canyon!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 谷 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:If you're going to travel through a huge ravine you have to stay hydrated. The best thing to bring is some taste, cold Coke (こく). Nothing quenches your thirst from sweating through a long, rough ravine like delicious Coke!"

example_sentences.japanese: この峡谷に架かる吊橋を渡ったことはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Have you ever crossed the bridge that spans over this ravine?

notes: "A public building where you welcome VIP guests is a reception hall. Or a guest house if they're staying the night." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、迎賓館に招待されました。
example_sentences.english: I was invited to the reception hall.

hiragana: あらじお, あらしお
notes: "If you want to find some coarse salt just dive in the sea and collect sea salt! The pieces are nice and big and lumpy, so you really taste it when you're cooking." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You've learned both of these readings by now so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: お風呂に粗塩を入れると体にいいらしいですよ。
example_sentences.english: Putting sea salt in baths seems to be good for you.

notes: "A robber who steals is a thief. And still a robber, I guess." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度こそ盗賊の隠れ家を突き止めてやる。
example_sentences.english: I’ll find the thief’s hiding place this time.

example_sentences.japanese: この土地は何坪ぐらいですか？
example_sentences.english: How many tsubo is this land?

notes: "You already know that 循環 means ""circulation"" or ""cycle,"" so adding bad to that makes it a vicious circle. Take a look if you've never heard of this before." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: まずは、あなたの心の悪循環を断ち切ることが大切です。
example_sentences.english: First of all, it’s important to cut off the vicious circle in your heart.

notes: "A rotation of wind forms a whirlwind!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Watch out because ふう becomes ぷう here (hehe)."

example_sentences.japanese: トフグは、日本語学習業界に旋風を巻き起こしています。
example_sentences.english: Tofugu is creating a whirlwind in the Japanese learning industry.

notes: "The mother of good fermentation is yeast! If you want to bake a pie or bread you have to have the best. And if you don't have any, maybe your neighbor has some extra that you can borrow?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 自作酵母を使ってパンを作っています。
example_sentences.english: I’m using my own yeast to make bread.

notes: "Pardon someone out of the kindness in your heart and you'll have granted them amnesty. How kind of you." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大統領は、七面鳥に恩赦を与えた。
example_sentences.english: The president granted amnesty to the turkey.

notes: "A butterfly with another butterfly added to it? It's still a butterfly, just a really big one with... with four wings. And laser eyes? Oh well, just go with it. It's a butterfly." The reading is just the on'yomi readings (which you learned with the kanji) twice in a row.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は蝶々のように自由な女性でした。
example_sentences.english: She was a woman who was as free as a butterfly.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you to remember: A chicken is a newer 鳥 (にわとり). Well, it's a newer type of 鳥 compared to falcons and condors that have been around for ages. But chickens have only been around as long as us humans. Making them newer birds."

example_sentences.japanese: 育てたひよこが鶏になりました。
example_sentences.english: The chick I raised became a chicken.

notes: "A chicken egg is a chicken egg." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 卵 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Who loves chicken eggs? Randy (らん) Savage! Especially when he eats them with slim jims. Mmm eggs and slim jims. You should give it a try."

example_sentences.japanese: 鶏卵は日本が自給自足できる唯一の蛋白源です。
example_sentences.english: Chicken eggs are the only source of protein in Japan that is self sufficient.

notes: "Foster a bunch of chickens and start chicken farming! They will be your best friends! Your only friends." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 養鶏経営の難しさを痛感しました。
example_sentences.english: I realized how difficult managing poultry raising is.

example_sentences.japanese: できるだけ鶏肉のささみを食べるようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I try to make sure I eat as much white meat from chicken as I can.

notes: "Write down the years of your genealogy in order and it makes a chronological record of your life. Look back on it when you're old and sigh about the old days." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この作家の年譜を作ってくれないか。
example_sentences.english: Will you make a chronological record for this author?

This word uses the kun'yomi reading for one kanji and the on'yomi reading for the other. Just remember that they're the two readings you didn't learn when you learned the kanji and you should be okay.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のおかしな言動に、みんな呆気に取られていました。
example_sentences.english: Everyone was taken aback by the woman’s odd behavior.

notes: "The master of a fiefdom is the feudal lord. We also call them Daimyo." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 棋譜の付け方を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach me how to record a game.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 紳士 means ""gentleman?"" Well when two men determine that the best thing to do is cooperate they form a gentlemen's agreement." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: They’re supposed to be tied to a gentlemen’s agreement.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人と間違われて手錠を掛けられたんだ。
example_sentences.english: I was mistaken for a criminal and handcuffed.

notes: "Remember how 縛る means ""to tie?"" Well if you tie something around someone's neck then it's called hanging. They'll probably die from it too, so it can also be death by hanging. " "This is a combination of the words 縛る and 首. Both use the kun'yomi readings, so just change the る to り and it's pretty simple!"

example_sentences.english: In the Edo period, there was a punishment called death by hanging.

english: Hero, Bold Person, Daring Person, Extraordinary Person

example_sentences.english: Who do you think the greatest hero in Japanese history is?

example_sentences.english: Good evening ladies and gentlemen.

example_sentences.english: For some reason I feel more comfortable getting information from paper media.

notes: "A muddy stream is a muddy stream!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: He rescued the things that were gulped down by the muddy stream.

notes: "On the surface of a score you'll find music. This is only written music though, so remember that this music has to be on the surface of some paper." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.english: I’m looking for a site where I can download music for free.

notes:

notes: "You take a dose of medicine but it gets locked in your throat because it's the kind of pill you chew, not swallow! You need to pay attention to which one is which or it won't help at all." notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji resent, so it means resentment." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. example_sentences.english: My wife put on a beautiful silk gown and died.

notes: "A silk thread is silk thread!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 糸 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:Who only uses silk thread in their clothes? Sheep (し)! Sheep can't wear wool thread, oh no, what are you, some kind of monster?! Sheep all wear clothes made from silk threads while they're waiting for their wool to grow back."

example_sentences.japanese: 西陣の糸屋で絹糸を買ってきてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Please go buy silk thread at the Nishijin thread store.

notes: "You already know that 楽器 means ""musical instrument"" so adding a couple of bowstrings to it will make it a stringed instrument." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の叔父は、弦楽器の修理をしています。
example_sentences.english: My uncle repairs stringed instruments.

notes: "Feelings that make you sigh out loud are really strong feelings. You wouldn't sigh if they didn't move you so much." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 感慨がこめられた彼女の歌声に感動しました。
example_sentences.english: I was deeply moved by the strong feelings in her voice when she sang.

notes: "Mix sulfur and acid and you'll get sulfuric acid! That's how science works! How simple!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どこで硫酸を手に入れたんだ。
example_sentences.english: Where did you get your hands on some sulfuric acid?

notes: "Remember how you learned that 猶予 means ""extension?"" Well you wake up ready to sue people when you're told there has been an extension, meaning there was a suspension of indictment on your case. What the heck, you woke up ready for this! Now you have to wait to try and sue them." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 起訴猶予処分がくだされました。
example_sentences.english: The suspension of indictment punishment was passed.

notes: "The child of musical beats is the tempo. You can only keep time if you have a good beat to guide you, like a father." "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 拍 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:You get the tempo and the rhythm going in your body. You can't help but sing out loud, ""Heyo (ひょう), heyo!"" Feel that rhythm and sing with me! HEYO HEYO!"

example_sentences.japanese: 拍子抜けしてしまったよ。
example_sentences.english: Well that was anticlimactic.

english: Tied Down By Money, Sleep Paralysis, Bound Hand And Foot, Temporary Paralysis
notes: "Remember how you learned that 縛る means ""to bind?"" Well if you're being bound because of gold then you're tied down by money. This word also means sleep paralysis. Just imagine if you were dreaming that your body felt like it had turned to gold and that you were tied down too." "This is a combination of the words 金 and 縛る. Both use the kun'yomi readings, but 金 becomes かな instead of かね. If you can remember that exception, this should be easy!"

example_sentences.japanese: 金縛りにあったことはありますか。
example_sentences.english: Have you ever had sleep paralysis before?

notes: "A reef in the shape of a loop is an atoll. If you don't know what that is, it's a circular coral reef. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: その時、日本のマグロ漁船「第五福竜丸」がたまたまビキニ環礁を航行しており、乗組員が被ばくしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: "The Japanese tuna boat ""S.S. Lucky Dragon 5"" accidentally sailed around Bikini Atoll and the crew was exposed to radiation."

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 岬の突端にカフェがあるんです。
example_sentences.english: There’s a cafe on the tip of the cape.

notes: "If you are saying congratulations and also giving your condolences then they are congratulations and condolences. Pretty easy, right?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 慶弔用の礼服は持っているのか。
example_sentences.english: Do you have ceremonial dress for celebration and condolences?

english: Crossing Gate, Railway Crossing Gate, Circuit Breaker
notes: "Remember how 遮断 means ""isolation?"" Well the machine that isolates you from a train is a crossing gate. That way you won't walk, bike, or drive your car into an oncoming train." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 遮断機が降りている時に、線路を渡ってはいけません。
example_sentences.english: When the railroad crossing gate comes down, do not cross the tracks.

notes: "Dairy farming is dairy farming!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは日本酪農発祥の地です。
example_sentences.english: This is the location of the origin of Japanese dairy farming.

notes: "The times when you are in mourning each year are for a loved one's death anniversary. They come around again every year. It's important you remember your loved ones at this time." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は祖父の三回忌です。
example_sentences.english: Today is the second anniversary of my grandfather’s death.

notes: "East Asia is East Asia! That's where Japan is!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 太平洋戦争のことを、大東亜戦争と呼ぶのは何故ですか。
example_sentences.english: Why is the Pacific War called The Greater East Asian War?

english: E. Coli, Escherichia Coli, E Coli
notes: "Remember how you learned that 大腸 means ""large intestines?"" Well when you get bacteria in there you end up with E. Coli. Go to a doctor right away! You're gonna be stuck in the bathroom for a while. Sorry..." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大腸菌を美少女に擬人化させたカードアプリ・ゲームがあります。
example_sentences.english: There’s a card app game that personifies E. Coli as a beautiful woman.

english: First Anniversary Of Death, First Death Anniversary
notes: "Remember how you learned that 一周 means ""one time around?"" Well if you're mourning one time like this a year, then it's because it's the first anniversary of death for a family member. Maybe it was the death of your mom, your grandad or your goldfish, this is the first year since they died. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 七月には、妻の父の一周忌の法事があります。
example_sentences.english: In July we’re having the ceremony for my wife’s father’s first death anniversary.

notes: "Stones that form in your guts are gallstones. Sometimes you have to get them surgically taken out. Scary!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 胆嚢炎は、ほとんどの場合、胆石が原因です。
example_sentences.english: With inflammation of the gallbladder, the most likely cause is gallstones.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. You learned this reading with the kanji, so you should be able to read it already!

example_sentences.japanese: お前はもう少し胆を練る必要がある。
example_sentences.english: You need to build up your courage.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You make lacquer out of uni root sh*t (うるし). You gotta get deep in the uni to the root of its sh*t and rub it into a paste to make the lacquer. Then rub that on wooden stuff! Yay! Uni root sh*t!"

example_sentences.japanese: 漆の葉を触ると手がかぶれますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you touch a lacquer leaf you’ll get a rash on your hand.

notes: "Lacquer containers are called Lacquerware. Those pretty bowls you're eating out of? That shininess is because it's lacquerware!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 漆器の手入れの仕方を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach me how to maintain lacquer ware.

notes: "The official method of doing anything requires hiring a lawyer. They have to be there when you sign forms or sue people, or it isn't official at all." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 法曹を目指そうと思ったきっかけは何ですか。
example_sentences.english: What made you pursue your dream of becoming a lawyer?

notes: "A dark reef is still a reef. It's just really deep underwater so it's kinda dark under there. Because of that it can also be called a sunken reef." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 船長は、暗礁に気をつけてと言って、僕に操縦を任せた。
example_sentences.english: The captain told me to be careful of reefs and then left the steering to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 捜査は暗礁に乗り上げてしまったな。
example_sentences.english: The investigation went cold unexpectedly.

english: Reef, Sunken Rocks, Shore Reef, Rock Reef
notes: "A reef made of boulders is still a reef, but it's made of sunken rocks." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 岩礁を埋め立て、人工島に造り替えたんです。
example_sentences.english: The reef was filled up and replaced with an artificial island.

notes: "A young woman who is planting rice from early morning into the latter evenings is a rice planting girl. You'll see them out there all day long, from dawn till dusk, planting, taking care of, and picking rice." "This is a really weird exception, sorry. You've kind of learned these reading, but they're like... weird variations of them.Take the さ from 早速, the おつ becomes おと, and then the 女 kun'yomi め (hey that one's normal!). And you get さおとめ. You might need to just memorize this one."

example_sentences.japanese: 昔は稲の苗を水田に植えつける女性のことを「早乙女」や「植女」と呼んでいました。
example_sentences.english: Long ago, women who planted rice seedlings were called Saotome or Ueme.

english: Root Of Evil, Source Of Evil
notes: "Evil's root is the root of evil. It's the source of evil things." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: できれば禍根を残すことは避けたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to avoid turning a blind eye to future trouble, if I can.

english: Spinning And Weaving, Weaving And Spinning
notes: "Spinning and weaving means spinning and weaving. Yay!" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 織 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:While you're spinning and weaving you are always absolutely shocked (しょく) by what you make. You never really know when you start and then BAM! You made elephant slippers. That's just how it works and it shocks you every single time."

example_sentences.japanese: 日本繊維産業は、綿紡織、化繊を中心として復興しました。
example_sentences.english: The Japanese textile industry was revived mainly by cotton spinning and weaving and synthetic fibers.

notes: "You should congratulate a person who speaks lots of different dialects because they have to be a really strong person to be able to do it. You think learning Japanese is hard now, just wait till you hear Osaka-ben and Hokkaido-ben. It takes a really strong person to learn all those dialects, so congratulate them and tell them how strong they are!Fun Fact: 弁慶 is the name of an actual historical figure who was really strong. They were so strong, that we now use their name to refer to all strong people. Think of it like calling someone Hercules or Achilles in Western languages." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 弁慶の泣き所を棚にぶつけたんだ。
example_sentences.english: I hit my Achille’s heel on a shelf.

english: Tsukemono, Japanese Pickled Vegetables, Pickled Vegetables, Preserved Vegetables
notes: "Pickled things are Japanese pickled vegetables! Or tsukemono if you've already been eating yummy pickled ginger, daikon, and umeboshi!" "You already learned 漬ける meaning ""to pickle"" so just take the る off there shove the け into the kanji. You read it still, but it's hiding. It probably shrunk in the pickling process. Stick some things (もの) on there are you know the reading! Not bad! By the way, sometimes you'll see this word spelled like 漬け物 too."

example_sentences.japanese: この漬物は誰が漬けたんですか。
example_sentences.english: Who pickled these tsukemono?

notes: "Someone who floats and wanders from place to place is a vagrant. They don't really have a home, but they keep hanging around yours. It's kind of annoying. (This word has a negative connotation, you wouldn't use it for someone who is just homeless, unless you're really mean.)" "This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 浮 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:All the vagrants you know are fools (ふ). They just left their homes and now they float around your city for no reason. You ask them why and they shrug. You've never seen a better definition of a fool before in your life!"

example_sentences.japanese: 浮浪者でも7割の人は何らかの仕事をして日銭を稼いでいる。
example_sentences.english: 70% of vagrants do some kind of work and earn a daily cash income.

notes: "One of the most evil things about war are the war damages that happen during it. Whole countrysides, cities, and lots of people can die. So I'd say the ravages of war are the most evil thing about war. Period." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 戦禍を逃れて田舎に疎開した。
example_sentences.english: We escaped the ravages of war and evacuated into the countryside.

notes: "Remember how you learned that 解剖 means ""autopsy?"" Well you have to learn about anatomy before you're going to be allowed to perform an autopsy or dissect anything. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学では解剖学を研究しています。
example_sentences.english: I study anatomy in college.

notes: "Hide your name for anonymity. There's lots of that here on the internet. In fact, you're probably using a pseudonym right now, aren't you? Yeah, you are. You can't hide THAT from me at least... uh... Ssssteve?" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 匿名で投書をしました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a letter to the editor anonymously.

notes: "Barbarians go around and commit acts of barbarism! What else would they do? They're barbarians!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつらはそこで蛮行を繰り返しているんだ。
example_sentences.english: They repeated the brutality over there.

notes: "A groom gets a flower on his lapel and he's finally a real bridegroom! Before that he was just waiting to be one. The flower makes it for real." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 花婿が結婚式場から逃げ出したらしいわよ。
example_sentences.english: The groom ran away from the wedding!

notes: "Remember how you learned that 死刑 means ""death penalty?"" Well a criminal who has been sentenced to it is a condemned criminal. They're condemned to death." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 死刑囚はこの階段を登って死刑台へと向かうんだ。
example_sentences.english: Condemned criminals climbed these stairs and faced the gallows.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: かわいい狐が茂みからひょこっと顔を出した。
example_sentences.english: A cute fox suddenly poked its head out of the thicket.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 作文の書き出しは、一升開けて下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please start your composition in the first box.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.english: My daughter is very fortunate to get such a nice husband.

example_sentences.japanese: 藍染の藍は天然ですが、ジーンズに使われる合成インディゴは人工的なものです。
example_sentences.english: Indigo plant dye is natural, but the synthetic dye used for jeans is artificial.

english: Long Shamisen Song, Epic Shamisen Song, Nagauta
notes: "A long shamisen song is a long shamisen song! They're also called nagauta, and they're usually pretty epic too." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 長唄教室に通い始めました。
example_sentences.english: I started to go to the nagauta class.

notes: "The pillar the sail is attached to is called a mast. Without it the sail wouldn't do it's job and your sailboat wouldn't move at all." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: この木は帆柱にちょうどいいぞ。
example_sentences.english: This tree is perfect for a mast.

notes: "A stream that runs through a valley is a mountain stream. Valleys happen in between mountains, so just picture the river running through the middle of them in your head." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: ラフティングで渓流を下りました。
example_sentences.english: We went rafting down the mountain stream.

notes: "Add a bridge to a jetty and you'll have a pretty cool pier. Put a ferris wheel on there and make some money!" "This word consists of the on'yomi reading for 桟 and the kun'yomi reading for 橋. example_sentences.japanese: 船は桟橋に繋いでいます。
example_sentences.english: The ship is tied to the pier.

notes: "Remember how 戯れる can mean ""to play"" or ""to flirt?"" Well this is when you play flirt! Or just make a joke." Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading already so you should be able to read it!

example_sentences.japanese: 戯れに文章を綴っただけなのに、賞を獲ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Even though I only wrote it as a joke, I won an award.

notes: "A criminal person will end up as a prisoner if they get caught! " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして囚人は縞々の服を着ているんですか。
example_sentences.english: Why do prisoners wear striped clothes?

notes: "A sail boat is a sailboat!" This word uses the on'yomi readings. You know them!

example_sentences.japanese: 店内は帆船をイメージした内装となっております。
example_sentences.english: The interior of the shop will be designed with images of sailboats.

notes: "What do you hear that is really ugly? A scandal. Scandals are the ugliest topics for gossip." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰がこんな根も葉もない醜聞を流したんだ。
example_sentences.english: Who spread this completely untrue scandal?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. example_sentences.japanese: この海藻は食べられますか。
example_sentences.english: Can you eat this seaweed?

english: Shameful Sight, Disgraceful Behavior, Disgraceful Behaviour
notes: "Something with an ugly appearance is a shameful sight. You feel bad just looking at it. It probably feels bad too." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: とんだ醜態を晒してしまったよ。
example_sentences.english: They were exposed to an unimaginably shameful sight.

notes: "Your daughter's groom will become your son in law. He's a great guy! Congratulations!" The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: いずれは娘婿を社長にするつもりです。
example_sentences.english: Sooner or later, I intend to make my son company president.

english: Southern Barbarians, Nanban, South Sea Countries
notes: "Southern barbarians are called Southern barbarians! They're pretty commonly called Nanban people in English if you've read the history. There's yummy food named after them too!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: チキン南蛮の簡単でおいしいレシピがあれば教えてください。
example_sentences.english: If you have a good, simple recipe for chicken nanban, please let me know.

hiragana: ゆうすい, わきみず
notes: "A well of water that pops up naturally is called a spring and that water is spring water." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 地下水が地表に自然に出てきたものを、湧水といいます。
example_sentences.english: Underground water that naturally comes to the surface is called a spring.

notes: "Measure that shape on the paper with your eyes. It's got four sides.. it's.. it's a square! Or a box from above maybe... But it's definitely the kind you fill in on a graph." The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You learned them when you learned the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 升目を数えると、全部で400ありました。
example_sentences.english: When I counted the boxes there were 400 total.

notes: "A pit that's used as a road is called a tunnel. Or a mine, if they're taking valuable things out of it." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 地下20mのところに坑道が掘られています。
example_sentences.english: They’re digging a tunnel somewhere 20 miles underground.

notes: "The containers your urine secretes into are your urinary organs. " This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 泌尿器の病気で入院することになりました。
example_sentences.english: I was hospitalized from a urinary organ disease.

notes: "A valley in a valley is still a valley!" This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 温泉湯舎から渓谷美を一望することができます。
example_sentences.english: We can overlook the beautiful valley from the onsen’s bath huts.

notes: "A widowed wife is a widow." This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

example_sentences.japanese: 寡婦控除について詳しく教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please explain widow deductions to me in detail.
